        logger.info("="*80 + "\n")


# ============================================================================
# ANTI-PATTERNS TO AVOID
# ============================================================================

class AntiPatterns:
    """
    Demonstrates common anti-patterns and how to avoid them
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def antipattern_no_cleanup():
        """
        ANTI-PATTERN: Not cleaning up resources at all
        """
        logger.warning("ANTI-PATTERN: No cleanup")
        
        spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("NoCleanup").getOrCreate()
        
        # BAD: Create many DataFrames without cleanup
        for i in range(10):
            df = spark.range(1000000)
            df.cache()  # Cache but never unpersist
            df.count()  # Trigger action
        
        # Memory keeps growing!
        # spark.stop() might be forgotten
        
        logger.warning("This will cause memory issues!")
    
    @staticmethod
    def antipattern_over_caching():
        """
        ANTI-PATTERN: Caching everything
        """
        logger.warning("ANTI-PATTERN: Over-caching")
        
        with SparkSessionManager("OverCaching") as spark:
            # BAD: Cache DataFrames that are only used once
            df1 = spark.range(1000).cache()  # Used only once - don't cache!
            df2 = df1.filter(col("id") > 500).cache()  # Used only once - don't cache!
            df3 = df2.groupBy().count().cache()  # Aggregated result - don't cache!
            
            # Write once
            df3.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/output")
            
            # All that caching was wasteful!
        
        logger.warning("Only cache DataFrames used multiple times!")
    
    @staticmethod
    def antipattern_forgot_unpersist():
        """
        ANTI-PATTERN: Caching without unpersisting
        """
        logger.warning("ANTI-PATTERN: Forgot to unpersist")
        
        with SparkSessionManager("ForgotUnpersist") as spark:
            # BAD: Cache but forget to unpersist
            df = spark.range(1000000).cache()
            df.count()
            
            # Do more work...
            result = df.filter(col("id") > 1000)
            result.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/output")
            
            # FORGOT: df.unpersist()
            # Memory not released!
        
        logger.warning("Always unpersist cached DataFrames when done!")
    
    @staticmethod
    def correct_pattern():
        """
        CORRECT: Proper resource management
        """
        logger.info("CORRECT PATTERN: Proper cleanup")
        
        with SparkSessionManager("CorrectPattern") as spark:
            with SparkDataFrameManager(spark, "data") as df_mgr:
                # GOOD: Use context manager
                df = df_mgr.load("/tmp/spark_cleanup_demo/input", cache=True)
                
                # Use DataFrame multiple times (justifies caching)
                count1 = df.count()
                count2 = df.filter(col("status") == "active").count()
                
                logger.info(f"Total: {count1}, Active: {count2}")
                
                # Write result
                df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/output")
            
            # Automatic cleanup via context manager
        
        logger.info("✓ Resources properly managed!")

# CONFIGURATION AND CONSTANTS
# ============================================================================

class CleanupConfig:
    """
    Configuration constants for cleanup patterns
    """
    
    # Memory thresholds (in MB)
    MEMORY_WARNING_THRESHOLD = 1024  # 1 GB
    MEMORY_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD = 2048  # 2 GB
    
    # Cleanup thresholds
    LAZY_CLEANUP_THRESHOLD = 5  # Number of cached DFs before cleanup
    REFERENCE_COUNT_WARNING = 10  # Warn if ref count exceeds this
    
    # Timing thresholds (in seconds)
    LONG_OPERATION_THRESHOLD = 60  # Log warning if operation takes longer
    
    # Spark configurations
    DEFAULT_SPARK_CONFIG = {
        "spark.sql.adaptive.enabled": "true",
        "spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled": "true",
        "spark.cleaner.referenceTracking.cleanCheckpoints": "true",
        "spark.cleaner.periodicGC.interval": "30min",
        "spark.cleaner.referenceTracking": "true"
    }
    
    # Logging configuration
    LOG_FORMAT = "%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"
    LOG_LEVEL = logging.INFO
    
    @classmethod
    def get_spark_config(cls, custom_config: dict = None) -> dict:
        """Get Spark configuration with optional custom settings"""
        config = cls.DEFAULT_SPARK_CONFIG.copy()
        if custom_config:
            config.update(custom_config)
        return config

# ADVANCED MONITORING
# ============================================================================

class AdvancedResourceMonitor:
    """
    Advanced monitoring with alerts and recommendations
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.metrics = ResourceMonitor()
        self.alerts = []
        self.start_time = datetime.now()
    
    def check_memory_usage(self):
        """Check current memory usage and raise alerts"""
        current_memory = get_memory_usage()
        
        if current_memory > CleanupConfig.MEMORY_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD:
            alert = f"CRITICAL: Memory usage at {current_memory:.2f} MB"
            self.alerts.append(alert)
            logger.critical(alert)
        elif current_memory > CleanupConfig.MEMORY_WARNING_THRESHOLD:
            alert = f"WARNING: Memory usage at {current_memory:.2f} MB"
            self.alerts.append(alert)
            logger.warning(alert)
    
    def check_cleanup_rate(self):
        """Check cleanup effectiveness and provide recommendations"""
        report = self.metrics.get_report()
        cleanup_rate = report['cleanup_rate_percent']
        
        if cleanup_rate < 80:
            recommendation = (
                f"Low cleanup rate ({cleanup_rate:.1f}%). "
                "Consider using more aggressive cleanup patterns."
            )
            self.alerts.append(recommendation)
            logger.warning(recommendation)
        elif cleanup_rate < 100:
            recommendation = (
                f"Cleanup rate at {cleanup_rate:.1f}%. "
                "Some resources may not be cleaned up."
            )
            self.alerts.append(recommendation)
            logger.info(recommendation)
    
    def get_runtime_stats(self) -> dict:
        """Get runtime statistics"""
        runtime = (datetime.now() - self.start_time).total_seconds()
        
        return {
            "runtime_seconds": runtime,
            "runtime_minutes": runtime / 60,
            "alerts_count": len(self.alerts),
            "memory_current_mb": get_memory_usage()
        }
    
    def print_final_report(self):
        """Print comprehensive final report"""
        runtime_stats = self.get_runtime_stats()
        cleanup_report = self.metrics.get_report()
        
        logger.info("\n" + "="*80)
        logger.info("ADVANCED MONITORING FINAL REPORT")
        logger.info("="*80)
        logger.info(f"Runtime: {runtime_stats['runtime_minutes']:.2f} minutes")
        logger.info(f"Current Memory: {runtime_stats['memory_current_mb']:.2f} MB")
        logger.info(f"Cleanup Rate: {cleanup_report['cleanup_rate_percent']:.2f}%")
        logger.info(f"Total Alerts: {runtime_stats['alerts_count']}")
        
        if self.alerts:
            logger.info("\nAlerts:")
            for i, alert in enumerate(self.alerts, 1):
                logger.info(f"  {i}. {alert}")
        
        logger.info("="*80 + "\n")

2. Lazy Cleanup Pattern
   - Deferred cleanup based on thresholds
   - Best for long-running batch jobs
   - Class: LazyCleanupPattern

3. Reference Counting Pattern
   - Cleanup when reference count reaches zero
   - Best for shared resources
   - Class: ReferenceCountedResource, ReferenceCountingPattern

4. Finalizer Pattern

   - Best as safety net for forgotten cleanup

def cryptographic_hash_pattern(dataframe):
    """
    Applies cryptographic hashing using various algorithms.
    Best for: Security-sensitive data, compliance requirements
    """
    
    # SHA-256 hashing (most common for security)
    result_df = dataframe.withColumn(

    )

    @udf(StringType())
    def salted_hash(value, salt="my_secret_salt"):
        """Add salt to increase security"""
        salted_value = value + salt
        return hashlib.sha256(salted_value.encode()).hexdigest()
    
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "email_salted_sha256",
        salted_hash(col("email"))
    )
    
    return result_df

def non_cryptographic_hash_pattern(dataframe):

        "bucket_id",
        expr("abs(hash(email)) % 10")
    )

    @udf(IntegerType())
    def simple_hash(value):

        for char in value:

        return hash_val
    
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "custom_simple_hash",
        simple_hash(col("email"))
    )
    
    return result_df

Purpose: Distribute data across nodes with minimal redistribution when nodes change
Characteristics:
- Minimal key redistribution when nodes added/removed
- Virtual nodes for better distribution
- Ring-based architecture
Use Cases: Distributed caching, load balancing, database sharding
""")


class ConsistentHash:
    """
    Consistent Hashing implementation for distributed systems.
    Uses virtual nodes for better distribution.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, nodes: List[str], virtual_nodes: int = 150):
        """
        Initialize consistent hash ring.
        
        Args:
            nodes: List of node identifiers
            virtual_nodes: Number of virtual nodes per physical node
        """
        self.virtual_nodes = virtual_nodes
        self.ring = {}
        self.sorted_keys = []
        
        for node in nodes:
            self.add_node(node)
    
    def _hash(self, key: str) -> int:
        """Generate hash value for a key"""
        return int(hashlib.md5(key.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
    
    def add_node(self, node: str):
        """Add a node to the hash ring"""
        for i in range(self.virtual_nodes):
            virtual_key = f"{node}:{i}"
            hash_val = self._hash(virtual_key)
            self.ring[hash_val] = node
        
        self.sorted_keys = sorted(self.ring.keys())
    
    def remove_node(self, node: str):
        """Remove a node from the hash ring"""
        for i in range(self.virtual_nodes):
            virtual_key = f"{node}:{i}"
            hash_val = self._hash(virtual_key)
            if hash_val in self.ring:
                del self.ring[hash_val]
        
        self.sorted_keys = sorted(self.ring.keys())
    
    def get_node(self, key: str) -> str:
        """Get the node responsible for a key"""
        if not self.ring:
            return None
        
        hash_val = self._hash(key)
        
        # Find the first node clockwise from the hash value
        idx = bisect.bisect_right(self.sorted_keys, hash_val)
        if idx == len(self.sorted_keys):
            idx = 0
        
        return self.ring[self.sorted_keys[idx]]


def consistent_hashing_pattern(dataframe):
    """
    Applies consistent hashing to distribute data across nodes.
    Best for: Distributed caching, sharding, load balancing
    """
    
    # Define nodes (e.g., cache servers, database shards)
    nodes = ["node1", "node2", "node3", "node4"]
    ch = ConsistentHash(nodes, virtual_nodes=100)
    
    # UDF to assign data to nodes using consistent hashing
    @udf(StringType())
    def get_assigned_node(key):
        """Assign key to a node using consistent hashing"""
        return ch.get_node(key)
    
    result_df = dataframe.withColumn(
        "assigned_node",
        get_assigned_node(col("email"))
    )
    
    # Show distribution
    print("\nData Distribution Across Nodes:")
    result_df.groupBy("assigned_node").count().show()
    
    # Demonstrate minimal redistribution when adding a node
    ch.add_node("node5")
    
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "assigned_node_after_scale",
        get_assigned_node(col("email"))
    )
    
    # Show which keys moved
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "moved",
        col("assigned_node") != col("assigned_node_after_scale")
    )
    
    print("\nAfter adding node5:")
    result_df.groupBy("assigned_node_after_scale").count().show()
    
    print("\nKeys that moved to different nodes:")
    result_df.filter(col("moved")).select("email", "assigned_node", "assigned_node_after_scale").show()
    
    return result_df

Characteristics:
- Very fast performance
- Good distribution properties
- Low collision rate
- Multiple variants (MurmurHash2, MurmurHash3)
Use Cases: Hash tables, bloom filters, data partitioning, checksums
""")


def murmur_hash_pattern(dataframe):
    """
    Applies MurmurHash3 for fast, well-distributed hashing.
    Best for: Hash tables, bloom filters, partitioning
    """
    
    # MurmurHash3 32-bit
    @udf(IntegerType())
    def murmur3_32(value, seed=0):
        """MurmurHash3 32-bit hash"""
        return mmh3.hash(value, seed)
    
    # MurmurHash3 128-bit (returns as string hex)
    @udf(StringType())
    def murmur3_128(value, seed=0):
        """MurmurHash3 128-bit hash"""
        hash_bytes = mmh3.hash128(value, seed, signed=False)
        return hex(hash_bytes)
    
    result_df = dataframe.withColumn(
        "email_murmur32",
        murmur3_32(col("email"))
    )
    
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "email_murmur128",
        murmur3_128(col("email"))
    )
    
    # Use MurmurHash for partitioning (positive values only)
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "partition_id",
        expr("abs(hash(email)) % 4")  # Spark uses MurmurHash3 internally
    )
    
    # Seeded hash for different hash spaces
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "email_murmur32_seed42",
        murmur3_32(col("email"), lit(42))
    )
    
    return result_df

Use Cases: Checksums, data deduplication, ETL tracking (not for passwords!)
""")


def md5_hash_pattern(dataframe):
    """
    Applies MD5 hashing for checksums and data deduplication.
    Best for: Checksums, ETL tracking, deduplication (NOT for security)
    """
    
    # Basic MD5 hash
    result_df = dataframe.withColumn(
        "email_md5",
        md5(col("email"))
    )
    
    # Composite MD5 for record fingerprinting
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "record_fingerprint",
        md5(concat_ws("|", col("id"), col("email"), col("ip_address")))
    )
    
    # Custom MD5 with prefix/suffix
    @udf(StringType())
    def custom_md5(value, prefix="", suffix=""):
        """MD5 with custom prefix/suffix"""
        full_value = prefix + value + suffix
        return hashlib.md5(full_value.encode()).hexdigest()
    
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "email_md5_custom",
        custom_md5(col("email"), lit("prefix_"), lit("_suffix"))
    )
    
    # Use MD5 for deduplication
    print("\nUsing MD5 for deduplication:")
    
    # Create duplicate data
    duplicate_data = data + [(6, "john.doe@email.com", "192.168.1.1", "sensitive_data_1")]
    dup_df = spark.createDataFrame(duplicate_data, ["id", "email", "ip_address", "sensitive_data"])
    
    dup_df = dup_df.withColumn(
        "record_hash",
        md5(concat_ws("|", col("email"), col("ip_address"), col("sensitive_data")))
    )
    
    print("\nBefore deduplication:")
    dup_df.show()
    
    print("\nAfter deduplication using MD5:")
    dedup_df = dup_df.dropDuplicates(["record_hash"])
    dedup_df.show()
    
    return result_df


md5_df = md5_hash_pattern(df)
md5_df.select("email", "email_md5", "record_fingerprint").show(truncate=False)


# =============================================================================
# 6. SHA HASH PATTERN
# =============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("6. SHA HASH PATTERN")
print("=" * 80)
print("""
Purpose: Secure crypt
```python
ographic hashing with various security levels
Characteristics:
- Multiple variants (SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512)
- Cryptographically secure (except SHA-1)
- Slower than MD5 but more secure
- Industry standard for security applications
Use Cases: Digital signatures, certificates, password hashing, data integrity
""")


def sha_hash_pattern(dataframe):
    """
    Applies SHA hashing with different variants for various security needs.
    Best for: Security, compliance, data integrity, digital signatures
    """
    
    # SHA-1 (160-bit) - Legacy, not recommended for security
    result_df = dataframe.withColumn(
        "email_sha1",
        sha1(col("email"))
    )
    
    # SHA-256 (256-bit) - Most common, good balance of security and performance
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "email_sha256",
        sha2(col("email"), 256)
    )
    
    # SHA-384 (384-bit) - Higher security
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "email_sha384",
        sha2(col("email"), 384)
    )
    
    # SHA-512 (512-bit) - Highest security
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "email_sha512",
        sha2(col("email"), 512)
    )
    
    # SHA-224 (224-bit) - Truncated SHA-256
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "email_sha224",
        sha2(col("email"), 224)
    )
    
    # Custom SHA with HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code)
    @udf(StringType())
    def hmac_sha256(value, secret_key="my_secret_key"):
        """HMAC-SHA256 for authenticated hashing"""
        import hmac
        return hmac.new(
            secret_key.encode(),
            value.encode(),
            hashlib.sha256
        ).hexdigest()
    
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "email_hmac_sha256",
        hmac_sha256(col("email"))
    )
    
    # Composite SHA for multi-field hashing
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "composite_sha256",
        sha2(concat_ws("|", col("email"), col("ip_address"), col("sensitive_data")), 256)
    )
    
    # SHA for data versioning/change detection
    @udf(StringType())
    def version_hash(id_val, email, ip, data):
        """Create version hash for change detection"""
        composite = f"{id_val}|{email}|{ip}|{data}"
        return hashlib.sha256(composite.encode()).hexdigest()
    
    result_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "version_hash",
        version_hash(col("id"), col("email"), col("ip_address"), col("sensitive_data"))
    )
    
    # Demonstrate change detection
    print("\nSHA for Change Detection:")
    print("Original record version hash:")
    result_df.select("id", "email", "version_hash").show(1, truncate=False)
    
    # Simulate data change
    changed_df = result_df.withColumn(
        "email",
        expr("case when id = 1 then 'changed.email@email.com' else email end")
    )
    
    changed_df = changed_df.withColumn(
        "new_version_hash",
        version_hash(col("id"), col("email"), col("ip_address"), col("sensitive_data"))
    )
    
    print("\nAfter email change for ID=1:")
    changed_df.filter(col("id") == 1).select(
        "id", "email", "version_hash", "new_version_hash"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Show hash length comparison
    print("\nHash Length Comparison:")
    result_df.select(
        expr("length(email_sha1) as sha1_length"),
        expr("length(email_sha224) as sha224_length"),
        expr("length(email_sha256) as sha256_length"),
        expr("length(email_sha384) as sha384_length"),
        expr("length(email_sha512) as sha512_length")
    ).distinct().show()
    
    return result_df


sha_df = sha_hash_pattern(df)
sha_df.select("email", "email_sha1", "email_sha256", "email_sha512").show(truncate=False)

def comprehensive_comparison(dataframe):
    """
    Compare all hashing patterns on the same dataset.
    """
    
    # Apply all hash patterns
    result_df = dataframe
    
    # Cryptographic hashes
    result_df = result_df.withColumn("crypto_sha256", sha2(col("email"), 256))
    result_df = result_df.withColumn("crypto_md5", md5(col("email")))
    
    # Non-cryptographic hash
    result_df = result_df.withColumn("non_crypto_hash", spark_hash(col("email")))
    
    # MurmurHash
    @udf(IntegerType())
    def murmur_hash(value):
        return mmh3.hash(value)
    
    result_df = result_df.withColumn("murmur_hash", murmur_hash(col("email")))
    
    print("\nAll Hash Patterns Applied:")
    result_df.select(
        "email",
        "crypto_sha256",
        "crypto_md5",
        "non_crypto_hash",
        "murmur_hash"
    ).show(2, truncate=False)
    
    # Performance comparison (conceptual)
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("HASH PATTERN SELECTION GUIDE")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    comparison_data = [
        ("Cryptographic (SHA-256)", "Security, Compliance", "Slow", "High", "Passwords, PII"),
        ("Cryptographic (MD5)", "Checksums, Legacy", "Medium", "Low*", "Non-security checksums"),
        ("Non-Cryptographic", "Partitioning, Bucketing", "Very Fast", "N/A", "Data distribution"),
        ("Consistent Hashing", "Load Balancing", "Fast", "N/A", "Distributed caching"),
        ("MurmurHash", "Hash Tables, Bloom Filters", "Very Fast", "N/A", "Performance-critical"),
        ("SHA-512", "High Security", "Slowest", "Highest", "Digital signatures"),
    ]
    
    comparison_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        comparison_data,
        ["Pattern", "Use Case", "Speed", "Security", "Best For"]
    )
    
    comparison_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    return result_df


comprehensive_df = comprehensive_comparison(df)

def advanced_hashing_patterns(dataframe):
    """
    Demonstrates advanced hashing techniques and best practices.
    """
    
    # 1. Salted Hashing for Password Security
    print("\n1. Salted Hashing (Password Security):")
    
    @udf(StringType())
    def bcrypt_style_hash(password, salt="random_salt_per_user"):
        """
        Simulated bcrypt-style hashing (use actual bcrypt in production)
        In production, use libraries like bcrypt or argon2
        """
        import hashlib
        # Multiple rounds of hashing (cost factor)
        hash_val = password + salt
        for _ in range(10):  # 10 rounds (bcrypt uses 2^cost)
            hash_val = hashlib.sha256(hash_val.encode()).hexdigest()
        return hash_val
    
    password_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        [(1, "user_password_123"), (2, "another_password_456")],
        ["user_id", "password"]
    )
    
    password_df = password_df.withColumn(
        "hashed_password",
        bcrypt_style_hash(col("password"))
    )
    
    password_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # 2. Hash-based Partitioning Strategy
    print("\n2. Hash-based Partitioning Strategy:")
    
    partitioned_df = dataframe.withColumn(
        "partition_key",
        expr("abs(hash(email)) % 4")
    )
    
    print("Distribution across partitions:")
    partitioned_df.groupBy("partition_key").count().show()
    
    # 3. Deterministic Anonymization
    print("\n3. Deterministic Anonymization:")
    
    @udf(StringType())
    def anonymize_email(email):
        """
        Anonymize email while preserving domain for analytics
        """
        local_part, domain = email.split("@")
        hashed_local = hashlib.sha256(local_part.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
        return f"{hashed_local}@{domain}"
    
    anon_df = dataframe.withColumn(
        "anonymized_email",
        anonymize_email(col("email"))
    )
    
    anon_df.select("email", "anonymized_email").show(truncate=False)
    
    # 4. Hash-based Data Masking
    print("\n4. Hash-based Data Masking:")
    
    @udf(StringType())
    def mask_sensitive_data(data, mask_char="*"):
        """
        Mask data but preserve hash for matching
        """
        hash_suffix = hashlib.md5(data.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
        return f"{mask_char * 10}_{hash_suffix}"
    
    masked_df = dataframe.withColumn(
        "masked_sensitive_data",
        mask_sensitive_data(col("sensitive_data"))
    )
    
    masked_df.select("sensitive_data", "masked_sensitive_data").show(truncate=False)
    
    # 5. Hash-based Deduplication with Window Functions
    print("\n5. Hash-based Deduplication with Window Functions:")
    
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    from pyspark.sql.functions import row_number
    
    # Create duplicates
    dup_data = data + data[:2]  # Duplicate first 2 records
    dup_df = spark.createDataFrame(dup_data, ["id", "email", "ip_address", "sensitive_data"])
    
    # Create hash for deduplication
    dup_df = dup_df.withColumn(
        "dedup_hash",
        md5(concat_ws("|", col("email"), col("ip_address")))
    )
    
    # Use window function to keep only first occurrence
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("dedup_hash").orderBy("id")
    
    dedup_df = dup_df.withColumn("row_num", row_number().over(window_spec)) \
                     .filter(col("row_num") == 1) \
                     .drop("row_num", "dedup_hash")
    
    print(f"Before deduplication: {dup_df.count()} records")
    print(f"After deduplication: {dedup_df.count()} records")
    
    # 6. Bloom Filter Pattern (using hashes)
    print("\n6. Bloom Filter Pattern (Probabilistic Set Membership):")
    
    @udf(StringType())
    def bloom_filter_hashes(value, num_hashes=3):
        """
        Generate multiple hash values for bloom filter
        Returns comma-separated hash values
        """
        hashes = []
        for i in range(num_hashes):
            hash_val = mmh3.hash(value, i) % 1000000  # Bloom filter size
            hashes.append(str(abs(hash_val)))
        return ",".join(hashes)
    
    bloom_df = dataframe.withColumn(
        "bloom_hashes",
        bloom_filter_hashes(col("email"))
    )
    
    bloom_df.select("email", "bloom_hashes").show(truncate=False)
    
    return dataframe


advanced_hashing_patterns(df)

def benchmark_hashing_performance():
    """
    Benchmark different hashing algorithms on larger dataset.
    """
    import time
    
    # Create larger dataset
    large_data = [(i, f"user{i}@email.com", f"192.168.1.{i%255}", f"data_{i}") 
                  for i in range(10000)]
    large_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        large_data, 
        ["id", "email", "ip_address", "sensitive_data"]
    ).cache()
    
    print(f"Dataset size: {large_df.count()} records\n")
    
    benchmarks = []
    
    # Benchmark MD5
    start = time.time()
    large_df.withColumn("hash", md5(col("email"))).count()
    md5_time = time.time() - start
    benchmarks.append(("MD5", md5_time))
    
    # Benchmark SHA-256
    start = time.time()
    large_df.withColumn("hash", sha2(col("email"), 256)).count()
    sha256_time = time.time() - start
    benchmarks.append(("SHA-256", sha256_time))
    
    # Benchmark SHA-512
    start = time.time()
    large_df.withColumn("hash", sha2(col("email"), 512)).count()
    sha512_time = time.time() - start
    benchmarks.append(("SHA-512", sha512_time))
    
    # Benchmark Spark Hash
    start = time.time()
    large_df.withColumn("hash", spark_hash(col("email"))).count()
    spark_hash_time = time.time() - start
    benchmarks.append(("Spark Hash (MurmurHash3)", spark_hash_time))
    
    # Create benchmark results DataFrame
    benchmark_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        benchmarks,
        ["Hash Algorithm", "Time (seconds)"]
    )
    
    print("Performance Benchmark Results:")
    benchmark_df.orderBy("Time (seconds)").show(truncate=False)
    
    large_df.unpersist()


benchmark_hashing_performance()

    source1_data = [

    ]

def use_case_distributed_cache():
    """
    Use Case 3: Distributed Cache Key Generation
    """
    print("\n--- Use Case 3: Distributed Cache with Consistent Hashing ---")
    
    # Simulate user session data
    session_data = [
        ("user_1", "session_abc123", "2024-01-01 10:00:00"),
        ("user_2", "session_def456", "2024-01-01 10:05:00"),
        ("user_3", "session_ghi789", "2024-01-01 10:10:00"),
        ("user_4", "session_jkl012", "2024-01-01 10:15:00"),
        ("user_5", "session_mno345", "2024-01-01 10:20:00"),
    ]
    
    session_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        session_data,
        ["user_id", "session_id", "timestamp"]
    )
    
    print("\nUser Session Data:")
    session_df.show()
    
    # Define cache nodes
    cache_nodes = ["cache_server_1", "cache_server_2", "cache_server_3"]
    ch = ConsistentHash(cache_nodes, virtual_nodes=100)
    
    # Assign sessions to cache nodes
    @udf(StringType())
    def get_cache_node(session_id):
        return ch.get_node(session_id)
    
    cache_df = session_df.withColumn(

    )
    
    # Generate cache key

        "cache_key",
        concat_ws(":", col("cache_node"), md5(col("session_id")))
    )
    
    print("\nSessions distributed across cache nodes:")

    print("\nDistribution statistics:")
    cache_df.groupBy("cache_node").count().show()
    
    return cache_df

def use_case_change_data_capture():
    """
    Use Case 5: Change Data Capture (CDC) using Hash Comparison
    """
    print("\n--- Use Case 5: Change Data Capture (CDC) ---")
    
    # Original data (Day 1)
    original_data = [
        (1, "Product A", 100.0, "Active"),
        (2, "Product B", 200.0, "Active"),
        (3, "Product C", 300.0, "Active"),
    ]
    
    # Updated data (Day 2)
    updated_data = [
        (1, "Product A", 150.0, "Active"),      # Price changed
        (2, "Product B", 200.0, "Active"),      # No change
        (3, "Product C", 300.0, "Inactive"),    # Status changed
        (4, "Product D", 400.0, "Active"),      # New record
    ]
    
    original_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        original_data,
        ["id", "name", "price", "status"]
    )
    
    updated_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        updated_data,
        ["id", "name", "price", "status"]
    )
    
    print("\nOriginal Data (Day 1):")
    original_df.show()
    
    print("\nUpdated Data (Day 2):")
    updated_df.show()
    
    # Create hash for each record
    @udf(StringType())
    def record_hash(name, price, status):
        """Generate hash for record content"""
        content = f"{name}|{price}|{status}"
        return hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest()
    
    original_hashed = original_df.withColumn(
        "hash",
        record_hash(col("name"), col("price"), col("status"))
    )
    
    updated_hashed = updated_df.withColumn(
        "hash",
        record_hash(col("name"), col("price"), col("status"))
    )
    
    # Detect changes
    from pyspark.sql.functions import when
    
    # Left join to find changes
    cdc_df = updated_hashed.alias("new").join(
        original_hashed.alias("old"),
        col("new.id") == col("old.id"),
        "full_outer"
    ).select(
        when(col("new.id").isNotNull(), col("new.id")).otherwise(col("old.id")).alias("id"),
        when(col("new.id").isNotNull(), col("new.name")).otherwise(col("old.name")).alias("name"),
        when(col("new.id").isNotNull(), col("new.price")).otherwise(col("old.price")).alias("price"),
        when(col("new.id").isNotNull(), col("new.status")).otherwise(col("old.status")).alias("status"),
        col("new.hash").alias("new_hash"),
        col("old.hash").alias("old_hash")
    ).withColumn(
        "change_type",
        when(col("old_hash").isNull(), "INSERT")
        .when(col("new_hash").isNull(), "DELETE")
        .when(col("new_hash") != col("old_hash"), "UPDATE")
        .otherwise("NO_CHANGE")
    )
    
    print("\nChange Data Capture Results:")
    cdc_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\nSummary of changes:")
    cdc_df.groupBy("change_type").count().show()
    
    return cdc_df


def use_case_data_masking():
    """
    Use Case 6: Production Data Masking for Non-Production Environments
    """
    print("\n--- Use Case 6: Data Masking for Non-Production ---")
    
    # Production data
    prod_data = [
        (1, "John Doe", "john.doe@company.com", "4532-1234-5678-9012", "123-45-6789"),
        (2, "Jane Smith", "jane.smith@company.com", "5412-9876-5432-1098", "987-65-4321"),
        (3, "Bob Wilson", "bob.wilson@company.com", "3782-4567-8901-2345", "456-78-9012"),
    ]
    
    prod_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        prod_data,
        ["employee_id", "name", "email", "credit_card", "ssn"]
    )
    
    print("\nProduction Data (Sensitive):")
    prod_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Mask data for non-production use
    @udf(StringType())
    def mask_with_hash(value, visible_chars=4):
        """
        Mask sensitive data but keep hash for referential integrity
        """
        hash_val = hashlib.md5(value.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
        masked = "*" * (len(value) - visible_chars) + value[-visible_chars:]
        return f"{masked}_{hash_val}"
    
    @udf(StringType())
    def mask_email(email):
        """Mask email but preserve domain"""
        local, domain = email.split("@")
        hash_local = hashlib.md5(local.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
        return f"user_{hash_local}@{domain}"
    
    masked_df = prod_df.withColumn(
        "masked_name",
        mask_with_hash(col("name"), lit(0))
    ).withColumn(
        "masked_email",
        mask_email(col("email"))
    ).withColumn(
        "masked_credit_card",
        mask_with_hash(col("credit_card"), lit(4))
    ).withColumn(
        "masked_ssn",
        mask_with_hash(col("ssn"), lit(4))
    ).drop("name", "email", "credit_card", "ssn")
    
    print("\nMasked Data for Non-Production:")
    masked_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    return masked_df

class HashingUtility:
    """
    Production-ready hashing utility class for PySpark applications.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def secure_hash(df, columns, algorithm='sha256', salt=None):
        """
        Apply secure cryptographic hash to specified columns.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            columns: List of column names to hash
            algorithm: Hash algorithm ('sha256', 'sha512', 'md5')
            salt: Optional salt value
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with hashed columns
        """
        from pyspark.sql.functions import concat, lit
        
        result_df = df
        
        for column in columns:
            new_col_name = f"{column}_hashed"
            
            if salt:
                # Add salt before hashing
                salted_col = concat(col(column), lit(salt))
            else:
                salted_col = col(column)
            
            if algorithm == 'sha256':
                result_df = result_df.withColumn(new_col_name, sha2(salted_col, 256))
            elif algorithm == 'sha512':
                result_df = result_df.withColumn(new_col_name, sha2(salted_col, 512))
            elif algorithm == 'md5':
                result_df = result_df.withColumn(new_col_name, md5(salted_col))
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported algorithm: {algorithm}")
        
        return result_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def partition_by_hash(df, column, num_partitions):
        """
        Partition DataFrame using hash-based partitioning.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column to use for partitioning
            num_partitions: Number of partitions
            
        Returns:
            Repartitioned DataFrame
        """
        df_with_partition = df.withColumn(
            "_partition_key",
            expr(f"abs(hash({column})) % {num_partitions}")
        )
        
        return df_with_partition.repartition(num_partitions, "_partition_key").drop("_partition_key")
    
    @staticmethod
    def deduplicate_by_hash(df, columns, keep='first'):
        """
        Deduplicate DataFrame using hash of specified columns.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            columns: Columns to include in deduplication hash
            keep: 'first' or 'last' occurrence to keep
            
        Returns:
            Deduplicated DataFrame
        """
        from pyspark.sql.window import Window
        from pyspark.sql.functions import row_number
        
        # Create hash column
        hash_col = concat_ws("|", *[col(c) for c in columns])
        df_with_hash = df.withColumn("_dedup_hash", md5(hash_col))
        
        # Create window specification
        if keep == 'first':
            window_spec = Window.partitionBy("_dedup_hash").orderBy(lit(1))
        else:
            window_spec = Window.partitionBy("_dedup_hash").orderBy(lit(1).desc())
        
        # Keep only first/last occurrence
        deduped_df = df_with_hash.withColumn("_row_num", row_number().over(window_spec)) \
                                  .filter(col("_row_num") == 1) \
                                  .drop("_dedup_hash", "_row_num")
        
        return deduped_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_composite_key(df, columns, algorithm='md5'):
        """
        Create composite key from multiple columns using hash.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            columns: Columns to include in composite key
            algorithm: Hash algorithm to use
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with composite_key column
        """
        composite_col = concat_ws("|", *[col(c).cast("string") for c in columns])
        
        if algorithm == 'md5':
            df = df.withColumn("composite_key", md5(composite_col))
        elif algorithm == 'sha256':
            df = df.withColumn("composite_key", sha2(composite_col, 256))
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported algorithm: {algorithm}")
        
        return df
    
    @staticmethod
    def anonymize_pii(df, pii_columns, method='hash', salt=None):
        """
        Anonymize PII columns using hashing.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            pii_columns: List of PII column names
            method: Anonymization method ('hash', 'mask')
            salt: Salt for hashing
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with anonymized PII
        """
        result_df = df
        
        for column in pii_columns:
            anon_col_name = f"{column}_anon"
            
            if method == 'hash':
                if salt:
                    salted = concat(col(column), lit(salt))
                    result_df = result_df.withColumn(anon_col_name, sha2(salted, 256))
                else:
                    result_df = result_df.withColumn(anon_col_name, sha2(col(column), 256))
            elif method == 'mask':
                # Simple masking with hash suffix
                @udf(StringType())
                def mask_value(value):
                    if not value:
                        return None
                    hash_suffix = hashlib.md5(value.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
                    return f"***MASKED***_{hash_suffix}"
                
                result_df = result_df.withColumn(anon_col_name, mask_value(col(column)))
        
        return result_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def detect_changes(old_df, new_df, key_columns, compare_columns):
        """
        Detect changes between two DataFrames using hash comparison.
        
        Args:
            old_df: Original DataFrame
            new_df: Updated DataFrame
            key_columns: Columns that uniquely identify records
            compare_columns: Columns to compare for changes
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with change detection results
        """
        # Create hash for comparison columns
        hash_expr = concat_ws("|", *[col(c).cast("string") for c in compare_columns])
        
        old_with_hash = old_df.withColumn("_old_hash", md5(hash_expr))
        new_with_hash = new_df.withColumn("_new_hash", md5(hash_expr))
        
        # Join on key columns
        key_join_condition = " AND ".join([f"old.{k} = new.{k}" for k in key_columns])
        
        changes_df = new_with_hash.alias("new").join(
            old_with_hash.alias("old"),
            expr(key_join_condition),
            "full_outer"
        ).select(
            *[when(col(f"new.{k}").isNotNull(), col(f"new.{k}"))
              .otherwise(col(f"old.{k}")).alias(k) for k in key_columns],
            col("new._new_hash").alias("new_hash"),
            col("old._old_hash").alias("old_hash"),
            when(col("old._old_hash").isNull(), lit("INSERT"))
            .when(col("new._new_hash").isNull(), lit("DELETE"))
            .when(col("new._new_hash") != col("old._old_hash"), lit("UPDATE"))
            .otherwise(lit("NO_CHANGE")).alias("change_type")
        )
        
        return changes_df

║                    PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION GUIDE                          ║

   # Slow (UDF)

   def hash_udf(value):

   Cache DataFrames when:
   - Applying multiple hash operations
   - Joining on hash columns
   - Iterative hash-based processing
   
   Example:
   df_cached = df.withColumn("hash", md5(col("email"))).cache()
   df_cached.count()  # Materialize cache

3. PARTITION APPROPRIATELY
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
   - Use hash-based partitioning for even distribution
   - Partition count should be 2-4x number of cores
   - Avoid too many small partitions
   
   Example:
   df.repartition(200, expr("hash(customer_id)"))

4. BROADCAST SMALL LOOKUP TABLES
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

   from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast

def test_hash_consistency():
    """Test that hash functions produce consistent results."""
    print("\n--- Testing Hash Consistency ---")
    
    test_data = [("test_value_1",), ("test_value_2",)]
    test_df = spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["value"])
    
    # Apply hash twice
    result1 = test_df.withColumn("hash1", md5(col("value")))
    result2 = test_df.withColumn("hash2", md5(col("value")))
    
    # Join and compare
    comparison = result1.alias("r1").join(
        result2.alias("r2"),
        col("r1.value") == col("r2.value")
    ).select(
        col("r1.value"),
        col("r1.hash1"),
        col("r2.hash2"),
        (col("r1.hash1") == col("r2.hash2")).alias("consistent")
    )
    
    comparison.show(truncate=False)
    
    all_consistent = comparison.filter(col("consistent") == False).count() == 0
    print(f"✓ Hash consistency test: {'PASSED' if all_consistent else 'FAILED'}")


def test_hash_distribution():
    """Test hash distribution quality."""
    print("\n--- Testing Hash Distribution ---")
    
    # Generate test data
    test_data = [(f"value_{i}",) for i in range(1000)]
    test_df = spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["value"])
    
    # Apply hash and partition
    hashed_df = test_df.withColumn(
        "partition",
        expr("abs(hash(value)) % 10")
    )
    
    # Check distribution
    distribution = hashed_df.groupBy("partition").count().orderBy("partition")
    distribution.show()
    
    # Calculate standard deviation
    from pyspark.sql.functions import stddev, avg
    stats = distribution.agg(
        avg("count").alias("avg_count"),
        stddev("count").alias("stddev_count")
    ).collect()[0]
    
    print(f"Average per partition: {stats['avg_count']:.2f}")
    print(f"Standard deviation: {stats['stddev_count']:.2f}")
    
    # Good distribution should have low stddev relative to mean
    cv = stats['stddev_count'] / stats['avg_count']  # Coefficient of variation
    print(f"Coefficient of variation: {cv:.4f}")
    print(f"✓ Distribution test: {'PASSED' if cv < 0.2 else 'WARNING - High variance'}")


def test_collision_resistance():
    """Test for hash collisions."""
    print("\n--- Testing Collision Resistance ---")
    
    # Generate similar values
    test_data = [
        ("value1",), ("value2",), ("value3",),
        ("value_1",), ("value_2",), ("value_3",),
    ]
    test_df = spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["value"])
    
    # Apply hash
    hashed_df = test_df.withColumn("hash", md5(col("value")))
    
    # Check for collisions
    collision_check = hashed_df.groupBy("hash").count().filter(col("count") > 1)
    
    collision_count = collision_check.count()
    
    if collision_count > 0:
        print("⚠ Collisions detected:")
        collision_check.show()
    else:
        print("✓ No collisions detected")
    
    print(f"✓ Collision test: {'PASSED' if collision_count == 0 else 'FAILED'}")


def test_performance_comparison():
    """Compare performance of different hash algorithms."""
    print("\n--- Testing Hash Performance ---")
    
    import time
    
    # Create larger test dataset
    test_data = [(f"test_email_{i}@example.com",) for i in range(10000)]
    test_df = spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["email"]).cache()
    test_df.count()  # Materialize
    
    algorithms = [
        ("Spark Hash", lambda df: df.withColumn("h", spark_hash(col("email")))),
        ("MD5", lambda df: df.withColumn("h", md5(col("email")))),
        ("SHA-256", lambda df: df.withColumn("h", sha2(col("email"), 256))),
        ("SHA-512", lambda df: df.withColumn("h", sha2(col("email"), 512))),
    ]
    
    results = []
    
    for name, hash_func in algorithms:
        start = time.time()
        hash_func(test_df).count()
        elapsed = time.time() - start
        results.append((name, elapsed))
        print(f"{name}: {elapsed:.4f} seconds")
    
    # Create comparison DataFrame
    perf_df = spark.createDataFrame(results, ["Algorithm", "Time (seconds)"])
    perf_df.orderBy("Time (seconds)").show(truncate=False)
    
    test_df.unpersist()


# Run all tests

test_hash_distribution()
test_collision_resistance()

def create_hash_metadata(df, hash_columns):
    """
    Create metadata tracking for hash operations.
    Useful for auditing and compliance.
    """
    print("\n--- Hash Metadata Tracking ---")
    
    from datetime import datetime
    
    metadata = []
    
    for col_name in hash_columns:
        if col_name in df.columns:
            # Sample hash value
            sample_hash = df.select(col_name).first()[0] if df.count() > 0 else None
            
            metadata.append({
                "column_name": col_name,
                "hash_algorithm": "SHA-256",  # Example
                "hash_length": len(sample_hash) if sample_hash else 0,
                "created_date": datetime.now().isoformat(),
                "purpose": "PII Anonymization",
                "reversible": False,
                "compliance": "GDPR Article 32"
            })
    
    metadata_df = spark.createDataFrame(metadata)
    
    print("\nHash Metadata:")
    metadata_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    return metadata_df

def locality_sensitive_hashing():
    """
    Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) for similarity detection.
    Useful for finding similar items efficiently.
    """
    print("\n--- Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) ---")
    
    from pyspark.ml.feature import MinHashLSH
    from pyspark.ml.linalg import Vectors
    
    # Create sample data with feature vectors
    data = [
        (0, Vectors.sparse(6, [0, 1, 2], [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]),),
        (1, Vectors.sparse(6, [2, 3, 4], [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]),),
        (2, Vectors.sparse(6, [0, 2, 4], [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]),),
    ]
    
    lsh_df = spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "features"])
    
    # Create LSH model
    mh = MinHashLSH(inputCol="features", outputCol="hashes", numHashTables=5)
    model = mh.fit(lsh_df)
    
    # Transform data
    transformed = model.transform(lsh_df)
    
    print("\nLSH Hash Values:")
    transformed.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Find similar items
    key = Vectors.sparse(6, [0, 1, 2], [1.0, 1.0, 1.0])
    similar = model.approxNearestNeighbors(lsh_df, key, 2)
    
    print("\nSimilar items to key vector:")
    similar.show()
    
    return transformed


def rolling_hash_pattern():
    """
    Rolling hash for efficient substring/window operations.
    Useful for pattern matching and sliding window computations.
    """
    print("\n--- Rolling Hash Pattern ---")
    
    @udf(StringType())
    def rolling_hash(text, window_size=3):
        """
        Compute rolling hash for substrings.
        Useful for pattern matching.
        """
        if not text or len(text) < window_size:
            return None
        
        hashes = []
        for i in range(len(text) - window_size + 1):
            substring = text[i:i + window_size]
            hash_val = hashlib.md5(substring.encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
            hashes.append(hash_val)
        
        return ",".join(hashes)
    
    text_data = [
        (1, "abcdefgh"),
        (2, "xyzabcde"),
        (3, "hello world"),
    ]
    
    text_df = spark.createDataFrame(text_data, ["id", "text"])
    
    rolling_df = text_df.withColumn(
        "rolling_hashes",
        rolling_hash(col("text"), lit(3))
    )
    
    print("\nRolling Hash Example:")
    rolling_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    return rolling_df


def geohash_pattern():
    """
    Geohash pattern for spatial data.
    Encodes geographic coordinates into short strings.
    """
    print("\n--- Geohash Pattern ---")
    
    import pygeohash as pgh  # pip install pygeohash
    
    @udf(StringType())
    def encode_geohash(lat, lon, precision=7):
        """Encode latitude/longitude to geohash"""
        if lat is None or lon is None:
            return None
        return pgh.encode(lat, lon, precision=precision)
    
    location_data = [
        (1, "New York", 40.7128, -74.0060),
        (2, "Los Angeles", 34.0522, -118.2437),
        (3, "Chicago", 41.8781, -87.6298),
    ]
    
    location_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        location_data,
        ["id", "city", "latitude", "longitude"]
    )
    
    geohash_df = location_df.withColumn(
        "geohash",
        encode_geohash(col("latitude"), col("longitude"))
    )
    
    print("\nGeohash Example:")
    geohash_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Group by geohash prefix for spatial clustering
    geohash_df = geohash_df.withColumn(
        "geohash_prefix",
        expr("substring(geohash, 1, 4)")
    )
    
    print("\nSpatial clustering by geohash prefix:")
    geohash_df.groupBy("geohash_prefix").count().show()
    
    return geohash_df


def feature_hashing_pattern():
    """
    Feature hashing (hashing trick) for machine learning.
    Converts categorical features to fixed-size numeric vectors.
    """
    print("\n--- Feature Hashing Pattern ---")
    
    from pyspark.ml.feature import FeatureHasher
    
    feature_data = [
        (1, "cat", "small", "red"),
        (2, "dog", "large", "brown"),
        (3, "cat", "medium", "black"),
        (4, "bird", "small", "blue"),
    ]
    
    feature_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        feature_data,
        ["id", "animal", "size", "color"]
    )
    
    # Create feature hasher
    hasher = FeatureHasher(
        inputCols=["animal", "size", "color"],
        outputCol="features",
        numFeatures=10
    )
    
    hashed_features = hasher.transform(feature_df)
    
    print("\nFeature Hashing Example:")
    hashed_features.select("id", "animal", "size", "color", "features").show(truncate=False)
    
    return hashed_features


def cryptographic_signature_pattern():
    """
    Digital signature pattern for data authenticity.
    Ensures data hasn't been tampered with.
    """
    print("\n--- Cryptographic Signature Pattern ---")
    
    @udf(StringType())
    def create_signature(data, secret_key="secret_signing_key"):
        """
        Create HMAC signature for data authenticity.
        In production, use proper key management.
        """
        import hmac
        signature = hmac.new(
            secret_key.encode(),
            data.encode(),
            hashlib.sha256
        ).hexdigest()
        return signature
    
    @udf(StringType())
    def verify_signature(data, signature, secret_key="secret_signing_key"):
        """Verify data signature"""
        import hmac
        expected_signature = hmac.new(
            secret_key.encode(),
            data.encode(),
            hashlib.sha256
        ).hexdigest()
        return "VALID" if signature == expected_signature else "INVALID"
    
    message_data = [
        (1, "Important message 1"),
        (2, "Important message 2"),
        (3, "Important message 3"),
    ]
    
    message_df = spark.createDataFrame(message_data, ["id", "message"])
    
    # Sign messages
    signed_df = message_df.withColumn(
        "signature",
        create_signature(col("message"))
    )
    
    print("\nSigned Messages:")
    signed_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Verify signatures
    verified_df = signed_df.withColumn(
        "verification",
        verify_signature(col("message"), col("signature"))
    )
    
    print("\nVerification Results:")
    verified_df.select("id", "message", "verification").show(truncate=False)
    
    # Simulate tampering
    tampered_df = verified_df.withColumn(
        "message",
        expr("case when id = 2 then 'TAMPERED MESSAGE' else message end")
    ).withColumn(
        "verification_after_tampering",
        verify_signature(col("message"), col("signature"))
    )
    
    print("\nAfter Tampering Detection:")
    tampered_df.select("id", "message", "verification_after_tampering").show(truncate=False)
    
    return verified_df

class BloomFilter:
    """
    Bloom Filter implementation for probabilistic set membership testing.
    Space-efficient data structure for large-scale membership queries.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, size=1000000, num_hashes=3):
        """
        Initialize Bloom Filter.
        
        Args:
            size: Size of bit array
            num_hashes: Number of hash functions
        """
        self.size = size
        self.num_hashes = num_hashes
        self.bit_array = [0] * size
    
    def _hash(self, item, seed):
        """Generate hash value for item with seed"""
        return mmh3.hash(str(item), seed) % self.size
    
    def add(self, item):
        """Add item to bloom filter"""
        for i in range(self.num_hashes):
            index = self._hash(item, i)
            self.bit_array[index] = 1
    
    def contains(self, item):
        """Check if item might be in set (probabilistic)"""
        for i in range(self.num_hashes):
            index = self._hash(item, i)
            if self.bit_array[index] == 0:
                return False
        return True  # Might be in set (possible false positive)


def bloom_filter_example():
    """Demonstrate Bloom Filter usage in PySpark"""
    print("\n--- Bloom Filter Example ---")
    
    # Create bloom filter
    bf = BloomFilter(size=10000, num_hashes=3)
    
    # Add known emails
    known_emails = [
        "user1@example.com",
        "user2@example.com",
        "user3@example.com",
    ]
    
    for email in known_emails:
        bf.add(email)
    
    # Test data
    test_data = [
        (1, "user1@example.com"),      # Should be found
        (2, "user2@example.com"),      # Should be found
        (3, "unknown@example.com"),    # Should not be found
        (4, "user3@example.com"),      # Should be found
        (5, "new_user@example.com"),   # Should not be found
    ]
    
    test_df = spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["id", "email"])
    
    # UDF to check bloom filter
    @udf(StringType())
    def check_bloom_filter(email):
        """Check if email exists in bloom filter"""
        return "MAYBE_EXISTS" if bf.contains(email) else "NOT_EXISTS"
    
    result_df = test_df.withColumn(
        "bloom_check",
        check_bloom_filter(col("email"))
    )
    
    print("\nBloom Filter Membership Test:")
    result_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\nNote: 'MAYBE_EXISTS' can have false positives, 'NOT_EXISTS' is definitive")
    
    return result_df

class HashingConfig:
    """
    Configuration class for hash-based operations in production.
    Centralizes all hashing-related settings.
    """
    
    # Security settings
    SALT_FOR_PII = "production_salt_2024_change_me"
    HMAC_SECRET_KEY = "hmac_secret_key_change_me"
    
    # Hash algorithm preferences
    SECURITY_HASH_ALGORITHM = "sha256"  # For PII and sensitive data
    PERFORMANCE_HASH_ALGORITHM = "murmur"  # For partitioning
    CHECKSUM_HASH_ALGORITHM = "md5"  # For checksums only
    
    # Partitioning settings
    DEFAULT_NUM_PARTITIONS = 200
    PARTITION_HASH_MODULO = 100
    
    # Bloom filter settings
    BLOOM_FILTER_SIZE = 10000000
    BLOOM_FILTER_NUM_HASHES = 5
    
    # Consistent hashing settings
    VIRTUAL_NODES_PER_PHYSICAL = 150
    
    # Deduplication settings
    DEDUP_HASH_COLUMNS = ["email", "phone", "ssn"]
    DEDUP_KEEP_STRATEGY = "first"  # or "last"
    
    # Change detection settings
    CDC_HASH_ALGORITHM = "sha256"
    CDC_INCLUDE_TIMESTAMP = True
    
    # Performance settings
    CACHE_HASH_RESULTS = True
    USE_BROADCAST_FOR_SMALL_TABLES = True
    BROADCAST_THRESHOLD_MB = 10
    
    @classmethod
    def get_hash_function(cls, purpose):
        """
        Get appropriate hash function based on purpose.
        
        Args:
            purpose: 'security', 'performance', or 'checksum'
            
        Returns:
            Hash function name
        """
        if purpose == "security":
            return cls.SECURITY_HASH_ALGORITHM
        elif purpose == "performance":
            return cls.PERFORMANCE_HASH_ALGORITHM
        elif purpose == "checksum":
            return cls.CHECKSUM_HASH_ALGORITHM
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown purpose: {purpose}")
    
    @classmethod
    def validate_config(cls):
        """Validate configuration settings"""
        errors = []
        
        # Check salt is not default
        if "change_me" in cls.SALT_FOR_PII.lower():
            errors.append("⚠ SALT_FOR_PII is using default value - CHANGE IN PRODUCTION")
        
        if "change_me" in cls.HMAC_SECRET_KEY.lower():
            errors.append("⚠ HMAC_SECRET_KEY is using default value - CHANGE IN PRODUCTION")
        
        # Check partition settings
        if cls.DEFAULT_NUM_PARTITIONS < 1:
            errors.append("❌ DEFAULT_NUM_PARTITIONS must be positive")
        
        # Check bloom filter settings
        if cls.BLOOM_FILTER_SIZE < 1000:
            errors.append("⚠ BLOOM_FILTER_SIZE is very small")
        
        return errors


# Validate configuration
print("\nValidating HashingConfig:")
config_errors = HashingConfig.validate_config()
if config_errors:
    for error in config_errors:
        print(error)
else:

def production_pipeline_with_config(input_df):
    """
    Production-ready pipeline using centralized configuration.
    """
    print("\n--- Production Pipeline with Configuration ---")
    
    # Step 1: Validate input
    print("\nStep 1: Input Validation")
    required_columns = ["customer_id", "email", "transaction_amount"]
    missing_columns = [col for col in required_columns if col not in input_df.columns]
    
    if missing_columns:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing_columns}")
    
    print(f"✓ Input validated: {input_df.count()} records")
    
    # Step 2: Apply security hashing for PII
    print("\nStep 2: PII Anonymization")
    secure_algorithm = HashingConfig.get_hash_function("security")
    
    pipeline_df = HashingUtility.secure_hash(
        input_df,
        ["email"],
        algorithm=secure_algorithm,
        salt=HashingConfig.SALT_FOR_PII
    )
    
    print(f"✓ PII hashed using {secure_algorithm}")
    
    # Step 3: Create composite key for deduplication
    print("\nStep 3: Composite Key Creation")
    pipeline_df = HashingUtility.create_composite_key(
        pipeline_df,
        ["customer_id", "transaction_amount"],
        algorithm=HashingConfig.CHECKSUM_HASH_ALGORITHM
    )
    
    print("✓ Composite key created")
    
    # Step 4: Hash-based partitioning
    print("\nStep 4: Hash-based Partitioning")
    pipeline_df = HashingUtility.partition_by_hash(
        pipeline_df,
        "customer_id",
        HashingConfig.DEFAULT_NUM_PARTITIONS
    )
    
    print(f"✓ Data partitioned into {HashingConfig.DEFAULT_NUM_PARTITIONS} partitions")
    
    # Step 5: Cache if configured
    if HashingConfig.CACHE_HASH_RESULTS:
        pipeline_df = pipeline_df.cache()
        pipeline_df.count()  # Materialize
        print("✓ Results cached")
    
    # Step 6: Add metadata
    print("\nStep 6: Adding Metadata")
    from datetime import datetime
    
    pipeline_df = pipeline_df.withColumn(
        "processing_timestamp",
        lit(datetime.now().isoformat())
    ).withColumn(
        "hash_algorithm_used",
        lit(secure_algorithm)
    ).withColumn(
        "pipeline_version",
        lit("v1.0.0")
    )
    
    print("✓ Metadata added")
    
    return pipeline_df

class HashingMonitor:
    """
    Monitoring class for hash operations in production.
    Tracks metrics and potential issues.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def monitor_hash_distribution(df, hash_column, num_buckets=10):
        """
        Monitor hash distribution quality.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame with hash column
            hash_column: Name of hash column to monitor
            num_buckets: Number of buckets for distribution
            
        Returns:
            Distribution statistics
        """
        print(f"\n--- Monitoring Hash Distribution for '{hash_column}' ---")
        
        # Create buckets
        bucketed_df = df.withColumn(
            "bucket",
            expr(f"abs(hash({hash_column})) % {num_buckets}")
        )
        
        # Calculate distribution
        distribution = bucketed_df.groupBy("bucket").count().orderBy("bucket")
        
        print("\nDistribution across buckets:")
        distribution.show()
        
        # Calculate statistics
        from pyspark.sql.functions import min as spark_min, max as spark_max
        
        stats = distribution.agg(
            spark_min("count").alias("min_count"),
            spark_max("count").alias("max_count"),
            avg("count").alias("avg_count"),
            stddev("count").alias("stddev_count")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        print(f"\nDistribution Statistics:")
        print(f"  Min: {stats['min_count']}")
        print(f"  Max: {stats['max_count']}")
        print(f"  Avg: {stats['avg_count']:.2f}")
        print(f"  StdDev: {stats['stddev_count']:.2f}")
        
        # Check for skew
        if stats['max_count'] > stats['avg_count'] * 2:
            print("⚠ WARNING: Significant data skew detected!")
        else:
            print("✓ Distribution looks good")
        
        return stats
    
    @staticmethod
    def monitor_collision_rate(df, hash_column):
        """
        Monitor hash collision rate.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame with hash column
            hash_column: Name of hash column
            
        Returns:
            Collision statistics
        """
        print(f"\n--- Monitoring Collision Rate for '{hash_column}' ---")
        
        total_records = df.count()
        unique_hashes = df.select(hash_column).distinct().count()
        
        collision_rate = (total_records - unique_hashes) / total_records * 100
        
        print(f"\nCollision Statistics:")
        print(f"  Total Records: {total_records}")
        print(f"  Unique Hashes: {unique_hashes}")
        print(f"  Collision Rate: {collision_rate:.4f}%")
        
        if collision_rate > 0.1:
            print("⚠ WARNING: High collision rate detected!")
        else:
            print("✓ Collision rate acceptable")
        
        return {
            "total_records": total_records,
            "unique_hashes": unique_hashes,
            "collision_rate": collision_rate
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def log_hash_operation(operation_name, df, hash_columns, algorithm):
        """
        Log hash operation for audit trail.
        
        Args:
            operation_name: Name of the operation
            df: DataFrame being processed
            hash_columns: Columns being hashed
            algorithm: Hash algorithm used
        """
        from datetime import datetime
        
        log_entry = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "operation": operation_name,
            "record_count": df.count(),
            "columns_hashed": hash_columns,
            "algorithm": algorithm,
            "partitions": df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        }
        
        print(f"\n[LOG] {operation_name}")
        for key, value in log_entry.items():
            print(f"  {key}: {value}")
        
        return log_entry


# Demonstrate monitoring

def robust_hash_operation(df, column, algorithm="sha256"):
    """
    Hash operation with comprehensive error handling.
    """
    print(f"\n--- Robust Hash Operation on '{column}' ---")
    
    try:
        # Validate input
        if column not in df.columns:
            raise ValueError(f"Column '{column}' not found in DataFrame")
        
        # Check for nulls
        null_count = df.filter(col(column).isNull()).count()
        if null_count > 0:
            print(f"⚠ Warning: {null_count} null values found in '{column}'")
            print("  Nulls will be handled separately")
        
        # Apply hash with null handling
        if algorithm == "sha256":
            result_df = df.withColumn(
                f"{column}_hashed",
                when(col(column).isNotNull(), sha2(col(column), 256))
                .otherwise(lit(None))
            )
        elif algorithm == "md5":
            result_df = df.withColumn(
                f"{column}_hashed",
                when(col(column).isNotNull(), md5(col(column)))
                .otherwise(lit(None))
            )
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported algorithm: {algorithm}")
        
        # Verify hash was applied
        hash_col = f"{column}_hashed"
        non_null_hashes = result_df.filter(col(hash_col).isNotNull()).count()
        
        print(f"✓ Successfully hashed {non_null_hashes} records")
        
        return result_df
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Error during hash operation: {str(e)}")
        print("  Returning original DataFrame")
        return df

# PySpark Data Hashing Patterns - Complete Guide

## Table of Contents

## Quick Reference Guide

### When to Use Each Pattern

| Pattern | Use Case | Security | Performance | Example |
|---------|----------|----------|-------------|---------|
| SHA-256 | PII, Passwords | High | Medium | User data anonymization |
| SHA-512 | High Security | Very High | Slow | Digital signatures |
| MD5 | Checksums | Low | Fast | Data deduplication |
| MurmurHash | Partitioning | None | Very Fast | Data distribution |
| Consistent Hash | Load Balancing | None | Fast | Distributed caching |
| Bloom Filter | Membership Test | None | Very Fast | Spam filtering |

---

## Pattern Details

### 1. Cryptographic Hash Pattern

**Purpose:** Secure, irreversible hashing for sensitive data

**Code Example:**
```python
from pyspark.sql.functions import sha2, md5, concat, lit

# SHA-256 with salt
df.withColumn("email_hash", 
    sha2(concat(col("email"), lit("salt")), 256))
```

**Best Practices:**
- Always use salt for passwords
- Use SHA-256 minimum for security
- Never use MD5 or SHA-1 for passwords
- Implement key rotation

---

### 2. Non-Cryptographic Hash Pattern

**Purpose:** Fast hashing for data distribution

**Code Example:**
```python
from pyspark.sql.functions import hash, expr

# Partition assignment
df.withColumn("partition_id", 
    expr("abs(hash(customer_id)) % 100"))
```

**Best Practices:**
- Use for partitioning, not security
- Monitor distribution quality
- Handle data skew with salting

---

### 3. Consistent Hashing Pattern

**Purpose:** Minimal redistribution when nodes change

**Code Example:**
```python
ch = ConsistentHash(["node1", "node2", "node3"], virtual_nodes=150)
assigned_node = ch.get_node("my_key")
```

**Best Practices:**
- Use 100-200 virtual nodes per physical node
- Implement node health checking
- Monitor distribution balance

---

## Production Deployment Checklist

### Security
- [ ] Change default salt values
- [ ] Implement key management
- [ ] Use SHA-256+ for sensitive data
- [ ] Enable audit logging
- [ ] Regular security reviews

### Performance
- [ ] Benchmark on production data
- [ ] Optimize partition count
- [ ] Cache frequently hashed data
- [ ] Monitor for data skew
- [ ] Use built-in functions over UDFs

### Monitoring
- [ ] Track hash distribution
- [ ] Monitor collision rates
- [ ] Log all hash operations
- [ ] Set up alerts for anomalies
- [ ] Regular performance reviews

### Compliance
- [ ] Document hash algorithms used
- [ ] Implement data retention policies
- [ ] Enable audit trails
- [ ] GDPR/HIPAA compliance checks
- [ ] Regular compliance audits

---

## Common Issues and Solutions

### Issue: Data Skew in Hash Partitioning
**Solution:** Use salting technique
```python
df.withColumn("salted_key", 
    concat(col("key"), lit("_"), 
    expr("cast(rand() * 10 as int)")))
```

### Issue: High Collision Rate
**Solution:** Use stronger hash algorithm or increase hash space
```python
# Use SHA-256 instead of MD5
df.withColumn("hash", sha2(col("data"), 256))
```

### Issue: Slow Hash Performance
**Solution:** Use non-cryptographic hash for non-security use cases
```python
# Use Spark's built-in hash for partitioning
df.withColumn("partition", expr("hash(key) % 100"))
```

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
import time
from functools import wraps
import hashlib
import pickle

# Initialize Spark Session with optimized configurations
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("QueryPlanCachingPatterns") \
    .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
    .config("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true") \
    .config("spark.sql.cbo.enabled", "true") \
    .config("spark.sql.statistics.histogram.enabled", "true") \
    .getOrCreate()

# ============================================================================
# 1. PARSED PLAN CACHE PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Parsed Plan Cache Pattern:
- Caches the initial parsed logical plan
- Useful for queries with same structure but different data
- Reduces parsing overhead
"""

class ParsedPlanCache:
    """
    Cache for parsed logical plans to avoid repeated parsing overhead.
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self.cache = {}
        
    def get_query_hash(self, query_template):
        """Generate hash for query template"""
        return hashlib.md5(query_template.encode()).hexdigest()
    
    def get_or_create_parsed_plan(self, query_template, params=None):
        """
        Get cached parsed plan or create new one.
        
        Args:
            query_template: SQL query template
            params: Dictionary of parameters to substitute
        
        Returns:
            DataFrame with parsed plan
        """
        query_hash = self.get_query_hash(query_template)
        
        if query_hash not in self.cache:
            print(f"[ParsedPlanCache] Creating new parsed plan for hash: {query_hash}")
            # Store the template for reuse
            self.cache[query_hash] = {
                'template': query_template,
                'created_at': time.time()
            }
        else:
            print(f"[ParsedPlanCache] Reusing parsed plan from cache: {query_hash}")
        
        # Apply parameters to template
        if params:
            query = query_template.format(**params)
        else:
            query = query_template
            
        return spark.sql(query)
    
    def clear_cache(self):
        """Clear all cached parsed plans"""
        self.cache.clear()
        print("[ParsedPlanCache] Cache cleared")

# Example usage of Parsed Plan Cache Pattern
def example_parsed_plan_cache():
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("1. PARSED PLAN CACHE PATTERN EXAMPLE")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create sample data
    data = [
        (1, "Alice", 30, "Engineering"),
        (2, "Bob", 25, "Marketing"),
        (3, "Charlie", 35, "Engineering"),
        (4, "David", 28, "Sales"),
        (5, "Eve", 32, "Engineering")
    ]
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, ["id", "name", "age", "department"])
    df.createOrReplaceTempView("employees")
    
    # Initialize cache
    parsed_cache = ParsedPlanCache()
    
    # Query template that can be reused
    query_template = """
        SELECT department, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(age) as avg_age
        FROM employees
        WHERE department = '{dept}'
        GROUP BY department
    """
    
    # First execution - creates parsed plan
    start = time.time()
    result1 = parsed_cache.get_or_create_parsed_plan(
        query_template, 
        {'dept': 'Engineering'}
    )
    result1.show()
    print(f"First execution time: {time.time() - start:.4f}s")
    
    # Second execution - reuses parsed plan
    start = time.time()
    result2 = parsed_cache.get_or_create_parsed_plan(
        query_template, 
        {'dept': 'Marketing'}
    )
    result2.show()
    print(f"Second execution time: {time.time() - start:.4f}s")
    
    # Show explain plan
    print("\nExplain Plan:")
    result1.explain(True)
