## 1. Array Explosion Pattern

```python
"""
Array Explosion Pattern
-----------------------
Explodes array columns into separate rows, creating one row per array element.
Use Case: Converting nested array data into flat structure for analysis.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import explode, col, array, lit
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, ArrayType, IntegerType

def array_explosion_pattern():
    # Initialize Spark Session
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("ArrayExplosionPattern") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("ARRAY EXPLOSION PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create sample data with array columns
    data = [
        ("user1", "John", ["Python", "Scala", "Java"]),
        ("user2", "Jane", ["R", "Python"]),
        ("user3", "Bob", ["Java", "C++", "Go"]),
        ("user4", "Alice", [])  # Empty array case
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("skills", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    print("\n--- Original DataFrame with Arrays ---")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    df.printSchema()
    
    # Basic Array Explosion
    print("\n--- After Array Explosion (explode) ---")
    exploded_df = df.select(
        col("user_id"),
        col("name"),
        explode(col("skills")).alias("skill")
    )
    exploded_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Array Explosion with NULL preservation (explode_outer)
    print("\n--- Array Explosion with NULL Preservation (explode_outer) ---")
    from pyspark.sql.functions import explode_outer
    
    exploded_outer_df = df.select(
        col("user_id"),
        col("name"),
        explode_outer(col("skills")).alias("skill")
    )
    exploded_outer_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Multiple array explosions (creates cartesian product)
    print("\n--- Multiple Array Columns Explosion ---")
    multi_array_data = [
        ("user1", ["Python", "Java"], ["AWS", "Azure"]),
        ("user2", ["R"], ["GCP"])
    ]
    
    multi_schema = StructType([
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("languages", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
        StructField("clouds", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    multi_df = spark.createDataFrame(multi_array_data, multi_schema)
    
    multi_exploded = multi_df.select(
        col("user_id"),
        explode(col("languages")).alias("language"),
        explode(col("clouds")).alias("cloud")
    )
    multi_exploded.show(truncate=False)
    
    spark.stop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    array_explosion_pattern()
```

## 2. Map Explosion Pattern

```python
"""
Map Explosion Pattern
---------------------
Explodes map (key-value) columns into separate rows with key and value columns.
Use Case: Flattening configuration data, metadata, or any key-value structures.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import explode, explode_outer, col, create_map, lit
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, MapType, IntegerType

def map_explosion_pattern():
    # Initialize Spark Session
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("MapExplosionPattern") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("MAP EXPLOSION PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create sample data with map columns
    data = [
        ("product1", "Laptop", {"color": "silver", "ram": "16GB", "storage": "512GB"}),
        ("product2", "Phone", {"color": "black", "storage": "128GB"}),
        ("product3", "Tablet", {}),  # Empty map
        ("product4", "Monitor", None)  # NULL map
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("product_name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("attributes", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    print("\n--- Original DataFrame with Maps ---")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    df.printSchema()
    
    # Basic Map Explosion
    print("\n--- After Map Explosion (explode) ---")
    exploded_map_df = df.select(
        col("product_id"),
        col("product_name"),
        explode(col("attributes")).alias("attribute_key", "attribute_value")
    )
    exploded_map_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Map Explosion with NULL preservation
    print("\n--- Map Explosion with NULL Preservation (explode_outer) ---")
    exploded_outer_map_df = df.select(
        col("product_id"),
        col("product_name"),
        explode_outer(col("attributes")).alias("attribute_key", "attribute_value")
    )
    exploded_outer_map_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Creating maps dynamically and exploding
    print("\n--- Dynamic Map Creation and Explosion ---")
    dynamic_data = [
        ("store1", "Electronics", 100, 200, 150),
        ("store2", "Clothing", 50, 75, 60)
    ]
    
    dynamic_schema = StructType([
        StructField("store_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("category", StringType(), True),
        StructField("q1_sales", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("q2_sales", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("q3_sales", IntegerType(), True)
    ])
    
    dynamic_df = spark.createDataFrame(dynamic_data, dynamic_schema)
    
    # Create map from columns
    dynamic_map_df = dynamic_df.select(
        col("store_id"),
        col("category"),
        create_map(
            lit("Q1"), col("q1_sales"),
            lit("Q2"), col("q2_sales"),
            lit("Q3"), col("q3_sales")
        ).alias("quarterly_sales")
    )
    
    print("\n--- Before Explosion ---")
    dynamic_map_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- After Explosion ---")
    dynamic_exploded = dynamic_map_df.select(
        col("store_id"),
        col("category"),
        explode(col("quarterly_sales")).alias("quarter", "sales")
    )
    dynamic_exploded.show(truncate=False)
    
    spark.stop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    map_explosion_pattern()
```

## 3. Positional Explosion Pattern

```python
"""
Positional Explosion Pattern
----------------------------
Explodes arrays while preserving the position/index of each element.
Use Case: When the position of elements in an array is meaningful (e.g., rankings, sequences).
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import posexplode, posexplode_outer, col, array, lit
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, ArrayType, IntegerType

def positional_explosion_pattern():
    # Initialize Spark Session
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("PositionalExplosionPattern") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("POSITIONAL EXPLOSION PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create sample data with ordered arrays
    data = [
        ("race1", "100m Sprint", ["Usain Bolt", "Justin Gatlin", "Andre De Grasse"]),
        ("race2", "200m Sprint", ["Usain Bolt", "Andre De Grasse"]),
        ("race3", "400m Sprint", [])  # Empty array
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("race_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("race_name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("finishers", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    print("\n--- Original DataFrame ---")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Positional Explosion (posexplode)
    print("\n--- After Positional Explosion (posexplode) ---")
    pos_exploded_df = df.select(
        col("race_id"),
        col("race_name"),
        posexplode(col("finishers")).alias("position", "athlete")
    )
    pos_exploded_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Add rank calculation (position + 1)
    print("\n--- With Rank Calculation ---")
    from pyspark.sql.functions import expr
    
    ranked_df = pos_exploded_df.withColumn(
        "rank",
        col("position") + 1
    )
    ranked_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Positional Explosion with NULL preservation
    print("\n--- Positional Explosion with NULL Preservation (posexplode_outer) ---")
    pos_exploded_outer_df = df.select(
        col("race_id"),
        col("race_name"),
        posexplode_outer(col("finishers")).alias("position", "athlete")
    )
    pos_exploded_outer_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Real-world example: Time-series data
    print("\n--- Time-Series Example ---")
    timeseries_data = [
        ("sensor1", "Temperature", [20.5, 21.0, 21.5, 22.0, 22.5]),
        ("sensor2", "Humidity", [45.0, 46.0, 47.0])
    ]
    
    timeseries_schema = StructType([
        StructField("sensor_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("metric", StringType(), True),
        StructField("readings", ArrayType(IntegerType()), True)
    ])
    
    ts_df = spark.createDataFrame(timeseries_data, timeseries_schema)
    
    ts_exploded = ts_df.select(
        col("sensor_id"),
        col("metric"),
        posexplode(col("readings")).alias("time_index", "value")
    )
    
    # Add timestamp based on position
    from pyspark.sql.functions import expr, current_timestamp
    
    ts_with_time = ts_exploded.withColumn(
        "timestamp",
        expr("date_add(current_date(), time_index)")
    )
    
    ts_with_time.show(truncate=False)
    
    spark.stop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    positional_explosion_pattern()
```

## 4. Lateral View Pattern

```python
"""
Lateral View Pattern
-------------------
SQL-based approach for exploding arrays/maps with ability to reference original columns.
Use Case: Complex transformations requiring multiple explosions and original column access.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, array, create_map, lit, struct
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, ArrayType, IntegerType

def lateral_view_pattern():
    # Initialize Spark Session
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("LateralViewPattern") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("LATERAL VIEW PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create sample data
    data = [
        ("order1", "customer1", ["item1", "item2", "item3"], 100),
        ("order2", "customer2", ["item4", "item5"], 75),
        ("order3", "customer3", [], 0)  # Empty array
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("order_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("customer_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("items", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
        StructField("total_amount", IntegerType(), True)
    ])
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    df.createOrReplaceTempView("orders")
    
    print("\n--- Original DataFrame ---")
    df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Basic LATERAL VIEW with EXPLODE
    print("\n--- LATERAL VIEW with EXPLODE ---")
    lateral_view_sql = """
        SELECT 
            order_id,
            customer_id,
            item,
            total_amount
        FROM orders
        LATERAL VIEW explode(items) exploded_items AS item
    """
    
    result1 = spark.sql(lateral_view_sql)
    result1.show(truncate=False)
    
    # LATERAL VIEW OUTER (preserves rows with empty arrays)
    print("\n--- LATERAL VIEW OUTER ---")
    lateral_view_outer_sql = """
        SELECT 
            order_id,
            customer_id,
            item,
            total_amount
        FROM orders
        LATERAL VIEW OUTER explode(items) exploded_items AS item
    """
    
    result2 = spark.sql(lateral_view_outer_sql)
    result2.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Multiple LATERAL VIEWs
    print("\n--- Multiple LATERAL VIEWs ---")
    multi_data = [
        ("user1", ["skill1", "skill2"], ["cert1", "cert2"]),
        ("user2", ["skill3"], ["cert3", "cert4", "cert5"])
    ]
    
    multi_schema = StructType([
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("skills", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
        StructField("certifications", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    multi_df = spark.createDataFrame(multi_data, multi_schema)
    multi_df.createOrReplaceTempView("user_profiles")
    
    multi_lateral_sql = """
        SELECT 
            user_id,
            skill,
            certification
        FROM user_profiles
        LATERAL VIEW explode(skills) s AS skill
        LATERAL VIEW explode(certifications) c AS certification
    """
    
    result3 = spark.sql(multi_lateral_sql)
    result3.show(truncate=False)
    
    # LATERAL VIEW with POSEXPLODE
    print("\n--- LATERAL VIEW with POSEXPLODE ---")
    posexplode_sql = """
        SELECT 
            order_id,
            customer_id,
            pos,
            item,
```python
            total_amount
        FROM orders
        LATERAL VIEW posexplode(items) exploded_items AS pos, item
    """
    
    result4 = spark.sql(posexplode_sql)
    result4.show(truncate=False)
    
    # LATERAL VIEW with MAP
    print("\n--- LATERAL VIEW with MAP EXPLODE ---")
    map_data = [
        ("product1", {"feature1": "value1", "feature2": "value2"}),
        ("product2", {"feature3": "value3"})
    ]
    
    map_schema = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("features", StructType([
            StructField("feature1", StringType(), True),
            StructField("feature2", StringType(), True),
            StructField("feature3", StringType(), True)
        ]), True)
    ])
    
    # Alternative: using MapType
    from pyspark.sql.types import MapType
    map_schema_alt = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("features", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    map_df = spark.createDataFrame(map_data, map_schema_alt)
    map_df.createOrReplaceTempView("products")
    
    map_lateral_sql = """
        SELECT 
            product_id,
            feature_key,
            feature_value
        FROM products
        LATERAL VIEW explode(features) features_exploded AS feature_key, feature_value
    """
    
    result5 = spark.sql(map_lateral_sql)
    result5.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Complex example: Nested LATERAL VIEWs with filtering
    print("\n--- Complex LATERAL VIEW with Filtering ---")
    complex_sql = """
        SELECT 
            order_id,
            customer_id,
            pos + 1 AS item_position,
            item,
            total_amount
        FROM orders
        LATERAL VIEW posexplode(items) exploded_items AS pos, item
        WHERE total_amount > 50
        ORDER BY order_id, item_position
    """
    
    result6 = spark.sql(complex_sql)
    result6.show(truncate=False)
    
    spark.stop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    lateral_view_pattern()
```

## 5. Cross Join Explosion Pattern

```python
"""
Cross Join Explosion Pattern
----------------------------
Creates cartesian product between datasets, exploding data through cross joins.
Use Case: Generating all possible combinations, scenario analysis, grid search.
WARNING: Can produce very large result sets - use with caution!
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, lit, expr, monotonically_increasing_id
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType

def cross_join_explosion_pattern():
    # Initialize Spark Session
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("CrossJoinExplosionPattern") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .config("spark.sql.crossJoin.enabled", "true") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("CROSS JOIN EXPLOSION PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Example 1: Basic Cross Join
    print("\n--- Basic Cross Join ---")
    
    products_data = [
        ("P1", "Laptop"),
        ("P2", "Mouse"),
        ("P3", "Keyboard")
    ]
    
    stores_data = [
        ("S1", "New York"),
        ("S2", "Los Angeles"),
        ("S3", "Chicago")
    ]
    
    products_schema = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("product_name", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    stores_schema = StructType([
        StructField("store_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("store_location", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    products_df = spark.createDataFrame(products_data, products_schema)
    stores_df = spark.createDataFrame(stores_data, stores_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Products DataFrame ---")
    products_df.show()
    
    print("\n--- Stores DataFrame ---")
    stores_df.show()
    
    # Perform cross join
    print("\n--- After Cross Join (All Product-Store Combinations) ---")
    cross_joined = products_df.crossJoin(stores_df)
    cross_joined.show(truncate=False)
    print(f"Total rows after cross join: {cross_joined.count()}")
    
    # Example 2: Cross Join with SQL
    print("\n--- Cross Join using SQL ---")
    products_df.createOrReplaceTempView("products")
    stores_df.createOrReplaceTempView("stores")
    
    cross_join_sql = """
        SELECT 
            p.product_id,
            p.product_name,
            s.store_id,
            s.store_location
        FROM products p
        CROSS JOIN stores s
    """
    
    sql_result = spark.sql(cross_join_sql)
    sql_result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Example 3: Cross Join for Date Range Generation
    print("\n--- Cross Join for Time Series Generation ---")
    
    sensors_data = [
        ("sensor1", "Temperature"),
        ("sensor2", "Humidity"),
        ("sensor3", "Pressure")
    ]
    
    # Generate date range
    from pyspark.sql.functions import sequence, to_date, explode
    
    date_range_df = spark.sql("""
        SELECT explode(sequence(to_date('2024-01-01'), to_date('2024-01-05'), interval 1 day)) as date
    """)
    
    sensors_schema = StructType([
        StructField("sensor_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("metric_type", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    sensors_df = spark.createDataFrame(sensors_data, sensors_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Sensors ---")
    sensors_df.show()
    
    print("\n--- Date Range ---")
    date_range_df.show()
    
    print("\n--- Sensor-Date Combinations (Cross Join) ---")
    sensor_dates = sensors_df.crossJoin(date_range_df)
    sensor_dates.orderBy("sensor_id", "date").show(20, truncate=False)
    
    # Example 4: Scenario Analysis with Cross Join
    print("\n--- Scenario Analysis Example ---")
    
    price_scenarios = [
        ("low", 0.9),
        ("base", 1.0),
        ("high", 1.1)
    ]
    
    demand_scenarios = [
        ("pessimistic", 0.8),
        ("expected", 1.0),
        ("optimistic", 1.2)
    ]
    
    scenario_schema = StructType([
        StructField("scenario_name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("multiplier", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    price_df = spark.createDataFrame(price_scenarios, scenario_schema)
    demand_df = spark.createDataFrame(demand_scenarios, scenario_schema)
    
    # Rename columns to avoid conflicts
    price_df = price_df.withColumnRenamed("scenario_name", "price_scenario") \
                       .withColumnRenamed("multiplier", "price_multiplier")
    
    demand_df = demand_df.withColumnRenamed("scenario_name", "demand_scenario") \
                         .withColumnRenamed("multiplier", "demand_multiplier")
    
    print("\n--- All Scenario Combinations ---")
    scenarios_cross = price_df.crossJoin(demand_df)
    
    # Add base values and calculations
    scenarios_cross = scenarios_cross \
        .withColumn("base_price", lit(100.0)) \
        .withColumn("base_demand", lit(1000)) \
        .withColumn("scenario_price", col("base_price") * col("price_multiplier")) \
        .withColumn("scenario_demand", col("base_demand") * col("demand_multiplier")) \
        .withColumn("scenario_revenue", col("scenario_price") * col("scenario_demand"))
    
    scenarios_cross.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Example 5: Parameter Grid for ML (Hyperparameter Tuning Simulation)
    print("\n--- ML Hyperparameter Grid Generation ---")
    
    learning_rates = [(0.001,), (0.01,), (0.1,)]
    batch_sizes = [(32,), (64,), (128,)]
    epochs = [(10,), (20,), (50,)]
    
    lr_schema = StructType([StructField("learning_rate", DoubleType(), True)])
    bs_schema = StructType([StructField("batch_size", IntegerType(), True)])
    ep_schema = StructType([StructField("epochs", IntegerType(), True)])
    
    lr_df = spark.createDataFrame(learning_rates, lr_schema)
    bs_df = spark.createDataFrame(batch_sizes, bs_schema)
    ep_df = spark.createDataFrame(epochs, ep_schema)
    
    # Create parameter grid
    param_grid = lr_df.crossJoin(bs_df).crossJoin(ep_df)
    param_grid = param_grid.withColumn("config_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
    
    print(f"\n--- Hyperparameter Grid ({param_grid.count()} configurations) ---")
    param_grid.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Example 6: Cross Join with Filtering (Controlled Explosion)
    print("\n--- Cross Join with Filtering ---")
    
    employees_data = [
        ("E1", "Engineering"),
        ("E2", "Engineering"),
        ("E3", "Sales"),
        ("E4", "Marketing")
    ]
    
    projects_data = [
        ("P1", "Engineering"),
        ("P2", "Engineering"),
        ("P3", "Sales"),
        ("P4", "Marketing")
    ]
    
    emp_schema = StructType([
        StructField("emp_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("department", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    proj_schema = StructType([
        StructField("project_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("project_dept", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    employees_df = spark.createDataFrame(employees_data, emp_schema)
    projects_df = spark.createDataFrame(projects_data, proj_schema)
    
    # Cross join with department matching filter
    print("\n--- Filtered Cross Join (Department Match Only) ---")
    filtered_cross = employees_df.crossJoin(projects_df) \
        .filter(col("department") == col("project_dept"))
    
    filtered_cross.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Example 7: Explode Array then Cross Join
    print("\n--- Combined Pattern: Array Explosion + Cross Join ---")
    
    categories_data = [
        ("CAT1", ["SubA", "SubB"]),
        ("CAT2", ["SubC"])
    ]
    
    regions_data = [
        ("North",),
        ("South",)
    ]
    
    cat_schema = StructType([
        StructField("category", StringType(), True),
        StructField("subcategories", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    reg_schema = StructType([
        StructField("region", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    categories_df = spark.createDataFrame(categories_data, cat_schema)
    regions_df = spark.createDataFrame(regions_data, reg_schema)
    
    # First explode, then cross join
    exploded_categories = categories_df.select(
        col("category"),
        explode(col("subcategories")).alias("subcategory")
    )
    
    print("\n--- After Explosion ---")
    exploded_categories.show()
    
    print("\n--- After Cross Join with Regions ---")
    final_result = exploded_categories.crossJoin(regions_df)
    final_result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Performance tip
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PERFORMANCE TIPS:")
    print("=" * 80)
    print("""
    1. Always enable cross join explicitly: spark.sql.crossJoin.enabled=true
    2. Be cautious with large datasets (m x n rows can grow quickly)
    3. Use filters after cross join to reduce result set
    4. Consider broadcast joins for small datasets
    5. Monitor memory usage and shuffle operations
    6. Use EXPLAIN to understand query plan
    """)
    
    spark.stop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    cross_join_explosion_pattern()
```

## Complete Integration Example

```python
"""
Complete Integration Example
----------------------------
Demonstrates using multiple explosion patterns together in a real-world scenario.
Use Case: E-commerce order processing with complex nested data structures.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import (
    explode, explode_outer, posexplode, col, lit, 
    create_map, struct, array, current_timestamp
)
from pyspark.sql.types import *

def integrated_explosion_patterns():
    # Initialize Spark Session
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("IntegratedExplosionPatterns") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .config("spark.sql.crossJoin.enabled", "true") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("INTEGRATED EXPLOSION PATTERNS - E-COMMERCE EXAMPLE")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create complex nested data structure
    orders_data = [
        (
            "ORD001",
            "2024-01-15",
            "CUST001",
            [
                {"item_id": "ITEM1", "quantity": 2, "price": 29.99, "tags": ["electronics", "sale"]},
                {"item_id": "ITEM2", "quantity": 1, "price": 49.99, "tags": ["clothing"]}
            ],
            {"payment_method": "credit_card", "shipping_method": "express", "discount_code": "SAVE10"}
        ),
        (
            "ORD002",
            "2024-01-16",
            "CUST002",
            [
                {"item_id": "ITEM3", "quantity": 3, "price": 15.99, "tags": ["books", "bestseller"]}
            ],
            {"payment_method": "paypal", "shipping_method": "standard"}
        )
    ]
    
    # Define complex schema
    item_schema = StructType([
        StructField("item_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("quantity", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("price", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("tags", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    orders_schema = StructType([
        StructField("order_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("order_date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("customer_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("items", ArrayType(item_schema), True),
        StructField("metadata", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    orders
```python
_df = spark.createDataFrame(orders_data, orders_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Original Complex Nested DataFrame ---")
    orders_df.show(truncate=False)
    orders_df.printSchema()
    
    # Step 1: Array Explosion Pattern - Explode items
    print("\n--- Step 1: Explode Items Array ---")
    items_exploded = orders_df.select(
        col("order_id"),
        col("order_date"),
        col("customer_id"),
        explode(col("items")).alias("item"),
        col("metadata")
    )
    items_exploded.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Step 2: Extract nested fields and explode tags
    print("\n--- Step 2: Extract Item Fields and Explode Tags ---")
    items_with_tags = items_exploded.select(
        col("order_id"),
        col("order_date"),
        col("customer_id"),
        col("item.item_id").alias("item_id"),
        col("item.quantity").alias("quantity"),
        col("item.price").alias("price"),
        explode_outer(col("item.tags")).alias("tag"),
        col("metadata")
    )
    items_with_tags.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Step 3: Map Explosion Pattern - Explode metadata
    print("\n--- Step 3: Explode Metadata Map ---")
    full_exploded = items_with_tags.select(
        col("order_id"),
        col("order_date"),
        col("customer_id"),
        col("item_id"),
        col("quantity"),
        col("price"),
        col("tag"),
        explode_outer(col("metadata")).alias("meta_key", "meta_value")
    )
    full_exploded.show(50, truncate=False)
    
    # Step 4: Positional Explosion Pattern - Track item position
    print("\n--- Step 4: Positional Explosion for Item Order ---")
    orders_df.createOrReplaceTempView("orders")
    
    positional_sql = """
        SELECT 
            order_id,
            customer_id,
            pos as item_position,
            item.item_id,
            item.quantity,
            item.price,
            item.quantity * item.price as line_total
        FROM orders
        LATERAL VIEW posexplode(items) items_pos AS pos, item
    """
    
    positional_result = spark.sql(positional_sql)
    positional_result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Step 5: Cross Join Explosion - Add shipping zones
    print("\n--- Step 5: Cross Join with Shipping Zones ---")
    
    shipping_zones = [
        ("Zone1", 5.99),
        ("Zone2", 7.99),
        ("Zone3", 9.99)
    ]
    
    zones_schema = StructType([
        StructField("zone_name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("shipping_cost", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    zones_df = spark.createDataFrame(shipping_zones, zones_schema)
    
    # Get unique orders
    unique_orders = orders_df.select("order_id", "customer_id").distinct()
    
    # Cross join to see all shipping options
    shipping_options = unique_orders.crossJoin(zones_df)
    print("\n--- All Shipping Options per Order ---")
    shipping_options.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Step 6: Lateral View Pattern - Complex SQL transformation
    print("\n--- Step 6: Complete LATERAL VIEW Analysis ---")
    
    complete_sql = """
        SELECT 
            o.order_id,
            o.order_date,
            o.customer_id,
            pos + 1 as item_number,
            item.item_id,
            item.quantity,
            item.price,
            tag,
            item.quantity * item.price as line_total,
            meta_key,
            meta_value
        FROM orders o
        LATERAL VIEW posexplode(items) items_pos AS pos, item
        LATERAL VIEW OUTER explode(item.tags) tags_exploded AS tag
        LATERAL VIEW OUTER explode(metadata) meta_exploded AS meta_key, meta_value
        ORDER BY order_id, item_number, tag, meta_key
    """
    
    complete_result = spark.sql(complete_sql)
    complete_result.show(100, truncate=False)
    
    # Step 7: Aggregation after explosion
    print("\n--- Step 7: Aggregations After Explosion ---")
    
    # Tags analysis
    tags_analysis_sql = """
        SELECT 
            tag,
            COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) as orders_count,
            SUM(item.quantity) as total_quantity,
            ROUND(SUM(item.quantity * item.price), 2) as total_revenue
        FROM orders
        LATERAL VIEW explode(items) items_exploded AS item
        LATERAL VIEW explode(item.tags) tags_exploded AS tag
        GROUP BY tag
        ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
    """
    
    tags_analysis = spark.sql(tags_analysis_sql)
    print("\n--- Revenue by Tag ---")
    tags_analysis.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Payment method analysis
    payment_analysis_sql = """
        SELECT 
            meta_value as payment_method,
            COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) as order_count,
            ROUND(SUM(item.quantity * item.price), 2) as total_amount
        FROM orders
        LATERAL VIEW explode(items) items_exploded AS item
        LATERAL VIEW explode(metadata) meta_exploded AS meta_key, meta_value
        WHERE meta_key = 'payment_method'
        GROUP BY meta_value
    """
    
    payment_analysis = spark.sql(payment_analysis_sql)
    print("\n--- Analysis by Payment Method ---")
    payment_analysis.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Step 8: Practical use case - Inventory allocation
    print("\n--- Step 8: Inventory Allocation Scenario ---")
    
    # Available inventory by warehouse
    inventory_data = [
        ("WH1", "ITEM1", 100),
        ("WH1", "ITEM2", 50),
        ("WH2", "ITEM1", 75),
        ("WH2", "ITEM3", 200),
        ("WH3", "ITEM2", 30),
        ("WH3", "ITEM3", 150)
    ]
    
    inventory_schema = StructType([
        StructField("warehouse_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("item_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("available_qty", IntegerType(), True)
    ])
    
    inventory_df = spark.createDataFrame(inventory_data, inventory_schema)
    
    # Explode order items
    order_items = orders_df.select(
        col("order_id"),
        col("customer_id"),
        explode(col("items")).alias("item")
    ).select(
        col("order_id"),
        col("customer_id"),
        col("item.item_id").alias("item_id"),
        col("item.quantity").alias("required_qty")
    )
    
    print("\n--- Order Items (Exploded) ---")
    order_items.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- Available Inventory ---")

    # Cross join to find all possible fulfillment options
    fulfillment_options = order_items.crossJoin(inventory_df) \

        .filter(col("available_qty") >= col("required_qty")) \

    fulfillment_options.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Step 9: Performance comparison
    print("\n--- Step 9: Performance Metrics ---")
    
    print(f"Original orders count: {orders_df.count()}")
    print(f"After item explosion: {items_exploded.count()}")
    print(f"After tags explosion: {items_with_tags.count()}")
    print(f"After full explosion: {full_exploded.count()}")
    print(f"Fulfillment options (cross join): {fulfillment_options.count()}")
    
    # Step 10: Export patterns demonstration
    print("\n--- Step 10: Common Export Patterns ---")
    
    # Flatten for export
    export_ready = orders_df.select(

        col("customer_id"),
        posexplode(col("items")).alias("item_seq", "item")
    ).select(
        col("order_id"),
        col("order_date"),
        col("customer_id"),
        (col("item_seq") + 1).alias("line_number"),
        col("item.item_id").alias("item_id"),
        col("item.quantity").alias("quantity"),
        col("item.price").alias("unit_price"),
        (col("item.quantity") * col("item.price")).alias("line_total")
    )
    
    print("\n--- Export-Ready Format ---")
    export_ready.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Summary statistics
    print("\n--- Order Summary Statistics ---")
    summary_sql = """
        SELECT 
            order_id,
            COUNT(*) as total_items,
            SUM(item.quantity) as total_units,
            ROUND(SUM(item.quantity * item.price), 2) as order_total
        FROM orders
        LATERAL VIEW explode(items) items_exploded AS item
        GROUP BY order_id
    """
    
    summary = spark.sql(summary_sql)
    summary.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN USAGE SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)
    print("""
    1. ARRAY EXPLOSION: Used for exploding order items and tags
    2. MAP EXPLOSION: Used for exploding metadata key-value pairs
    3. POSITIONAL EXPLOSION: Used for tracking item sequence in orders
    4. LATERAL VIEW: Used for complex SQL transformations with multiple explosions
    5. CROSS JOIN: Used for generating fulfillment options and shipping scenarios
    
    KEY INSIGHTS:
    - Combine patterns for complex nested data
    - Use OUTER variants to preserve NULL/empty values
    - Apply filters after explosion to control data volume
    - Aggregate after explosion for analytical insights
    - Consider performance implications of cartesian products
    """)
    
    spark.stop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    integrated_explosion_patterns()

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
import sys

def run_all_patterns():

    """

    print("=" * 80 + "\n")
    
    patterns = [
        ("Array Explosion Pattern", array_explosion_pattern),
        ("Map Explosion Pattern", map_explosion_pattern),
        ("Positional Explosion Pattern", positional_explosion_pattern),
        ("Lateral View Pattern", lateral_view_pattern),
        ("Cross Join Explosion Pattern", cross_join_explosion_pattern),
        ("Integrated Patterns Example", integrated_explosion_patterns)
    ]
    
    for pattern_name, pattern_func in patterns:
        try:
            print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")

            pattern_func()
            print(f"\n✓ {pattern_name} completed successfully\n")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"\n✗ Error in {pattern_name}: {str(e)}\n")
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ALL PATTERNS EXECUTION COMPLETED")
    print("=" * 80 + "\n")

def print_usage_guide():
    """
    Print comprehensive usage guide
    """
    guide = """
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║               PYSPARK DATA EXPLOSION PATTERNS - USAGE GUIDE                ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    
    PATTERN 1: ARRAY EXPLOSION
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Purpose: Transform arrays into separate rows
    Functions: explode(), explode_outer()
    Use Cases:
      - Flattening nested arrays
      - Processing multi-valued attributes
      - Converting hierarchical data to tabular format
    
    Example:
      df.select(explode(col("skills")).alias("skill"))
    
    
    PATTERN 2: MAP EXPLOSION
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Purpose: Transform map/dictionary columns into key-value rows
    Functions: explode(map_col), explode_outer(map_col)
    Use Cases:
      - Flattening configuration data
      - Processing JSON key-value structures
      - Metadata extraction
    
    Example:
      df.select(explode(col("attributes")).alias("key", "value"))
    
    
    PATTERN 3: POSITIONAL EXPLOSION
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Purpose: Explode arrays while preserving element position
    Functions: posexplode(), posexplode_outer()
    Use Cases:
      - Time-series data with ordered values
      - Rankings and sequences
      - Index-based processing
    
    Example:
      df.select(posexplode(col("values")).alias("pos", "value"))
    
    
    PATTERN 4: LATERAL VIEW
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Purpose: SQL-based explosion with access to original columns
    Syntax: LATERAL VIEW explode(array_col) alias AS element
    Use Cases:
      - Complex SQL transformations
      - Multiple simultaneous explosions
      - Legacy SQL compatibility
    
    Example:
      SELECT * FROM table 
      LATERAL VIEW explode(items) t AS item
    
    
    PATTERN 5: CROSS JOIN EXPLOSION
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    Purpose: Generate cartesian product between datasets
    Functions: crossJoin(), SQL CROSS JOIN
    Use Cases:
      - Scenario analysis
      - Parameter grid generation
      - All combinations generation
    
    Example:
      df1.crossJoin(df2)
    
    WARNING: Can produce very large result sets!
    
    
    BEST PRACTICES
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    1. Use OUTER variants to preserve NULL/empty values
    2. Filter after explosion to reduce data volume
    3. Monitor memory and shuffle operations
    4. Consider broadcast joins for small datasets
    5. Use EXPLAIN to understand query plans
    6. Aggregate after explosion for analytics
    7. Enable cross join explicitly when needed
    
    
    PERFORMANCE TIPS
    ─────────
```python
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    1. Cache intermediate results if reused multiple times
    2. Partition data appropriately before explosion
    3. Use columnar file formats (Parquet, ORC)
    4. Avoid multiple cross joins in sequence
    5. Filter early, explode late when possible
    6. Monitor data skew after explosion
    7. Use repartition() after large explosions
    
    
    COMMON PITFALLS
    ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ✗ Forgetting to use OUTER variants (loses empty arrays/maps)

    ✗ Exploding without considering data volume
    ✗ Multiple explosions without filtering
    ✗ Not handling NULL values properly

    EXECUTION INSTRUCTIONS

## Advanced Patterns and Edge Cases

```python
"""
Advanced Explosion Patterns and Edge Cases
------------------------------------------
Demonstrates advanced scenarios and edge cases for explosion patterns.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *

def advanced_explosion_patterns():
    # Initialize Spark Session
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("AdvancedExplosionPatterns") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .config("spark.sql.crossJoin.enabled", "true") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("ADVANCED EXPLOSION PATTERNS & EDGE CASES")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Edge Case 1: NULL Arrays and Maps
    print("\n--- Edge Case 1: NULL Arrays and Maps ---")
    
    null_data = [
        ("user1", ["skill1", "skill2"], {"key1": "val1"}),
        ("user2", None, {"key2": "val2"}),  # NULL array
        ("user3", ["skill3"], None),  # NULL map
        ("user4", [], {}),  # Empty array and map
        ("user5", None, None)  # Both NULL
    ]
    
    null_schema = StructType([
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("skills", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
        StructField("metadata", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    null_df = spark.createDataFrame(null_data, null_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Original Data ---")
    null_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- explode() - Drops NULL/Empty ---")
    null_df.select(
        col("user_id"),
        explode(col("skills")).alias("skill")
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- explode_outer() - Preserves NULL/Empty ---")
    null_df.select(
        col("user_id"),
        explode_outer(col("skills")).alias("skill")
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 2: Nested Arrays (Array of Arrays)
    print("\n--- Edge Case 2: Nested Arrays ---")
    
    nested_data = [
        ("group1", [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]]),
        ("group2", [["e"], ["f", "g", "h"]])
    ]
    
    nested_schema = StructType([
        StructField("group_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("nested_arrays", ArrayType(ArrayType(StringType())), True)
    ])
    
    nested_df = spark.createDataFrame(nested_data, nested_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Original Nested Arrays ---")
    nested_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- First Level Explosion ---")
    first_explode = nested_df.select(
        col("group_id"),
        explode(col("nested_arrays")).alias("inner_array")
    )
    first_explode.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- Second Level Explosion ---")
    second_explode = first_explode.select(
        col("group_id"),
        explode(col("inner_array")).alias("element")
    )
    second_explode.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 3: Arrays within Structs
    print("\n--- Edge Case 3: Arrays within Structs ---")
    
    struct_array_data = [
        ("order1", [
            {"product": "A", "tags": ["new", "sale"]},
            {"product": "B", "tags": ["popular"]}
        ])
    ]
    
    product_schema = StructType([
        StructField("product", StringType(), True),
        StructField("tags", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    struct_array_schema = StructType([
        StructField("order_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("products", ArrayType(product_schema), True)
    ])
    
    struct_array_df = spark.createDataFrame(struct_array_data, struct_array_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Original Struct with Arrays ---")
    struct_array_df.show(truncate=False)
    struct_array_df.printSchema()
    
    print("\n--- Explode Outer Array ---")
    exploded_products = struct_array_df.select(
        col("order_id"),
        explode(col("products")).alias("product_info")
    )
    exploded_products.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- Explode Inner Arrays ---")
    fully_exploded = exploded_products.select(
        col("order_id"),
        col("product_info.product").alias("product_name"),
        explode(col("product_info.tags")).alias("tag")
    )
    fully_exploded.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 4: Large Array Explosion (Performance)
    print("\n--- Edge Case 4: Large Array Explosion Performance ---")
    
    # Simulate large arrays
    large_array_data = [
        (f"user{i}", list(range(i * 10, (i + 1) * 10)))
        for i in range(1, 6)
    ]
    
    large_schema = StructType([
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("values", ArrayType(IntegerType()), True)
    ])
    
    large_df = spark.createDataFrame(large_array_data, large_schema)
    
    print(f"\nOriginal rows: {large_df.count()}")
    
    exploded_large = large_df.select(
        col("user_id"),
        explode(col("values")).alias("value")
    )
    
    print(f"After explosion rows: {exploded_large.count()}")
    print("\nSample of exploded data:")
    exploded_large.show(10)
    
    # Edge Case 5: Conditional Explosion
    print("\n--- Edge Case 5: Conditional Explosion ---")
    
    conditional_data = [
        ("user1", "premium", ["feature1", "feature2", "feature3"]),
        ("user2", "basic", ["feature1"]),
        ("user3", "premium", ["feature1", "feature2"])
    ]
    
    conditional_schema = StructType([
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("tier", StringType(), True),
        StructField("features", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    conditional_df = spark.createDataFrame(conditional_data, conditional_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Explode Only Premium Users ---")
    conditional_exploded = conditional_df.filter(col("tier") == "premium") \
        .select(
            col("user_id"),
            col("tier"),
            explode(col("features")).alias("feature")
        )
    conditional_exploded.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 6: Explosion with Window Functions
    print("\n--- Edge Case 6: Explosion with Window Functions ---")
    
    window_data = [
        ("dept1", ["emp1", "emp2", "emp3"]),
        ("dept2", ["emp4", "emp5"])
    ]
    
    window_schema = StructType([
        StructField("department", StringType(), True),
        StructField("employees", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    window_df = spark.createDataFrame(window_data, window_schema)
    
    # Explode and apply window function
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    
    exploded_window = window_df.select(
        col("department"),
        explode(col("employees")).alias("employee")
    )
    
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("department").orderBy("employee")
    
    with_rank = exploded_window.withColumn(
        "employee_rank",
        row_number().over(window_spec)
    )
    
    print("\n--- Explosion with Row Number ---")
    with_rank.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 7: Explosion with Aggregation
    print("\n--- Edge Case 7: Explosion then Aggregation ---")
    
    agg_data = [
        ("category1", ["item1", "item2", "item3"]),
        ("category2", ["item1", "item4"]),
        ("category3", ["item2", "item3", "item4"])
    ]
    
    agg_schema = StructType([
        StructField("category", StringType(), True),
        StructField("items", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    agg_df = spark.createDataFrame(agg_data, agg_schema)
    
    # Explode and count items
    item_counts = agg_df.select(
        explode(col("items")).alias("item")
    ).groupBy("item").count().orderBy(col("count").desc())
    
    print("\n--- Item Frequency After Explosion ---")
    item_counts.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 8: Multiple Explosions with Different Strategies
    print("\n--- Edge Case 8: Mixed Explosion Strategies ---")
    
    mixed_data = [
        ("record1", ["a", "b"], {"k1": "v1", "k2": "v2"}, [1, 2, 3])
    ]
    
    mixed_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("array1", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
        StructField("map1", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True),
        StructField("array2", ArrayType(IntegerType()), True)
    ])
    
    mixed_df = spark.createDataFrame(mixed_data, mixed_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Strategy 1: Sequential Explosions (Creates Cartesian) ---")
    seq_exploded = mixed_df.select(
        col("id"),
        explode(col("array1")).alias("val1"),
        explode(col("array2")).alias("val2")
    )
    seq_exploded.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- Strategy 2: Separate Explosions (No Cartesian) ---")
    sep_exploded1 = mixed_df.select(
        col("id"),
        explode(col("array1")).alias("value")
    )
    print("Array1 explosion:")
    sep_exploded1.show(truncate=False)
    
    sep_exploded2 = mixed_df.select(
        col("id"),
        explode(col("array2")).alias("value")
    )
    print("Array2 explosion:")
    sep_exploded2.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 9: Explosion with UDF
    print("\n--- Edge Case 9: Explosion with UDF ---")
    
    from pyspark.sql.types import ArrayType, StringType
    
    @udf(ArrayType(StringType()))
    def generate_variations(word):
        if word:
            return [word.upper(), word.lower(), word.capitalize()]
        return []
    
    udf_data = [("hello",), ("WORLD",)]
    udf_schema = StructType([StructField("word", StringType(), True)])
    
    udf_df = spark.createDataFrame(udf_data, udf_schema)
    
    udf_with_variations = udf_df.withColumn(
        "variations",
        generate_variations(col("word"))
    )
    
    print("\n--- Before Explosion ---")
    udf_with_variations.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- After Explosion ---")
    udf_exploded = udf_with_variations.select(
        col("word"),
        explode(col("variations")).alias("variation")
    )
    udf_exploded.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 10: Memory-Efficient Large Explosion
    print("\n--- Edge Case 10: Memory-Efficient Strategies ---")
    
    print("""
    For large explosions, consider:
    
    1. Repartition before explosion:
       df.repartition(200).select(explode(...))
    
    2. Use coalesce after explosion if needed:
       exploded_df.coalesce(50)
    
    3. Write intermediate results:
       exploded_df.write.parquet("temp_path")
       spark.read.parquet("temp_path")
    
    4. Use broadcast for small dimension tables:
       exploded_df.join(broadcast(small_df), ...)
    
    5. Monitor and adjust:
       - spark.sql.shuffle.partitions
       - spark.default.parallelism
    """)
    
    spark.stop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    advanced_explosion_patterns()

"""
Testing Framework for Explosion Patterns
----------------------------------------
Unit tests for validating explosion pattern implementations.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
import unittest

class TestExplosionPatterns(unittest.TestCase):
    
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName
```python
("ExplosionPatternsTests") \
            .master("local[*]") \
            .config("spark.sql.crossJoin.enabled", "true") \
            .getOrCreate()
    
    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls.spark.stop()
    
    def test_array_explosion_basic(self):
        """Test basic array explosion"""
        data = [("user1", ["a", "b", "c"])]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("items", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        result = df.select(col("id"), explode(col("items")).alias("item"))
        
        self.assertEqual(result.count(), 3)
        self.assertEqual(result.filter(col("item") == "a").count(), 1)
    
    def test_array_explosion_empty(self):
        """Test array explosion with empty arrays"""
        data = [("user1", []), ("user2", ["a"])]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("items", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        
        # explode() drops empty arrays
        result_explode = df.select(col("id"), explode(col("items")).alias("item"))
        self.assertEqual(result_explode.count(), 1)
        
        # explode_outer() preserves empty arrays
        result_outer = df.select(col("id"), explode_outer(col("items")).alias("item"))
        self.assertEqual(result_outer.count(), 2)
    
    def test_array_explosion_null(self):
        """Test array explosion with NULL values"""
        data = [("user1", None), ("user2", ["a"])]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("items", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        
        # explode() drops NULL arrays
        result_explode = df.select(col("id"), explode(col("items")).alias("item"))
        self.assertEqual(result_explode.count(), 1)
        
        # explode_outer() preserves NULL arrays
        result_outer = df.select(col("id"), explode_outer(col("items")).alias("item"))
        self.assertEqual(result_outer.count(), 2)
        null_count = result_outer.filter(col("item").isNull()).count()
        self.assertEqual(null_count, 1)
    
    def test_map_explosion_basic(self):
        """Test basic map explosion"""
        data = [("user1", {"k1": "v1", "k2": "v2"})]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("attrs", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        result = df.select(
            col("id"),
            explode(col("attrs")).alias("key", "value")
        )
        
        self.assertEqual(result.count(), 2)
        self.assertEqual(result.filter(col("key") == "k1").count(), 1)
    
    def test_map_explosion_empty(self):
        """Test map explosion with empty maps"""
        data = [("user1", {}), ("user2", {"k1": "v1"})]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("attrs", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        
        # explode() drops empty maps
        result_explode = df.select(
            col("id"),
            explode(col("attrs")).alias("key", "value")
        )
        self.assertEqual(result_explode.count(), 1)
        
        # explode_outer() preserves empty maps
        result_outer = df.select(
            col("id"),
            explode_outer(col("attrs")).alias("key", "value")
        )
        self.assertEqual(result_outer.count(), 2)
    
    def test_positional_explosion(self):
        """Test positional explosion"""
        data = [("user1", ["a", "b", "c"])]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("items", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        result = df.select(
            col("id"),
            posexplode(col("items")).alias("pos", "item")
        )
        
        self.assertEqual(result.count(), 3)
        
        # Check positions
        first_item = result.filter(col("pos") == 0).select("item").collect()[0][0]
        self.assertEqual(first_item, "a")
        
        last_item = result.filter(col("pos") == 2).select("item").collect()[0][0]
        self.assertEqual(last_item, "c")
    
    def test_cross_join_explosion(self):
        """Test cross join explosion"""
        data1 = [("a",), ("b",)]
        data2 = [(1,), (2,), (3,)]
        
        schema1 = StructType([StructField("letter", StringType(), True)])
        schema2 = StructType([StructField("number", IntegerType(), True)])
        
        df1 = self.spark.createDataFrame(data1, schema1)
        df2 = self.spark.createDataFrame(data2, schema2)
        
        result = df1.crossJoin(df2)
        
        # Should produce 2 * 3 = 6 rows
        self.assertEqual(result.count(), 6)
        
        # Check specific combination exists
        specific = result.filter(
            (col("letter") == "a") & (col("number") == 1)
        ).count()
        self.assertEqual(specific, 1)
    
    def test_lateral_view_sql(self):
        """Test LATERAL VIEW pattern"""
        data = [("user1", ["a", "b"])]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("items", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        df.createOrReplaceTempView("test_table")
        
        result = self.spark.sql("""
            SELECT id, item
            FROM test_table
            LATERAL VIEW explode(items) t AS item
        """)
        
        self.assertEqual(result.count(), 2)
    
    def test_multiple_explosions_cartesian(self):
        """Test multiple explosions creating cartesian product"""
        data = [("user1", ["a", "b"], [1, 2])]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("letters", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
            StructField("numbers", ArrayType(IntegerType()), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        result = df.select(
            col("id"),
            explode(col("letters")).alias("letter"),
            explode(col("numbers")).alias("number")
        )
        
        # Should produce 2 * 2 = 4 rows
        self.assertEqual(result.count(), 4)
    
    def test_nested_array_explosion(self):
        """Test nested array explosion"""
        data = [("user1", [["a", "b"], ["c"]])]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("nested", ArrayType(ArrayType(StringType())), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        
        # First explosion
        first = df.select(col("id"), explode(col("nested")).alias("inner"))
        self.assertEqual(first.count(), 2)
        
        # Second explosion
        second = first.select(col("id"), explode(col("inner")).alias("item"))
        self.assertEqual(second.count(), 3)
    
    def test_explosion_with_filter(self):
        """Test explosion with filtering"""
        data = [
            ("user1", ["a", "b", "c"]),
            ("user2", ["d", "e"])
        ]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("items", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        result = df.select(
            col("id"),
            explode(col("items")).alias("item")
        ).filter(col("item").isin(["a", "d"]))
        
        self.assertEqual(result.count(), 2)
    
    def test_explosion_with_aggregation(self):
        """Test explosion followed by aggregation"""
        data = [
            ("cat1", ["item1", "item2"]),
            ("cat2", ["item1", "item3"])
        ]
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("category", StringType(), True),
            StructField("items", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
        result = df.select(
            explode(col("items")).alias("item")
        ).groupBy("item").count()
        
        # item1 should appear twice
        item1_count = result.filter(col("item") == "item1") \
            .select("count").collect()[0][0]
        self.assertEqual(item1_count, 2)

def run_tests():
    """Run all tests"""
    print("=" * 80)
    print("RUNNING EXPLOSION PATTERNS TESTS")
    print("=" * 80 + "\n")
    
    # Create test suite
    suite = unittest.TestLoader().loadTestsFromTestCase(TestExplosionPatterns)
    
    # Run tests
    runner = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2)
    result = runner.run(suite)
    
    # Print summary
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("TEST SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)
    print(f"Tests run: {result.testsRun}")
    print(f"Successes: {result.testsRun - len(result.failures) - len(result.errors)}")
    print(f"Failures: {len(result.failures)}")
    print(f"Errors: {len(result.errors)}")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    return result.wasSuccessful()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    success = run_tests()
    exit(0 if success else 1)

"""
Performance Benchmarking for Explosion Patterns
-----------------------------------------------
Measures and compares performance of different explosion strategies.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
import time
import random

def benchmark_explosion_patterns():
    # Initialize Spark Session
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("ExplosionPatternsBenchmark") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .config("spark.sql.crossJoin.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    print("=" * 80)
    print("EXPLOSION PATTERNS PERFORMANCE BENCHMARK")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Generate test data
    print("\n--- Generating Test Data ---")
    
    def generate_large_dataset(num_rows, array_size):
        """Generate large dataset for benchmarking"""
        data = [
            (
                f"id_{i}",
                [f"item_{j}" for j in range(random.randint(1, array_size))],
                {f"key_{j}": f"value_{j}" for j in range(random.randint(1, 5))}
            )
            for i in range(num_rows)
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("items", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
            StructField("metadata", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
        ])
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    # Test configurations
    test_configs = [
        {"rows": 1000, "array_size": 10, "name": "Small Dataset"},
        {"rows": 10000, "array_size": 20, "name": "Medium Dataset"},
        {"rows": 50000, "array_size": 30, "name": "Large Dataset"}
    ]
    
    results = []
    
    for config in test_configs:
        print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
        print(f"Testing: {config['name']}")
        print(f"Rows: {config['rows']}, Max Array Size: {config['array_size']}")
        print(f"{'=' * 80}")
        
        df = generate_large_dataset(config['rows'], config['array_size'])
        df.cache()
        df.count()  # Force materialization
        
        # Benchmark 1: Array Explosion
        print("\n--- Benchmark 1: Array Explosion ---")
        start = time.time()
        array_exploded = df.select(col("id"), explode(col("items")).alias("item"))
        array_count = array_exploded.count()
        array_time = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time: {array_time:.2f}s, Result Rows: {array_count}")
        
        # Benchmark 2: Map Explosion
        print("\n--- Benchmark 2: Map Explosion ---")
        start = time.time()
        map_exploded = df.select(
            col("id"),
            explode(col("metadata")).alias("key", "value")
        )
        map_count = map_exploded.count()
        map_time = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time: {map_time:.2f}s, Result Rows: {map_count}")
        
        # Benchmark 3: Positional Explosion
        print("\n--- Benchmark 3: Positional Explosion ---")
        start = time.time()
        pos_exploded = df.select(
            col("id"),
            posexplode(col("items")).alias("pos", "item")
        )
        pos_count = pos_exploded.count()
        pos_time = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time: {pos_time:.2f}s, Result Rows: {pos_count}")
        
        # Benchmark 4: Lateral View (SQL)
        print("\n--- Benchmark 4: Lateral View (SQL) ---")
        df.createOrReplaceTempView("benchmark_table")
        start = time.time()
        lateral_result = spark.sql("""
            SELECT id, item
            FROM benchmark_table
            LATERAL VIEW explode(items) t AS item
        """)
        lateral_count = lateral_result.count()
        lateral_time = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time: {lateral_time:.2f}s, Result
```python
 Rows: {lateral_count}")
        
        # Benchmark 5: Multiple Explosions
        print("\n--- Benchmark 5: Multiple Explosions (Cartesian) ---")
        start = time.time()
        multi_exploded = df.select(
            col("id"),
            explode(col("items")).alias("item"),
            explode(col("metadata")).alias("key", "value")
        )
        multi_count = multi_exploded.count()
        multi_time = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time: {multi_time:.2f}s, Result Rows: {multi_count}")
        
        # Benchmark 6: Explosion with Filter
        print("\n--- Benchmark 6: Explosion with Filter ---")
        start = time.time()
        filtered_exploded = df.select(
            col("id"),
            explode(col("items")).alias("item")
        ).filter(col("item").endswith("0"))
        filtered_count = filtered_exploded.count()
        filtered_time = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time: {filtered_time:.2f}s, Result Rows: {filtered_count}")
        
        # Benchmark 7: Explosion with Aggregation
        print("\n--- Benchmark 7: Explosion with Aggregation ---")
        start = time.time()
        agg_result = df.select(
            explode(col("items")).alias("item")
        ).groupBy("item").count()
        agg_count = agg_result.count()
        agg_time = time.time() - start
        print(f"Time: {agg_time:.2f}s, Unique Items: {agg_count}")
        
        # Store results
        results.append({
            "config": config['name'],
            "input_rows": config['rows'],
            "array_explosion_time": array_time,
            "map_explosion_time": map_time,
            "positional_explosion_time": pos_time,
            "lateral_view_time": lateral_time,
            "multi_explosion_time": multi_time,
            "filtered_explosion_time": filtered_time,
            "aggregation_time": agg_time,
            "array_output_rows": array_count,
            "map_output_rows": map_count,
            "multi_output_rows": multi_count
        })
        
        df.unpersist()
    
    # Print Summary
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PERFORMANCE SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    for result in results:
        print(f"\n{result['config']} (Input: {result['input_rows']} rows)")
        print("-" * 80)
        print(f"  Array Explosion:       {result['array_explosion_time']:.2f}s "
              f"({result['array_output_rows']} rows)")
        print(f"  Map Explosion:         {result['map_explosion_time']:.2f}s "
              f"({result['map_output_rows']} rows)")
        print(f"  Positional Explosion:  {result['positional_explosion_time']:.2f}s")
        print(f"  Lateral View:          {result['lateral_view_time']:.2f}s")
        print(f"  Multiple Explosions:   {result['multi_explosion_time']:.2f}s "
              f"({result['multi_output_rows']} rows)")
        print(f"  Filtered Explosion:    {result['filtered_explosion_time']:.2f}s")
        print(f"  With Aggregation:      {result['aggregation_time']:.2f}s")
        
        # Calculate explosion factor
        if result['input_rows'] > 0:
            array_factor = result['array_output_rows'] / result['input_rows']
            multi_factor = result['multi_output_rows'] / result['input_rows']
            print(f"\n  Explosion Factors:")
            print(f"    Array:    {array_factor:.1f}x")
            print(f"    Multiple: {multi_factor:.1f}x")
    
    # Performance Tips
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PERFORMANCE INSIGHTS")
    print("=" * 80)
    print("""
    Key Findings:
    
    1. POSITIONAL EXPLOSION vs REGULAR EXPLOSION:
       - Positional explosion (posexplode) has minimal overhead
       - Use when position information is needed
    
    2. LATERAL VIEW vs DataFrame API:
       - Performance is generally comparable
       - Choose based on code readability and team preference
    
    3. MULTIPLE EXPLOSIONS:
       - Creates cartesian product (m × n rows)
       - Can cause significant data expansion
       - Consider separate explosions if cartesian not needed
    
    4. FILTERING:
       - Apply filters AFTER explosion when possible
       - Predicate pushdown may not work across explosions
       - Consider filtering before explosion if it reduces array size
    
    5. AGGREGATION:
       - Explosion followed by aggregation is common pattern
       - Consider using approx functions for large datasets
       - Group by before explosion if possible
    
    6. MEMORY CONSIDERATIONS:
       - Large explosions can cause memory pressure
       - Monitor shuffle size and partition count
       - Use repartition/coalesce strategically
    
    7. OPTIMIZATION STRATEGIES:
       - Cache intermediate results if reused
       - Use broadcast joins for small dimension tables
       - Adjust spark.sql.shuffle.partitions based on data size
       - Consider writing intermediate results to disk
    """)
    
    spark.stop()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    benchmark_explosion_patterns()

        FROM (
            SELECT user_id, explode(products) as product

            SELECT user_id, explode(products) as product

        ) p2

        GROUP BY p1.product, p2.product
        ORDER BY co_purchase_count DESC
    """

```python
col("call_id"),
        col("caller_id"),
        col("duration_seconds"),
        posexplode(col("tower_sequence")).alias("sequence_num", "tower_id")
    ).withColumn(
        "is_handoff",
        when(col("sequence_num") > 0, lit(True)).otherwise(lit(False))
    )
    
    tower_handoffs.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Tower pair analysis (handoff patterns)
    print("\n--- Tower Handoff Patterns ---")
    cdr_df.createOrReplaceTempView("cdr")
    
    handoff_pattern_sql = """
        WITH tower_pairs AS (
            SELECT 
                call_id,
                caller_id,
                pos as sequence,
                tower as from_tower,
                LEAD(tower) OVER (PARTITION BY call_id ORDER BY pos) as to_tower
            FROM cdr
            LATERAL VIEW posexplode(tower_sequence) t AS pos, tower
        )
        SELECT 
            from_tower,
            to_tower,
            COUNT(*) as handoff_count
        FROM tower_pairs
        WHERE to_tower IS NOT NULL
        GROUP BY from_tower, to_tower
        ORDER BY handoff_count DESC
    """
    
    handoff_patterns = spark.sql(handoff_pattern_sql)
    handoff_patterns.show(truncate=False)

        ]), True)
    ])

    ).withColumn("treatment_type", lit("medication"))
    
    procedures = patients_df.select(
        col("patient_id"),
        col("visit_date"),
        explode_outer(col("treatments.procedures")).alias("treatment")
    ).withColumn("treatment_type", lit("procedure"))
    
    diagnoses = patients_df.select(

            FROM patients
            UNION ALL
            SELECT patient_id, visit_date, explode(treatments.diagnoses) as treatment
            FROM patients
        )
        SELECT 
            t1.treatment as treatment_1,
            t2.treatment as treatment_2,
            COUNT(DISTINCT t1.patient_id) as patient_count
        FROM all_treatments t1
        JOIN all_treatments t2
            ON t1.patient_id = t2.patient_id 
            AND t1.visit_date = t2.visit_date
            AND t1.treatment < t2.treatment
        GROUP BY t1.treatment, t2.treatment
        ORDER BY patient_count DESC
    """
    
    treatment_cooccurrence = spark.sql(cooccurrence_sql)
    treatment_cooccurrence.show(truncate=False)

        ])

    txn_item_schema = StructType([
