        StructField("line_items", ArrayType(txn_item_schema), True)
    ])
    
    transactions_df = spark.createDataFrame(transaction_data, transaction_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Original Transactions ---")
    transactions_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Explode line items
    print("\n--- Detailed Line Items ---")
    line_items = transactions_df.select(
        col("transaction_id"),
        col("account_id"),
        col("transaction_date"),
        explode(col("line_items")).alias("item")
    ).select(
        col("transaction_id"),
        col("account_id"),
        col("transaction_date"),
        col("item.merchant").alias("merchant"),
        col("item.amount").alias("amount"),
        col("item.category").alias("category")
    )
    
    line_items.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Spending analysis by category
    print("\n--- Spending by Category ---")
    category_spending = line_items.groupBy("category").agg(
        sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
        count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
        round(avg("amount"), 2).alias("avg_amount")
    ).orderBy(col("total_amount").desc())
    
    category_spending.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Merchant analysis
    print("\n--- Merchant Analysis ---")
    merchant_analysis = line_items.groupBy("merchant").agg(
        sum("amount").alias("total_revenue"),
        countDistinct("account_id").alias("unique_customers"),
        count("*").alias("transaction_count")
    ).orderBy(col("total_revenue").desc())
    
    merchant_analysis.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Use Case 8: Marketing - Campaign Performance
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("USE CASE 8: Marketing Campaign Performance")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    campaign_data = [
        ("campaign_A", ["email", "social", "display"], 
         {"email": "1000", "social": "5000", "display": "10000"},
         {"email": "50", "social": "150", "display": "200"}),
        ("campaign_B", ["email", "search"],
         {"email": "2000", "search": "8000"},
         {"email": "100", "search": "400"})
    ]
    
    campaign_schema = StructType([
        StructField("campaign_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("channels", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
        StructField("impressions", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True),
        StructField("clicks", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    campaigns_df = spark.createDataFrame(campaign_data, campaign_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Original Campaign Data ---")
    campaigns_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Explode to channel level
    print("\n--- Channel-Level Metrics ---")
    campaigns_df.createOrReplaceTempView("campaigns")
    
    channel_metrics_sql = """
        SELECT 
            c.campaign_id,
            channel,
            CAST(i.impressions as INT) as impressions,
            CAST(cl.clicks as INT) as clicks,
            ROUND(CAST(cl.clicks as DOUBLE) / CAST(i.impressions as DOUBLE) * 100, 2) as ctr_percent
        FROM campaigns c
        LATERAL VIEW explode(channels) ch AS channel
        LATERAL VIEW explode(impressions) i AS imp_channel, impressions
        LATERAL VIEW explode(clicks) cl AS click_channel, clicks
        WHERE channel = imp_channel AND channel = click_channel
        ORDER BY campaign_id, ctr_percent DESC
    """
    
    channel_metrics = spark.sql(channel_metrics_sql)
    channel_metrics.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Cross-channel analysis
    print("\n--- Cross-Channel Performance Comparison ---")
    channel_comparison = channel_metrics.groupBy("channel").agg(
        sum("impressions").alias("total_impressions"),
        sum("clicks").alias("total_clicks"),
        round(avg("ctr_percent"), 2).alias("avg_ctr")
    ).orderBy(col("avg_ctr").desc())
    
    channel_comparison.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Use Case 9: Retail - Inventory Management
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("USE CASE 9: Retail Inventory Management")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Generate all store-product combinations
    stores_data = [("store_1", "NYC"), ("store_2", "LA"), ("store_3", "Chicago")]
    products_data = [("prod_A", "Electronics"), ("prod_B", "Clothing"), ("prod_C", "Food")]
    
    stores_schema = StructType([
        StructField("store_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("location", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    products_schema = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("category", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    stores_df = spark.createDataFrame(stores_data, stores_schema)
    products_df = spark.createDataFrame(products_data, products_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Stores ---")
    stores_df.show()
    
    print("\n--- Products ---")
    products_df.show()
    
    # Cross join to create inventory template
    print("\n--- All Store-Product Combinations (Inventory Template) ---")
    inventory_template = stores_df.crossJoin(products_df)
    inventory_template.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Add random stock levels
    print("\n--- With Stock Levels ---")
    from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, when
    
    inventory_with_stock = inventory_template.withColumn(
        "stock_level",
        (rand() * 100).cast("int")
    ).withColumn(
        "reorder_needed",
        when(col("stock_level") < 20, lit(True)).otherwise(lit(False))
    )
    
    inventory_with_stock.orderBy("store_id", "product_id").show(truncate=False)
    
    # Reorder analysis
    print("\n--- Reorder Requirements ---")
    reorder_summary = inventory_with_stock.filter(col("reorder_needed") == True) \
        .groupBy("store_id", "location").agg(
            count("*").alias("products_to_reorder"),
            collect_list("product_id").alias("product_list")
        )
    
    reorder_summary.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Use Case 10: Education - Student Course Enrollment
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("USE CASE 10: Student Course Enrollment Analysis")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    enrollment_data = [
        ("student_001", "John", ["MATH101", "CS101", "ENG101"]),
        ("student_002", "Jane", ["MATH101", "PHYS101"]),
        ("student_003", "Bob", ["CS101", "MATH101", "CHEM101"])
    ]
    
    enrollment_schema = StructType([
        StructField("student_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("student_name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("courses", ArrayType(StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    enrollments_df = spark.createDataFrame(enrollment_data, enrollment_schema)
    
    print("\n--- Student Enrollments ---")
    enrollments_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Course enrollment counts
    print("\n--- Course Popularity ---")
    course_popularity = enrollments_df.select(
        explode(col("courses")).alias("course_id")
    ).groupBy("course_id").agg(
        count("*").alias("enrollment_count")
    ).orderBy(col("enrollment_count").desc())
    
    course_popularity.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Student pairs in same courses (study group suggestions)
    print("\n--- Potential Study Groups (Students in Same Courses) ---")
    enrollments_df.createOrReplaceTempView("enrollments")
    
    study_groups_sql = """
        SELECT 
            e1.student_name as student_1,
            e2.student_name as student_2,
            e1.course as shared_course
        FROM (
            SELECT student_id, student_name, explode(courses) as course
            FROM enrollments
        ) e1
        JOIN (
            SELECT student_id, student_name, explode(courses) as course
            FROM enrollments
        ) e2
        ON e1.course = e2.course AND e1.student_id < e2.student_id
        ORDER BY shared_course, student_1
    """
    
    study_groups = spark.sql(study_groups_sql)
    study_groups.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Summary
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("USE CASE SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)
    print("""
    Demonstrated 10 Real-World Use Cases:
    
    1.  E-Commerce: Product recommendation through co-purchase analysis
    2.  IoT: Sensor data
```python
 time-series expansion and analysis
    3.  Social Media: Hashtag extraction and trend analysis
    4.  Log Analysis: Error tracking and frequency analysis

    8.  Marketing: Multi-channel campaign performance metrics

    Common Patterns Used:
    - Array explosion for multi-valued attributes

## Complete Documentation

```python
"""
Complete Documentation and Examples Index
-----------------------------------------
Comprehensive guide to all explosion patterns with quick reference.
"""

def print_complete_documentation():
    documentation = """
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║           PYSPARK DATA EXPLOSION PATTERNS - COMPLETE REFERENCE             ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

TABLE OF CONTENTS
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
1. Array Explosion Pattern
2. Map Explosion Pattern
3. Positional Explosion Pattern
4. Lateral View Pattern
5. Cross Join Explosion Pattern
6. Advanced Patterns
7. Performance Optimization
8. Real-World Use Cases
9. Testing and Validation
10. Best Practices


1. ARRAY EXPLOSION PATTERN
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Purpose: Transform array columns into separate rows

Functions:
  • explode(col)         - Explodes array, drops NULL/empty
  • explode_outer(col)   - Explodes array, preserves NULL/empty

Syntax (DataFrame API):
  df.select(col("id"), explode(col("array_col")).alias("element"))

Syntax (SQL):
  SELECT id, element FROM table
  LATERAL VIEW explode(array_col) t AS element

Use Cases:
  ✓ Flattening nested arrays
  ✓ Processing multi-valued attributes
  ✓ Tag/category analysis
  ✓ Skill/feature expansion

Example:
  Input:  [("user1", ["Python", "Java"])]
  Output: [("user1", "Python"), ("user1", "Java")]

Edge Cases:
  • NULL arrays: explode drops, explode_outer preserves
  • Empty arrays: explode drops, explode_outer preserves
  • Nested arrays: requires multiple explosions


2. MAP EXPLOSION PATTERN
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Purpose: Transform map/dictionary columns into key-value rows

Functions:
  • explode(map_col)       - Explodes map, drops NULL/empty
  • explode_outer(map_col) - Explodes map, preserves NULL/empty

Syntax (DataFrame API):
  df.select(col("id"), explode(col("map_col")).alias("key", "value"))

Syntax (SQL):
  SELECT id, key, value FROM table
  LATERAL VIEW explode(map_col) t AS key, value

Use Cases:
  ✓ Configuration data flattening
  ✓ Metadata extraction
  ✓ JSON key-value processing
  ✓ Dynamic attributes

Example:
  Input:  [("prod1", {"color": "red", "size": "L"})]
  Output: [("prod1", "color", "red"), ("prod1", "size", "L")]

Edge Cases:
  • NULL maps: explode drops, explode_outer preserves
  • Empty maps: explode drops, explode_outer preserves


3. POSITIONAL EXPLOSION PATTERN
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Purpose: Explode arrays while preserving element position/index

Functions:
  • posexplode(col)       - Explodes with position, drops NULL/empty
  • posexplode_outer(col) - Explodes with position, preserves NULL/empty

Syntax (DataFrame API):
  df.select(col("id"), posexplode(col("array_col")).alias("pos", "element"))

Syntax (SQL):
  SELECT id, pos, element FROM table
  LATERAL VIEW posexplode(array_col) t AS pos, element

Use Cases:
  ✓ Time-series data (position = time interval)
  ✓ Rankings and sequences
  ✓ Order-dependent processing
  ✓ Index-based calculations

Example:
  Input:  [("race1", ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"])]
  Output: [("race1", 0, "Alice"), ("race1", 1, "Bob"), ("race1", 2, "Charlie")]

Notes:
  • Position is 0-indexed
  • Add 1 to position for 1-indexed ranks
  • Minimal performance overhead vs regular explode


4. LATERAL VIEW PATTERN
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Purpose: SQL-based explosion with access to original columns

Syntax:
  SELECT columns
  FROM table
  LATERAL VIEW explode(array_col) alias AS element
  [LATERAL VIEW explode(another_col) alias2 AS element2]

Variants:
  • LATERAL VIEW explode(...)       - Drops NULL/empty
  • LATERAL VIEW OUTER explode(...) - Preserves NULL/empty

Use Cases:
  ✓ Complex SQL transformations
  ✓ Multiple simultaneous explosions
  ✓ Legacy SQL compatibility
  ✓ When SQL is preferred over DataFrame API

Example:
  SELECT user_id, skill, certification
  FROM users
  LATERAL VIEW explode(skills) s AS skill
  LATERAL VIEW explode(certifications) c AS certification

Multiple LATERAL VIEWs:
  • Creates cartesian product between explosions
  • Use separate queries if cartesian not needed


5. CROSS JOIN EXPLOSION PATTERN
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Purpose: Generate cartesian product between datasets

Syntax (DataFrame API):
  df1.crossJoin(df2)

Syntax (SQL):
  SELECT * FROM table1 CROSS JOIN table2

Configuration Required:
  spark.sql.crossJoin.enabled = true

Use Cases:
  ✓ Scenario analysis
  ✓ Parameter grid generation
  ✓ All combinations generation
  ✓ Inventory templates
  ✓ Simulation scenarios

Example:
  products (3 rows) CROSS JOIN stores (4 rows) = 12 rows

⚠️  WARNING:
  • Can produce VERY large result sets (m × n rows)
  • Monitor memory and shuffle operations
  • Consider filtering after cross join
  • Use broadcast for small tables

Performance Tips:
  • Filter before cross join when possible
  • Use broadcast() for small dimension tables
  • Monitor data skew
  • Consider writing intermediate results


6. ADVANCED PATTERNS
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Nested Array Explosion:
  df.select(explode(col("outer_array")).alias("inner_array"))
    .select(explode(col("inner_array")).alias("element"))

Struct with Arrays:
  df.select(explode(col("array_of_structs")).alias("struct"))
    .select(col("struct.field1"), explode(col("struct.array_field")))

Conditional Explosion:
  df.filter(condition).select(explode(col("array_col")))

Explosion with Window Functions:
  exploded_df.withColumn("rank", row_number().over(window_spec))

Explosion with UDF:
  @udf(ArrayType(StringType()))
  def transform(value):
      return [value.upper(), value.lower()]
  
  df.withColumn("variations", transform(col("value")))
    .select(explode(col("variations")))

Dynamic Map Creation:
  df.select(create_map(
      lit("key1"), col("val1"),
      lit("key2"), col("val2")
  ).alias("map_col"))


7. PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Before Explosion:
  ✓ Filter data to reduce volume
  ✓ Cache if reusing multiple times
  ✓ Partition appropriately
  ✓ Use columnar formats (Parquet/ORC)

During Explosion:
  ✓ Use OUTER variants only when needed
  ✓ Apply filters immediately after explosion
  ✓ Avoid multiple sequential cross joins
  ✓ Monitor shuffle operations

After Explosion:
  ✓ Repartition if data is skewed
  ✓ Coalesce if too many small partitions
  ✓ Cache if reusing results
  ✓ Write intermediate results for large explosions

Configuration Tuning:
  spark.sql.shuffle.partitions        (default: 200)
  spark.default.parallelism           (default: cores)
  spark.sql.adaptive.enabled          (default: true in Spark 3+)
  spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled

Memory Management:
  • Monitor executor memory usage
  • Increase driver/executor memory for large explosions
  • Use spillable data structures
  • Consider iterative processing for huge datasets


8. COMMON ANTI-PATTERNS (AVOID)
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

❌ Multiple Cross Joins in Sequence:
   df1.crossJoin(df2).crossJoin(df3).crossJoin(df4)
   → Exponential data growth

❌ Exploding Without Filtering:
   df.select(explode(col("huge_array")))
   → Consider filtering first

❌ Not Using OUTER Variants:
   explode(col("array_with_nulls"))
   → Silently loses data

❌ Forgetting Cross Join Configuration:
   crossJoin without spark.sql.crossJoin.enabled
   → Runtime error

❌ Exploding in Loops:
   for item in array:
       df.select(explode(...))
   → Use single explosion instead


9. TESTING CHECKLIST
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

□ Test with NULL values
□ Test with empty arrays/maps
□ Test with nested structures
□ Test with large datasets
□ Verify row counts after explosion
□ Check for data loss (use OUTER variants)
□ Validate position indices (posexplode)
□ Test cross join result sizes
□ Monitor memory usage
□ Verify query performance


10. QUICK REFERENCE CHEAT SHEET
═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Function              Input       Output        Preserves NULL/Empty
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
explode()             Array       Rows          No
explode_outer()       Array       Rows          Yes
posexplode()          Array       Pos + Rows    No
posexplode_outer()    Array       Pos + Rows    Yes
explode()             Map         Key-Val Rows  No
explode_outer()       Map         Key-Val Rows  Yes
crossJoin()           DataFrame   Cartesian     N/A

SQL Equivalents:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
LATERAL VIEW explode(col)
LATERAL VIEW OUTER explode(col)
LATERAL VIEW posexplode(col)
LATERAL VIEW OUTER posexplode(col)
CROSS JOIN

## README.md

```markdown
# PySpark Data Explosion Patterns

Comprehensive guide and examples for data explosion patterns in PySpark.

## Overview

This package provides complete, production-ready examples of all major data explosion patterns in PySpark:

1. **Array Explosion Pattern** - Exploding array columns into rows
2. **Map Explosion Pattern** - Exploding map/dictionary columns into key-value rows
3. **Positional Explosion Pattern** - Exploding arrays while preserving element positions
4. **Lateral View Pattern** - SQL-based explosion with multiple simultaneous explosions
5. **Cross Join Explosion Pattern** - Creating cartesian products between datasets

## Features

✅ Complete working examples for each pattern
✅ Real-world use cases from 10+ industries
✅ Edge case handling and best practices
✅ Performance benchmarking suite
✅ Comprehensive unit tests
✅ Detailed documentation and comments
✅ Integration examples combining multiple patterns

## Quick Start

### Installation

```bash
# Ensure PySpark is installed
pip install pyspark

# Clone or download this repository
git clone <repository-url>
cd pyspark-explosion-patterns
```

### Run All Examples

```bash
python master_script.py --all
```

### Run Individual Patterns

```bash
# Array explosion
python array_explosion_pattern.py

# Map explosion
python map_explosion_pattern.py

# Positional explosion
python positional_explosion_pattern.py

# Lateral view
python lateral_view_pattern.py

# Cross join
python cross_join_explosion_pattern.py
```

## Pattern Examples

### Array Explosion

```python
from pyspark.sql.functions import explode, col

# Input: [("user1", ["Python", "Java", "Scala"])]
# Output: [("user1", "Python"), ("user1", "Java"), ("user1", "Scala")]

df.select(
    col("user_id"),
    explode(col("skills")).alias("skill")
)
```

### Map Explosion

```python
from pyspark.sql.functions import explode

# Input: [("prod1", {"color": "red", "size": "L"})]
# Output: [("prod1", "color", "red"), ("prod1", "size", "L")]

df.select(
    col("product_id"),
    explode(col("attributes")).alias("key", "value")
)
```

### Positional Explosion

```python
from pyspark.sql.functions import posexplode

# Input: [("race1", ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"])]
# Output: [("race1", 0, "Alice"), ("race1", 1, "Bob"), ("race1", 2, "Charlie")]

df.select(
    col("race_id"),
    posexplode(col("finishers")).alias("position", "athlete")
)
```

### Lateral View

```sql
SELECT 
    order_id,
    customer_id,
    item,
    total_amount
FROM orders
LATERAL VIEW explode(items) exploded_items AS item
```

### Cross Join

```python
# Generate all product-store combinations
products_df.crossJoin(stores_df)
```

## Best Practices

### When to Use Each Pattern

| Pattern | Use When |
|---------|----------|
| Array Explosion | Multi-valued attributes need separate rows |
| Map Explosion | Key-value metadata needs flattening |
| Positional Explosion | Element position/order is meaningful |
| Lateral View | Complex SQL with multiple explosions |
| Cross Join | Need all combinations of datasets |

### Performance Tips

1. **Filter Early** - Apply filters before explosion when possible
2. **Use OUTER Variants** - Only when NULL/empty preservation is needed
3. **Cache Wisely** - Cache results if reusing multiple times
4. **Monitor Shuffle** - Watch shuffle size with large explosions
5. **Partition Appropriately** - Adjust partitions based on data size
6. **Avoid Multiple Cross Joins** - Can cause exponential growth

### Common Pitfalls

❌ Not using `explode_outer()` and losing data
❌ Multiple sequential cross joins causing memory issues
❌ Forgetting to enable cross join configuration
❌ Exploding without considering data volume
❌ Not filtering after explosion

print("\n1. MODULO PARTITIONER PATTERN")
print("-" * 80)
print("Use Case: Evenly distribute data based on numeric keys")
print("Best for: Integer keys, load balancing")

class ModuloPartitioner(Partitioner):
    """
    Partitions data using modulo operation on numeric keys.
    Ensures even distribution across partitions.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_partitions: int):
        self._num_partitions = num_partitions
    
    def numPartitions(self) -> int:
        return self._num_partitions
    
    def getPartition(self, key: Any) -> int:
        """
        Calculate partition using modulo operation.
        
        Args:
            key: Numeric key (int or can be converted to int)
            
        Returns:
            Partition number (0 to num_partitions - 1)
        """
        try:
            # Convert key to integer if possible
            numeric_key = int(key) if not isinstance(key, int) else key
            return numeric_key % self._num_partitions
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            # Fallback to hash for non-numeric keys
            return hash(key) % self._num_partitions


# Example: Distribute user IDs across partitions

]

print(f"\nOriginal data count: {user_rdd.count()}")
print(f"Number of partitions: {partitioned_users.getNumPartitions()}")

print("\n\n2. RANGE PARTITIONER PATTERN")
print("-" * 80)
print("Use Case: Partition data based on value ranges")
print("Best for: Sorted data, time-series, ordered processing")

class RangePartitioner(Partitioner):
    """
    Partitions data based on predefined ranges.
    Useful for time-series, age groups, price ranges, etc.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, ranges: List[Tuple[Any, Any]]):
        """
        Args:
            ranges: List of (min, max) tuples defining partition boundaries
                    Example: [(0, 100), (100, 200), (200, 300)]
        """
        self.ranges = sorted(ranges, key=lambda x: x[0])
        self._num_partitions = len(ranges)
    
    def numPartitions(self) -> int:
        return self._num_partitions
    
    def getPartition(self, key: Any) -> int:
        """
        Find appropriate partition based on key value.
        
        Args:
            key: Value to partition
            
        Returns:
            Partition number based on range
        """
        for idx, (min_val, max_val) in enumerate(self.ranges):
            if min_val <= key < max_val:
                return idx
        
        # Default to last partition if key exceeds all ranges
        return self._num_partitions - 1

print("\n\n3. HASH PARTITIONER PATTERN")
print("-" * 80)
print("Use Case: Distribute data using hash functions")
print("Best for: String keys, consistent hashing, custom distribution")

class CustomHashPartitioner(Partitioner):
    """
    Custom hash-based partitioner with different hashing strategies.
    Provides better control over hash distribution.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_partitions: int, hash_type: str = "md5"):
        """
        Args:
            num_partitions: Number of partitions
            hash_type: Type of hash function ('md5', 'sha256', 'builtin')
        """
        self._num_partitions = num_partitions
        self.hash_type = hash_type
    
    def numPartitions(self) -> int:
        return self._num_partitions
    
    def getPartition(self, key: Any) -> int:
        """
        Calculate partition using selected hash function.
        
        Args:
            key: Key to hash
            
        Returns:
            Partition number
        """
        key_str = str(key)
        
        if self.hash_type == "md5":
            hash_value = int(hashlib.md5(key_str.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
        elif self.hash_type == "sha256":
            hash_value = int(hashlib.sha256(key_str.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
        else:  # builtin
            hash_value = hash(key_str)
        
        return abs(hash_value) % self._num_partitions

]

print("\n\n4. COMPOSITE KEY PARTITIONER PATTERN")
print("-" * 80)
print("Use Case: Partition based on multiple key components")
print("Best for: Multi-dimensional data, hierarchical structures")

class CompositeKeyPartitioner(Partitioner):
    """
    Partitions data based on composite keys (tuples with multiple components).
    Allows prioritizing different components of the key.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_partitions: int, primary_key_index: int = 0):
        """
        Args:
            num_partitions: Number of partitions
            primary_key_index: Index of the primary key component in tuple
        """
        self._num_partitions = num_partitions
        self.primary_key_index = primary_key_index
    
    def numPartitions(self) -> int:
        return self._num_partitions
    
    def getPartition(self, key: Tuple) -> int:
        """
        Calculate partition based on composite key.
        
        Args:
            key: Tuple of key components (e.g., (country, state, city))
            
        Returns:
            Partition number
        """
        if not isinstance(key, tuple):
            key = (key,)
        
        # Use primary key component for partitioning
        if len(key) > self.primary_key_index:
            primary_key = key[self.primary_key_index]
        else:
            primary_key = key[0]
        
        # Combine all key components for better distribution
        combined_hash = hash(str(key))
        
        return abs(combined_hash) % self._num_partitions

print("\n\n5. GEOGRAPHIC PARTITIONER PATTERN")
print("-" * 80)
print("Use Case: Partition data by geographic regions or coordinates")
print("Best for: Location-based data, spatial analysis, geo-distributed processing")

class GeographicPartitioner(Partitioner):
    """
    Partitions data based on geographic regions or coordinate ranges.
    Supports both region-based and coordinate-based partitioning.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, region_mapping: dict = None, num_partitions: int = 4):
        """
        Args:
            region_mapping: Dictionary mapping regions to partition numbers
                           Example: {"North": 0, "South": 1, "East": 2, "West": 3}
            num_partitions: Number of partitions (used if region_mapping not provided)
        """
        self.region_mapping = region_mapping or {}
        self._num_partitions = num_partitions if not region_mapping else len(set(region_mapping.values()))
    
    def numPartitions(self) -> int:
        return self._num_partitions
    
    def getPartition(self, key: Any) -> int:
        """
        Calculate partition based on geographic information.
        
        Args:
            key: Can be:
                 - String region name (e.g., "North America")
                 - Tuple of (latitude, longitude)
                 - Dictionary with 'region' or 'coordinates'
                 
        Returns:
            Partition number
        """
        # Handle string region
        if isinstance(key, str):
            return self.region_mapping.get(key, hash(key) % self._num_partitions)
        
        # Handle coordinate tuple (latitude, longitude)
        if isinstance(key, tuple) and len(key) == 2:
            lat, lon = key
            # Quadrant-based partitioning
            # NE: lat >= 0, lon >= 0 -> 0
            # NW: lat >= 0, lon < 0  -> 1
            # SW: lat < 0, lon < 0   -> 2
            # SE: lat < 0, lon >= 0  -> 3
            if lat >= 0 and lon >= 0:
                return 0
            elif lat >= 0 and lon < 0:
                return 1
            elif lat < 0 and lon < 0:
                return 2
            else:
                return 3
        
        # Handle dictionary
        if isinstance(key, dict):
            if 'region' in key:
                return self.region_mapping.get(key['region'], 0)
            elif 'coordinates' in key:
                lat, lon = key['coordinates']
                return self.getPartition((lat, lon))
        
        # Default fallback
        return hash(str(key)) % self._num_partitions

print("=" * 80)
print("Combining multiple partitioning strategies for complex scenarios")

class HybridPartitioner(Partitioner):
    """
    Advanced partitioner that combines multiple strategies.
    Useful for complex data with multiple partitioning requirements.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_partitions: int, strategy: str = "auto"):
        """
        Args:
            num_partitions: Number of partitions
            strategy: Partitioning strategy ('auto', 'balanced', 'optimized')
        """
        self._num_partitions = num_partitions
        self.strategy = strategy
    
    def numPartitions(self) -> int:
        return self._num_partitions
    
    def getPartition(self, key: Any) -> int:
        """
        Intelligently partition based on key characteristics.
        
        Args:
            key: Can be various types - the partitioner adapts
            
        Returns:
            Partition number
        """
        # Integer keys - use modulo
        if isinstance(key, int):
            return key % self._num_partitions
        
        # Tuple keys - use composite strategy
        if isinstance(key, tuple):
            if len(key) == 2 and all(isinstance(x, (int, float)) for x in key):
                # Assume coordinates
                lat, lon = key
                quadrant = 0
                if lat >= 0 and lon >= 0:
                    quadrant = 0
                elif lat >= 0 and lon < 0:
                    quadrant = 1
                elif lat < 0 and lon < 0:
                    quadrant = 2
                else:
                    quadrant = 3
                return quadrant % self._num_partitions
            else:
                # Generic tuple - hash all components
                return abs(hash(key)) % self._num_partitions
        
        # String keys - use hash
        if isinstance(key, str):
            return abs(hash(key)) % self._num_partitions
        
        # Dictionary keys - use specific field if available
        if isinstance(key, dict):
            if 'partition_key' in key:
                return self.getPartition(key['partition_key'])
            else:
                return abs(hash(str(key))) % self._num_partitions
        
        # Default fallback
        return abs(hash(str(key))) % self._num_partitions

def analyze_partition_distribution(rdd_or_df, name: str = "Dataset"):
    """
    Analyze and report partition distribution statistics.
    
    Args:
        rdd_or_df: RDD or DataFrame to analyze
        name: Name for the dataset (for reporting)
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary with distribution statistics
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"Partition Analysis: {name}")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    
    if hasattr(rdd_or_df, 'toDF'):  # It's an RDD
        # Get partition sizes
        partition_sizes = rdd_or_df.mapPartitions(
            lambda it: [sum(1 for _ in it)]
        ).collect()
        
        total_records = sum(partition_sizes)
        num_partitions = len(partition_sizes)
        
    else:  # It's a DataFrame
        # Use DataFrame API
        partition_dist = rdd_or_df.groupBy(spark_partition_id().alias("partition")) \
            .agg(count("*").alias("count")) \
            .orderBy("partition") \
            .collect()
        
        partition_sizes = [row['count'] for row in partition_dist]
        total_records = sum(partition_sizes)
        num_partitions = len(partition_sizes)
    
    # Calculate statistics
    avg_size = total_records / num_partitions if num_partitions > 0 else 0
    min_size = min(partition_sizes) if partition_sizes else 0
    max_size = max(partition_sizes) if partition_sizes else 0
    
    variance =
```python
    variance = sum((s - avg_size) ** 2 for s in partition_sizes) / num_partitions if num_partitions > 0 else 0
    std_dev = variance ** 0.5
    
    # Calculate skew metrics
    skew_ratio = max_size / avg_size if avg_size > 0 else 0
    balance_score = 100 * (1 - std_dev / avg_size) if avg_size > 0 else 0
    
    # Determine skew level
    if skew_ratio < 1.2:
        skew_level = "Excellent"
    elif skew_ratio < 1.5:
        skew_level = "Good"
    elif skew_ratio < 2.0:

    else:

    stats = {

def recommend_partitioner(data_sample, key_type: str = "auto"):
    """
    Recommend the best partitioner based on data characteristics.
    
    Args:
        data_sample: Sample of keys from the dataset
        key_type: Type of key ('auto', 'numeric', 'string', 'composite', 'geo')
    
    Returns:
        Recommended partitioner class and configuration
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("Partitioner Recommendation Engine")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    
    # Analyze sample
    sample_list = list(data_sample[:100]) if hasattr(data_sample, '__getitem__') else data_sample
    
    if key_type == "auto":
        # Auto-detect key type
        first_key = sample_list[0] if sample_list else None
        
        if isinstance(first_key, int):
            key_type = "numeric"
        elif isinstance(first_key, str):
            key_type = "string"
        elif isinstance(first_key, tuple):
            if len(first_key) == 2 and all(isinstance(x, (int, float)) for x in first_key):
                key_type = "geo"
            else:
                key_type = "composite"
        else:
            key_type = "string"
    
    print(f"Detected Key Type: {key_type}")
    
    recommendations = {
        "numeric": {
            "partitioner": "ModuloPartitioner",
            "reason": "Keys are numeric - modulo provides even distribution",
            "config": {"num_partitions": 8},
            "alternatives": ["CustomHashPartitioner (builtin)"]
        },
        "string": {
            "partitioner": "CustomHashPartitioner",
            "reason": "String keys benefit from hash-based distribution",
            "config": {"num_partitions": 8, "hash_type": "md5"},
            "alternatives": ["CustomHashPartitioner (sha256)"]
        },
        "composite": {
            "partitioner": "CompositeKeyPartitioner",
            "reason": "Composite keys allow hierarchical partitioning",
            "config": {"num_partitions": 8, "primary_key_index": 0},
            "alternatives": ["HybridPartitioner"]
        },
        "geo": {
            "partitioner": "GeographicPartitioner",
            "reason": "Geographic coordinates enable spatial partitioning",
            "config": {"num_partitions": 4},
            "alternatives": ["CompositeKeyPartitioner"]
        }
    }
    
    recommendation = recommendations.get(key_type, recommendations["string"])
    
    print(f"\nRecommended Partitioner: {recommendation['partitioner']}")
    print(f"Reason: {recommendation['reason']}")
    print(f"Configuration: {json.dumps(recommendation['config'], indent=2)}")
    print(f"Alternatives: {', '.join(recommendation['alternatives'])}")
    
    return recommendation


def optimize_partition_count(data_size: int, cluster_cores: int, 
                            target_partition_size_mb: int = 128) -> int:
    """
    Calculate optimal partition count based on data size and cluster resources.
    
    Args:
        data_size: Total data size in MB
        cluster_cores: Total number of cores in cluster
        target_partition_size_mb: Target size per partition in MB
    
    Returns:
        Recommended number of partitions
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print("Partition Count Optimization")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    
    # Calculate based on data size
    size_based = max(1, data_size // target_partition_size_mb)
    
    # Calculate based on cluster resources (2-3x cores is typical)
    resource_based_min = cluster_cores * 2
    resource_based_max = cluster_cores * 4
    
    # Choose optimal value
    if size_based < resource_based_min:
        optimal = resource_based_min
        reason = "Resource-based (minimum for parallelism)"
    elif size_based > resource_based_max:
        optimal = resource_based_max
        reason = "Resource-based (avoid too many small partitions)"
    else:
        optimal = size_based
        reason = "Size-based (balanced approach)"
    
    print(f"Data Size: {data_size} MB")
    print(f"Cluster Cores: {cluster_cores}")
    print(f"Target Partition Size: {target_partition_size_mb} MB")
    print(f"\nCalculations:")
    print(f"  Size-based partitions: {size_based}")
    print(f"  Resource-based range: {resource_based_min} - {resource_based_max}")
    print(f"\nRecommended Partitions: {optimal}")
    print(f"Reason: {reason}")
    print(f"Expected partition size: ~{data_size / optimal:.2f} MB")
    
    return optimal


class PartitionMonitor:
    """
    Monitor and track partition health metrics over time.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.metrics_history = []
    
    def collect_metrics(self, rdd_or_df, timestamp: str = None):
        """
        Collect partition metrics at a point in time.
        
        Args:
            rdd_or_df: RDD or DataFrame to monitor
            timestamp: Optional timestamp (defaults to current time)
        """
        from datetime import datetime
        
        if timestamp is None:
            timestamp = datetime.now().isoformat()
        
        # Get partition sizes
        if hasattr(rdd_or_df, 'toDF'):  # RDD
            partition_sizes = rdd_or_df.mapPartitions(
                lambda it: [sum(1 for _ in it)]
            ).collect()
        else:  # DataFrame
            partition_dist = rdd_or_df.groupBy(spark_partition_id().alias("partition")) \
                .agg(count("*").alias("count")) \
                .collect()
            partition_sizes = [row['count'] for row in partition_dist]
        
        # Calculate metrics
        total = sum(partition_sizes)
        avg = total / len(partition_sizes) if partition_sizes else 0
        max_size = max(partition_sizes) if partition_sizes else 0
        
        metrics = {
            'timestamp': timestamp,
            'total_records': total,
            'num_partitions': len(partition_sizes),
            'partition_sizes': partition_sizes,
            'avg_size': avg,
            'max_size': max_size,
            'skew_ratio': max_size / avg if avg > 0 else 0
        }
        
        self.metrics_history.append(metrics)
        return metrics
    
    def detect_skew_trend(self, threshold: float = 2.0):
        """
        Detect if partition skew is increasing over time.
        
        Args:
            threshold: Skew ratio threshold for alerts
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with trend analysis
        """
        if len(self.metrics_history) < 2:
            return {"status": "Insufficient data", "alert": False}
        
        recent_skew = [m['skew_ratio'] for m in self.metrics_history[-5:]]
        avg_recent_skew = sum(recent_skew) / len(recent_skew)
        
        trend = "increasing" if recent_skew[-1] > recent_skew[0] else "decreasing"
        alert = avg_recent_skew > threshold
        
        return {
            "status": f"Skew is {trend}",
            "current_skew": recent_skew[-1],
            "avg_recent_skew": avg_recent_skew,
            "threshold": threshold,
            "alert": alert,
            "recommendation": "Consider repartitioning" if alert else "Partitioning is healthy"
        }
    
    def generate_report(self):
        """
        Generate a comprehensive monitoring report.
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("Partition Monitoring Report")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        if not self.metrics_history:
            print("No metrics collected yet.")
            return
        
        print(f"Total Snapshots: {len(self.metrics_history)}")
        print(f"First Snapshot: {self.metrics_history[0]['timestamp']}")
        print(f"Last Snapshot: {self.metrics_history[-1]['timestamp']}")
        
        # Trend analysis
        trend = self.detect_skew_trend()
        print(f"\nSkew Trend Analysis:")
        print(f"  Status: {trend['status']}")
        print(f"  Current Skew: {trend.get('current_skew', 0):.2f}x")
        print(f"  Alert: {'⚠️ YES' if trend.get('alert') else '✓ NO'}")
        print(f"  Recommendation: {trend.get('recommendation', 'N/A')}")
        
        # Historical stats
        all_skews = [m['skew_ratio'] for m in self.metrics_history]
        print(f"\nHistorical Statistics:")
        print(f"  Min Skew: {min(all_skews):.2f}x")
        print(f"  Max Skew: {max(all_skews):.2f}x")
        print(f"  Avg Skew: {sum(all_skews)/len(all_skews):.2f}x")

class PartitionerFactory:
    """
    Factory class to create and configure partitioners based on requirements.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create(partitioner_type: str, num_partitions: int, **kwargs):
        """
        Create a partitioner instance based on type.
        
        Args:
            partitioner_type: Type of partitioner to create
            num_partitions: Number of partitions
            **kwargs: Additional configuration parameters
        
        Returns:
            Configured partitioner instance
        """
        partitioners = {
            'modulo': lambda: Modulo
```python
        partitioners = {
            'modulo': lambda: ModuloPartitioner(num_partitions),
            'range': lambda: RangePartitioner(kwargs.get('ranges', [(0, 100), (100, 200), (200, 1000)])),
            'hash': lambda: CustomHashPartitioner(num_partitions, kwargs.get('hash_type', 'md5')),
            'composite': lambda: CompositeKeyPartitioner(num_partitions, kwargs.get('primary_key_index', 0)),
            'geographic': lambda: GeographicPartitioner(kwargs.get('region_mapping'), num_partitions),
            'hybrid': lambda: HybridPartitioner(num_partitions, kwargs.get('strategy', 'auto'))
        }
        
        partitioner_type = partitioner_type.lower()
        if partitioner_type not in partitioners:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown partitioner type: {partitioner_type}. "
                           f"Available types: {list(partitioners.keys())}")
        
        return partitioners[partitioner_type]()
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_from_config(config: dict):
        """
        Create partitioner from configuration dictionary.
        
        Args:
            config: Configuration dictionary with partitioner settings
            
        Example:
            config = {
                'type': 'hash',
                'num_partitions': 8,
                'hash_type': 'md5'
            }
        
        Returns:
            Configured partitioner instance
        """
        partitioner_type = config.get('type', 'hash')
        num_partitions = config.get('num_partitions', 4)
        
        # Remove type and num_partitions from kwargs
        kwargs = {k: v for k, v in config.items() 
                 if k not in ['type', 'num_partitions']}
        
        return PartitionerFactory.create(partitioner_type, num_partitions, **kwargs)

class PartitionerTestSuite:
    """
    Comprehensive testing suite for partitioner validation.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_context):
        self.sc = spark_context
        self.test_results = []
    
    def test_distribution_uniformity(self, partitioner, test_data, 
                                     tolerance: float = 0.2):
        """
        Test if partitioner provides uniform distribution.
        
        Args:
            partitioner: Partitioner instance to test
            test_data: List of (key, value) tuples
            tolerance: Acceptable deviation from perfect balance (0.2 = 20%)
        
        Returns:
            Test result dictionary
        """
        rdd = self.sc.parallelize(test_data)
        partitioned = rdd.partitionBy(partitioner.numPartitions(), partitioner)
        
        partition_sizes = partitioned.mapPartitions(
            lambda it: [sum(1 for _ in it)]
        ).collect()
        
        avg_size = sum(partition_sizes) / len(partition_sizes)
        max_deviation = max(abs(s - avg_size) / avg_size for s in partition_sizes)
        
        passed = max_deviation <= tolerance
        
        result = {
            'test': 'Distribution Uniformity',
            'partitioner': partitioner.__class__.__name__,
            'partition_sizes': partition_sizes,
            'avg_size': avg_size,
            'max_deviation': max_deviation,
            'tolerance': tolerance,
            'passed': passed
        }
        
        self.test_results.append(result)
        return result
    
    def test_determinism(self, partitioner, test_data, iterations: int = 3):
        """
        Test if partitioner produces consistent results.
        
        Args:
            partitioner: Partitioner instance to test
            test_data: List of (key, value) tuples
            iterations: Number of times to repeat the test
        
        Returns:
            Test result dictionary
        """
        partition_assignments = []
        
        for _ in range(iterations):
            rdd = self.sc.parallelize(test_data)
            partitioned = rdd.partitionBy(partitioner.numPartitions(), partitioner)
            
            # Get partition assignment for each key
            assignments = partitioned.mapPartitionsWithIndex(
                lambda idx, it: [(key, idx) for key, val in it]
            ).collectAsMap()
            
            partition_assignments.append(assignments)
        
        # Check if all iterations produced same assignments
        consistent = all(
            partition_assignments[0] == assignment 
            for assignment in partition_assignments[1:]
        )
        
        result = {
            'test': 'Determinism',
            'partitioner': partitioner.__class__.__name__,
            'iterations': iterations,
            'consistent': consistent,
            'passed': consistent
        }
        
        self.test_results.append(result)
        return result
    
    def test_partition_coverage(self, partitioner, test_data):
        """
        Test if all partitions are utilized.
        
        Args:
            partitioner: Partitioner instance to test
            test_data: List of (key, value) tuples
        
        Returns:
            Test result dictionary
        """
        rdd = self.sc.parallelize(test_data)
        partitioned = rdd.partitionBy(partitioner.numPartitions(), partitioner)
        
        partition_sizes = partitioned.mapPartitions(
            lambda it: [sum(1 for _ in it)]
        ).collect()
        
        empty_partitions = sum(1 for s in partition_sizes if s == 0)
        coverage_ratio = (len(partition_sizes) - empty_partitions) / len(partition_sizes)
        
        # Consider it passed if at least 75% of partitions are used
        passed = coverage_ratio >= 0.75
        
        result = {
            'test': 'Partition Coverage',
            'partitioner': partitioner.__class__.__name__,
            'total_partitions': len(partition_sizes),
            'empty_partitions': empty_partitions,
            'coverage_ratio': coverage_ratio,
            'passed': passed
        }
        
        self.test_results.append(result)
        return result
    
    def run_all_tests(self, partitioner, test_data):
        """
        Run all tests for a partitioner.
        
        Args:
            partitioner: Partitioner instance to test
            test_data: List of (key, value) tuples
        
        Returns:
            Summary of all test results
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print(f"Testing {partitioner.__class__.__name__}")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Run all tests
        uniformity = self.test_distribution_uniformity(partitioner, test_data)
        determinism = self.test_determinism(partitioner, test_data)
        coverage = self.test_partition_coverage(partitioner, test_data)
        
        # Print results
        all_tests = [uniformity, determinism, coverage]
        
        for test in all_tests:
            status = "✓ PASS" if test['passed'] else "✗ FAIL"
            print(f"\n{test['test']}: {status}")
            for key, value in test.items():
                if key not in ['test', 'passed', 'partitioner']:
                    print(f"  {key}: {value}")
        
        # Overall summary
        passed_count = sum(1 for t in all_tests if t['passed'])
        total_count = len(all_tests)
        
        print(f"\nOverall: {passed_count}/{total_count} tests passed")
        
        return {
            'partitioner': partitioner.__class__.__name__,
            'tests': all_tests,
            'passed': passed_count,
            'total': total_count,
            'success_rate': passed_count / total_count
        }
    
    def generate_summary_report(self):
        """
        Generate summary report of all tests.
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print("PARTITIONER TEST SUITE - SUMMARY REPORT")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        if not self.test_results:
            print("No tests have been run yet.")
            return
        
        # Group by partitioner
        partitioners = {}
        for result in self.test_results:
            partitioner_name = result['partitioner']
            if partitioner_name not in partitioners:
                partitioners[partitioner_name] = []
            partitioners[partitioner_name].append(result)
        
        # Print summary for each partitioner
        for partitioner_name, results in partitioners.items():
            passed = sum(1 for r in results if r['passed'])
            total = len(results)
            
            print(f"\n{partitioner_name}:")
            print(f"  Tests Passed: {passed}/{total}")
            print(f"  Success Rate: {passed/total*100:.1f}%")

# ==============================================================================
# ADVANCED PATTERN: ADAPTIVE PARTITIONER
# ==============================================================================

class AdaptivePartitioner(Partitioner):
    """
    Advanced partitioner that adapts based on runtime statistics.
    Monitors data distribution and adjusts partitioning strategy dynamically.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_partitions: int, adaptation_threshold: float = 2.0):
        """
        Args:
            num_partitions: Number of partitions
            adaptation_threshold: Skew ratio threshold to trigger adaptation
        """
        self._num_partitions = num_partitions
        self.adaptation_threshold = adaptation_threshold
        self.partition_stats = {}
        self.adaptation_count = 0
        self.current_strategy = 'hash'  # Start with hash strategy
    
    def numPartitions(self) -> int:
        return self._num_partitions
    
    def getPartition(self, key: Any) -> int:
        """
        Adaptively partition based on current strategy and statistics.
        
        Args:
            key: Key to partition
            
        Returns:
            Partition number
        """
        # Track key frequency
        key_str = str(key)
        if key_str not in self.partition_stats:
            self.partition_stats[key_str] = 0
        self.partition_stats[key_str] += 1
        
        # Use current strategy
        if self.current_strategy == 'hash':
            return abs(hash(key)) % self._num_partitions
        elif self.current_strategy == 'modulo' and isinstance(key, int):
            return key % self._num_partitions
        else:
            return abs(hash(key)) % self._num_partitions
    
    def analyze_and_adapt(self):
        """
        Analyze current distribution and adapt strategy if needed.
        """
        if not self.partition_stats:
            return
        
        # Calculate distribution metrics
        values = list(self.partition_stats.values())
        avg_freq = sum(values) / len(values)
        max_freq = max(values)
        skew = max_freq / avg_freq if avg_freq > 0 else 0
        
        # Adapt if skew exceeds threshold
        if skew > self.adaptation_threshold:
            self.adaptation_count += 1
            # Switch strategy
            self.current_strategy = 'modulo' if self.current_strategy == 'hash' else 'hash'
            print(f"Adapted partitioning strategy to: {self.current_strategy} "
                  f"(skew: {skew:.2f}x)")


# ==============================================================================
# PATTERN: TIME-BASED PARTITIONER
# ==============================================================================

class TimeBasedPartitioner(Partitioner):
    """
    Partitions data based on temporal characteristics.
    Useful for time-series data, event streams, and temporal analytics.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_partitions: int, time_unit: str = 'hour'):
        """
        Args:
            num_partitions: Number of partitions
            time_unit: Time granularity ('hour', 'day', 'week', 'month')
        """
        self._num_partitions = num_partitions
        self.time_unit = time_unit
    
    def numPartitions(self) -> int:
        return self._num_partitions
    
    def getPartition(self, key: Any) -> int:
        """
        Partition based on timestamp.
        
        Args:
            key: Can be timestamp, datetime object, or string date
            
        Returns:
            Partition number based on time unit
        """
        from datetime import datetime
        
        # Convert key to datetime
        if isinstance(key, datetime):
            dt = key
        elif isinstance(key, (int, float)):
            # Assume Unix timestamp
            dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(key)
        elif isinstance(key, str):
            # Try to parse string
            try:
                dt = datetime.fromisoformat(key)
            except:
                return 0
        else:
            return 0
        
        # Partition based on time unit
        if self.time_unit == 'hour':
            partition_key = dt.hour
        elif self.time_unit == 'day':
            partition_key = dt.day
        elif self.time_unit == 'week':
            partition_key = dt.isocalendar()[1]  # Week number
        elif self.time_unit == 'month':
            partition_key = dt.month
        else:
            partition_key = dt.hour
        
        return partition_key % self._num_partitions


# ==============================================================================
# PATTERN: WEIGHTED PARTITIONER
# ==============================================================================

class WeightedPartitioner(Partitioner):
    """
    Partitions data with weighted distribution for handling skewed datasets.
    Assigns more partitions to heavy keys.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_partitions: int, weight_map: dict = None):
        """
        Args:
            num_partitions: Number of partitions
            weight_map: Dictionary mapping keys to weights (higher = more partitions)
                       Example: {'hot_key': 3, 'normal_key': 1}
        """
        self._num_partitions = num_partitions
        self.weight_map = weight_map or {}
        self._build_partition_mapping()
    
    def _build_partition_mapping(self):
        """
        Build mapping of keys to partition ranges based on weights.
        """
        total_weight = sum(self.weight_map.values())
        
        self.key_partition_ranges = {}
        current_partition = 0
        
        for key, weight in self.weight_map.items():
            # Allocate partitions proportional to weight
            num_partitions_for_key = max(1, int(
                (weight / total_weight) * self._num_partitions
            ))
            
            self.key_partition_ranges[key] = (
                current_partition,
                min(current_partition + num_partitions_for_key, self._num_partitions)
            )
            current_partition += num_partitions_for_key
    
    def numPartitions(self) -> int:
        return self._num_partitions
    
    def getPartition(self, key: Any) -> int:
        """
        Partition based on key weights.
        
        Args:
            key: Key to partition
            
        Returns:
            Partition number considering weights
        """
        key_str = str(key)
        
        # Check if key has specific weight
        if key_str in self.key_partition_ranges:
            start, end = self.key_partition_ranges[key_str]
            # Distribute within allocated range
            return start + (abs(hash(key)) % (end - start))
        
        # Default partitioning for unweighted keys
        return abs(hash(key)) % self._num_partitions


# ==============================================================================
# PATTERN: CUSTOM BUSINESS LOGIC PARTITIONER
# ==============================================================================

class BusinessLogicPartitioner(Partitioner):
    """
    Partitioner that implements custom business rules.
    Example: VIP customers, premium products, priority orders.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_partitions: int, business_rules: dict = None):
        """
        Args:
            num_partitions: Number of partitions
            business_rules: Dictionary defining business logic
                Example: {
                    'vip_partition': 0,
                    'priority_partition': 1,
                    'standard_partition': 2
                }
        """
        self._num_partitions = num_partitions
        self.business_rules = business_rules or {}
    
    def numPartitions(self) -> int:
        return self._num_partitions
    
    def getPartition(self, key: Any) -> int:
        """
        Partition based on business logic.
        
        Args:
            key: Dictionary or tuple with business attributes
                 Example: {'customer_type': 'VIP', 'order_value': 1000}
            
        Returns:
            Partition number based on business rules
        """
        # Handle dictionary keys with business attributes
        if isinstance(key, dict):
            # VIP customers get dedicated partition
            if key.get('customer_type') == 'VIP':
                return self.business_rules.get('vip_partition', 0)
            
            # High-value orders get priority partition
            if key.get('order_value', 0) > 500:
                return self.business_rules.get('priority_partition', 1)
            
            # Standard processing
            return self.business_rules.get('standard_partition', 2)
        
        # Handle tuple keys (customer_type, order_value)
        if isinstance(key, tuple) and len(key) >= 2:
            customer_type, order_value = key[0], key[1]
            
            if customer_type == 'VIP':
                return self.business_rules.get('vip_partition', 0)
            elif order_value > 500:
                return self.business_rules.get('priority_partition', 1)
            else:
                return self.business_rules.get('standard_partition', 2)
        
        # Default
        return abs(hash(key)) % self._num_partitions

            'customer_id': random.randint(1, 1000),

            'category': random.choice(categories),
            'order_value': random.randint(10, 2000),
            'timestamp': base_time + timedelta(hours=random.randint(0, 168)),  # 1 week
            'region': random.choice(['NA', 'EU', 'APAC']),
            'priority': 'high' if tier == 'VIP' or random.random() < 0.1 else 'normal'
        }
        orders.append(order)
    
    print(f"Generated {len(orders)} orders")
    
    # =========================================================================
    # STAGE 1: Initial partitioning by customer tier (Business Logic)
    # =========================================================================
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("STAGE 1: Partitioning by Customer Tier")
    print("-"*60)
    
    business_rules = {
        'vip_partition': 0,
        'priority_partition': 1,
        'standard_partition': 2
    }
    
    # Create RDD with composite key
    order_rdd = sc.parallelize([
        (
            {
                'customer_type': order['customer_tier'],
                'order_value': order['order_value']
            },
            order
        )
        for order in orders
    ])
    
    tier_partitioner = BusinessLogicPartitioner(4, business_rules=business_rules)
    tier_partitioned = order_rdd.partitionBy(4, tier_partitioner)
    
    print("\nPartitioning by business logic (customer tier + order value)")
    
    # Analyze tier distribution
    tier_stats = tier_partitioned.mapPartitionsWithIndex(
        lambda idx, it: [(idx, list(it))]
    ).collect()
    
    for idx, items in tier_stats:
        if items:
            vip_count = sum(1 for k, v in items if v['customer_tier'] == 'VIP')
            premium_count = sum(1 for k, v in items if v['customer_tier'] == 'Premium')
            total_value = sum(v['order_value'] for k, v in items)
            
            print(f"Partition {idx}: {len(items)} orders")
            print(f"  VIP: {vip_count}, Premium: {premium_count}")
            print(f"  Total Value: ${total_value:,}")
    
    # =========================================================================
    # STAGE 2: Re-partition by region for geographic processing
    # =========================================================================
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("STAGE 2: Re-partitioning by Region")
    print("-"*60)
    
    region_map = {
        'NA': 0,
        'EU': 1,
        'APAC': 2
    }
    
    # Extract and re-partition by region
    region_rdd = tier_partitioned.map(lambda x: (x[1]['region'], x[1]))
    geo_partitioner = GeographicPartitioner(region_mapping=region_map, num_partitions=3)
    region_partitioned = region_rdd.partitionBy(3, geo_partitioner)
    
    print("\nRe-partitioned by geographic region")
    
    region_stats = region_partitioned.mapPartitionsWithIndex(
        lambda idx, it: [(idx, list(it))]
    ).collect()
    
    region_names = {0: 'NA', 1: 'EU', 2: 'APAC'}
    for idx, items in region_stats:
        if items:
            total_value = sum(v['order_value'] for k, v in items)
            categories_count = {}
            for k, v in items:
                cat = v['category']
                categories_count[cat] = categories_count.get(cat, 0) + 1
            
            print(f"Partition {idx} ({region_names[idx]}): {len(items)} orders")
            print(f"  Total Value: ${total_value:,}")
            print(f"  Top Categories: {sorted(categories_count.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:3]}")
    
    # =========================================================================
    # STAGE 3: Time-based partitioning for temporal analysis
    # =========================================================================
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("STAGE 3: Time-based Partitioning")
    print("-"*60)
    
    # Re-partition by timestamp
    time_rdd = sc.parallelize([
        (order['timestamp'], order) for order in orders
    ])
    
    time_partitioner = TimeBasedPartitioner(4, time_unit='day')
    time_partitioned = time_rdd.partitionBy(4, time_partitioner)
    
    print("\nPartitioned by day of month")
    
    time_stats = time_partitioned.mapPartitionsWithIndex(
        lambda idx, it: [(idx, list(it))]
    ).collect()
    
    for idx, items in time_stats:
        if items:
            dates = [v['timestamp'].date() for k, v in items]
            unique_dates = set(dates)
            total_value = sum(v['order_value'] for k, v in items)
            
            print(f"Partition {idx}: {len(items)} orders")
            print(f"  Date range: {min(unique_dates)} to {max(unique_dates)}")
            print(f"  Total Value: ${total_value:,}")
    
    # =========================================================================
    # STAGE 4: Performance metrics and optimization
    # =========================================================================
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("STAGE 4: Performance Analysis")
    print("-"*60)
    
    # Compare different partitioning strategies
    strategies = {
        'Business Logic': tier_partitioned,
        'Geographic': region_partitioned,
        'Time-based': time_partitioned
    }
    
    print("\nPartitioning Strategy Comparison:")
    print(f"{'Strategy':<20} {'Partitions':<12} {'Balance Score':<15} {'Recommendation'}")
    print("-" * 70)
    
    for name, rdd in strategies.items():
        partition_sizes = rdd.mapPartitions(lambda it: [sum(1 for _ in it)]).collect()
        avg = sum(partition_sizes) / len(partition_sizes) if partition_sizes else 0
        std_dev = (sum((s - avg) ** 2 for s in partition_sizes) / len(partition_sizes)) ** 0.5 if partition_sizes else 0
        balance = 100 * (1 - std_dev / avg) if avg > 0 else 0
        
        recommendation = "Excellent" if balance > 90 else "Good" if balance > 75 else "Needs tuning"
        
        print(f"{name:<20} {len(partition_sizes):<12} {balance:<15.2f} {recommendation}")
    
    # =========================================================================
    # STAGE 5: Final optimized pipeline
    # =========================================================================
    print("\n" + "-"*60)
    print("STAGE 5: Optimized Multi-Stage Pipeline")
    print("-"*60)
    
    print("""

# Example 1.1: Moving average of last 3 rows (including current)
window_rows_preceding = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("date") \
    .rowsBetween(-2, 0)  # 2 rows before current + current row

df_rows_pattern_1 = df.withColumn(
    "moving_avg_3rows",
    avg("amount").over(window_rows_preceding)
).withColumn(
    "rolling_sum_3rows",
    sum("amount").over(window_rows_preceding)
).withColumn(
    "count_rows_window",
    count("*").over(window_rows_preceding)
)

Description: Defines a window frame based on logical value ranges in the ORDER BY column.

# Example 2.1: Range-based window on amount values
# All rows where amount is within 100 of current row's amount
window_range_amount = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("amount") \
    .rangeBetween(-100, 100)  # Values within ±100 of current amount

df_range_pattern_1 = df.withColumn(
    "similar_price_count",
    count("*").over(window_range_amount)
).withColumn(
    "similar_price_avg",

)

print("\n2.1 Range-Based Window (Products within ±$100 price range)")

).orderBy("category", "amount").show(truncate=False)

# Example 2.2: Range with quantity ordering
window_range_quantity = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("quantity") \
    .rangeBetween(-1, 1)  # Quantities within ±1 of current

df_range_pattern_2 = df.withColumn(
    "similar_qty_sum",
    sum("amount").over(window_range_quantity)
).withColumn(
    "similar_qty_count",
    count("*").over(window_range_quantity)
)

print("\n2.2 Range-Based Window (Similar Quantities ±1)")

).orderBy("category", "quantity").show(truncate=False)

print("""
Description: Window starts from the first row of the partition and extends to a specified point.
Use Case: Running totals, cumulative sums, expanding window calculations.
""")

# Example 3.1: Running total from start to current row
window_unbounded_preceding = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("date") \
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)  # From start to current

df_unbounded_prec_1 = df.withColumn(
    "running_total",
    sum("amount").over(window_unbounded_preceding)
).withColumn(
    "running_avg",
    avg("amount").over(window_unbounded_preceding)
).withColumn(
    "cumulative_count",
    count("*").over(window_unbounded_preceding)
).withColumn(
    "running_max",
    max("amount").over(window_unbounded_preceding)
)

print("\n3.1 Running Totals and Cumulative Statistics")

# Example 3.2: Percentage of total so far
df_unbounded_prec_2 = df.withColumn(
    "running_total",
    sum("amount").over(window_unbounded_preceding)
).withColumn(
    "current_amount",
    col("amount")
).withColumn(
    "pct_of_running_total",
    (col("amount") / sum("amount").over(window_unbounded_preceding) * 100)
)

print("\n3.2 Percentage of Running Total")
df_unbounded_prec_2.select(
    "date", "category", "product", "amount",
    "running_total", "pct_of_running_total"
).show(truncate=False)

# Example 3.3: First value in partition (using unbounded preceding)
window_first_value = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("date") \
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.unboundedFollowing)

df_unbounded_prec_3 = df.withColumn(
    "first_product",
    first("product").over(window_unbounded_preceding)
).withColumn(
    "first_amount",
    first("amount").over(window_unbounded_preceding)
).withColumn(
    "diff_from_first",
    col("amount") - first("amount").over(window_unbounded_preceding)
)

print("\n3.3 Comparison with First Value in Partition")
df_unbounded_prec_3.select(
    "date", "category", "product", "amount",
    "first_product", "first_amount", "diff_from_first"
).show(truncate=False)

print("\n" + "=" * 100)
print("PATTERN 4: UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING PATTERN")

print("""
Description: Window starts from a specified point and extends to the last row of the partition.

# Example 4.1: Remaining sum from current to end
window_unbounded_following = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("date") \
    .rowsBetween(0, Window.unboundedFollowing)  # Current to end

df_unbounded_foll_1 = df.withColumn(
    "remaining_sum",
    sum("amount").over(window_unbounded_following)
).withColumn(
    "remaining_count",

).show(truncate=False)

# Example 4.2: Last value in partition

    "last_product",

    "last_amount",

print("\n4.2 Comparison with Last Value in Partition")
df_unbounded_foll_2.select(
    "date", "category", "product", "amount",
    "last_product", "last_amount", "diff_from_last"
).show(truncate=False)

# Example 4.3: Future maximum value
df_unbounded_foll_3 = df.withColumn(
    "future_max",
    max("amount").over(window_unbounded_following)
).withColumn(

    col("amount") < max("amount").over(window_unbounded_following)

print("\n4.3 Future Maximum Value")

# Example 5.3: Lag and Lead (relative to current row)
window_ordered = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("date")

df_current_row_3 = df.withColumn(
    "prev_amount",
    lag("amount", 1).over(window_ordered)
).withColumn(

).withColumn(
    "current_amount",
    col("amount")
).withColumn(

    col("amount") - lag("amount", 1).over(window_ordered)
)

print("\n5.3 Lag and Lead (Relative to Current Row)")
df_current_row_3.select(
    "date", "category", "product",

).show(truncate=False)

```python
# =============================================================================
# COMBINED PATTERNS EXAMPLE
# =============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 100)
print("COMBINED PATTERNS EXAMPLE - Real-World Use Case")
print("=" * 100)
print("""
Description: Combining multiple window frame patterns for comprehensive analysis.
Use Case: Sales analysis with multiple perspectives.
""")

# Define multiple windows for different analyses
window_running = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("date") \
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)

window_remaining = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("date") \
    .rowsBetween(0, Window.unboundedFollowing)

window_moving_3 = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("date") \
    .rowsBetween(-2, 0)

window_full_partition = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("date") \
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.unboundedFollowing)

window_lag_lead = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("date")

# Apply all patterns together
df_combined = df \
    .withColumn("running_total", sum("amount").over(window_running)) \
    .withColumn("remaining_total", sum("amount").over(window_remaining)) \
    .withColumn("category_total", sum("amount").over(window_full_partition)) \
    .withColumn("moving_avg_3", avg("amount").over(window_moving_3)) \
    .withColumn("prev_amount", lag("amount", 1).over(window_lag_lead)) \
    .withColumn("next_amount", lead("amount", 1).over(window_lag_lead)) \
    .withColumn("pct_of_category", 
                (col("amount") / sum("amount").over(window_full_partition) * 100)) \
    .withColumn("pct_complete", 
                (sum("amount").over(window_running) / 
                 sum("amount").over(window_full_partition) * 100)) \
    .withColumn("rank_in_category", 
                rank().over(Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy(col("amount").desc())))

print("\nComprehensive Sales Analysis Using All Window Patterns")
df_combined.select(
    "date", "category", "product", "amount",
    "running_total", "remaining_total", "category_total",
    "moving_avg_3", "pct_of_category", "pct_complete", "rank_in_category"
).show(truncate=False)

# WINDOW FRAME SPECIFICATIONS SUMMARY
