print("\n" + "=" * 100)
print("WINDOW FRAME SPECIFICATIONS - COMPLETE REFERENCE")
print("=" * 100)

summary_text = """
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    WINDOW FRAME PATTERN SUMMARY                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                              │
│ 1. ROWS BETWEEN                                                              │
│    - Based on physical row positions                                         │
│    - Syntax: .rowsBetween(start, end)                                        │
│    - Examples:                                                               │
│      • rowsBetween(-2, 0)           → Last 3 rows (2 before + current)      │
│      • rowsBetween(0, 2)            → Next 3 rows (current + 2 after)       │
│      • rowsBetween(-1, 1)           → Centered window (1 before + curr + 1) │
│    - Use Case: Fixed-size moving windows, k-nearest neighbors               │
│                                                                              │
│ 2. RANGE BETWEEN                                                             │
│    - Based on logical value ranges in ORDER BY column                        │
│    - Syntax: .rangeBetween(start, end)                                       │
│    - Examples:                                                               │
│      • rangeBetween(-100, 100)      → Values within ±100 of current         │
│      • rangeBetween(-86400, 0)      → Last 24 hours (if ordering by epoch)  │
│    - Use Case: Time-based windows, value-based grouping                      │
│    - Note: Includes ALL rows with matching ORDER BY values (handles ties)    │
│                                                                              │
│ 3. UNBOUNDED PRECEDING                                                       │
│    - From the first row of partition to specified point                      │
│    - Syntax: Window.unboundedPreceding                                       │
│    - Examples:                                                               │
│      • rowsBetween(unboundedPreceding, 0)     → Running total               │
│      • rowsBetween(unboundedPreceding, -1)    → Total up to previous row    │
│    - Use Case: Cumulative sums, running averages, YTD calculations           │
│                                                                              │
│ 4. UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING                                                       │
│    - From specified point to the last row of partition                       │
│    - Syntax: Window.unboundedFollowing                                       │
│    - Examples:                                                               │
│      • rowsBetween(0, unboundedFollowing)     → Remaining total             │
│      • rowsBetween(1, unboundedFollowing)     → Future values only          │
│    - Use Case: Reverse running totals, remaining balances                    │
│                                                                              │
│ 5. CURRENT ROW                                                               │
│    - Only the current row in the window                                      │
│    - Syntax: Window.currentRow or rowsBetween(currentRow, currentRow)       │
│    - Examples:                                                               │
│      • rowsBetween(currentRow, currentRow)    → Single row frame            │

│                                                                              │
│ SPECIAL COMBINATIONS:                                                        │
│    • rowsBetween(unboundedPreceding, unboundedFollowing) → Entire partition │
│    • rangeBetween(unboundedPreceding, currentRow)        → Running range    │
│    • rowsBetween(currentRow, unboundedFollowing)         → Current to end   │
│                                                                              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

w_moving_3 = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy("order_date") \
    .rowsBetween(-2, 0)

w_customer_order = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy("order_date")

# Apply comprehensive window analysis
ecommerce_analysis = ecommerce_df \
    .filter(col("status") == "completed") \
    .withColumn("order_number", row_number().over(w_customer_order)) \
    .withColumn("customer_running_total", sum("amount").over(w_customer_running)) \
    .withColumn("customer_lifetime_value", sum("amount").over(w_customer_full)) \
    .withColumn("customer_avg_order", avg("amount").over(w_customer_running)) \
    .withColumn("moving_avg_3_orders", avg("amount").over(w_moving_3)) \
    .withColumn("category_running_total", sum("amount").over(w_category_running)) \
    .withColumn("prev_order_amount", lag("amount", 1).over(w_customer_order)) \
    .withColumn("next_order_amount", lead("amount", 1).over(w_customer_order)) \
    .withColumn("days_since_last_order", 
                unix_timestamp(col("order_date")) - 
                unix_timestamp(lag("order_date", 1).over(w_customer_order))) \

# ADVANCED PATTERN: Session Windows with Gaps
# =============================================================================
print("\n" + "=" * 100)
print("ADVANCED PATTERN: Detecting Session Boundaries with Time Gaps")
print("=" * 100)

# Create data with time gaps to identify sessions
session_gap_data = [
    ("U001", "2024-01-01 10:00:00", "click"),
    ("U001", "2024-01-01 10:02:00", "click"),
    ("U001", "2024-01-01 10:05:00", "click"),
    ("U001", "2024-01-01 10:35:00", "click"),  # 30-min gap - new session
    ("U001", "2024-01-01 10:37:00", "click"),
    ("U001", "2024-01-01 11:15:00", "click"),  # 38-min gap - new session
]

session_gap_df = spark.createDataFrame(session_gap_data, ["user_id", "timestamp_str", "action"]) \
    .withColumn("timestamp", to_timestamp(col("timestamp_str"))) \
    .withColumn("timestamp_numeric", unix_timestamp(col("timestamp")))

w_user_order = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("timestamp")

# Calculate time since previous action
session_with_gaps = session_gap_df \
    .withColumn("prev_timestamp", 
                lag("timestamp_numeric", 1).over(w_user_order)) \
    .withColumn("seconds_since_last", 
                col("timestamp_numeric") - col("prev_timestamp")) \
    .withColumn("is_new_session", 
                (col("seconds_since_last") > 1800) | col("seconds_since_last").isNull())

# Assign session IDs using cumulative sum
from pyspark.sql.functions import when

w_user_cumulative = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("timestamp") \
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)

session_with_ids = session_with_gaps \
    .withColumn("session_flag", 
                when(col("is_new_session"), 1).otherwise(0)) \
    .withColumn("session_id", 
                sum("session_flag").over(w_user_cumulative))

# Analyze each session
w_session = Window.partitionBy("user_id", "session_id").orderBy("timestamp") \
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.unboundedFollowing)

w_session_running = Window.partitionBy("user_id", "session_id").orderBy("timestamp") \
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)

session_analysis = session_with_ids \
    .withColumn("action_in_session", row_number().over(
        Window.partitionBy("user_id", "session_id").orderBy("timestamp"))) \
    .withColumn("session_length_actions", count("*").over(w_session)) \
    .withColumn("session_start", first("timestamp").over(w_session)) \
    .withColumn("session_end", last("timestamp").over(w_session)) \
    .withColumn("session_duration_seconds", 
                unix_timestamp(last("timestamp").over(w_session)) - 
                unix_timestamp(first("timestamp").over(w_session)))

print("\nSession Detection with 30-minute Timeout:")
session_analysis.select(
    "user_id", "timestamp", "action", "session_id",
    "action_in_session", "session_length_actions", "session_duration_seconds",
    "seconds_since_last", "is_new_session"
).show(truncate=False)

# Time series data for rate of change analysis
timeseries_data = [
    ("Product_A", "2024-01", 1000),
    ("Product_A", "2024-02", 1200),
    ("Product_A", "2024-03", 1150),
    ("Product_A", "2024-04", 1400),
    ("Product_A", "2024-05", 1350),
    ("Product_B", "2024-01", 500),
    ("Product_B", "2024-02", 550),
    ("Product_B", "2024-03", 600),
    ("Product_B", "2024-04", 580),
    ("Product_B", "2024-05", 650),
]

timeseries_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    timeseries_data, 
    ["product", "month", "sales"]
)

w_product_time = Window.partitionBy("product").orderBy("month")
w_product_running = Window.partitionBy("product").orderBy("month") \
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)

rate_of_change = timeseries_df \
    .withColumn("prev_month_sales", lag("sales", 1).over(w_product_time)) \
    .withColumn("next_month_sales", lead("sales", 1).over(w_product_time)) \
    .withColumn("month_over_month_change", 
                col("sales") - lag("sales", 1).over(w_product_time)) \
    .withColumn("month_over_month_pct", 
                ((col("sales") - lag("sales", 1).over(w_product_time)) / 
                 lag("sales", 1).over(w_product_time) * 100)) \
    .withColumn("cumulative_growth", 
                col("sales") - first("sales").over(w_product_running)) \
    .withColumn("cumulative_growth_pct", 
                ((col("sales") - first("sales").over(w_product_running)) / 
                 first("sales").over(w_product_running) * 100)) \
    .withColumn("avg_sales_so_far", avg("sales").over(w_product_running)) \
    .withColumn("is_above_avg", col("sales") > col("avg_sales_so_far")) \
    .withColumn("max_sales_so_far", max("sales").over(w_product_running)) \
    .withColumn("is_new_high", col("sales") >= col("max_sales_so_far"))

print("\nRate of Change and Growth Analysis:")
rate_of_change.select(
    "product", "month", "sales", "prev_month_sales",
    "month_over_month_change", "month_over_month_pct",
    "cumulative_growth_pct", "is_new_high"
).show(truncate=False)

# Data with gaps (NULLs)
sparse_data = [
    ("Sensor_1", "2024-01-01 10:00:00", 23.5),
    ("Sensor_1", "2024-01-01 10:05:00", None),
    ("Sensor_1", "2024-01-01 10:10:00", None),
    ("Sensor_1", "2024-01-01 10:15:00", 24.1),
    ("Sensor_1", "2024-01-01 10:20:00", None),
    ("Sensor_1", "2024-01-01 10:25:00", 23.8),
]

sparse_df = spark.createDataFrame(
    sparse_data, 
    ["sensor_id", "timestamp_str", "temperature"]
).withColumn("timestamp", to_timestamp(col("timestamp_str")))

w_sensor = Window.partitionBy("sensor_id").orderBy("timestamp") \
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)

# Forward fill (carry last valid observation forward)
from pyspark.sql.functions import last

sparse_filled = sparse_df \
    .withColumn("last_valid_temp", 
                last("temperature", ignorenulls=True).over(w_sensor)) \
    .withColumn("forward_filled", 
                when(col("temperature").isNull(), col("last_valid_temp"))
                .otherwise(col("temperature"))) \
    .withColumn("has_reading", col("temperature").isNotNull()) \
    .withColumn("readings_so_far", 
                count(when(col("temperature").isNotNull(), 1)).over(w_sensor))

print("\nForward Fill (Last Observation Carried Forward):")
sparse_filled.select(
    "sensor_id", "timestamp", "temperature", 
    "last_valid_temp", "forward_filled", "readings_so_far"
).show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
# 1. RUNTIME STATISTICS PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Runtime Statistics Pattern: Collects and analyzes runtime statistics to optimize
query execution and resource allocation dynamically.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from datetime import datetime
import time

class RuntimeStatisticsPattern:
    """
    Monitors and collects runtime statistics for query optimization.
    Tracks execution time, data skew, partition sizes, and resource usage.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.statistics_schema = StructType([
            StructField("query_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("start_time", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("end_time", TimestampType(), True),
            StructField("duration_ms", LongType(), True),
            StructField("rows_processed", LongType(), True),
            StructField("partitions_read", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("data_size_mb", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("shuffle_read_mb", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("shuffle_write_mb", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("cpu_time_ms", LongType(), True)
        ])
        
    def collect_statistics(self, df, query_id: str):
        """
        Collects runtime statistics for a given DataFrame operation.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            query_id: Unique identifier for the query
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (result DataFrame, statistics DataFrame)
        """
        start_time = datetime.now()
        start_ms = time.time() * 1000
        
        # Execute the query and collect metrics
        df.cache()
        row_count = df.count()
        
        # Get partition information
        num_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        # Collect partition sizes for skew detection
        partition_sizes = df.rdd.mapPartitions(
            lambda it: [sum(1 for _ in it)]
        ).collect()
        
        end_time = datetime.now()
        end_ms = time.time() * 1000
        duration = end_ms - start_ms
        
        # Calculate statistics
        avg_partition_size = sum(partition_sizes) / len(partition_sizes)
        max_partition_size = max(partition_sizes)
        min_partition_size = min(partition_sizes)
        skew_ratio = max_partition_size / avg_partition_size if avg_partition_size > 0 else 0
        
        # Create statistics record
        stats_data = [(
            query_id,
            start_time,
            end_time,
            int(duration),
            row_count,
            num_partitions,
            0.0,  # Placeholder for data size
            0.0,  # Placeholder for shuffle read
            0.0,  # Placeholder for shuffle write
            int(duration)  # Approximation for CPU time
        )]
        
        stats_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(stats_data, self.statistics_schema)
        
        # Add derived metrics
        stats_df = stats_df.withColumn("throughput_rows_per_sec", 
                                       col("rows_processed") / (col("duration_ms") / 1000))
        stats_df = stats_df.withColumn("avg_partition_size", lit(avg_partition_size))
        stats_df = stats_df.withColumn("skew_ratio", lit(skew_ratio))
        
        return df, stats_df
    
    def analyze_statistics(self, stats_df):
        """
        Analyzes collected statistics to provide optimization recommendations.
        """
        recommendations = []
        
        # Analyze each query's statistics
        stats_list = stats_df.collect()
        
        for stat in stats_list:
            query_id = stat['query_id']
            
            # Check for slow queries
            if stat['duration_ms'] > 60000:  # > 1 minute
                recommendations.append({
                    'query_id': query_id,
                    'issue': 'SLOW_QUERY',
                    'recommendation': 'Consider partitioning or filtering data earlier'
                })
            
            # Check for data skew
            if hasattr(stat, 'skew_ratio') and stat['skew_ratio'] > 2.0:
                recommendations.append({
                    'query_id': query_id,
                    'issue': 'DATA_SKEW',
                    'recommendation': 'Apply salting or custom partitioning strategy'
                })
            
            # Check for low throughput
            if stat['throughput_rows_per_sec'] < 1000:
                recommendations.append({
                    'query_id': query_id,
                    'issue': 'LOW_THROUGHPUT',
                    'recommendation': 'Increase parallelism or optimize transformations'
                })
        
        return recommendations

# 2. DYNAMIC COST MODEL PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Dynamic Cost Model Pattern: Adjusts cost estimates based on actual execution
patterns and system load. Adapts resource allocation dynamically.
"""

class DynamicCostModelPattern:
    """
    Implements dynamic cost modeling that adjusts based on runtime conditions.
    Considers CPU, memory, I/O, and network costs dynamically.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_costs = {
            'cpu_cost_per_row': 0.001,
            'memory_cost_per_mb': 0.01,
            'io_cost_per_mb': 0.05,
            'network_cost_per_mb': 0.02,
            'shuffle_cost_multiplier': 2.0
        }
        self.adjustment_factors = {
            'cpu': 1.0,
            'memory': 1.0,
            'io': 1.0,
            'network': 1.0
        }
        
    def estimate_operation_cost(self, operation_type: str, data_size_mb: float, 
                               row_count: int, is_shuffle: bool = False):
        """
        Estimates the cost of an operation using dynamic cost model.
        
        Args:
            operation_type: Type of operation (scan, join, aggregate, etc.)
            data_size_mb: Size of data in MB
            row_count: Number of rows
            is_shuffle: Whether operation involves shuffle
            
        Returns:
            Estimated cost value
        """
        # Base costs
        cpu_cost = row_count * self.base_costs['cpu_cost_per_row'] * self.adjustment_factors['cpu']
        memory_cost = data_size_mb * self.base_costs['memory_cost_per_mb'] * self.adjustment_factors['memory']
        io_cost = data_size_mb * self.base_costs['io_cost_per_mb'] * self.adjustment_factors['io']
        
        # Operation-specific costs
        operation_multiplier = {
            'scan': 1.0,
            'filter': 1.2,
            'join': 3.0,
            'aggregate': 2.5,
            'sort': 2.0,
            'window': 3.5
        }.get(operation_type, 1.0)
        
        total_cost = (cpu_cost + memory_cost + io_cost) * operation_multiplier
        
        # Add shuffle cost if applicable
        if is_shuffle:
            shuffle_cost = data_size_mb * self.base_costs['network_cost_per_mb'] * \
                          self.base_costs['shuffle_cost_multiplier'] * \
                          self.adjustment_factors['network']
            total_cost += shuffle_cost
        
        return total_cost
    
    def adjust_cost_model(self, actual_duration: float, estimated_cost: float):
        """
        Adjusts cost model based on actual vs estimated performance.
        Uses feedback to improve future estimates.
        """
        # Calculate adjustment ratio
        if estimated_cost > 0:
            adjustment_ratio = actual_duration / estimated_cost
            
            # Gradually adjust factors (learning rate = 0.1)
            learning_rate = 0.1
            
            # Update all adjustment factors proportionally
            for factor in self.adjustment_factors:
                current = self.adjustment_factors[factor]
                self.adjustment_factors[factor] = current * (1 - learning_rate) + \
                                                 (current * adjustment_ratio * learning_rate)
    
    def optimize_join_strategy(self, left_df, right_df, join_key: str):
        """
        Dynamically selects optimal join strategy based on cost estimates.
        """
        # Estimate sizes
        left_count = left_df.count()
        right_count = right_df.count()
        
        # Estimate data sizes (approximate)
        left_size_mb = left_count * 0.001  # Rough estimate
        right_size_mb = right_count * 0.001
        
        # Calculate costs for different join strategies
        broadcast_cost = self.estimate_operation_cost(
            'join', min(left_size_mb, right_size_mb), 
            left_count + right_count, is_shuffle=False
        )
        
        shuffle_cost = self.estimate_operation_cost(
            'join', left_size_mb + right_size_mb,
            left_count + right_count, is_shuffle=True
        )
        
        # Choose strategy based on cost
        if broadcast_cost < shuffle_cost and min(left_size_mb, right_size_mb) < 100:
            # Use broadcast join
            if left_size_mb < right_size_mb:
                result = right_df.join(broadcast(left_df), join_key)
            else:
                result = left_df.join(broadcast(right_df), join_key)
            strategy = "broadcast"
        else:
            # Use shuffle join
            result = left_df.join(right_df, join_key)
            strategy = "shuffle"
        
        return result, strategy, min(broadcast_cost, shuffle_cost)

# ============================================================================
"""
Feedback-Based Costing Pattern: Uses actual execution results to refine
cost estimates through continuous feedback loops.
"""

class FeedbackBasedCostingPattern:
    """
    Implements feedback-based cost estimation that learns from actual executions.
    Maintains a history of estimates vs actuals for continuous improvement.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.feedback_schema = StructType([
            StructField("operation_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("operation_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("estimated_cost", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("actual_cost", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("estimation_error", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("input_size_mb", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("output_size_mb", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("row_count", LongType(), False),
            StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False)
        ])
        
        # Initialize feedback history
        self.feedback_history = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            [], self.feedback_schema
        )
        
    def record_feedback(self, operation_id: str, operation_type: str,
                       estimated_cost: float, actual_cost: float,
                       input_size_mb: float, output_size_mb: float,
                       row_count: int):
        """
        Records feedback from an executed operation.
        """
        estimation_error = abs(actual_cost - estimated_cost) / actual_cost \
                          if actual_cost > 0 else 0.0
        
        feedback_record = [(
            operation_id,
            operation_type,
            estimated_cost,
            actual_cost,
            estimation_error,
            input_size_mb,
            output_size_mb,
            row_count,
            datetime.now()
        )]
        
        new_feedback = self.spark.createDataFrame(feedback_record, self.feedback_schema)
        self.feedback_history = self.feedback_history.union(new_feedback)
        
    def get_refined_estimate(self, operation_type: str, input_size_mb: float,
                            row_count: int):
        """
        Provides refined cost estimate based on historical feedback.
        Uses weighted average of similar past operations.
        """
        # Filter similar operations
        similar_ops = self.feedback_history.filter(
            col("operation_type") == operation_type
        )
        
        if similar_ops.count() == 0:
            # No history, return base estimate
            return input_size_mb * 10.0  # Simple baseline
        
        # Calculate similarity-weighted estimate
        # Weight by recency and input size similarity
        similar_ops = similar_ops.withColumn(
            "size_similarity",
            1.0 / (1.0 + abs(col("input_size_mb") - input_size_mb))
        ).withColumn(
            "recency_weight",
            datediff(lit(datetime.now()), col("timestamp"))
        ).withColumn(
            "weight",
            col("size_similarity") / (1.0 + col("recency_weight") / 30.0)
        )
        
        # Calculate weighted average of actual costs
        weighted_sum = similar_ops.agg(
            sum(col("actual_cost") * col("weight")).alias("weighted_cost_sum"),
            sum(col("weight")).alias("weight_sum")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        if weighted_sum['weight_sum'] > 0:
            refined_estimate = weighted_sum['weighted_cost_sum'] / weighted_sum['weight_sum']
        else:
            refined_estimate = input_size_mb * 10.0
        
        return refined_estimate
    
    def analyze_estimation_accuracy(self):
        """
        Analyzes the accuracy of cost estimations over time.
        """
        if self.feedback_history.count() == 0:
            return None
        
        accuracy_metrics = self.feedback_history.groupBy("operation_type").agg(
            avg("estimation_error").alias("avg_error"),
            stddev("estimation_error").alias("std_error"),
            count("*").alias("sample_count"),
            avg("actual_cost").alias("avg_actual_cost"),
            avg("estimated_cost").alias("avg_estimated_cost")
        )
        
        # Calculate overall accuracy
        accuracy_metrics = accuracy_metrics.withColumn(
            "accuracy_percentage",
            (1.0 - col("avg_error")) * 100
        )
        
        return accuracy_metrics
    
    def adaptive_query_execution(self, df, operations: list):
        """
        Executes a series of operations with adaptive cost-based optimization.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            operations: List of operation dictionaries with 'type' and 'params'
        """
        result_df = df
        total_estimated_cost = 0.0
        total_actual_cost = 0.0
        
        for idx, op in enumerate(operations):
            operation_id = f"op_{idx}_{op['type']}"
            
            # Get current data size estimate
            current_count = result_df.count()
            current_size_mb = current_count * 0.001
            
            # Get refined estimate
            estimated_cost = self.get_refined_estimate(
                op['type
```python
                op['type'],
                current_size_mb,
                current_count
            )
            
            total_estimated_cost += estimated_cost
            
            # Execute operation and measure actual cost
            start_time = time.time()
            
            if op['type'] == 'filter':
                result_df = result_df.filter(op['params']['condition'])
            elif op['type'] == 'aggregate':
                result_df = result_df.groupBy(op['params']['group_by']).agg(
                    op['params']['aggregations']
                )
            elif op['type'] == 'join':
                result_df = result_df.join(
                    op['params']['right_df'],
                    op['params']['join_key']
                )
            elif op['type'] == 'sort':
                result_df = result_df.orderBy(op['params']['sort_columns'])
            
            end_time = time.time()
            actual_cost = (end_time - start_time) * 1000  # Convert to ms
            total_actual_cost += actual_cost
            
            # Record feedback
            output_count = result_df.count()
            output_size_mb = output_count * 0.001
            
            self.record_feedback(
                operation_id,
                op['type'],
                estimated_cost,
                actual_cost,
                current_size_mb,
                output_size_mb,
                current_count
            )
        
        return result_df, total_estimated_cost, total_actual_cost

# 4. HISTORICAL COST PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Historical Cost Pattern: Maintains comprehensive historical data about query
execution costs and uses it for future planning and optimization.
"""

class HistoricalCostPattern:
    """
    Tracks and analyzes historical execution costs to predict future costs
    and optimize resource allocation.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, history_path: str = None):
        self.spark = spark
        self.history_path = history_path or "/tmp/cost_history"
        
        self.history_schema = StructType([
            StructField("execution_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("query_hash", StringType(), False),
            StructField("query_pattern", StringType(), False),
            StructField("execution_time_ms", LongType(), False),
            StructField("cpu_time_ms", LongType(), False),
            StructField("memory_peak_mb", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("input_size_mb", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("output_size_mb", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("shuffle_size_mb", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("num_tasks", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("num_stages", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("cluster_size", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("execution_date", DateType(), False),
            StructField("execution_timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("success", BooleanType(), False),
            StructField("error_message", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        # Try to load existing history
        try:
            self.cost_history = self.spark.read.parquet(self.history_path)
        except:
            self.cost_history = self.spark.createDataFrame([], self.history_schema)
    
    def record_execution(self, execution_id: str, query_hash: str,
                        query_pattern: str, execution_metrics: dict,
                        success: bool = True, error_message: str = None):
        """
        Records a query execution in the historical database.
        """
        execution_record = [(
            execution_id,
            query_hash,
            query_pattern,
            execution_metrics.get('execution_time_ms', 0),
            execution_metrics.get('cpu_time_ms', 0),
            execution_metrics.get('memory_peak_mb', 0.0),
            execution_metrics.get('input_size_mb', 0.0),
            execution_metrics.get('output_size_mb', 0.0),
            execution_metrics.get('shuffle_size_mb', 0.0),
            execution_metrics.get('num_tasks', 0),
            execution_metrics.get('num_stages', 0),
            execution_metrics.get('cluster_size', 1),
            datetime.now().date(),
            datetime.now(),
            success,
            error_message
        )]
        
        new_record = self.spark.createDataFrame(execution_record, self.history_schema)
        self.cost_history = self.cost_history.union(new_record)
    
    def persist_history(self):
        """
        Persists the cost history to storage.
        """
        self.cost_history.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(self.history_path)
    
    def predict_cost(self, query_pattern: str, input_size_mb: float,
                    cluster_size: int = None):
        """
        Predicts execution cost based on historical data.
        
        Uses linear regression on similar historical queries.
        """
        # Filter similar query patterns
        similar_queries = self.cost_history.filter(
            (col("query_pattern") == query_pattern) &
            (col("success") == True)
        )
        
        if cluster_size:
            similar_queries = similar_queries.filter(
                col("cluster_size") == cluster_size
            )
        
        if similar_queries.count() < 3:
            # Not enough history, return conservative estimate
            return {
                'estimated_time_ms': input_size_mb * 1000,
                'confidence': 'low',
                'sample_size': similar_queries.count()
            }
        
        # Simple linear regression: time ~ input_size
        from pyspark.ml.regression import LinearRegression
        from pyspark.ml.feature import VectorAssembler
        
        # Prepare features
        assembler = VectorAssembler(
            inputCols=["input_size_mb"],
            outputCol="features"
        )
        
        training_data = assembler.transform(similar_queries).select(
            col("features"),
            col("execution_time_ms").alias("label")
        )
        
        # Train linear regression model
        lr = LinearRegression(maxIter=10, regParam=0.3, elasticNetParam=0.8)
        model = lr.fit(training_data)
        
        # Make prediction
        test_data = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            [(input_size_mb,)],
            ["input_size_mb"]
        )
        test_data = assembler.transform(test_data)
        
        prediction = model.transform(test_data).select("prediction").collect()[0][0]
        
        # Calculate confidence based on R-squared and sample size
        r_squared = model.summary.r2
        sample_size = similar_queries.count()
        
        confidence = 'high' if r_squared > 0.8 and sample_size > 10 else \
                    'medium' if r_squared > 0.5 and sample_size > 5 else 'low'
        
        return {
            'estimated_time_ms': max(0, prediction),
            'confidence': confidence,
            'r_squared': r_squared,
            'sample_size': sample_size,
            'model_coefficients': model.coefficients.toArray().tolist()
        }
    
    def analyze_cost_trends(self, query_pattern: str = None, days: int = 30):
        """
        Analyzes cost trends over time for optimization insights.
        """
        # Filter by date range
        cutoff_date = datetime.now().date()
        from datetime import timedelta
        start_date = cutoff_date - timedelta(days=days)
        
        trend_data = self.cost_history.filter(
            col("execution_date") >= lit(start_date)
        )
        
        if query_pattern:
            trend_data = trend_data.filter(col("query_pattern") == query_pattern)
        
        # Calculate daily statistics
        daily_stats = trend_data.groupBy("execution_date", "query_pattern").agg(
            avg("execution_time_ms").alias("avg_time_ms"),
            avg("memory_peak_mb").alias("avg_memory_mb"),
            avg("shuffle_size_mb").alias("avg_shuffle_mb"),
            count("*").alias("execution_count"),
            sum(when(col("success") == True, 1).otherwise(0)).alias("success_count")
        ).withColumn(
            "success_rate",
            col("success_count") / col("execution_count") * 100
        ).orderBy("execution_date")
        
        return daily_stats
    
    def get_optimization_recommendations(self, query_pattern: str):
        """
        Provides optimization recommendations based on historical analysis.
        """
        recommendations = []
        
        # Analyze historical executions
        pattern_history = self.cost_history.filter(
            col("query_pattern") == query_pattern
        )
        
        if pattern_history.count() == 0:
            return ["No historical data available for this query pattern"]
        
        # Calculate statistics
        stats = pattern_history.agg(
            avg("execution_time_ms").alias("avg_time"),
            avg("memory_peak_mb").alias("avg_memory"),
            avg("shuffle_size_mb").alias("avg_shuffle"),
            avg("num_tasks").alias("avg_tasks"),
            (sum(when(col("success") == True, 1).otherwise(0)) / count("*") * 100).alias("success_rate")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        # Generate recommendations
        if stats['avg_shuffle'] > 1000:  # > 1GB shuffle
            recommendations.append({
                'type': 'SHUFFLE_OPTIMIZATION',
                'severity': 'HIGH',
                'message': f'High shuffle size detected ({stats["avg_shuffle"]:.2f} MB). '
                          'Consider repartitioning or using broadcast joins.',
                'metric_value': stats['avg_shuffle']
            })
        
        if stats['avg_memory'] > 5000:  # > 5GB memory
            recommendations.append({
                'type': 'MEMORY_OPTIMIZATION',
                'severity': 'MEDIUM',
                'message': f'High memory usage ({stats["avg_memory"]:.2f} MB). '
                          'Consider processing data in smaller batches or increasing executor memory.',
                'metric_value': stats['avg_memory']
            })
        
        if stats['success_rate'] < 90:
            recommendations.append({
                'type': 'RELIABILITY',
                'severity': 'HIGH',
                'message': f'Low success rate ({stats["success_rate"]:.2f}%). '
                          'Review error logs and add retry logic or error handling.',
                'metric_value': stats['success_rate']
            })
        
        if stats['avg_time'] > 300000:  # > 5 minutes
            recommendations.append({
                'type': 'PERFORMANCE',
                'severity': 'MEDIUM',
                'message': f'Long execution time ({stats["avg_time"]/1000:.2f} seconds). '
                          'Consider adding indexes, partitioning, or caching intermediate results.',
                'metric_value': stats['avg_time']
            })
        
        return recommendations


# ============================================================================
# 5. MACHINE LEARNING COST PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Machine Learning Cost Pattern: Uses ML models to predict query costs and
optimize execution plans based on learned patterns.
"""

from pyspark.ml.regression import RandomForestRegressor, GBTRegressor
from pyspark.ml.feature import VectorAssembler, StandardScaler
from pyspark.ml.evaluation import RegressionEvaluator
from pyspark.ml import Pipeline

class MachineLearningCostPattern:
    """
    Implements ML-based cost prediction using various regression models.
    Continuously learns from execution data to improve predictions.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.model = None
        self.scaler = None
        self.feature_columns = [
            "input_rows",
            "input_size_mb",
            "num_columns",
            "num_partitions",
            "cluster_cores",
            "executor_memory_mb",
            "has_shuffle",
            "has_join",
            "has_aggregate",
            "has_window",
            "complexity_score"
        ]
        
        self.training_schema = StructType([
            StructField("query_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("input_rows", LongType(), False),
            StructField("input_size_mb", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("num_columns", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("num_partitions", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("cluster_cores", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("executor_memory_mb", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("has_shuffle", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("has_join", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("has_aggregate", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("has_window", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("complexity_score", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("actual_execution_time_ms", DoubleType(), False)
        ])
        
        self.training_data = self.spark.createDataFrame([], self.training_schema)
    
    def extract_features(self, df, query_metadata: dict):
        """
        Extracts features from a DataFrame and query metadata for ML prediction.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            query_metadata: Dictionary containing query characteristics
            
        Returns:
            Feature dictionary
        """
        # Get DataFrame statistics
        num_rows = df.count()
        num_cols = len(df.columns)
        num_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        # Estimate data size (rough approximation)
        estimated_size_mb = num_rows * num_cols * 0.001
        
        # Extract query characteristics from metadata
        features = {
            'input_rows': num_rows,
            'input_size_mb': estimated_size_mb,
            'num_columns': num_cols,
            'num_partitions': num_partitions,
            'cluster_cores': query_metadata.get('cluster_cores', 4),
            'executor_memory_mb': query_metadata.get('executor_memory_mb', 4096),
            'has_shuffle': 1 if query_metadata.get('has_shuffle', False) else 0,
            'has_join': 1 if query_metadata.get('has_join', False) else 0,
            'has_aggregate': 1 if query_metadata.get('has_aggregate', False) else 0,
            'has_window': 1 if query_metadata.get('has_window', False) else 0,
            'complexity_score': self._calculate_complexity_score(query_metadata)
        }
        
        return features
    
    def _calculate_complexity_score(self, query_metadata: dict):
        """
        Calculates a complexity score based on query characteristics.
        """
        score = 1.0
        
        # Add complexity for different operations
        if query_metadata.get('has_join'):
            score *= 2.0
        if query_metadata.get('has_aggregate'):
            score *= 1.5
        if query_metadata.get('has_window'):
            score *= 2.5
        if query_metadata.get('has_shuffle'):
            score *= 1.8
        
        # Adjust for number of operations
        num_operations = query
```python
_metadata.get('num_operations', 1)
        score *= (1 + num_operations * 0.2)
        
        return score
    
    def add_training_sample(self, query_id: str, features: dict, 
                           actual_execution_time_ms: float):
        """
        Adds a training sample to the training dataset.
        """
        training_sample = [(
            query_id,
            features['input_rows'],
            features['input_size_mb'],
            features['num_columns'],
            features['num_partitions'],
            features['cluster_cores'],
            features['executor_memory_mb'],
            features['has_shuffle'],
            features['has_join'],
            features['has_aggregate'],
            features['has_window'],
            features['complexity_score'],
            actual_execution_time_ms
        )]
        
        new_sample = self.spark.createDataFrame(training_sample, self.training_schema)
        self.training_data = self.training_data.union(new_sample)
    
    def train_model(self, model_type: str = 'random_forest'):
        """
        Trains an ML model on collected training data.
        
        Args:
            model_type: Type of model ('random_forest', 'gradient_boosting', 'both')
        """
        if self.training_data.count() < 10:
            raise ValueError("Insufficient training data. Need at least 10 samples.")
        
        # Prepare features
        assembler = VectorAssembler(
            inputCols=self.feature_columns,
            outputCol="raw_features"
        )
        
        # Scale features
        scaler = StandardScaler(
            inputCol="raw_features",
            outputCol="features",
            withStd=True,
            withMean=True
        )
        
        # Split data for training and validation
        train_data, test_data = self.training_data.randomSplit([0.8, 0.2], seed=42)
        
        # Choose model
        if model_type == 'random_forest':
            regressor = RandomForestRegressor(
                featuresCol="features",
                labelCol="actual_execution_time_ms",
                numTrees=50,
                maxDepth=10,
                seed=42
            )
        elif model_type == 'gradient_boosting':
            regressor = GBTRegressor(
                featuresCol="features",
                labelCol="actual_execution_time_ms",
                maxIter=50,
                maxDepth=5,
                seed=42
            )
        else:
            # Default to random forest
            regressor = RandomForestRegressor(
                featuresCol="features",
                labelCol="actual_execution_time_ms",
                numTrees=50,
                maxDepth=10,
                seed=42
            )
        
        # Create pipeline
        pipeline = Pipeline(stages=[assembler, scaler, regressor])
        
        # Train model
        self.model = pipeline.fit(train_data)
        
        # Evaluate model
        predictions = self.model.transform(test_data)
        
        evaluator = RegressionEvaluator(
            labelCol="actual_execution_time_ms",
            predictionCol="prediction",
            metricName="rmse"
        )
        
        rmse = evaluator.evaluate(predictions)
        
        evaluator.setMetricName("r2")
        r2 = evaluator.evaluate(predictions)
        
        evaluator.setMetricName("mae")
        mae = evaluator.evaluate(predictions)
        
        return {
            'model_type': model_type,
            'rmse': rmse,
            'r2': r2,
            'mae': mae,
            'training_samples': train_data.count(),
            'test_samples': test_data.count()
        }
    
    def predict_execution_time(self, features: dict):
        """
        Predicts execution time using the trained ML model.
        
        Args:
            features: Dictionary of feature values
            
        Returns:
            Predicted execution time in milliseconds
        """
        if self.model is None:
            raise ValueError("Model not trained. Call train_model() first.")
        
        # Create DataFrame from features
        feature_data = [(
            "prediction_query",
            features['input_rows'],
            features['input_size_mb'],
            features['num_columns'],
            features['num_partitions'],
            features['cluster_cores'],
            features['executor_memory_mb'],
            features['has_shuffle'],
            features['has_join'],
            features['has_aggregate'],
            features['has_window'],
            features['complexity_score'],
            0.0  # Placeholder for actual time
        )]
        
        feature_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(feature_data, self.training_schema)
        
        # Make prediction
        prediction = self.model.transform(feature_df)
        predicted_time = prediction.select("prediction").collect()[0][0]
        
        return max(0, predicted_time)  # Ensure non-negative
    
    def optimize_query_plan(self, df, operations: list, 
                           time_budget_ms: float = None):
        """
        Optimizes query execution plan using ML cost predictions.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            operations: List of operations to perform
            time_budget_ms: Optional time budget constraint
            
        Returns:
            Optimized execution plan and estimated time
        """
        if self.model is None:
            raise ValueError("Model not trained. Call train_model() first.")
        
        # Generate alternative execution plans
        execution_plans = self._generate_execution_plans(df, operations)
        
        # Predict cost for each plan
        plan_costs = []
        
        for plan_id, plan in enumerate(execution_plans):
            # Extract features for this plan
            features = self.extract_features(df, plan['metadata'])
            
            # Predict execution time
            predicted_time = self.predict_execution_time(features)
            
            plan_costs.append({
                'plan_id': plan_id,
                'plan': plan,
                'predicted_time_ms': predicted_time,
                'within_budget': predicted_time <= time_budget_ms if time_budget_ms else True
            })
        
        # Sort by predicted time
        plan_costs.sort(key=lambda x: x['predicted_time_ms'])
        
        # Select best plan within budget
        if time_budget_ms:
            for plan_cost in plan_costs:
                if plan_cost['within_budget']:
                    return plan_cost
            # No plan within budget, return fastest
            return plan_costs[0]
        else:
            return plan_costs[0]
    
    def _generate_execution_plans(self, df, operations: list):
        """
        Generates alternative execution plans for the same operations.
        """
        plans = []
        
        # Plan 1: Standard execution
        plans.append({
            'name': 'standard',
            'operations': operations,
            'metadata': {
                'has_shuffle': any(op.get('type') in ['join', 'aggregate', 'sort'] 
                                  for op in operations),
                'has_join': any(op.get('type') == 'join' for op in operations),
                'has_aggregate': any(op.get('type') == 'aggregate' for op in operations),
                'has_window': any(op.get('type') == 'window' for op in operations),
                'num_operations': len(operations),
                'cluster_cores': 4,
                'executor_memory_mb': 4096
            }
        })
        
        # Plan 2: With caching intermediate results
        plans.append({
            'name': 'cached',
            'operations': operations,
            'use_caching': True,
            'metadata': {
                'has_shuffle': any(op.get('type') in ['join', 'aggregate', 'sort'] 
                                  for op in operations),
                'has_join': any(op.get('type') == 'join' for op in operations),
                'has_aggregate': any(op.get('type') == 'aggregate' for op in operations),
                'has_window': any(op.get('type') == 'window' for op in operations),
                'num_operations': len(operations),
                'cluster_cores': 4,
                'executor_memory_mb': 8192  # Higher memory for caching
            }
        })
        
        # Plan 3: With repartitioning
        plans.append({
            'name': 'repartitioned',
            'operations': operations,
            'repartition_factor': 2,
            'metadata': {
                'has_shuffle': True,  # Repartitioning adds shuffle
                'has_join': any(op.get('type') == 'join' for op in operations),
                'has_aggregate': any(op.get('type') == 'aggregate' for op in operations),
                'has_window': any(op.get('type') == 'window' for op in operations),
                'num_operations': len(operations) + 1,  # +1 for repartition
                'cluster_cores': 4,
                'executor_memory_mb': 4096
            }
        })
        
        return plans
    
    def continuous_learning(self, query_id: str, df, query_metadata: dict,
                           actual_execution_time_ms: float):
        """
        Implements continuous learning by adding new samples and retraining.
        
        Args:
            query_id: Unique query identifier
            df: DataFrame that was executed
            query_metadata: Metadata about the query
            actual_execution_time_ms: Actual execution time
        """
        # Extract features
        features = self.extract_features(df, query_metadata)
        
        # Add to training data
        self.add_training_sample(query_id, features, actual_execution_time_ms)
        
        # Retrain if we have enough new samples (every 20 samples)
        if self.training_data.count() % 20 == 0:
            try:
                metrics = self.train_model()
                print(f"Model retrained. R²: {metrics['r2']:.4f}, RMSE: {metrics['rmse']:.2f}")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Retraining failed: {str(e)}")
    
    def feature_importance_analysis(self):
        """
        Analyzes feature importance from the trained model.
        """
        if self.model is None:
            raise ValueError("Model not trained. Call train_model() first.")
        
        # Extract the regressor from the pipeline
        stages = self.model.stages
        regressor = stages[-1]  # Last stage is the regressor
        
        if hasattr(regressor, 'featureImportances'):
            importances = regressor.featureImportances.toArray()
            
            # Create importance DataFrame
            importance_data = [
                (self.feature_columns[i], float(importances[i]))
                for i in range(len(self.feature_columns))
            ]
            
            importance_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
                importance_data,
                ["feature", "importance"]
            ).orderBy(col("importance").desc())
            
            return importance_df
        else:
            return None

    # ========================================================================

            'executor_memory_mb': 4096
        }
        
        # Simulate features
        features = {
            'input_rows': 1000 * (i + 1),
            'input_size_mb': 1.0 * (i + 1),
            'num_columns': 5 + (i % 10),
            'num_partitions': 10 + (i % 20),
            'cluster_cores': 4,
            'executor_memory_mb': 4096,
            'has_shuffle': 1 if query_metadata['has_shuffle'] else 0,
            'has_join': 1 if query_metadata['has_join'] else 0,
            'has_aggregate': 1 if query_metadata['has_aggregate'] else 0,
            'has_window': 1 if query_metadata['has_window'] else 0,
            'complexity_score': ml_cost._calculate_complexity_score(query_metadata)
        }
        
        # Simulate actual execution time based on features
        base_time = features['input_rows'] * 0.01
        complexity_factor = features['complexity_score']
        actual_time = base_time * complexity_factor + (i % 100)
        
        ml_cost.add_training_sample(
            f"training_query_{i}",
            features,
            actual_time
        )
    
    print(f"Training samples collected: {ml_cost.training_data.count()}")
    
    # Train the model
    print("\nTraining Random Forest model...")
    metrics = ml_cost.train_model(model_type='random_forest')
    
    print(f"\nModel Training Metrics:")

    print(f"  RMSE: {metrics['rmse']:.2f}")
    print(f"  R²: {metrics['r2']:.4f}")
    print(f"  MAE: {metrics['mae']:.2f}")
    print(f"  Training samples: {metrics['training_samples']}")
    print(f"  Test samples: {metrics['test_samples']}")
    
    # Feature importance analysis

    }
    
    predicted_time = ml_cost.predict_execution_time(test_features)

def create_cost_monitoring_dashboard(spark: SparkSession, 
                                    historical_pattern: HistoricalCostPattern):
    """
    Creates a monitoring dashboard for cost patterns.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COST MONITORING DASHBOARD")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Overall statistics
    total_executions = historical_pattern.cost_history.count()
    successful_executions = historical_pattern.cost_history.filter(
        col("success") == True
    ).count()
    
    success_rate = (successful_executions / total_executions * 100) if total_executions > 0 else 0
    
    print(f"\nOverall Statistics:")
    print(f"  Total Executions: {total_executions}")
    print(f"  Successful: {successful_executions}")
    print(f"  Success Rate: {success_rate:.2f}%")
    
    # Performance metrics by query pattern
    print("\nPerformance by Query Pattern:")
    pattern_metrics = historical_pattern.cost_history.groupBy("query_pattern").agg(
        count("*").alias("executions"),
        avg("execution_time_ms").alias("avg_time_ms"),
        min("execution_time_ms").alias("min_time_ms"),
        max("execution_time_ms").alias("max_time_ms"),
        avg("memory_peak_mb").alias("avg_memory_mb")
    ).orderBy(col("avg_time_ms").desc())
    
    pattern_metrics.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Resource utilization
    print("\nResource Utilization:")
    resource_metrics = historical_pattern.cost_history.agg(
        avg("memory_peak_mb").alias("avg_memory_mb"),
        max("memory_peak_mb").alias("max_memory_mb"),
        avg("shuffle_size_mb").alias("avg_shuffle_mb"),
        avg("num_tasks").alias("avg_tasks")
    )
    
    resource_metrics.show(truncate=False)


def export_cost_patterns_report(spark: SparkSession, output_path: str,
                               runtime_stats: RuntimeStatisticsPattern,
                               historical_cost: HistoricalCostPattern,
                               ml_cost: MachineLearningCostPattern):
    """
    Exports comprehensive cost analysis report.
    """
    print(f"\nExporting cost patterns report to {output_path}...")
    
    # Create report structure
```python
    # Create report structure
    report_data = {
        'generation_time': datetime.now().isoformat(),
        'patterns_analyzed': 5,
        'total_executions': historical_cost.cost_history.count()
    }
    
    # Save runtime statistics
    if runtime_stats:
        print("  - Saving runtime statistics...")
        # Note: In actual implementation, you would save the statistics DataFrame
    
    # Save historical data
    if historical_cost.cost_history.count() > 0:
        print("  - Saving historical cost data...")
        historical_cost.cost_history.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(
            f"{output_path}/historical_costs"
        )
    
    # Save ML model
    if ml_cost.model:
        print("  - Saving ML model...")
        ml_cost.model.write().overwrite().save(f"{output_path}/ml_model")
    
    # Save training data
    if ml_cost.training_data.count() > 0:
        print("  - Saving ML training data...")
        ml_cost.training_data.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(
            f"{output_path}/ml_training_data"
        )
    
    # Generate summary report
    summary_schema = StructType([
        StructField("metric", StringType(), False),
        StructField("value", StringType(), False),
        StructField("category", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    summary_data = [
        ("Total Patterns Implemented", "5", "Overview"),
        ("Runtime Statistics Available", "Yes", "Capabilities"),
        ("Dynamic Cost Model Active", "Yes", "Capabilities"),
        ("Feedback Loop Enabled", "Yes", "Capabilities"),
        ("Historical Data Records", str(report_data['total_executions']), "Metrics"),
        ("ML Model Trained", "Yes" if ml_cost.model else "No", "Capabilities"),
        ("Report Generated At", report_data['generation_time'], "Metadata")
    ]
    
    summary_df = spark.createDataFrame(summary_data, summary_schema)
    summary_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(f"{output_path}/summary_report")
    
    print(f"\nReport exported successfully to {output_path}")
    print("\nReport Contents:")
    print("  - historical_costs/")
    print("  - ml_model/")
    print("  - ml_training_data/")
    print("  - summary_report/")

class AdaptiveCostOptimizer:
    """
    Integrated optimizer that combines all five cost patterns for
    comprehensive query optimization.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.runtime_stats = RuntimeStatisticsPattern(spark)
        self.dynamic_cost = DynamicCostModelPattern(spark)
        self.feedback_cost = FeedbackBasedCostingPattern(spark)
        self.historical_cost = HistoricalCostPattern(spark)
        self.ml_cost = MachineLearningCostPattern(spark)
        
        self.optimization_history = []
    
    def optimize_and_execute(self, df, query_id: str, operations: list,
                            optimization_level: str = 'aggressive'):
        """
        Optimizes and executes a query using all available cost patterns.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            query_id: Unique query identifier
            operations: List of operations to perform
            optimization_level: 'conservative', 'balanced', or 'aggressive'
            
        Returns:
            Optimized execution results with comprehensive metrics
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print(f"ADAPTIVE COST OPTIMIZATION: {query_id}")
        print(f"Optimization Level: {optimization_level}")
        print(f"{'='*80}")
        
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Step 1: Analyze query characteristics
        print("\n[1/6] Analyzing query characteristics...")
        query_metadata = self._analyze_query(operations)
        print(f"      Operations: {len(operations)}")
        print(f"      Complexity: {query_metadata['complexity_score']:.2f}")
        
        # Step 2: Check historical patterns
        print("\n[2/6] Checking historical execution patterns...")
        historical_prediction = None
        if self.historical_cost.cost_history.count() > 0:
            try:
                historical_prediction = self.historical_cost.predict_cost(
                    query_metadata['pattern_type'],
                    query_metadata['estimated_size_mb']
                )
                print(f"      Historical estimate: {historical_prediction['estimated_time_ms']:.2f} ms")
                print(f"      Confidence: {historical_prediction['confidence']}")
            except:
                print("      No sufficient historical data")
        
        # Step 3: ML-based prediction
        print("\n[3/6] Generating ML-based cost prediction...")
        ml_prediction = None
        if self.ml_cost.model:
            try:
                features = self.ml_cost.extract_features(df, query_metadata)
                ml_prediction = self.ml_cost.predict_execution_time(features)
                print(f"      ML estimate: {ml_prediction:.2f} ms")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"      ML prediction failed: {str(e)}")
        
        # Step 4: Dynamic cost estimation
        print("\n[4/6] Computing dynamic cost estimates...")
        dynamic_estimates = []
        for op in operations:
            op_cost = self.dynamic_cost.estimate_operation_cost(
                op['type'],
                query_metadata['estimated_size_mb'],
                query_metadata['estimated_rows'],
                is_shuffle=query_metadata.get('has_shuffle', False)
            )
            dynamic_estimates.append(op_cost)
        
        total_dynamic_cost = sum(dynamic_estimates)
        print(f"      Dynamic total estimate: {total_dynamic_cost:.2f}")
        
        # Step 5: Select optimal execution strategy
        print("\n[5/6] Selecting optimal execution strategy...")
        execution_strategy = self._select_strategy(
            optimization_level,
            historical_prediction,
            ml_prediction,
            total_dynamic_cost,
            query_metadata
        )
        print(f"      Strategy: {execution_strategy['name']}")
        print(f"      Estimated cost: {execution_strategy['estimated_cost']:.2f}")
        
        # Step 6: Execute with monitoring
        print("\n[6/6] Executing query with runtime monitoring...")
        result_df, execution_metrics = self._execute_with_monitoring(
            df,
            operations,
            execution_strategy
        )
        
        execution_time = (time.time() - start_time) * 1000
        
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print(f"EXECUTION COMPLETE")
        print(f"{'='*80}")
        print(f"Actual execution time: {execution_time:.2f} ms")
        print(f"Estimated cost: {execution_strategy['estimated_cost']:.2f}")
        print(f"Estimation error: {abs(execution_time - execution_strategy['estimated_cost']) / execution_time * 100:.2f}%")
        
        # Record feedback for all patterns
        self._record_feedback(
            query_id,
            query_metadata,
            execution_strategy,
            execution_metrics,
            execution_time
        )
        
        # Store optimization history
        self.optimization_history.append({
            'query_id': query_id,
            'timestamp': datetime.now(),
            'estimated_cost': execution_strategy['estimated_cost'],
            'actual_cost': execution_time,
            'strategy': execution_strategy['name'],
            'optimization_level': optimization_level
        })
        
        return result_df, execution_metrics
    
    def _analyze_query(self, operations: list):
        """Analyzes query to extract metadata."""
        metadata = {
            'has_shuffle': any(op['type'] in ['join', 'aggregate', 'sort'] 
                             for op in operations),
            'has_join': any(op['type'] == 'join' for op in operations),
            'has_aggregate': any(op['type'] == 'aggregate' for op in operations),
            'has_window': any(op['type'] == 'window' for op in operations),
            'num_operations': len(operations),
            'pattern_type': 'complex' if len(operations) > 3 else 'simple',
            'estimated_size_mb': 10.0,  # Placeholder
            'estimated_rows': 10000,  # Placeholder
            'cluster_cores': 4,
            'executor_memory_mb': 4096
        }
        
        # Calculate complexity score
        complexity = 1.0
        if metadata['has_join']:
            complexity *= 2.0
        if metadata['has_aggregate']:
            complexity *= 1.5
        if metadata['has_window']:
            complexity *= 2.5
        complexity *= (1 + len(operations) * 0.2)
        
        metadata['complexity_score'] = complexity
        
        return metadata
    
    def _select_strategy(self, optimization_level: str, 
                        historical_pred, ml_pred, dynamic_cost,
                        query_metadata: dict):
        """Selects optimal execution strategy based on predictions."""
        
        # Collect all predictions
        predictions = []
        
        if historical_pred:
            predictions.append(historical_pred['estimated_time_ms'])
        if ml_pred:
            predictions.append(ml_pred)
        predictions.append(dynamic_cost)
        
        # Select strategy based on optimization level
        if optimization_level == 'conservative':
            # Use maximum estimate for safety
            estimated_cost = max(predictions) if predictions else dynamic_cost
            strategy_name = 'conservative_max_estimate'
        elif optimization_level == 'aggressive':
            # Use minimum estimate for speed
            estimated_cost = min(predictions) if predictions else dynamic_cost
            strategy_name = 'aggressive_min_estimate'
        else:  # balanced
            # Use average or median
            estimated_cost = sum(predictions) / len(predictions) if predictions else dynamic_cost
            strategy_name = 'balanced_avg_estimate'
        
        # Determine execution parameters
        use_caching = query_metadata['num_operations'] > 3
        repartition = query_metadata['has_shuffle']
        
        return {
            'name': strategy_name,
            'estimated_cost': estimated_cost,
            'use_caching': use_caching,
            'repartition': repartition,
            'parallelism': 200 if optimization_level == 'aggressive' else 100
        }
    
    def _execute_with_monitoring(self, df, operations, strategy):
        """Executes query with runtime monitoring."""
        result_df = df
        
        # Apply strategy optimizations
        if strategy.get('repartition'):
            result_df = result_df.repartition(strategy['parallelism'])
        
        execution_start = time.time()
        
        # Execute operations
        for op in operations:
            if op['type'] == 'filter':
                result_df = result_df.filter(op['params']['condition'])
            elif op['type'] == 'aggregate':
                result_df = result_df.groupBy(op['params']['group_by']).agg(
                    op['params']['aggregations']
                )
            elif op['type'] == 'join':
                result_df = result_df.join(
                    op['params']['right_df'],
                    op['params']['join_key']
                )
            elif op['type'] == 'sort':
                result_df = result_df.orderBy(op['params']['sort_columns'])
            
            # Apply caching if strategy recommends it
            if strategy.get('use_caching') and op != operations[-1]:
                result_df = result_df.cache()
        
        # Trigger execution
        row_count = result_df.count()
        execution_time = (time.time() - execution_start) * 1000
        
        metrics = {
            'execution_time_ms': execution_time,
            'row_count': row_count,
            'num_partitions': result_df.rdd.getNumPartitions(),
            'strategy_applied': strategy['name']
        }
        
        return result_df, metrics
    
    def _record_feedback(self, query_id, query_metadata, strategy,
                        execution_metrics, actual_time):
        """Records feedback in all applicable patterns."""
        
        # Record in historical cost pattern
        self.historical_cost.record_execution(
            query_id,
            f"hash_{query_id}",
            query_metadata['pattern_type'],
            {
                'execution_time_ms': int(actual_time),
                'cpu_time_ms': int(actual_time * 0.9),
                'memory_peak_mb': 1024.0,
                'input_size_mb': query_metadata['estimated_size_mb'],
                'output_size_mb': execution_metrics['row_count'] * 0.001,
                'shuffle_size_mb': 10.0 if query_metadata['has_shuffle'] else 0.0,
                'num_tasks': 100,
                'num_stages': query_metadata['num_operations'],
                'cluster_size': 4
            }
        )
        
        # Record in ML cost pattern for continuous learning
        if self.ml_cost.model or self.ml_cost.training_data.count() >= 10:
            try:
                features = {
                    'input_rows': query_metadata['estimated_rows'],
                    'input_size_mb': query_metadata['estimated_size_mb'],
                    'num_columns': 5,
                    'num_partitions': execution_metrics['num_partitions'],
                    'cluster_cores': 4,
                    'executor_memory_mb': 4096,
                    'has_shuffle': 1 if query_metadata['has_shuffle'] else 0,
                    'has_join': 1 if query_metadata['has_join'] else 0,
                    'has_aggregate': 1 if query_metadata['has_aggregate'] else 0,
                    'has_window': 1 if query_metadata['has_window'] else 0,
                    'complexity_score': query_metadata['complexity_score']
                }
                
                self.ml_cost.add_training_sample(query_id, features, actual_time)
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Warning: Could not record ML feedback: {str(e)}")
    
    def get_optimization_report(self):
        """Generates comprehensive optimization report."""
        if not self.optimization_history:
            return "No optimization history available"
        
        report_data = []
        for opt in self.optimization_history:
            error_pct = abs(opt['actual_cost'] - opt['estimated_cost']) / opt['actual_cost'] * 100
            report_data.append((
                opt['query_id'],
                opt['timestamp'].isoformat(),
                opt['strategy'],
                opt['optimization_level'],
                opt['estimated_cost'],
                opt['actual_cost'],
                error_pct
            ))
        
        report_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            report_data,
            ["query_id", "timestamp", "strategy", "level", 
             "estimated_cost", "actual_cost", "error_pct"]
        )
        
        return report_df
