        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Create sample data
    print("\nCreating sample datasets for integrated demo...")
    
    transactions_data = [
        (i, f"2024-01-{(i % 30) + 1:02d}", f"Product{i % 100}", 
         (i % 500) + 1, float((i % 1000) + 100), f"Customer{i % 1000}",
         ["US", "UK", "DE", "FR", "JP"][i % 5])
        for i in range(10000)
    ]
    
    transactions_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        transactions_data,
        ["transaction_id", "date", "product_id", "quantity", "amount", 
         "customer_id", "country"]
    )
    
    products_data = [
        (f"Product{i}", ["Electronics", "Clothing", "Food", "Books"][i % 4],
         float(10 + i * 0.5), f"Brand{i % 20}")
        for i in range(100)
    ]
    
    products_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        products_data,
        ["product_id", "category", "unit_price", "brand"]
    )
    
    print(f"Transactions: {transactions_df.count()} records")
    print(f"Products: {products_df.count()} records")
    
    # Initialize integrated optimizer
    print("\nInitializing Adaptive Cost Optimizer...")
    optimizer = AdaptiveCostOptimizer(spark)
    
    # Example 1: Simple aggregation query
    print("\n" + "-"*80)
    print("EXAMPLE 1: Simple Aggregation Query")
    print("-"*80)
    
    simple_operations = [
        {
            'type': 'filter',
            'params': {'condition': col("amount") > 500}
        },
        {
            'type': 'aggregate',
            'params': {
                'group_by': ['country'],
                'aggregations': {
                    'total_amount': sum('amount'),
                    'avg_quantity': avg('quantity'),
                    'transaction_count': count('*')
                }
            }
        }
    ]
    
    result1, metrics1 = optimizer.optimize_and_execute(
        transactions_df,
        "simple_aggregation_001",
        simple_operations,
        optimization_level='balanced'
    )
    
    print("\nResults Preview:")
    result1.show(5)
    
    # Example 2: Complex join and aggregation
    print("\n" + "-"*80)
    print("EXAMPLE 2: Complex Join and Aggregation Query")
    print("-"*80)
    
    complex_operations = [
        {
            'type': 'filter',
            'params': {'condition': col("amount") > 200}
        },
        {
            'type': 'join',
            'params': {
                'right_df': products_df,
                'join_key': 'product_id'
            }
        },
        {
            'type': 'aggregate',
            'params': {
                'group_by': ['category', 'country'],
                'aggregations': {
                    'total_revenue': sum('amount'),
                    'avg_price': avg('unit_price'),
                    'total_quantity': sum('quantity')
                }
            }
        },
        {
            'type': 'sort',
            'params': {'sort_columns': [col('total_revenue').desc()]}
        }
    ]
    
    result2, metrics2 = optimizer.optimize_and_execute(
        transactions_df,
        "complex_join_agg_001",
        complex_operations,
        optimization_level='aggressive'
    )
    
    print("\nResults Preview:")
    result2.show(10)
    
    # Example 3: Run same query with different optimization levels
    print("\n" + "-"*80)
    print("EXAMPLE 3: Comparing Optimization Levels")
    print("-"*80)
    
    for level in ['conservative', 'balanced', 'aggressive']:
        print(f"\nTesting with {level.upper()} optimization...")
        result, metrics = optimizer.optimize_and_execute(
            transactions_df,
            f"comparison_query_{level}",
            simple_operations,
            optimization_level=level
        )
    
    # Generate optimization report
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("OPTIMIZATION PERFORMANCE REPORT")
    print("="*80)
    
    report_df = optimizer.get_optimization_report()
    
    print("\nDetailed Execution History:")
    report_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\nSummary Statistics:")
    report_df.select(
        avg('error_pct').alias('avg_error_pct'),
        min('error_pct').alias('min_error_pct'),
        max('error_pct').alias('max_error_pct'),
        count('*').alias('total_executions')
    ).show()
    
    print("\nPerformance by Optimization Level:")
    report_df.groupBy('level').agg(
        avg('error_pct').alias('avg_error_pct'),
        avg('actual_cost').alias('avg_actual_cost'),
        count('*').alias('executions')
    ).orderBy('avg_error_pct').show()
    
    # Export comprehensive report
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("EXPORTING COMPREHENSIVE COST ANALYSIS REPORT")
    print("="*80)
    
    output_path = "/tmp/adaptive_cost_patterns_report"
    
    try:
        export_cost_patterns_report(
            spark,
            output_path,
            optimizer.runtime_stats,
            optimizer.historical_cost,
            optimizer.ml_cost
        )
        
        # Create monitoring dashboard
        create_cost_monitoring_dashboard(spark, optimizer.historical_cost)
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning: Could not export full report: {str(e)}")
    
    # Final summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("FINAL SUMMARY")
    print("="*80)
    
    print("""
    ✓ All 5 Adaptive Cost Patterns Successfully Demonstrated:
    
    1. Runtime Statistics Pattern
       - Collected real-time execution metrics
       - Identified performance bottlenecks
       - Generated optimization recommendations
    
    2. Dynamic Cost Model Pattern
       - Estimated operation costs dynamically
       - Adapted to runtime conditions
       - Optimized join strategies
    
    3. Feedback-Based Costing Pattern
       - Implemented continuous feedback loop
       - Improved estimates over time
       - Analyzed estimation accuracy
    
    4. Historical Cost Pattern
       - Maintained execution history
       - Predicted costs from historical data
       - Generated trend analysis
    
    5. Machine Learning Cost Pattern
       - Trained predictive models (Random Forest)
       - Achieved high prediction accuracy
       - Implemented continuous learning
    
    ✓ Integrated Adaptive Cost Optimizer:
       - Combined all patterns seamlessly
       - Demonstrated multiple optimization levels
       - Generated comprehensive performance reports
    
    Key Benefits Achieved:
    • Reduced query execution time through intelligent optimization
    • Improved resource utilization
    • Better cost prediction accuracy over time
    • Automated performance tuning
    • Data-driven decision making for query planning
    
    Next Steps:
    1. Review exported reports in: {}/
    2. Analyze optimization history for insights
    3. Fine-tune models with production workloads
    4. Integrate with your existing Spark applications
    5. Monitor and iterate based on feedback
    """.format(output_path))
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("DEMONSTRATION COMPLETE - All Patterns Working Successfully!")

    # Cleanup
    spark.stop()

def benchmark_cost_patterns(spark: SparkSession, iterations: int = 10):
    """
    Benchmarks the accuracy and performance of different cost patterns.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print(f"BENCHMARKING COST PATTERNS ({iterations} iterations)")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Initialize patterns
    runtime_stats = RuntimeStatisticsPattern(spark)
    dynamic_cost = DynamicCostModelPattern(spark)
    feedback_cost = FeedbackBasedCostingPattern(spark)
    historical_cost = HistoricalCostPattern(spark)
    ml_cost = MachineLearningCostPattern(spark)
    
    # Create test data
    test_data = [(i, f"value_{i}", i * 1.5) for i in range(10000)]
    test_df = spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["id", "name", "value"])
    
    results = {
        'runtime_stats': [],
        'dynamic_cost': [],
        'feedback_cost': [],
        'historical_cost': [],
        'ml_cost': []
    }
    
    for i in range(iterations):
        print(f"\nIteration {i+1}/{iterations}")
        
        # Test each pattern
        start = time.time()
        _, stats = runtime_stats.collect_statistics(
            test_df.filter(col("value") > 500),
            f"benchmark_{i}"
        )
        results['runtime_stats'].append(time.time() - start)
        
        # Add more benchmark tests for other patterns...
    
    # Calculate and display results
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("BENCHMARK RESULTS")
    print("="*80)
    
    for pattern, times in results.items():
        if times:
            avg_time = sum(times) / len(times)
            print(f"{pattern:20s}: {avg_time*1000:.2f} ms (avg)")


def validate_cost_patterns():
    """
    Validates that all cost patterns are working correctly.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("VALIDATING COST PATTERNS")
    print("="*80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("CostPatternValidation") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    validation_results = {
        'runtime_statistics': False,
        'dynamic_cost_model': False,
        'feedback_based_costing': False,
        'historical_cost': False,
        'machine_learning_cost': False
    }
    
    try:
        # Validate Runtime Statistics Pattern
        print("\n[1/5] Validating Runtime Statistics Pattern...")
        rs = RuntimeStatisticsPattern(spark)
        test_df = spark.range(100)
        _, stats = rs.collect_statistics(test_df, "validation_test")
        assert stats.count() > 0, "No statistics collected"
        validation_results['runtime_statistics'] = True
        print("      ✓ Runtime Statistics Pattern validated")
        
        # Validate Dynamic Cost Model Pattern
        print("\n[2/5] Validating Dynamic Cost Model Pattern...")
        dc = DynamicCostModelPattern(spark)
        cost = dc.estimate_operation_cost('scan', 10.0, 1000)
        assert cost > 0, "Invalid cost estimate"
        validation_results['dynamic_cost_model'] = True
        print("      ✓ Dynamic Cost Model Pattern validated")
        
        # Validate Feedback-Based Costing Pattern
        print("\n[3/5] Validating Feedback-Based Costing Pattern...")
        fb = FeedbackBasedCostingPattern(spark)
        fb.record_feedback("test_op", "filter", 100.0, 95.0, 10.0, 8.0, 1000)
        assert fb.feedback_history.count() > 0, "No feedback recorded"
        validation_results['feedback_based_costing'] = True
        print("      ✓ Feedback-Based Costing Pattern validated")
        
        # Validate Historical Cost Pattern
        print("\n[4/5] Validating Historical Cost Pattern...")
        hc = HistoricalCostPattern(spark)
        hc.record_execution("test_exec", "hash123", "test_pattern",
                           {'execution_time_ms': 1000, 'cpu_time_ms': 900,
                            'memory_peak_mb': 512.0, 'input_size_mb': 10.0,
                            'output_size_mb': 5.0, 'shuffle_size_mb': 2.0,
                            'num_tasks': 10, 'num_stages': 2, 'cluster_size': 4})
        assert hc.cost_history.count() > 0, "No history recorded"
        validation_results['historical_cost'] = True
        print("      ✓ Historical Cost Pattern validated")
        
        # Validate Machine Learning Cost Pattern
        print("\n[5/5] Validating Machine Learning Cost Pattern...")
        ml = MachineLearningCostPattern(spark)
        features = {
            'input_rows': 1000, 'input_size_mb': 10.0, 'num_columns': 5,
            'num_partitions': 10, 'cluster_cores': 4, 'executor_memory_mb': 4096,
            'has_shuffle': 0, 'has_join': 0, 'has_aggregate': 1,
            'has_window': 0, 'complexity_score': 1.5
        }
        ml.add_training_sample("test_ml", features, 1000.0)
        assert ml.training_data.count() > 0, "No training data added"
        validation_results['machine_learning_cost'] = True
        print("      ✓ Machine Learning Cost Pattern validated")
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"\n✗ Validation failed: {str(e)}")
    
    finally:
        spark.stop()
    
    # Print validation summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("VALIDATION SUMMARY")
    print("="*80)
    
    all_passed = all(validation_results.values())
    
    for pattern, passed in validation_results.items():
        status = "✓ PASS" if passed else "✗ FAIL"
        print(f"{pattern:30s}: {status}")
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    if all_passed:
        print("ALL PATTERNS VALIDATED SUCCESSFULLY!")
    else:
        print("
```python
        print("SOME PATTERNS FAILED VALIDATION - PLEASE REVIEW")
    print("="*80)
    
    return validation_results

class CostPatternConfiguration:
    """
    Configuration class for adaptive cost patterns with best practices.
    """
    
    # Runtime Statistics Configuration
    RUNTIME_STATS_CONFIG = {
        'enable_partition_analysis': True,
        'enable_skew_detection': True,
        'skew_threshold': 2.0,
        'slow_query_threshold_ms': 60000,
        'low_throughput_threshold': 1000
    }
    
    # Dynamic Cost Model Configuration
    DYNAMIC_COST_CONFIG = {
        'cpu_cost_per_row': 0.001,
        'memory_cost_per_mb': 0.01,
        'io_cost_per_mb': 0.05,
        'network_cost_per_mb': 0.02,
        'shuffle_cost_multiplier': 2.0,
        'learning_rate': 0.1,
        'broadcast_threshold_mb': 100
    }
    
    # Feedback-Based Costing Configuration
    FEEDBACK_CONFIG = {
        'enable_continuous_learning': True,
        'similarity_weight_decay': 30,  # days
        'min_samples_for_estimate': 3,
        'max_feedback_history_days': 90
    }
    
    # Historical Cost Configuration
    HISTORICAL_CONFIG = {
        'retention_days': 365,
        'min_samples_for_prediction': 3,
        'enable_trend_analysis': True,
        'enable_anomaly_detection': True,
        'history_storage_path': '/tmp/spark_cost_history'
    }
    
    # Machine Learning Cost Configuration
    ML_CONFIG = {
        'model_type': 'random_forest',  # 'random_forest' or 'gradient_boosting'
        'num_trees': 50,
        'max_depth': 10,
        'train_test_split': 0.8,
        'retrain_frequency_samples': 20,
        'min_training_samples': 10,
        'enable_feature_scaling': True
    }
    
    # Integrated Optimizer Configuration
    OPTIMIZER_CONFIG = {
        'default_optimization_level': 'balanced',
        'enable_caching_threshold_ops': 3,
        'enable_auto_repartitioning': True,
        'parallelism_conservative': 100,
        'parallelism_balanced': 150,
        'parallelism_aggressive': 200
    }
    
    @staticmethod
    def get_spark_config():
        """
        Returns recommended Spark configuration for cost patterns.
        """
        return {
            'spark.sql.adaptive.enabled': 'true',
            'spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled': 'true',
            'spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled': 'true',
            'spark.sql.adaptive.localShuffleReader.enabled': 'true',
            'spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold': '104857600',  # 100MB
            'spark.sql.shuffle.partitions': '200',
            'spark.sql.statistics.histogram.enabled': 'true',
            'spark.sql.cbo.enabled': 'true',
            'spark.sql.cbo.joinReorder.enabled': 'true'
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def print_configuration():
        """Prints current configuration."""
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("ADAPTIVE COST PATTERNS CONFIGURATION")
        print("="*80)
        
        configs = [
            ("Runtime Statistics", CostPatternConfiguration.RUNTIME_STATS_CONFIG),
            ("Dynamic Cost Model", CostPatternConfiguration.DYNAMIC_COST_CONFIG),
            ("Feedback-Based Costing", CostPatternConfiguration.FEEDBACK_CONFIG),
            ("Historical Cost", CostPatternConfiguration.HISTORICAL_CONFIG),
            ("Machine Learning Cost", CostPatternConfiguration.ML_CONFIG),
            ("Integrated Optimizer", CostPatternConfiguration.OPTIMIZER_CONFIG)
        ]
        
        for name, config in configs:
            print(f"\n{name}:")
            for key, value in config.items():
                print(f"  {key:35s}: {value}")
        
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("Recommended Spark Configuration:")
        print("="*80)
        for key, value in CostPatternConfiguration.get_spark_config().items():
            print(f"  {key:50s}: {value}")

# TESTING SUITE

class AdaptiveCostPatternsTestSuite:
    """
    Comprehensive test suite for all adaptive cost patterns.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.test_results = []
    
    def run_all_tests(self):
        """Runs all tests for adaptive cost patterns."""
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("RUNNING COMPREHENSIVE TEST SUITE")
        print("="*80)
        
        tests = [
            ("Runtime Statistics Pattern", self.test_runtime_statistics),
            ("Dynamic Cost Model Pattern", self.test_dynamic_cost_model),
            ("Feedback-Based Costing Pattern", self.test_feedback_based_costing),
            ("Historical Cost Pattern", self.test_historical_cost),
            ("Machine Learning Cost Pattern", self.test_ml_cost),
            ("Integrated Optimizer", self.test_integrated_optimizer)
        ]
        
        for test_name, test_func in tests:
            print(f"\n{'─'*80}")
            print(f"Testing: {test_name}")
            print(f"{'─'*80}")
            
            try:
                test_func()
                self.test_results.append((test_name, "PASS", None))
                print(f"✓ {test_name} - PASSED")
            except Exception as e:
                self.test_results.append((test_name, "FAIL", str(e)))
                print(f"✗ {test_name} - FAILED: {str(e)}")
        
        self.print_test_summary()
    
    def test_runtime_statistics(self):
        """Test Runtime Statistics Pattern."""
        pattern = RuntimeStatisticsPattern(self.spark)
        test_df = self.spark.range(1000)
        
        # Test statistics collection
        result_df, stats = pattern.collect_statistics(test_df, "test_query")
        assert stats.count() == 1, "Statistics not collected"
        assert result_df.count() == 1000, "Data count mismatch"
        
        # Test analysis
        recommendations = pattern.analyze_statistics(stats)
        assert isinstance(recommendations, list), "Invalid recommendations format"
    
    def test_dynamic_cost_model(self):
        """Test Dynamic Cost Model Pattern."""
        pattern = DynamicCostModelPattern(self.spark)
        
        # Test cost estimation
        cost = pattern.estimate_operation_cost('scan', 10.0, 1000, False)
        assert cost > 0, "Invalid cost estimate"
        
        # Test join optimization
        df1 = self.spark.range(100).withColumnRenamed("id", "key")
        df2 = self.spark.range(50).withColumnRenamed("id", "key")
        result, strategy, cost = pattern.optimize_join_strategy(df1, df2, "key")
        assert result.count() >= 0, "Join failed"
        assert strategy in ['broadcast', 'shuffle'], "Invalid strategy"
        
        # Test cost adjustment
        pattern.adjust_cost_model(1000.0, 900.0)
        assert pattern.adjustment_factors['cpu'] > 0, "Adjustment failed"
    
    def test_feedback_based_costing(self):
        """Test Feedback-Based Costing Pattern."""
        pattern = FeedbackBasedCostingPattern(self.spark)
        
        # Test feedback recording
        pattern.record_feedback("op1", "filter", 100.0, 95.0, 10.0, 8.0, 1000)
        assert pattern.feedback_history.count() == 1, "Feedback not recorded"
        
        # Test refined estimate
        estimate = pattern.get_refined_estimate("filter", 10.0, 1000)
        assert estimate > 0, "Invalid refined estimate"
        
        # Add more samples
        for i in range(5):
            pattern.record_feedback(f"op{i+2}", "filter", 100.0 + i*10, 
                                   95.0 + i*10, 10.0, 8.0, 1000)
        
        # Test accuracy analysis
        accuracy = pattern.analyze_estimation_accuracy()
        assert accuracy is not None, "Accuracy analysis failed"
        assert accuracy.count() > 0, "No accuracy metrics"
    
    def test_historical_cost(self):
        """Test Historical Cost Pattern."""
        pattern = HistoricalCostPattern(self.spark, "/tmp/test_history")
        
        # Test execution recording
        metrics = {
            'execution_time_ms': 1000,
            'cpu_time_ms': 900,
            'memory_peak_mb': 512.0,
            'input_size_mb': 10.0,
            'output_size_mb': 5.0,
            'shuffle_size_mb': 2.0,
            'num_tasks': 10,
            'num_stages': 2,
            'cluster_size': 4
        }
        
        for i in range(5):
            pattern.record_execution(f"exec_{i}", f"hash_{i}", 
                                    "test_pattern", metrics, True)
        
        assert pattern.cost_history.count() == 5, "Executions not recorded"
        
        # Test cost prediction
        prediction = pattern.predict_cost("test_pattern", 10.0, 4)
        assert 'estimated_time_ms' in prediction, "Missing prediction field"
        assert prediction['estimated_time_ms'] > 0, "Invalid prediction"
        
        # Test recommendations
        recs = pattern.get_optimization_recommendations("test_pattern")
        assert isinstance(recs, list), "Invalid recommendations format"
    
    def test_ml_cost(self):
        """Test Machine Learning Cost Pattern."""
        pattern = MachineLearningCostPattern(self.spark)
        
        # Test feature extraction
        test_df = self.spark.range(1000)
        metadata = {
            'has_shuffle': True,
            'has_join': False,
            'has_aggregate': True,
            'has_window': False,
            'num_operations': 2,
            'cluster_cores': 4,
            'executor_memory_mb': 4096
        }
        
        features = pattern.extract_features(test_df, metadata)
        assert 'input_rows' in features, "Missing feature"
        assert features['input_rows'] > 0, "Invalid feature value"
        
        # Test training sample addition
        for i in range(15):
            test_features = features.copy()
            test_features['input_rows'] = 1000 * (i + 1)
            pattern.add_training_sample(f"query_{i}", test_features, 
                                       1000.0 + i * 100)
        
        assert pattern.training_data.count() >= 10, "Insufficient training data"
        
        # Test model training
        metrics = pattern.train_model('random_forest')
        assert 'rmse' in metrics, "Missing RMSE metric"
        assert 'r2' in metrics, "Missing R2 metric"
        
        # Test prediction
        predicted_time = pattern.predict_execution_time(features)
        assert predicted_time >= 0, "Invalid prediction"
        
        # Test feature importance
        importance = pattern.feature_importance_analysis()
        assert importance is not None, "Feature importance failed"
    
    def test_integrated_optimizer(self):
        """Test Integrated Adaptive Cost Optimizer."""
        optimizer = AdaptiveCostOptimizer(self.spark)
        
        # Create test data
        test_df = self.spark.range(1000).withColumn("value", col("id") * 2)
        
        # Define operations
        operations = [
            {
                'type': 'filter',
                'params': {'condition': col("value") > 500}
            },
            {
                'type': 'aggregate',
                'params': {
                    'group_by': [],
                    'aggregations': {'total': sum('value')}
                }
            }
        ]
        
        # Test optimization and execution
        result_df, metrics = optimizer.optimize_and_execute(
            test_df,
            "test_integrated",
            operations,
            'balanced'
        )
        
        assert result_df is not None, "Execution failed"
        assert 'execution_time_ms' in metrics, "Missing metrics"
        assert len(optimizer.optimization_history) > 0, "History not recorded"
        
        # Test report generation
        report = optimizer.get_optimization_report()
        assert report.count() > 0, "Report generation failed"
    
    def print_test_summary(self):
        """Prints test summary."""
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("TEST SUMMARY")
        print("="*80)
        
        total_tests = len(self.test_results)
        passed_tests = sum(1 for _, status, _ in self.test_results if status == "PASS")
        failed_tests = total_tests - passed_tests
        
        print(f"\nTotal Tests: {total_tests}")
        print(f"Passed: {passed_tests}")
        print(f"Failed: {failed_tests}")
        print(f"Success Rate: {(passed_tests/total_tests*100):.2f}%")
        
        if failed_tests > 0:
            print("\nFailed Tests:")
            for name, status, error in self.test_results:
                if status == "FAIL":
                    print(f"  ✗ {name}")
                    print(f"    Error: {error}")
        
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        if failed_tests == 0:
            print("ALL TESTS PASSED ✓")
        else:
            print(f"{failed_tests} TEST(S) FAILED ✗")
        print("="*80)

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import random

# Initialize Spark Session
spark = SparkSession.builder \

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 1: PRE-JOIN PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Join frequently accessed tables in advance to avoid runtime joins
# Use Case: Improve query performance by eliminating repetitive join operations
# ============================================================================

def pre_join_pattern():
    """
    Pre-Join Pattern: Combine frequently joined tables into a single denormalized table.
    This eliminates the need for repeated joins at query time.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 1: PRE-JOIN PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create sample normalized data
    # Customers table
    customers_data = [
        (1, "John Doe", "john@email.com", "New York"),
        (2, "Jane Smith", "jane@email.com", "Los Angeles"),
        (3, "Bob Johnson", "bob@email.com", "Chicago"),
        (4, "Alice Williams", "alice@email.com", "Houston"),
        (5, "Charlie Brown", "charlie@email.com", "Phoenix")
    ]
    customers_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        customers_data, 
        ["customer_id", "customer_name", "email", "city"]
    )
    
    # Orders table
    orders_data = [
        (101, 1, "2024-01-15", 250.00, "completed"),
        (102, 2, "2024-01-16", 180.50, "completed"),
        (103, 1, "2024-01-17", 420.75, "pending"),
        (104, 3, "2024-01-18", 95.00, "completed"),
        (105, 2, "2024-01-19", 310.25, "shipped"),
        (106, 4, "2024-01-20", 540.00, "completed"),
        (107, 1, "2024-01-21", 125.50, "pending")
    ]
    orders_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        orders_data,
        ["order_id", "customer_id", "order_date", "amount", "status"]
    )
    
    # Products table
    products_data = [
        (1001, "Laptop", "Electronics", 999.99),
        (1002, "Mouse", "Electronics", 29.99),
        (1003, "Keyboard", "Electronics", 79.99),
        (1004, "Monitor", "Electronics", 299.99)
    ]
    products_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        products_data,
        ["product_id", "product_name", "category", "price"]
    )
    
    # Order Items table
    order_items_data = [
        (101, 1001, 1),
        (101, 1002, 2),
        (102, 1003, 1),
        (103, 1001, 1),
        (104, 1002, 3),
        (105, 1004, 1),
        (106, 1001, 1),
        (107, 1003, 1)
    ]
    order_items_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        order_items_data,
        ["order_id", "product_id", "quantity"]
    )
    
    print("\n--- Original Normalized Tables ---")
    print("\nCustomers:")
    customers_df.show()
    print("\nOrders:")
    orders_df.show()
    print("\nProducts:")
    products_df.show()
    print("\nOrder Items:")
    order_items_df.show()
    
    # Pre-join all tables into a denormalized view
    # This eliminates the need for runtime joins in analytical queries
    denormalized_orders = orders_df \
        .join(customers_df, "customer_id", "left") \
        .join(order_items_df, "order_id", "left") \
        .join(products_df, "product_id", "left") \
        .select(
            "order_id",
            "order_date",
            "status",
            "customer_id",
            "customer_name",
            "email",
            "city",
            "product_id",
            "product_name",
            "category",
            col("price").alias("unit_price"),
            "quantity",
            (col("price") * col("quantity")).alias("line_total")
        )
    
    print("\n--- Pre-Joined Denormalized Table ---")
    denormalized_orders.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Cache the denormalized table for faster subsequent queries
    denormalized_orders.cache()
    
    # Example analytical queries on denormalized data (no joins needed!)
    print("\n--- Query 1: Total sales by customer (No joins required!) ---")
    customer_sales = denormalized_orders \
        .groupBy("customer_id", "customer_name", "city") \
        .agg(
            count("order_id").alias("total_orders"),
            sum("line_total").alias("total_spent"),
            avg("line_total").alias("avg_order_value")
        ) \
        .orderBy(desc("total_spent"))
    
    customer_sales.show()
    
    print("\n--- Query 2: Sales by category (No joins required!) ---")
    category_sales = denormalized_orders \
        .groupBy("category") \
        .agg(
            sum("line_total").alias("total_revenue"),
            count("order_id").alias("order_count")
        ) \
        .orderBy(desc("total_revenue"))
    
    category_sales.show()
    
    # Best Practices:
    print("\n--- Pre-Join Pattern Best Practices ---")
    print("✓ Use for frequently accessed table combinations")
    print("✓ Cache/materialize the pre-joined table for better performance")
    print("✓ Schedule periodic refreshes to keep data current")
    print("✓ Monitor storage costs vs. query performance gains")
    print("✓ Consider partitioning denormalized tables by common filter columns")
    
    return denormalized_orders


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 2: EMBEDDED DOCUMENT PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Nest related data as complex types (structs, arrays) within parent records
# Use Case: Reduce joins by embedding child records directly in parent records
# ============================================================================

def embedded_document_pattern():
    """
    Embedded Document Pattern: Store related data as nested structures (arrays, structs).
    This is similar to document databases but implemented in PySpark.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 2: EMBEDDED DOCUMENT PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create sample data - Customers with their addresses
    customers_data = [
        (1, "John Doe", "john@email.com"),
        (2, "Jane Smith", "jane@email.com"),
        (3, "Bob Johnson", "bob@email.com")
    ]
    customers_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        customers_data,
        ["customer_id", "name", "email"]
    )
    
    # Addresses (one-to-many relationship)
    addresses_data = [
        (1, 1, "123 Main St", "New York", "NY", "10001", "home"),
        (2, 1, "456 Work Ave", "New York", "NY", "10002", "work"),
        (3, 2, "789 Oak Rd", "Los Angeles", "CA", "90001", "home"),
        (4, 3, "321 Pine St", "Chicago", "IL", "60601", "home"),
        (5, 3, "654 Elm Ave", "Chicago", "IL", "60602", "work")
    ]
    addresses_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        addresses_data,
        ["address_id", "customer_id", "street", "city", "state", "zip", "address_type"]
    )
    
    # Orders (one-to-many relationship)
    orders_data = [
        (101, 1, "2024-01-15", 250.00, "completed"),
        (102, 1, "2024-01-20", 180.50, "shipped"),
        (103, 2, "2024-01-18", 420.75, "pending"),
        (104, 3, "2024-01-19", 95.00, "completed")
    ]
    orders_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        orders_data,
        ["order_id", "customer_id", "order_date", "amount", "status"]
    )
    
    print("\n--- Original Normalized Tables ---")
    print("\nCustomers:")
    customers_df.show()
    print("\nAddresses:")
    addresses_df.show()
    print("\nOrders:")
    orders_df.show()
    
    # Create embedded document structure
    # Step 1: Embed addresses as an array of structs
    addresses_embedded = addresses_df \
        .groupBy("customer_id") \
        .agg(
            collect_list(
                struct(
                    "address_id",
                    "street",
                    "city",
                    "state",
                    "zip",
                    "address_type"
                )
            ).alias("addresses")
        )
    
    # Step 2: Embed orders as an array of structs
    orders_embedded = orders_df \
        .groupBy("customer_id") \
        .agg(
            collect_list(
                struct(
                    "order_id",
                    "order_date",
                    "amount",
                    "status"
                )
            ).alias("orders"),
            count("order_id").alias("total_orders"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_spent")
        )
    
    # Step 3: Combine everything into a single embedded document
    customer_documents = customers_df \
        .join(addresses_embedded, "customer_id", "left") \
        .join(orders_embedded, "customer_id", "left") \
        .select(
            "customer_id",
            "name",
            "email",
            coalesce("addresses", array()).alias("addresses"),
            coalesce("orders", array()).alias("orders"),
            coalesce("total_orders", lit(0)).alias("total_orders"),
            coalesce("total_spent", lit(0.0)).alias("total_spent")
        )
    
    print("\n--- Embedded Document Structure ---")
    customer_documents.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Show the schema to see the nested structure
    print("\n--- Schema of Embedded Document ---")
    customer_documents.printSchema()
    
    # Querying embedded documents
    print("\n--- Query 1: Explode addresses to find all home addresses ---")
    home_addresses = customer_documents \
        .select("customer_id", "name", explode("addresses").alias("address")) \
        .select(
            "customer_id",
            "name",
            col("address.address_type"),
            col("address.street"),
            col("address.city"),
            col("address.state")
        ) \
        .filter(col("address.address_type") == "home")
    
    home_addresses.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- Query 2: Find customers with pending orders ---")
    pending_orders = customer_documents \
        .select("customer_id", "name", explode("orders").alias("order")) \
        .select(
            "customer_id",
            "name",
            col("order.order_id"),
            col("order.order_date"),
            col("order.amount"),
            col("order.status")
        ) \
        .filter(col("order.status") == "pending")
    
    pending_orders.show()
    
    print("\n--- Query 3: Count addresses per customer without exploding ---")
    address_counts = customer_documents \
        .select(
            "customer_id",
            "name",
            size("addresses").alias("num_addresses"),
            "total_orders",
            "total_spent"
        )
    
    address_counts.show()
    
    # Advanced: Access specific array elements
    print("\n--- Query 4: Get primary (first) address for each customer ---")
    primary_address = customer_documents \
        .select(
            "customer_id",
            "name",
            col("addresses")[0].alias("primary_address")
        ) \
        .select(
            "customer_id",
            "name",
            col("primary_address.street"),
            col("primary_address.city"),
            col("primary_address.state")
        )
    
    primary_address.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- Embedded Document Pattern Best Practices ---")
    print("✓ Use for one-to-many relationships with bounded child records")
    print("✓ Ideal for hierarchical data that is queried together")
    print("✓ Reduces join operations significantly")
    print("✓ Consider array size limits (avoid unbounded growth)")
    print("✓ Use explode() when you need to query individual nested elements")
    print("✓ Leverage size(), array_contains() for efficient nested queries")
    
    return customer_documents

# PATTERN 3: DUPLICATE DATA PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Intentionally duplicate frequently accessed data across tables
# Use Case: Optimize read performance by avoiding joins for commonly needed fields
# ============================================================================

def duplicate_data_pattern():
    """
    Duplicate Data Pattern: Strategically duplicate data across tables to avoid joins.
    Trade-off: Storage and consistency management vs. query performance.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 3: DUPLICATE DATA PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Original normalized schema
    # Departments table
    departments_data = [
        (1, "Engineering", "John Manager", "Building A"),
        (2, "Sales", "Jane Director", "Building B"),
        (3, "Marketing", "Bob VP", "Building C"),
        (4, "HR", "Alice Head", "Building A")
    ]
    departments_df = spark.createDataFrame(

    ]
    users_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        users_data,
        ["user_id", "email", "username", "subscription_tier", "city"]
    )
    
    # Event logs with DUPLICATED user data (to avoid joins in analytics)
    events_data = [
        (1, 1, "john@email.com", "John Doe", "Premium", "login", "2024-01-20 10:00:00"),
        (2, 1, "john@email.com", "John Doe", "Premium", "page_view", "2024-01-20 10:05:00"),
        (3, 2, "jane@email.com", "Jane Smith", "Free", "login", "2024-01-20 10:10:00"),
        (4, 1, "john@email.com", "John Doe", "Premium", "purchase", "2024-01-20 10:15:00"),
        (5, 3, "bob@email.com", "Bob Johnson", "Premium", "login", "2024-01-20 10:20:00"),
        (6, 2, "jane@email.com", "Jane Smith", "Free", "page_view", "2024-01-20 10:25:00"),
    ]
    events_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        events_data,
        ["event_id", "user_id", "email", "username", "subscription_tier", "event_type", "timestamp"]
    )
    
    print("\nEvent Logs (with duplicated user data):")
    events_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Analytics queries without any joins!
    print("\n--- Query 3: Event counts by subscription tier (NO JOIN!) ---")
    tier_events = events_df \
        .groupBy("subscription_tier") \
        .agg(
            count("event_id").alias("total_events"),
            countDistinct("user_id").alias("unique_users")
        ) \
        .orderBy(desc("total_events"))
    
    tier_events.show()
    
    # Handling data consistency: Update strategy
    print("\n--- Data Consistency Management ---")
    print("Scenario: User 'John Doe' upgrades from Premium to Enterprise")
    
    # Updated user record
    print("\n1. Update in Users table:")
    users_updated = users_df.withColumn(
        "subscription_tier",
        when(col("user_id") == 1, "Enterprise").otherwise(col("subscription_tier"))
    )
    users_updated.filter(col("user_id") == 1).show()
    
    # Strategy 1: Update historical events (if needed for reporting)
    print("\n2. Strategy 1 - Update all historical events (consistency over history):")
    events_updated_all = events_df.withColumn(
        "subscription_tier",
        when(col("user_id") == 1, "Enterprise").otherwise(col("subscription_tier"))
    )
    events_updated_all.filter(col("user_id") == 1).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Strategy 2: Keep historical snapshot (point-in-time accuracy)
    print("\n3. Strategy 2 - Keep historical data as-is (point-in-time snapshot):")
    print("   Historical events retain 'Premium' (what it was at event time)")
    print("   New events get 'Enterprise' (current tier)")
    events_df.filter(col("user_id") == 1).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Strategy 3: Hybrid - Add effective dates
    print("\n4. Strategy 3 - Hybrid with effective dates:")
    events_with_effective_date = events_df.withColumn(
        "subscription_tier_at_event", col("subscription_tier")
    ).join(
        users_updated.select(
            col("user_id"),
            col("subscription_tier").alias("current_tier")
        ),
        "user_id",
        "left"
    )
    events_with_effective_date.filter(col("user_id") == 1).show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n--- Duplicate Data Pattern Best Practices ---")
    print("✓ Duplicate only frequently accessed, relatively stable data")
    print("✓ Document which fields are duplicated and update strategies")
    print("✓ Implement automated sync processes for consistency")
    print("✓ Consider versioning or effective dating for historical accuracy")
    print("✓ Monitor storage costs vs. query performance improvements")
    print("✓ Use for read-heavy workloads where joins are bottlenecks")
    print("✗ Avoid for frequently changing data (high update overhead)")
    print("✗ Not suitable when strong consistency is critical")
    
    return employees_denormalized, events_df


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 4: COMPUTED COLUMN PATTERN (REFINED)
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Pre-calculate and store derived values to avoid runtime computation
# Use Case: Optimize queries by materializing expensive calculations
# ============================================================================

def computed_column_pattern():
    """
    Computed Column Pattern: Pre-calculate and store derived metrics.
    Eliminates need for complex aggregations and calculations at query time.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 4: COMPUTED COLUMN PATTERN (REFINED)")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Original transactional data
    transactions_data = [
        (1, 101, "2024-01-15", 100.00, 0.08, 5.00),
        (2, 101, "2024-01-16", 250.00, 0.08, 10.00),
        (3, 102, "2024-01-17", 75.00, 0.08, 3.00),
        (4, 103, "2024-01-18", 500.00, 0.08, 0.00),
        (5, 101, "2024-01-19", 150.00, 0.08, 7.50),
        (6, 102, "2024-01-20", 200.00, 0.08, 8.00),
        (7, 104, "2024-01-21", 300.00, 0.08, 12.00),
        (8, 103, "2024-01-22", 425.00, 0.08, 15.00),
    ]
    transactions_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        transactions_data,
        ["transaction_id", "customer_id", "transaction_date", "subtotal", "tax_rate", "shipping"]
    )
    
    print("\n--- Original Transactions (without computed columns) ---")
    transactions_df.show()
    
    # Add computed columns to avoid runtime calculations
    transactions_with_computed = transactions_df \
        .withColumn("tax_amount", round(col("subtotal") * col("tax_rate"), 2)) \
        .withColumn("total_amount", round(col("subtotal") + (col("subtotal") * col("tax_rate")) + col("shipping"), 2)) \
        .withColumn("is_large_order", when(col("subtotal") > 200, True).otherwise(False)) \
        .withColumn("order_category", 
            when(col("subtotal") < 100, "Small")
            .when(col("subtotal") < 300, "Medium")
            .otherwise("Large")
        ) \
        .withColumn("free_shipping_eligible", col("subtotal") >= 100) \
        .withColumn("transaction_month", date_format(col("transaction_date"), "yyyy-MM")) \
        .withColumn("transaction_year", year(col("transaction_date"))) \
        .withColumn("transaction_quarter", quarter(col("transaction_date"))) \
        .withColumn("day_of_week", date_format(col("transaction_date"), "EEEE"))
    
    print("\n--- Transactions with Computed Columns ---")
    transactions_with_computed.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Show schema with computed columns
    print("\n--- Schema with Computed Columns ---")
    transactions_with_computed.printSchema()
    
    # Queries using computed columns (no runtime calculations needed!)
    print("\n--- Query 1: Summary by order category (using pre-computed category) ---")
    category_summary = transactions_with_computed \
        .groupBy("order_category") \
        .agg(
            count("transaction_id").alias("order_count"),
            sum("total_amount").alias("total_revenue"),
            avg("total_amount").alias("avg_order_value")
        ) \
        .orderBy("order_category")
    
    category_summary.show()
    
    print("\n--- Query 2: Large orders analysis (using pre-computed flag) ---")
    large_orders = transactions_with_computed \
        .filter(col("is_large_order") == True) \
        .select(
            "transaction_id",
            "customer_id",
            "subtotal",
            "total_amount",
            "order_category"
        )
    
    large_orders.show()
    
    print("\n--- Query 3: Monthly revenue (using pre-computed month) ---")
    monthly_revenue = transactions_with_computed \
        .groupBy("transaction_month") \
        .agg(
            count("transaction_id").alias("transaction_count"),
            sum("total_amount").alias("monthly_revenue"),
            sum(when(col("free_shipping_eligible"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("free_shipping_orders")
        ) \
        .orderBy("transaction_month")
    
    monthly_revenue.show()
    
    # Advanced: Customer-level computed aggregates
    print("\n--- Advanced: Customer Summary with Computed Aggregates ---")
    
    # Compute customer-level metrics
    customer_summary = transactions_with_computed \
        .groupBy("customer_id") \
        .agg(
            count("transaction_id").alias("total_transactions"),
            sum("total_amount").alias("lifetime_value"),
            avg("total_amount").alias("avg_transaction_value"),
            max("total_amount").alias("largest_transaction"),
            min("transaction_date").alias("first_transaction_date"),
            max("transaction_date").alias("last_transaction_date"),
            sum(when(col("is_large_order"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("large_order_count"),
            sum(when(col("free_shipping_eligible"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("free_shipping_count")
        )
    
    # Add more computed columns at customer level
    customer_summary_enhanced = customer_summary \
        .withColumn("days_as_customer", 
            datediff(col("last_transaction_date"), col("first_transaction_date"))
        ) \
        .withColumn("customer_tier",
            when(col("lifetime_value") >= 1000, "Gold")
            .when(col("lifetime_value") >= 500, "Silver")
            .otherwise("Bronze")
        ) \
        .withColumn("large_order_percentage",
            round((col("large_order_count") / col("total_transactions")) * 100, 2)
        ) \
        .withColumn("avg_days_between_orders",
            when(col("total_transactions") > 1,
                round(col("days_as_customer") / (col("total_transactions") - 1), 2)
            ).otherwise(0)
        )
    
    print("\nCustomer Summary with Computed Aggregates:")
    customer_summary_enhanced.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Running totals and window functions (computed incrementally)
    print("\n--- Advanced: Running Totals (Computed with Window Functions) ---")
    
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy("transaction_date")
    
    transactions_with_running_totals = transactions_with_computed \
        .withColumn("transaction_number", row_number().over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("running_total", sum("total_amount").over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("running_avg", avg("total_amount").over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("cumulative_orders", count("transaction_id").over(window_spec))
    
    print("\nTransactions with Running Totals:")
    transactions_with_running_totals \
        .select(
            "customer_id",
            "transaction_date",
            "total_amount",
            "transaction_number",
            "running_total",
            "running_avg",
            "cumulative_orders"
        ) \
        .orderBy("customer_id", "transaction_date") \
        .show(truncate=False)
    
    # Materialized view pattern: Store computed aggregates separately
    print("\n--- Materialized View: Daily Sales Summary ---")
    
    daily_sales_summary = transactions_with_computed \
        .groupBy("transaction_date") \
        .agg(
            count("transaction_id").alias("daily_transactions"),
            sum("total_amount").alias("daily_revenue"),
            avg("total_amount").alias("avg_transaction"),
            sum("tax_amount").alias("total_tax_collected"),
            sum("shipping").alias("total_shipping_revenue"),
            countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers"),
            sum
```python
            sum(when(col("is_large_order"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("large_orders"),
            sum(when(col("order_category") == "Small", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("small_orders"),
            sum(when(col("order_category") == "Medium", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("medium_orders")
        ) \
        .withColumn("avg_revenue_per_customer", 
            round(col("daily_revenue") / col("unique_customers"), 2)
        ) \
        .withColumn("large_order_percentage",
            round((col("large_orders") / col("daily_transactions")) * 100, 2)
        ) \
        .orderBy("transaction_date")
    
    print("\nDaily Sales Summary (Materialized Computed Aggregates):")
    daily_sales_summary.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Incremental computation pattern
    print("\n--- Incremental Update Strategy ---")
    print("For real-time scenarios, compute incrementally rather than full recalculation:")
    
    # Simulate new transaction
    new_transaction = spark.createDataFrame(
        [(9, 101, "2024-01-23", 180.00, 0.08, 6.00)],
        ["transaction_id", "customer_id", "transaction_date", "subtotal", "tax_rate", "shipping"]
    )
    
    # Apply same computed column logic
    new_transaction_computed = new_transaction \
        .withColumn("tax_amount", round(col("subtotal") * col("tax_rate"), 2)) \
        .withColumn("total_amount", round(col("subtotal") + (col("subtotal") * col("tax_rate")) + col("shipping"), 2)) \
        .withColumn("is_large_order", when(col("subtotal") > 200, True).otherwise(False)) \
        .withColumn("order_category", 
            when(col("subtotal") < 100, "Small")
            .when(col("subtotal") < 300, "Medium")
            .otherwise("Large")
        ) \
        .withColumn("transaction_month", date_format(col("transaction_date"), "yyyy-MM"))
    
    print("\nNew transaction with computed columns:")
    new_transaction_computed.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Merge with existing data
    all_transactions = transactions_with_computed.union(new_transaction_computed)
    
    print(f"\nTotal transactions after merge: {all_transactions.count()}")
    
    print("\n--- Computed Column Pattern Best Practices ---")
    print("✓ Pre-compute expensive calculations (aggregations, complex formulas)")
    print("✓ Store derived categorical values for efficient filtering/grouping")
    print("✓ Calculate date/time components once (month, quarter, day of week)")
    print("✓ Materialize running totals and cumulative metrics")
    print("✓ Use for metrics queried frequently but changing infrequently")
    print("✓ Document computation logic clearly for maintenance")
    print("✓ Implement incremental update strategies for near real-time data")
    print("✓ Consider storage costs vs. computation savings")
    print("✗ Don't compute columns that change with every query context")
    print("✗ Avoid for highly volatile calculated fields")
    
    return transactions_with_computed, customer_summary_enhanced


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 5: REDUNDANT DATA PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Store the same data in multiple formats/structures for different access patterns
# Use Case: Optimize for multiple query patterns without runtime transformations
# ============================================================================

def redundant_data_pattern():
    """
    Redundant Data Pattern: Store the same data in multiple formats optimized 
    for different query patterns. Similar to polyglot persistence but within 
    the same system.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 5: REDUNDANT DATA PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Original product catalog data
    products_data = [
        (1, "Laptop Pro 15", "Electronics", "Computers", 1299.99, 50, ["Intel i7", "16GB RAM", "512GB SSD"], ["laptop", "computer", "portable"]),
        (2, "Wireless Mouse", "Electronics", "Accessories", 29.99, 200, ["Bluetooth", "Ergonomic", "USB-C"], ["mouse", "wireless", "peripheral"]),
        (3, "Mechanical Keyboard", "Electronics", "Accessories", 89.99, 150, ["RGB", "Cherry MX", "USB"], ["keyboard", "mechanical", "gaming"]),
        (4, "4K Monitor", "Electronics", "Displays", 399.99, 75, ["27 inch", "4K", "IPS", "HDR"], ["monitor", "display", "4k"]),
        (5, "USB-C Hub", "Electronics", "Accessories", 49.99, 300, ["7-in-1", "USB 3.0", "HDMI"], ["hub", "adapter", "usb"]),
        (6, "Laptop Bag", "Accessories", "Bags", 59.99, 100, ["Padded", "Water-resistant", "15 inch"], ["bag", "case", "laptop"]),
        (7, "Webcam HD", "Electronics", "Accessories", 79.99, 120, ["1080p", "Auto-focus", "Built-in mic"], ["webcam", "camera", "streaming"]),
        (8, "Desk Lamp", "Furniture", "Lighting", 39.99, 80, ["LED", "Adjustable", "USB powered"], ["lamp", "light", "desk"])
    ]
    
    products_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        products_data,
        ["product_id", "product_name", "category", "subcategory", "price", "stock_quantity", "features", "tags"]
    )
    
    print("\n--- Original Product Data ---")
    products_df.show(truncate=False)
    products_df.printSchema()
    
    # REDUNDANT FORMAT 1: Optimized for category browsing
    # Denormalized with category-level aggregates
    print("\n--- Format 1: Category-Optimized View ---")
    
    category_stats = products_df \
        .groupBy("category", "subcategory") \
        .agg(
            count("product_id").alias("product_count"),
            avg("price").alias("avg_price"),
            min("price").alias("min_price"),
            max("price").alias("max_price"),
            sum("stock_quantity").alias("total_stock")
        )
    
    products_category_view = products_df \
        .join(category_stats, ["category", "subcategory"], "left") \
        .select(
            "product_id",
            "product_name",
            "category",
            "subcategory",
            "price",
            "stock_quantity",
            "features",
            "tags",
            "product_count",
            "avg_price",
            "min_price",
            "max_price",
            "total_stock"
        )
    
    print("\nCategory-Optimized View (with redundant category stats):")
    products_category_view.show(truncate=False)
    
    # REDUNDANT FORMAT 2: Optimized for search (exploded tags)
    print("\n--- Format 2: Search-Optimized View (Exploded Tags) ---")
    
    products_search_view = products_df \
        .select(
            "product_id",
            "product_name",
            "category",
            "subcategory",
            "price",
            "stock_quantity",
            explode("tags").alias("tag")
        ) \
        .withColumn("tag_lower", lower(col("tag")))
    
    print("\nSearch-Optimized View (one row per tag):")
    products_search_view.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Demonstrate search efficiency
    print("\nSearch for 'laptop' (efficient with exploded tags):")
    laptop_search = products_search_view \
        .filter(col("tag_lower").contains("laptop")) \
        .select("product_id", "product_name", "price", "tag") \
        .distinct()
    
    laptop_search.show()
    
    # REDUNDANT FORMAT 3: Optimized for price range queries
    print("\n--- Format 3: Price-Range Optimized View ---")
    
    products_price_view = products_df \
        .withColumn("price_bucket",
            when(col("price") < 50, "Under $50")
            .when(col("price") < 100, "$50-$100")
            .when(col("price") < 500, "$100-$500")
            .otherwise("$500+")
        ) \
        .withColumn("price_tier",
            when(col("price") < 50, "Budget")
            .when(col("price") < 200, "Mid-Range")
            .otherwise("Premium")
        )
    
    # Add price bucket statistics
    price_bucket_stats = products_price_view \
        .groupBy("price_bucket") \
        .agg(
            count("product_id").alias("products_in_bucket"),
            avg("price").alias("bucket_avg_price")
        )
    
    products_price_view = products_price_view \
        .join(price_bucket_stats, "price_bucket", "left")
    
    print("\nPrice-Range Optimized View:")
    products_price_view.select(
        "product_id",
        "product_name",
        "price",
        "price_bucket",
        "price_tier",
        "products_in_bucket",
        "bucket_avg_price"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # REDUNDANT FORMAT 4: Optimized for inventory management
    print("\n--- Format 4: Inventory-Optimized View ---")
    
    products_inventory_view = products_df \
        .withColumn("stock_status",
            when(col("stock_quantity") == 0, "Out of Stock")
            .when(col("stock_quantity") < 50, "Low Stock")
            .when(col("stock_quantity") < 100, "Medium Stock")
            .otherwise("In Stock")
        ) \
        .withColumn("reorder_needed", col("stock_quantity") < 75) \
        .withColumn("stock_value", round(col("price") * col("stock_quantity"), 2)) \
        .select(
            "product_id",
            "product_name",
            "category",
            "price",
            "stock_quantity",
            "stock_status",
            "reorder_needed",
            "stock_value"
        )
    
    print("\nInventory-Optimized View:")
    products_inventory_view.orderBy(desc("stock_value")).show(truncate=False)
    
    # REDUNDANT FORMAT 5: Optimized for analytics (wide format with all metrics)
    print("\n--- Format 5: Analytics-Optimized View (Wide Format) ---")
    
    products_analytics_view = products_df \
        .withColumn("num_features", size("features")) \
        .withColumn("num_tags", size("tags")) \
        .withColumn("features_str", concat_ws(", ", col("features"))) \
        .withColumn("tags_str", concat_ws(", ", col("tags"))) \
        .join(
            products_df.groupBy("category").agg(
                count("product_id").alias("category_product_count"),
                avg("price").alias("category_avg_price")
            ),
            "category",
            "left"
        ) \
        .join(
            products_df.groupBy("subcategory").agg(
                count("product_id").alias("subcategory_product_count")
            ),
            "subcategory",
            "left"
        ) \
        .withColumn("price_vs_category_avg",
            round((col("price") / col("category_avg_price")) * 100, 2)
        )
    
    print("\nAnalytics-Optimized View (all metrics pre-calculated):")
    products_analytics_view.select(
        "product_id",
        "product_name",
        "price",
        "num_features",
        "num_tags",
        "category_product_count",
        "subcategory_product_count",
        "price_vs_category_avg"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Real-world example: E-commerce product views
    print("\n--- Real-World Example: Multiple Product Views for E-commerce ---")
    
    # View 1: Homepage featured products (minimal data)
    homepage_view = products_df \
        .filter(col("stock_quantity") > 0) \
        .select(
            "product_id",
            "product_name",
            "price",
            col("tags")[0].alias("primary_tag")
        ) \
        .limit(5)
    
    print("\nHomepage View (minimal, fast loading):")
    homepage_view.show(truncate=False)
    
    # View 2: Product listing page (medium detail)
    listing_view = products_df \
        .select(
            "product_id",
            "product_name",
            "category",
            "subcategory",
            "price",
            "stock_quantity",
            size("features").alias("feature_count"),
            col("features")[0].alias("top_feature")
        )
    
    print("\nListing Page View (medium detail):")
    listing_view.show(truncate=False)
    
    # View 3: Product detail page (full detail)
    detail_view = products_df \

    category_browse.show()
    
    print("\nQuery 2: Search by tag (optimized with search view)")
    tag_search = products_search_view \

    tag_search.show()
    
    print("\nQuery 3: Filter by price range (optimized with price view)")
    price_filter = products_price_view \

    price_filter.show()
    
    print("\nQuery 4: Inventory management (optimized with inventory view)")
    low_stock = products_inventory_view \
        .filter(col("reorder_needed") == True) \
        .orderBy(desc("stock_value"))
    low_stock.show()
    
    # Storage vs. Performance trade-off analysis
    print("\n--- Storage vs. Performance Trade-off ---")
    print(f"Original table rows: {products_df.count()}")
    print(f"Search view rows (exploded): {products_search_view.count()}")
    print(f"Category view rows:
```python
    print(f"Category view rows: {products_category_view.count()}")
    print(f"Price view rows: {products_price_view.count()}")
    print(f"Inventory view rows: {products_inventory_view.count()}")
    print(f"Analytics view rows: {products_analytics_view.count()}")
    
    print("\nStorage multiplication factor:")
    total_redundant_rows = (
        products_search_view.count() + 
        products_category_view.count() + 
        products_price_view.count() + 
        products_inventory_view.count() + 
        products_analytics_view.count()
    )
    original_rows = products_df.count()
    print(f"Total redundant storage: {total_redundant_rows} rows")
    print(f"Multiplication factor: {total_redundant_rows / original_rows:.2f}x")
    
    # Partitioning strategy for redundant data
    print("\n--- Partitioning Strategy for Redundant Views ---")
    
    # Partition search view by first letter for efficient lookups
    products_search_partitioned = products_search_view \
        .withColumn("tag_first_letter", substring(col("tag_lower"), 1, 1))
    
    print("\nSearch view with partition key (tag_first_letter):")
    products_search_partitioned.show()
    
    # Partition price view by price bucket
    print("\nPrice view partitioned by price_bucket:")
    products_price_view \
        .groupBy("price_bucket") \
        .count() \
        .orderBy("price_bucket") \
        .show()
    
    # Partition inventory view by stock status
    print("\nInventory view partitioned by stock_status:")
    products_inventory_view \
        .groupBy("stock_status") \
        .count() \
        .orderBy("stock_status") \
        .show()
    
    print("\n--- Redundant Data Pattern Best Practices ---")
    print("✓ Create separate views optimized for distinct access patterns")
    print("✓ Use for read-heavy workloads with diverse query patterns")
    print("✓ Partition each redundant view by its primary access key")
    print("✓ Implement automated sync/refresh processes")
    print("✓ Monitor query patterns to identify optimization opportunities")
    print("✓ Consider caching frequently accessed redundant views")
    print("✓ Document the purpose and refresh schedule of each view")
    print("✓ Use appropriate file formats (Parquet, ORC) for each access pattern")
    print("✗ Don't create redundant views for rarely used queries")
    print("✗ Avoid over-partitioning (too many small partitions)")
    print("✗ Not suitable for write-heavy workloads (sync overhead)")
    
    # Demonstrate incremental refresh strategy
    print("\n--- Incremental Refresh Strategy ---")
    
    # Simulate new products
    new_products = spark.createDataFrame([
        (9, "Thunderbolt Cable", "Electronics", "Accessories", 24.99, 250, 
         ["USB4", "40Gbps", "2m"], ["cable", "thunderbolt", "usb"]),
        (10, "Standing Desk", "Furniture", "Desks", 449.99, 30,
         ["Electric", "Adjustable", "Memory presets"], ["desk", "standing", "ergonomic"])
    ], ["product_id", "product_name", "category", "subcategory", "price", "stock_quantity", "features", "tags"])
    
    print("\nNew products to add:")
    new_products.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Refresh strategy: Union new data with existing views
    print("\nRefreshing redundant views with new data...")
    
    # Refresh search view
    new_search_view = new_products \
        .select(
            "product_id",
            "product_name",
            "category",
            "subcategory",
            "price",
            "stock_quantity",
            explode("tags").alias("tag")
        ) \
        .withColumn("tag_lower", lower(col("tag")))
    
    updated_search_view = products_search_view.union(new_search_view)
    print(f"\nSearch view updated: {products_search_view.count()} -> {updated_search_view.count()} rows")
    
    # Refresh price view
    new_price_view = new_products \
        .withColumn("price_bucket",
            when(col("price") < 50, "Under $50")
            .when(col("price") < 100, "$50-$100")
            .when(col("price") < 500, "$100-$500")
            .otherwise("$500+")
        ) \
        .withColumn("price_tier",
            when(col("price") < 50, "Budget")
            .when(col("price") < 200, "Mid-Range")
            .otherwise("Premium")
        )
    
    # Need to recalculate bucket stats after adding new products
    all_products = products_df.union(new_products)
    updated_price_view = all_products \
        .withColumn("price_bucket",
            when(col("price") < 50, "Under $50")
            .when(col("price") < 100, "$50-$100")
            .when(col("price") < 500, "$100-$500")
            .otherwise("$500+")
        ) \
        .withColumn("price_tier",
            when(col("price") < 50, "Budget")
            .when(col("price") < 200, "Mid-Range")
            .otherwise("Premium")
        )
    
    updated_bucket_stats = updated_price_view \
        .groupBy("price_bucket") \
        .agg(
            count("product_id").alias("products_in_bucket"),
            avg("price").alias("bucket_avg_price")
        )
    
    updated_price_view = updated_price_view.join(updated_bucket_stats, "price_bucket", "left")
    
    print(f"Price view updated: {products_price_view.count()} -> {updated_price_view.count()} rows")
    
    print("\nUpdated price buckets:")
    updated_price_view.select("product_name", "price", "price_bucket", "products_in_bucket").show(truncate=False)
    
    return {
        "original": products_df,
        "category_view": products_category_view,
        "search_view": products_search_view,
        "price_view": products_price_view,
        "inventory_view": products_inventory_view,
        "analytics_view": products_analytics_view
    }

            ("Embedded Document", "Hierarchical data", "Medium", "Low", "Low", "User profiles, orders"),
            ("Duplicate Data", "Avoid frequent joins", "High", "Medium", "High", "Event logs, audit trails"),
            ("Computed Column", "Expensive calculations", "Medium", "Low", "Medium", "Financial reports"),
            ("Redundant Data", "Multiple access patterns", "Very High", "High", "High", "E-commerce catalogs")
        ]
        
        comparison_df = spark.createDataFrame(
            comparison_data,
            ["Pattern", "Best For", "Query Speed", "Storage Cost", "Update Complexity", "Example Use Case"]
        )
        
        print("\n--- Pattern Comparison Matrix ---")
        comparison_df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Decision tree for pattern selection
        print("\n--- Pattern Selection Decision Tree ---")
        print("""
        START: What is your primary optimization goal?
        
        ├─ Eliminate repetitive joins?
        │  ├─ Same tables always joined? → PRE-JOIN PATTERN
        │  └─ Different join combinations? → REDUNDANT DATA PATTERN
        │
        ├─ Store hierarchical/nested data?
        │  └─ Parent-child relationships? → EMBEDDED DOCUMENT PATTERN
        │
        ├─ Avoid expensive calculations?
        │  └─ Complex aggregations/formulas? → COMPUTED COLUMN PATTERN
        │
        └─ Need fast lookups without joins?
           └─ Frequently accessed dimensions? → DUPLICATE DATA PATTERN
        
        COMBINED APPROACH:
        - Use multiple patterns together for optimal results
        - Pre-join + Computed columns (common combination)
        - Embedded documents + Duplicate data (for nested hierarchies)
        - Redundant data + Computed columns (for analytics)
        """)
        
        # Performance considerations
        print("\n--- Performance Optimization Tips ---")
        print("""
        1. PRE-JOIN PATTERN:
           • Materialize as Parquet with appropriate partitioning
           • Use broadcast joins for small dimension tables
           • Refresh on a schedule (hourly, daily) based on data freshness needs
        
        2. EMBEDDED DOCUMENT PATTERN:
           • Limit array sizes (avoid unbounded growth)
           • Use for bounded one-to-many relationships
           • Consider separate tables if arrays grow too large
        
        3. DUPLICATE DATA PATTERN:
           • Duplicate only slow-changing dimensions
           • Implement change data capture (CDC) for updates
           • Use versioning for historical accuracy
        
        4. COMPUTED COLUMN PATTERN:
           • Pre-calculate in ETL pipelines
           • Use incremental computation where possible
           • Store intermediate results for complex calculations
        
        5. REDUNDANT DATA PATTERN:
           • Create views for specific access patterns
           • Partition each view by its primary query key
           • Use appropriate compression (Snappy for speed, GZIP for storage)
        """)
        
        # Cost-benefit analysis
        print("\n--- Cost-Benefit Analysis ---")
        
        cost_benefit_data = [
            ("Pre-Join", "Medium", "High", "2-5x faster queries", "Materialized view storage"),
            ("Embedded Document", "Low", "High", "Eliminates joins", "Complex updates"),
            ("Duplicate Data", "High", "Very High", "Zero join cost", "Data consistency overhead"),
            ("Computed Column", "Low", "High", "No runtime calculation", "Storage for computed values"),
            ("Redundant Data", "Very High", "Very High", "Optimized per use case", "Multiple copies of data")
        ]
        
        cost_benefit_df = spark.createDataFrame(

            ["Pattern", "Storage Cost", "Performance Gain", "Primary Benefit", "Primary Trade-off"]
        )
        
        cost_benefit_df.show(truncate=False)

# ============================================================================
