## 3. Hierarchical Quota Pattern

```python
"""
Hierarchical Quota Pattern: Implements nested quota structures.
Supports organizational hierarchies with parent-child quota relationships.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, sum as _sum, when, lit, current_timestamp, broadcast
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, TimestampType
from datetime import datetime
import logging

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("HierarchicalQuotaPattern") \
    .getOrCreate()

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class HierarchicalQuotaManager:
    """
    Manages hierarchical quotas with parent-child relationships.
    Child quotas cannot exceed parent quotas.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        
        # Hierarchical quota schema
        self.quota_schema = StructType([
            StructField("entity_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("parent_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("entity_type", StringType(), False),  # ORG, DEPT, TEAM, USER
            StructField("resource_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("quota_limit", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("current_usage", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("level", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("last_updated", TimestampType(), False)
        ])
    
    def initialize_quotas(self, quota_data):
        """Initialize hierarchical quota structure"""
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(quota_data, schema=self.quota_schema)
    
    def get_hierarchy_path(self, quotas_df, entity_id):
        """
        Get full hierarchy path from entity to root.
        Returns list of entity IDs from child to root.
        """
        path = [entity_id]
        current_df = quotas_df.filter(col("entity_id") == entity_id).first()
        
        while current_df and current_df["parent_id"]:
            parent_id = current_df["parent_id"]
            path.append(parent_id)
            current_df = quotas_df.filter(col("entity_id") == parent_id).first()
        
        return path
    
    def check_hierarchical_quota(self, quotas_df, entity_id, resource_type, requested_amount):
        """
        Check quota availability across entire hierarchy.
        Ensures allocation doesn't violate any parent quota.
        """
        hierarchy_path = self.get_hierarchy_path(quotas_df, entity_id)
        
        # Check each level in hierarchy
        for entity in hierarchy_path:
            entity_quota = quotas_df.filter(
                (col("entity_id") == entity) & 
                (col("resource_type") == resource_type)
            ).first()
            
            if not entity_quota:
                logger.warning(f"No quota defined for entity {entity}, resource {resource_type}")
                return False, f"No quota at level {entity}", 0
            
            available = entity_quota["quota_limit"] - entity_quota["current_usage"]
            
            if requested_amount > available:
                logger.warning(
                    f"Hierarchical quota check failed at {entity} ({entity_quota['entity_type']}): "
                    f"requested {requested_amount}, available {available}"
                )
                return False, f"Quota exceeded at {entity_quota['entity_type']} level", available
        
        return True, "Allocation allowed", requested_amount
    
    def allocate_resource(self, quotas_df, entity_id, resource_type, amount):
        """
        Allocate resources and update all levels in hierarchy.
        Updates current usage for entity and all parents.
        """
        allowed, message, available = self.check_hierarchical_quota(
            quotas_df, entity_id, resource_type, amount
        )
        
        if not allowed:
            raise Exception(f"Hierarchical Quota Violation: {message}. Available: {available}")
        
        hierarchy_path = self.get_hierarchy_path(quotas_df, entity_id)
        
        # Update usage for entity and all parents
        updated_quotas = quotas_df
        for entity in hierarchy_path:
            updated_quotas = updated_quotas.withColumn(
                "current_usage",
                when(
                    (col("entity_id") == entity) & (col("resource_type") == resource_type),
                    col("current_usage") + amount
                ).otherwise(col("current_usage"))
            ).withColumn(
                "last_updated",
                when(
                    (col("entity_id") == entity) & (col("resource_type") == resource_type),
                    current_timestamp()
                ).otherwise(col("last_updated"))
            )
        
        logger.info(f"Allocated {amount} {resource_type} to {entity_id} and updated hierarchy")
        return updated_quotas
    
    def release_resource(self, quotas_df, entity_id, resource_type, amount):
        """
        Release resources and update all levels in hierarchy.
        Decrements usage for entity and all parents.
        """
        hierarchy_path = self.get_hierarchy_path(quotas_df, entity_id)
        
        # Update usage for entity and all parents
        updated_quotas = quotas_df
        for entity in hierarchy_path:
            updated_quotas = updated_quotas.withColumn(
                "current_usage",
                when(
                    (col("entity_id") == entity) & (col("resource_type") == resource_type),
                    when(col("current_usage") - amount >= 0, col("current_usage") - amount).otherwise(0)
                ).otherwise(col("current_usage"))
            ).withColumn(
                "last_updated",
                when(
                    (col("entity_id") == entity) & (col("resource_type") == resource_type),
                    current_timestamp()
                ).otherwise(col("last_updated"))
            )
        
        logger.info(f"Released {amount} {resource_type} from {entity_id} and updated hierarchy")
        return updated_quotas
    
    def get_hierarchy_status(self, quotas_df, resource_type=None):
        """Get quota status with hierarchy visualization"""
        status_df = quotas_df.withColumn(
            "utilization_percent",
            (col("current_usage") / col("quota_limit") * 100).cast("decimal(5,2)")
        ).withColumn(
            "available",
            col("quota_limit") - col("current_usage")
        )
        
        if resource_type:
            status_df = status_df.filter(col("resource_type") == resource_type)
        
        return status_df.orderBy("level", "entity_id")
    
    def validate_hierarchy_integrity(self, quotas_df):
        """
        Validate that child quotas don't exceed parent quotas.
        Returns DataFrame with validation results.
        """
        # Self-join to compare child with parent
        child_df = quotas_df.alias("child")
        parent_df = quotas_df.alias("parent")
        
        validation_df = child_df.join(
            parent_df,
            (col("child.parent_id") == col("parent.entity_id")) &
            (col("child.resource_type") == col("parent.resource_type")),
            "left"
        ).select(
            col("child.entity_id").alias("child_id"),
            col("child.entity_type").alias("child_type"),
            col("parent.entity_id").alias("parent_id"),
            col("parent.entity_type").alias("parent_type"),
            col("child.resource_type"),
            col("child.quota_limit").alias("child_limit"),
            col("parent.quota_limit").alias("parent_limit"),
            col("child.current_usage").alias("child_usage"),
            col("parent.current_usage").alias("parent_usage")
        ).withColumn(
            "quota_valid",
            when(col("parent_limit").isNull(), lit(True))
            .when(col("child_limit") <= col("parent_limit"), lit(True))
            .otherwise(lit(False))
        ).withColumn(
            "usage_valid",
            when(col("parent_usage").isNull(), lit(True))
            .when(col("child_usage") <= col("parent_usage"), lit(True))
            .otherwise(lit(False))
        ).withColumn(
            "overall_valid",
            col("quota_valid") & col("usage_valid")
        )
        
        return validation_df


# Example Usage
if __name__ == "__main__":

## 4. Time-Based Quota Pattern

```python
"""
Time-Based Quota Pattern: Implements quotas that reset or adjust based on time periods.
Supports daily, weekly, monthly quotas with automatic resets.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import (
    col, sum as _sum, when, lit, current_timestamp, 
    date_format, year, month, dayofmonth, weekofyear, hour
)
from pyspark.sql.types import (
    StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, 
    TimestampType, DateType
)
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import logging

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("TimeBasedQuotaPattern") \
    .getOrCreate()

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class TimeBasedQuotaManager:
    """
    Manages time-based quotas with automatic reset periods.
    Supports hourly, daily, weekly, and monthly quota cycles.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        
        # Time-based quota schema
        self.quota_schema = StructType([
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("resource_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("quota_period", StringType(), False),  # HOURLY, DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY
            StructField("quota_limit", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("current_usage", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("period_start", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("period_end", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("last_updated", TimestampType(), False)
        ])
        
        # Usage history schema
        self.history_schema = StructType([
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("resource_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("amount", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("period", StringType(), False)
        ])
    
    def initialize_quotas(self, quota_data):
        """Initialize time-based quotas"""
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(quota_data, schema=self.quota_schema)
    
    def get_current_period_boundaries(self, period_type, reference_time=None):
        """
        Calculate period start and end times based on period type.
        Returns: (period_start, period_end)
        """
        if reference_time is None:
            reference_time = datetime.now()
        
        if period_type == "HOURLY":
            period_start = reference_time.replace(minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
            period_end = period_start + timedelta(hours=1)
        
        elif period_type == "DAILY":
            period_start = reference_time.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
            period_end = period_start + timedelta(days=1)
        
        elif period_type == "WEEKLY":
            # Week starts on Monday
            days_since_monday = reference_time.weekday()
            period_start = (reference_time - timedelta(days=days_since_monday)).replace(
                hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0
            )
            period_end = period_start + timedelta(days=7)
        
        elif period_type == "MONTHLY":
            period_start = reference_time.replace(day=1, hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
            # Next month's first day
            if reference_time.month == 12:
                period_end = period_start.replace(year=reference_time.year + 1, month=1)
            else:
                period_end = period_start.replace(month=reference_time.month + 1)
        
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported period type: {period_type}")
        
        return period_start, period_end
    
    def check_and_reset_quota(self, quotas_df):
        """
        Check if quota periods have expired and reset them.
        Returns updated quotas DataFrame with reset periods.
        """
        from pyspark.sql.functions import udf
        from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, TimestampType
        
        # Define UDF to calculate new period boundaries
        def calculate_new_period(period_type):
            start, end = self.get_current_period_boundaries(period_type)
            return (start, end)
        
        # Check each quota and reset if period expired
        current_time = datetime.now()
        
        updated_quotas = quotas_df.withColumn(
            "needs_reset",
            col("period_end") < lit(current_time)
        )
        
        # Reset quotas where period has expired
        reset_quotas = updated_quotas.rdd.map(lambda row: self._reset_quota_row(row)).toDF()
        
        return reset_quotas
    
    def _reset_quota_row(self, row):
        """Helper function to reset individual quota row"""
        if row["needs_reset"]:
            period_start, period_end = self.get_current_period_boundaries(row["quota_period"])
            return (
                row["user_id"],
                row["resource_type"],
                row["quota_period"],
                row["quota_limit"],
                0,  # Reset current usage
                period_start,
                period_end,
                datetime.now()
            )
        else:
            return (
                row["user_id"],
                row["resource_type"],
                row["quota_period"],
                row["quota_limit"],
                row["current_usage"],
                row["period_start"],
                row["period_end"],
                row["last_updated"]
            )
    
    def check_quota_availability(self, quotas_df, user_id, resource_type, requested_amount):
        """
        Check if requested amount is within time-based quota.
        Automatically resets quota if period expired.
        """
        # First, check and reset expired quotas
        quotas_df = self.check_and_reset_quota(quotas_df)
        
        user_quota = quotas_df.filter(
            (col("user_id") == user_id) & 
            (col("resource_type") == resource_type)
        ).first()
        
        if not user_quota:
            logger.warning(f"No quota defined for user {user_id}, resource {resource_type}")
            return False, 0, quotas_df
        
        available = user_quota["quota_limit"] - user_quota["current_usage"]
        
        if requested_amount <= available:
            logger.info(
                f"Time-based quota check PASSED: User {user_id} can allocate {requested_amount} "
                f"{resource_type} (Period: {user_quota['quota_period']})"
            )
            return True, requested_amount, quotas_df
        else:
            logger.warning(
                f"Time-based quota check FAILED: User {user_id} requested {requested_amount}, "
                f"only {available} available in current {user_quota['quota_period']} period"
            )
            return False, available, quotas_df
    
    def allocate_resource(self, quotas_df, user_id, resource_type, amount, usage_history_df=None):
        """
        Allocate resources within time-based quota.
        Updates quota and optionally records in usage history.
        """
        allowed, available, quotas_df = self.check_quota_availability(
            quotas_df, user_id, resource_type, amount
        )
        
        if not allowed:
            raise Exception(
                f"Time-based quota exceeded: Cannot allocate {amount}. "
                f"Only {available} available in current period."
            )
        
        # Update current usage
        updated_quotas = quotas_df.withColumn(
            "current_usage",
            when(
                (col("user_id") == user_id) & (col("resource_type") == resource_type),
                col("current_usage") + amount
            ).otherwise(col("current_usage"))
        ).withColumn(
            "last_updated",
            when(
                (col("user_id") == user_id) & (col("resource_type") == resource_type),
                current_timestamp()
            ).otherwise(col("last_updated"))
        )
        
        # Record in usage history if provided
        if usage_history_df is not None:
            quota_info = quotas_df.filter(
                (col("user_id") == user_id) & (col("resource_type") == resource_type)
            ).first()
            
            new_history = self.spark.createDataFrame(
                [(user_id, resource_type, amount, datetime.now(), quota_info["quota_period"])],
                schema=self.history_schema
            )
            usage_history_df = usage_history_df.union(new_history)
        
        logger.info(f"Successfully allocated {amount} {resource_type} to user {user_id}")
        
        if usage_history_df is not None:
            return updated_quotas, usage_history_df
        return updated_quotas
    
    def get_quota_status(self, quotas_df):
        """Get time-based quota status with period information"""
        from pyspark.sql.functions import unix_timestamp
        
        current_time = datetime.now()
        
        return quotas_df.withColumn(
            "utilization_percent",
            (col("current_usage") / col("quota_limit") * 100).cast("decimal(5,2)")
        ).withColumn(
            "available",
            col("quota_limit") - col("current_usage")
        ).withColumn(
            "time_remaining_hours",
            ((unix_timestamp(col("period_end")) - unix_timestamp(lit(current_time))) / 3600).cast("decimal(10,2)")
        ).withColumn(
            "period_expired",
            col("period_end") < lit(current_time)
        ).withColumn(
            "status",
            when(col("period_end") < lit(current_time), "EXPIRED")
            .when(col("current_usage") >= col("quota_limit"), "EXHAUSTED")
            .when(col("current_usage") >= col("quota_limit") * 0.9, "CRITICAL")
            .when(col("current_usage") >= col("quota_limit") * 0.75, "WARNING")
            .otherwise("NORMAL")
        )
    
    def get_usage_analytics(self, usage_history_df, user_id=None, period_type=None):
        """
        Analyze usage patterns over time.
        Provides insights into quota consumption trends.
        """
        analytics_df = usage_history_df
        
        if user_id:
            analytics_df = analytics_df.filter(col("user_id") == user_id)
        
        if period_type:
            analytics_df = analytics_df.filter(col("period") == period_type)
        
        # Add time-based grouping columns
        analytics_df = analytics_df.withColumn("date", date_format(col("timestamp"), "yyyy-MM-dd"))
        analytics_df = analytics_df.withColumn("hour", hour(col("timestamp")))
        analytics_df = analytics_df.withColumn("week", weekofyear(col("timestamp")))
        
        # Aggregate usage by different time periods
        daily_usage = analytics_df.groupBy("user_id", "resource_type", "date").agg(
            _sum("amount").alias("daily_total")
        )
        
        hourly_usage = analytics_df.groupBy("user_id", "resource_type", "date", "hour").agg(
            _sum("amount").alias("hourly_total")
        )
        
        return {
            "daily_usage": daily_usage,
            "hourly_usage": hourly_usage,
            "raw_history": analytics_df
        }


# Example Usage
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Initialize Time-Based Quota Manager
    time_quota_manager = TimeBasedQuotaManager(spark)
    
    # Calculate period boundaries
    daily_start, daily_end = time_quota_manager.get_current_period_boundaries("DAILY")
    weekly_start, weekly_end = time_quota_manager.get_current_period_boundaries("WEEKLY")
    monthly_start, monthly_end = time_quota_manager.get_current_period_boundaries("MONTHLY")

    # Initialize usage history
    usage_history_data = [

        ("user_001", "API_CALLS", 200, datetime.now() - timedelta(minutes=15), "HOURLY"),
        ("user_

## 5. Usage-Based Quota Pattern

```python
"""
Usage-Based Quota Pattern: Implements dynamic quotas based on actual usage patterns.
Adjusts quotas based on historical usage, priorities, and resource availability.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import (
    col, sum as _sum, avg as _avg, max as _max, min as _min,
    when, lit, current_timestamp, lag, lead, stddev, percentile_approx
)
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.types import (
    StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, 
    DoubleType, TimestampType, DateType
)
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import logging

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("UsageBasedQuotaPattern") \
    .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
    .getOrCreate()

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class UsageBasedQuotaManager:
    """
    Manages dynamic quotas based on usage patterns and behavior.
    Automatically adjusts quotas based on historical consumption.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        
        # Usage-based quota schema
        self.quota_schema = StructType([
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("resource_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("base_quota", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("current_quota", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("current_usage", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("priority_level", IntegerType(), False),  # 1-5, 5 being highest
            StructField("quota_adjustment_factor", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("last_adjusted", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("last_updated", TimestampType(), False)
        ])
        
        # Usage metrics schema
        self.metrics_schema = StructType([
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("resource_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("usage_amount", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("date", DateType(), False)
        ])
        
        # Usage statistics schema
        self.stats_schema = StructType([
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("resource_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("avg_daily_usage", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("max_daily_usage", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("min_daily_usage", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("stddev_usage", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("percentile_95", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("total_usage", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("days_tracked", IntegerType(), False)
        ])
    
    def initialize_quotas(self, quota_data):
        """Initialize usage-based quotas"""
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(quota_data, schema=self.quota_schema)
    
    def record_usage(self, usage_metrics_df, user_id, resource_type, amount):
        """Record usage event for analysis"""
        new_metric = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            [(user_id, resource_type, amount, datetime.now(), datetime.now().date())],
            schema=self.metrics_schema
        )
        
        if usage_metrics_df is None:
            return new_metric
        
        return usage_metrics_df.union(new_metric)
    
    def calculate_usage_statistics(self, usage_metrics_df, lookback_days=30):
        """
        Calculate usage statistics for quota adjustment.
        Analyzes patterns over specified lookback period.
        """
        cutoff_date = datetime.now().date() - timedelta(days=lookback_days)
        
        # Filter recent usage
        recent_usage = usage_metrics_df.filter(col("date") >= lit(cutoff_date))
        
        # Calculate daily aggregates
        daily_usage = recent_usage.groupBy("user_id", "resource_type", "date").agg(
            _sum("usage_amount").alias("daily_usage")
        )
        
        # Calculate statistics
        usage_stats = daily_usage.groupBy("user_id", "resource_type").agg(
            _avg("daily_usage").alias("avg_daily_usage"),
            _max("daily_usage").alias("max_daily_usage"),
            _min("daily_usage").alias("min_daily_usage"),
            stddev("daily_usage").alias("stddev_usage"),
            percentile_approx("daily_usage", 0.95).alias("percentile_95"),
            _sum("daily_usage").alias("total_usage"),
            col("date").alias("days_tracked")
        ).withColumn(
            "days_tracked",
            lit(lookback_days)
        )
        
        return usage_stats
    
    def adjust_quotas_based_on_usage(self, quotas_df, usage_stats_df, adjustment_policy="PERCENTILE_95"):
        """
        Adjust quotas based on usage patterns.
        
        Adjustment Policies:
        - PERCENTILE_95: Set quota to 95th percentile of daily usage
        - AVERAGE_PLUS_STDDEV: Set quota to average + 2 * stddev
        - MAX_USAGE: Set quota to historical maximum usage
        - PRIORITY_WEIGHTED: Adjust based on priority level and usage
        """
        # Join quotas with usage statistics
        joined_df = quotas_df.alias("q").join(
            usage_stats_df.alias("s"),
            (col("q.user_id") == col("s.user_id")) & 
            (col("q.resource_type") == col("s.resource_type")),
            "left"
        )
        
        # Calculate new quota based on policy
        if adjustment_policy == "PERCENTILE_95":
            adjusted_df = joined_df.withColumn(
                "calculated_quota",
                when(
                    col("s.percentile_95").isNotNull(),
                    (col("s.percentile_95") * 1.2).cast("integer")  # 20% buffer
                ).otherwise(col("q.base_quota"))
            )
        
        elif adjustment_policy == "AVERAGE_PLUS_STDDEV":
            adjusted_df = joined_df.withColumn(
                "calculated_quota",
                when(
                    col("s.avg_daily_usage").isNotNull(),
                    (col("s.avg_daily_usage") + 2 * col("s.stddev_usage")).cast("integer")
                ).otherwise(col("q.base_quota"))
            )
        
        elif adjustment_policy == "MAX_USAGE":
            adjusted_df = joined_df.withColumn(
                "calculated_quota",
                when(
                    col("s.max_daily_usage").isNotNull(),
                    (col("s.max_daily_usage") * 1.1).cast("integer")  # 10% buffer
                ).otherwise(col("q.base_quota"))
            )
        
        elif adjustment_policy == "PRIORITY_WEIGHTED":
            adjusted_df = joined_df.withColumn(
                "calculated_quota",
                when(
                    col("s.percentile_95").isNotNull(),
                    (col("s.percentile_95") * (1 + col("q.priority_level") * 0.1)).cast("integer")
                ).otherwise(col("q.base_quota"))
            )
        
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported adjustment policy: {adjustment_policy}")
        
        # Apply minimum and maximum bounds
        adjusted_df = adjusted_df.withColumn(
            "new_quota",
            when(
                col("calculated_quota") < col("q.base_quota") * 0.5,
                (col("q.base_quota") * 0.5).cast("integer")  # Min 50% of base
            ).when(
                col("calculated_quota") > col("q.base_quota") * 3,
                (col("q.base_quota") * 3).cast("integer")  # Max 300% of base
            ).otherwise(col("calculated_quota"))
        )
        
        # Calculate adjustment factor
        adjusted_df = adjusted_df.withColumn(
            "new_adjustment_factor",
            (col("new_quota") / col("q.base_quota")).cast("double")
        )
        
        # Update quota DataFrame
        updated_quotas = adjusted_df.select(
            col("q.user_id").alias("user_id"),
            col("q.resource_type").alias("resource_type"),
            col("q.base_quota").alias("base_quota"),
            col("new_quota").alias("current_quota"),
            col("q.current_usage").alias("current_usage"),
            col("q.priority_level").alias("priority_level"),
            col("new_adjustment_factor").alias("quota_adjustment_factor"),
            current_timestamp().alias("last_adjusted"),
            col("q.last_updated").alias("last_updated")
        )
        
        logger.info(f"Adjusted quotas using policy: {adjustment_policy}")
        return updated_quotas
    
    def allocate_resource(self, quotas_df, user_id, resource_type, amount, usage_metrics_df=None):
        """
        Allocate resources within usage-based quota.
        Optionally records usage for future adjustments.
        """
        user_quota = quotas_df.filter(
            (col("user_id") == user_id) & 
            (col("resource_type") == resource_type)
        ).first()
        
        if not user_quota:
            raise Exception(f"No quota defined for user {user_id}, resource {resource_type}")
        
        available = user_quota["current_quota"] - user_quota["current_usage"]
        
        if amount > available:
            raise Exception(
                f"Usage-based quota exceeded: Cannot allocate {amount}. "
                f"Only {available} available (Current quota: {user_quota['current_quota']})"
            )
        
        # Update current usage
        updated_quotas = quotas_df.withColumn(
            "current_usage",
            when(
                (col("user_id") == user_id) & (col("resource_type") == resource_type),
                col("current_usage") + amount
            ).otherwise(col("current_usage"))
        ).withColumn(
            "last_updated",
            when(
                (col("user_id") == user_id) & (col("resource_type") == resource_type),
                current_timestamp()
            ).otherwise(col("last_updated"))
        )
        
        # Record usage for future analysis
        if usage_metrics_df is not None:
            usage_metrics_df = self.record_usage(usage_metrics_df, user_id, resource_type, amount)
            logger.info(f"Allocated {amount} {resource_type} to {user_id} and recorded usage")
            return updated_quotas, usage_metrics_df
        
        logger.info(f"Allocated {amount} {resource_type} to {user_id}")
        return updated_quotas
    
    def get_quota_recommendations(self, quotas_df, usage_stats_df):
        """
        Generate quota adjustment recommendations based on usage patterns.
        Identifies users who need quota increases or decreases.
        """
        joined_df = quotas_df.alias("q").join(
            usage_stats_df.alias("s"),
            (col("q.user_id") == col("s.user_id")) & 
            (col("q.resource_type") == col("s.resource_type")),
            "left"
        )
        
        recommendations = joined_df.withColumn(
            "avg_utilization_percent",
            when(

            ).otherwise(lit(0))
        ).withColumn(
            "peak_utilization_percent",

        ).withColumn(

            .otherwise("MAINTAIN")
        ).withColumn(

            when(
                col("recommendation").like("INCREASE%"),

                col("recommendation").like("DECREASE%"),
                (col("s.avg_daily_usage") * 1.2).cast("integer")
            ).otherwise(col("q.current_quota"))

        return recommendations.select(
            col("q.user_id"),

    def get_quota_status(self, quotas_df):
        """Get comprehensive usage-based quota status"""
        return quotas_df.withColumn(
            "utilization_percent",
            (col("current_usage") / col("current_quota") * 100).cast("decimal(5,2)")
        ).withColumn(
            "available",
            col("current_quota") - col("current_usage")
        ).withColumn(
            "quota_vs_base_percent",
            ((col("current_quota") - col("base_quota")) / col("base_quota") * 100).cast("decimal(5,2)")
        ).withColumn(
            "status",
            when(col("current_usage") >= col("current_quota"), "EXHAUSTED")
            .when(col("current_usage") >= col("current_quota") * 0.9, "CRITICAL")
            .when(col("current_usage") >= col("current_quota") * 0.75, "WARNING")
            .when(col("current_usage") < col("current_quota") * 0.3, "UNDERUTILIZED")
            .otherwise("NORMAL")
        )
    
    def analyze_usage_trends(self, usage_metrics_df, user_id=None):
        """
        Analyze usage trends over time.
        Identifies patterns like increasing/decreasing usage.
        """
        df = usage_metrics_df
        if user_id:
            df = df.filter(col("user_id") == user_id)
        
        # Calculate daily totals
        daily_totals = df.groupBy("user_id", "resource_type", "date").agg(
            _sum("usage_amount").alias("daily_usage")
        )
        
        # Create window for trend analysis
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("user_id", "resource_type").orderBy("date")
        
        # Calculate moving averages and trends
        trend_df = daily_totals.withColumn(
            "prev_usage",
            lag("daily_usage", 1).over(window_spec)
        ).withColumn(
            "next_usage",
            lead("daily_usage", 1).over(window_spec)
        ).withColumn(
            "usage_change",
            when(
                col("prev_usage").isNotNull(),
                col("daily_usage") - col("prev_usage")
            ).otherwise(lit(0))
        ).withColumn(
            "usage_change_percent",
            when(
                (col("prev_usage").isNotNull()) & (col("prev_usage") > 0),
                ((col("daily_usage") - col("prev_usage")) / col("prev_usage") * 100).cast("decimal(5,2)")
            ).otherwise(lit(0))
        )
        
        # Calculate 7-day moving average
        window_7day = Window.partitionBy("user_id", "resource_type").orderBy("date").rowsBetween(-6, 0)
        
        trend_df = trend_df.withColumn(
            "moving_avg_7day",
            _avg("daily_usage").over(window_7day)
        )
        
        return trend_df
    
    def predict_future_quota_needs(self, usage_metrics_df, forecast_days=30):
        """
        Predict future quota needs based on historical trends.
        Simple linear trend projection.
        """
        # Calculate daily usage
        daily_usage = usage_metrics_df.groupBy("user_id", "resource_type", "date").agg(
            _sum("usage_amount").alias("daily_usage")
        )
        
        # Calculate average daily growth rate
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("user_id", "resource_type").orderBy("date")
        
        growth_df = daily_usage.withColumn(
            "prev_usage",
            lag("daily_usage", 1).over(window_spec)
        ).withColumn(
            "daily_growth_rate",
            when(
                (col("prev_usage").isNotNull()) & (col("prev_usage") > 0),
                (col("daily_usage") - col("prev_usage")) / col("prev_usage")
            ).otherwise(lit(0))
        )
        
        # Calculate average growth rate per user/resource
        avg_growth = growth_df.groupBy("user_id", "resource_type").agg(
            _avg("daily_growth_rate").alias("avg_growth_rate"),
            _max("daily_usage").alias("current_max_usage")
        )
        
        # Project future needs
        predictions = avg_growth.withColumn(
            "predicted_daily_usage",
            (col("current_max_usage") * (1 + col("avg_growth_rate") * forecast_days)).cast("integer")
        ).withColumn(
            "recommended_quota",
            (col("predicted_daily_usage") * 1.2).cast("integer")  # 20% safety buffer
        ).withColumn(
            "forecast_days",
            lit(forecast_days)
        )
        
        return predictions

## Summary and Best Practices

```python
"""
RESOURCE QUOTA PATTERNS - SUMMARY AND BEST PRACTICES

1. HARD QUOTA PATTERN
   - Use when: Strict resource limits must be enforced
   - Benefits: Predictable resource allocation, prevents oversubscription
   - Considerations: May reject valid requests during temporary spikes
   - Best for: Production systems, billing systems, SLA guarantees

2. SOFT QUOTA PATTERN
   - Use when: Flexibility needed with warnings
   - Benefits: Accommodates temporary bursts, user-friendly
   - Considerations: Requires monitoring grace periods
   - Best for: Development environments, internal tools

3. HIERARCHICAL QUOTA PATTERN
   - Use when: Multi-level organizational structures exist
   - Benefits: Delegated quota management, fair distribution
   - Considerations: Complex to maintain, cascading updates
   - Best for: Enterprise systems, multi-tenant platforms

4. TIME-BASED QUOTA PATTERN
   - Use when: Resources reset periodically
   - Benefits: Fair allocation over time, prevents hoarding
   - Considerations: Requires period tracking, reset logic
   - Best for: API rate limiting, subscription services

5. USAGE-BASED QUOTA PATTERN
   - Use when: Dynamic adjustment based on behavior needed
   - Benefits: Optimizes resource allocation, adapts to patterns
   - Considerations: Requires historical data, complex calculations
   - Best for: Cloud services, adaptive systems

IMPLEMENTATION TIPS:
- Use broadcast joins for small quota lookup tables
- Implement atomic updates to prevent race conditions
- Cache frequently accessed quota data
- Use checkpointing for long-running quota adjustments
- Implement comprehensive logging and monitoring
- Consider using Delta Lake for ACID transactions
- Implement quota alerts and notifications
- Regular quota audits and cleanup
- Performance optimization with partitioning by user_id or resource_type
"""

print(__doc__)

def direct_lookup_pattern():
    """
    Direct Lookup Pattern: Simple join-based lookup without optimization
    
    Use Case:
    - Small to medium-sized datasets
    - One-time lookups
    - When data doesn't need to be reused
    
    Advantages:
    - Simple and straightforward
    - No additional memory overhead
    
    Disadvantages:
    - Can be slow for large datasets
    - No optimization for repeated lookups
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 1: DIRECT LOOKUP PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    transactions_df, customers_df, _ = create_sample_data()
    
    # Direct join lookup - most basic approach
    result = transactions_df.join(
        customers_df,
        on="customer_id",
        how="left"
    ).select(
        "transaction_id",
        "customer_name",
        "tier",
        "amount",
        "transaction_date"
    )
    
    print("\n--- Direct Lookup Result ---")
    result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Example: Multiple direct lookups (inefficient for repeated use)
    print("\n--- Filtering with Direct Lookup ---")
    gold_customers = result.filter(col("tier") == "Gold")
    gold_customers.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Show execution plan
    print("\n--- Execution Plan ---")
    result.explain(extended=False)
    
    return result

# ============================================================================
def index_lookup_pattern():
    """
    Index Lookup Pattern: Using partitioning and bucketing for optimized lookups
    
    Use Case:
    - Large datasets with frequent lookups
    - When join keys are known in advance
    - Repeated queries on same data
    
    Advantages:
    - Faster lookups through data organization
    - Reduces shuffle operations
    - Better for repeated queries
    
    Disadvantages:
    - Requires preprocessing
    - Additional storage overhead
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 2: INDEX LOOKUP PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    transactions_df, customers_df, _ = create_sample_data()
    
    # Create indexed/partitioned versions of data
    # Repartition by lookup key for better performance
    indexed_transactions = transactions_df.repartition(4, "customer_id")
    indexed_customers = customers_df.repartition(4, "customer_id")
    
    # Cache the indexed data for repeated use
    indexed_transactions.cache()
    indexed_customers.cache()
    
    # Perform lookup with indexed data
    result = indexed_transactions.join(
        indexed_customers,
        on="customer_id",
        how="left"
    ).select(
        "transaction_id",
        "customer_name",
        "tier",
        "amount",
        "country"
    )
    
    print("\n--- Index Lookup Result ---")
    result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Demonstrate efficiency with multiple queries
    print("\n--- Multiple Queries on Indexed Data ---")
    usa_transactions = result.filter(col("country") == "USA")
    print("USA Transactions:")
    usa_transactions.show(truncate=False)
    
    high_value = result.filter(col("amount") > 2000)
    print("High Value Transactions:")
    high_value.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Show partition information
    print(f"\n--- Partition Information ---")
    print(f"Transactions Partitions: {indexed_transactions.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    print(f"Customers Partitions: {indexed_customers.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    return result


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 3: CACHE LOOKUP PATTERN
# ============================================================================
def cache_lookup_pattern():
    """
    Cache Lookup Pattern: Caching lookup tables in memory for fast access
    
    Use Case:
    - Frequently accessed lookup tables
    - Static or slowly changing reference data
    - Multiple operations on same data
    
    Advantages:
    - Extremely fast repeated lookups
    - Reduces recomputation
    - Optimal for iterative algorithms
    
    Disadvantages:
    - Memory consumption
    - Not suitable for very large lookup tables
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 3: CACHE LOOKUP PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    transactions_df, customers_df, products_df = create_sample_data()
    
    # Cache lookup tables in memory
    customers_df.cache()
    products_df.cache()
    
    # Force caching by triggering an action
    print(f"\n--- Caching Lookup Tables ---")
    print(f"Customers cached: {customers_df.count()} records")
    print(f"Products cached: {products_df.count()} records")
    
    # Perform multiple lookups using cached data
    print("\n--- First Lookup (Customer Info) ---")
    result1 = transactions_df.join(
        customers_df,
        on="customer_id",
        how="left"
    )
    result1.show(5, truncate=False)
    
    # Second lookup on same cached data (much faster)
    print("\n--- Second Lookup (Aggregation by Tier) ---")
    tier_summary = result1.groupBy("tier").agg(
        count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
        sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
        avg("amount").alias("avg_amount")
    ).orderBy(desc("total_amount"))
    tier_summary.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Third lookup - country-wise analysis
    print("\n--- Third Lookup (Country Analysis) ---")
    country_summary = result1.groupBy("country").agg(
        countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers"),
        sum("amount").alias("total_revenue")
    ).orderBy(desc("total_revenue"))
    country_summary.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Check cache status
    print("\n--- Cache Statistics ---")
    print(f"Customers is cached: {customers_df.is_cached}")
    print(f"Storage Level: {customers_df.storageLevel}")
    
    # Unpersist when done
    customers_df.unpersist()
    products_df.unpersist()
    
    return result1


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 4: BROADCAST LOOKUP PATTERN
# ============================================================================
def broadcast_lookup_pattern():
    """
    Broadcast Lookup Pattern: Broadcasting small lookup tables to all nodes
    
    Use Case:
    - Small dimension tables (< 10MB typically)
    - Joining large fact table with small dimension
    - Avoiding shuffle operations
    
    Advantages:
    - No shuffle required
    - Extremely fast for small lookup tables
    - Reduces network overhead
    
    Disadvantages:
    - Limited to small datasets
    - Memory overhead on all executors
    - Can cause OOM if table is too large
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 4: BROADCAST LOOKUP PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    transactions_df, customers_df, _ = create_sample_data()
    
    # Broadcast the smaller lookup table
    print("\n--- Broadcasting Customer Lookup Table ---")
    broadcasted_customers = broadcast(customers_df)
    
    # Perform broadcast join
    result = transactions_df.join(
        broadcasted_customers,
        on="customer_id",
        how="left"
    ).select(
        "transaction_id",
        "customer_name",
        "tier",
        "country",
        "amount"
    )
    
    print("\n--- Broadcast Join Result ---")
    result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Show that this is a broadcast join in the plan
    print("\n--- Execution Plan (Note: BroadcastHashJoin) ---")
    result.explain(extended=False)
    
    # Example: Multiple broadcast joins
    print("\n--- Complex Query with Broadcast ---")
    complex_result = transactions_df.join(
        broadcast(customers_df),
        on="customer_id",
        how="left"
    ).filter(
        col("tier").isin(["Gold", "Platinum"])
    ).groupBy("tier", "country").agg(
        count("*").alias("txn_count"),
        sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
        avg("amount").alias("avg_amount")
    ).orderBy(desc("total_amount"))
    
    complex_result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Performance comparison
    print("\n--- Performance Comparison ---")
    
    # Without broadcast
    start_time = time.time()
    regular_join = transactions_df.join(customers_df, "customer_id").count()
    regular_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    # With broadcast
    start_time = time.time()
    broadcast_join = transactions_df.join(broadcast(customers_df), "customer_id").count()
    broadcast_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    print(f"Regular Join Time: {regular_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"Broadcast Join Time: {broadcast_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"Speedup: {regular_time/broadcast_time:.2f}x")
    
    return result

# PATTERN 5: HASH LOOKUP PATTERN
# ============================================================================
def hash_lookup_pattern():
    """
    Hash Lookup Pattern: Using hash-based data structures for O(1) lookups
    
    Use Case:
    - Key-value pair lookups
    - When you need to enrich data with lookup values
    - Custom lookup logic required
    
    Advantages:
    - O(1) lookup time complexity
    - Flexible for custom logic
    - Good for complex transformations
    
    Disadvantages:
    - Requires converting to map/dictionary
    - Memory overhead for hash structure
    - Not suitable for very large lookup tables
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 5: HASH LOOKUP PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    transactions_df, customers_df, _ = create_sample_data()
    
    # Method 1: Using map type column
    print("\n--- Method 1: Map Type Column Approach ---")
    
    # Create a map of customer_id -> customer_info
    customer_map = customers_df.select(
        col("customer_id"),
        struct(
            col("customer_name"),
            col("tier"),
            col("country")
        ).alias("customer_info")
    ).groupBy().agg(
        map_from_entries(
            collect_list(
                struct("customer_id", "customer_info")
            )
        ).alias("customer_lookup")
    )
    
    # Broadcast the map for efficient lookup
    customer_map_broadcast = customer_map.first()["customer_lookup"]
    
    # Create UDF for hash lookup
    def lookup_customer_info(customer_id, lookup_map):
        if customer_id in lookup_map:
            info = lookup_map[customer_id]
            return f"{info.customer_name}|{info.tier}|{info.country}"
        return "Unknown|Unknown|Unknown"
    
    lookup_udf = udf(lambda x: lookup_customer_info(x, customer_map_broadcast), StringType())
    
    # Apply hash lookup
    result1 = transactions_df.withColumn(
        "customer_details",
        lookup_udf(col("customer_id"))
    ).withColumn(
        "customer_name", split(col("customer_details"), "\\|")[0]
    ).withColumn(
        "tier", split(col("customer_details"), "\\|")[1]
    ).withColumn(
        "country", split(col("customer_details"), "\\|")[2]
    ).drop("customer_details")
```python
    
    print("\n--- Hash Lookup Result (Method 1) ---")
    result1.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Method 2: Using Python dictionary broadcast
    print("\n--- Method 2: Python Dictionary Broadcast Approach ---")
    
    # Collect lookup table as dictionary
    customer_dict = {
        row['customer_id']: {
            'name': row['customer_name'],
            'tier': row['tier'],
            'country': row['country']
        }
        for row in customers_df.collect()
    }
    
    # Broadcast the dictionary
    broadcast_dict = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(customer_dict)
    
    # Create UDF using broadcasted dictionary
    def hash_lookup(customer_id):
        lookup_table = broadcast_dict.value
        if customer_id in lookup_table:
            info = lookup_table[customer_id]
            return (info['name'], info['tier'], info['country'])
        return ("Unknown", "Unknown", "Unknown")
    
    hash_lookup_udf = udf(hash_lookup, StructType([
        StructField("customer_name", StringType()),
        StructField("tier", StringType()),
        StructField("country", StringType())
    ]))
    
    # Apply hash lookup
    result2 = transactions_df.withColumn(
        "customer_info",
        hash_lookup_udf(col("customer_id"))
    ).select(
        "transaction_id",
        "customer_id",
        "customer_info.customer_name",
        "customer_info.tier",
        "customer_info.country",
        "amount",
        "transaction_date"
    )
    
    print("\n--- Hash Lookup Result (Method 2) ---")
    result2.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Method 3: Using map_from_arrays for inline hash lookup
    print("\n--- Method 3: Inline Map Lookup Approach ---")
    
    # Create arrays for keys and values
    keys_values = customers_df.select(
        collect_list("customer_id").alias("keys"),
        collect_list(
            struct("customer_name", "tier", "country")
        ).alias("values")
    ).first()
    
    # Create a literal map
    from pyspark.sql.functions import create_map, lit, array
    
    # Build map entries
    map_entries = []
    for k, v in zip(keys_values['keys'], keys_values['values']):
        map_entries.extend([
            lit(k),
            lit(f"{v.customer_name}|{v.tier}|{v.country}")
        ])
    
    # Apply inline lookup
    result3 = transactions_df.withColumn(
        "customer_info",
        create_map(*map_entries)[col("customer_id")]
    ).withColumn(
        "customer_name", split(col("customer_info"), "\\|")[0]
    ).withColumn(
        "tier", split(col("customer_info"), "\\|")[1]
    ).withColumn(
        "country", split(col("customer_info"), "\\|")[2]
    ).drop("customer_info")
    
    print("\n--- Inline Map Lookup Result (Method 3) ---")
    result3.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Method 4: Advanced - Hash-based partitioning with custom lookup
    print("\n--- Method 4: Hash Partitioned Lookup ---")
    
    # Hash partition both datasets on join key
    def hash_partition_key(key, num_partitions=4):
        return hash(key) % num_partitions
    
    hash_partition_udf = udf(lambda x: hash_partition_key(x), IntegerType())
    
    # Add hash partition column
    transactions_hashed = transactions_df.withColumn(
        "hash_partition",
        hash_partition_udf(col("customer_id"))
    )
    
    customers_hashed = customers_df.withColumn(
        "hash_partition",
        hash_partition_udf(col("customer_id"))
    )
    
    # Repartition by hash
    transactions_partitioned = transactions_hashed.repartition("hash_partition")
    customers_partitioned = customers_hashed.repartition("hash_partition")
    
    # Join on both hash partition and customer_id
    result4 = transactions_partitioned.join(
        customers_partitioned,
        on=["customer_id", "hash_partition"],
        how="left"
    ).select(
        "transaction_id",
        "customer_name",
        "tier",
        "country",
        "amount",
        "hash_partition"
    )
    
    print("\n--- Hash Partitioned Lookup Result ---")
    result4.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Performance metrics
    print("\n--- Hash Lookup Performance Metrics ---")
    print(f"Dictionary size: {len(customer_dict)} entries")
    print(f"Hash partitions: {result4.select('hash_partition').distinct().count()}")
    
    # Cleanup
    broadcast_dict.unpersist()
    
    return result2

# COMPREHENSIVE COMPARISON AND BEST PRACTICES
# ============================================================================
def compare_all_patterns():
    """
    Compare all lookup patterns and provide recommendations
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COMPREHENSIVE PATTERN COMPARISON")
    print("="*80)
    
    transactions_df, customers_df, _ = create_sample_data()
    
    patterns = {
        "Direct Lookup": lambda: transactions_df.join(customers_df, "customer_id"),
        "Index Lookup": lambda: transactions_df.repartition("customer_id").join(
            customers_df.repartition("customer_id"), "customer_id"
        ),
        "Cache Lookup": lambda: transactions_df.join(customers_df.cache(), "customer_id"),
        "Broadcast Lookup": lambda: transactions_df.join(broadcast(customers_df), "customer_id"),
    }
    
    print("\n--- Performance Comparison ---")
    print(f"{'Pattern':<20} {'Time (sec)':<15} {'Records':<10}")
    print("-" * 50)
    
    results = {}
    for pattern_name, pattern_func in patterns.items():
        start_time = time.time()
        result = pattern_func()
        count = result.count()
        elapsed_time = time.time() - start_time
        results[pattern_name] = elapsed_time
        print(f"{pattern_name:<20} {elapsed_time:<15.4f} {count:<10}")
    
    # Recommendations
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN SELECTION GUIDE")
    print("="*80)
    
    recommendations = """
    1. DIRECT LOOKUP PATTERN
       Use When:
       - Simple one-time lookups
       - Both datasets are similar in size
       - Memory is limited
       
       Example Use Cases:
       - Ad-hoc analysis
       - Data exploration
       - Simple ETL jobs
    
    2. INDEX LOOKUP PATTERN
       Use When:
       - Large datasets with repeated queries
       - Join keys are known in advance
       - Need to optimize shuffle operations
       
       Example Use Cases:
       - Data warehouse queries
       - Repeated analytical queries
       - Large-scale batch processing
    
    3. CACHE LOOKUP PATTERN
       Use When:
       - Lookup table accessed multiple times
       - Iterative algorithms
       - Interactive analysis sessions
       
       Example Use Cases:
       - Machine learning pipelines
       - Interactive dashboards
       - Multi-step transformations
    
    4. BROADCAST LOOKUP PATTERN
       Use When:
       - Lookup table is small (<10MB)
       - Joining large fact with small dimension
       - Want to avoid shuffle completely
       
       Example Use Cases:
       - Dimension table lookups
       - Reference data enrichment
       - Star schema queries
    
    5. HASH LOOKUP PATTERN
       Use When:
       - Need O(1) lookup performance
       - Custom lookup logic required
       - Working with key-value pairs
       
       Example Use Cases:
       - Complex transformations
       - Custom business rules
       - Dynamic lookup logic
    """
    
    print(recommendations)
    
    # Best practices summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("BEST PRACTICES")
    print("="*80)
    
    best_practices = """
    1. Size Matters:
       - Small lookup (<10MB): Use Broadcast
       - Medium lookup (10MB-1GB): Use Cache + Index
       - Large lookup (>1GB): Use Index or Direct
    
    2. Access Frequency:
       - One-time: Direct Lookup
       - Multiple times: Cache Lookup
       - Continuous: Broadcast or Hash
    
    3. Memory Considerations:
       - Limited memory: Direct or Index
       - Ample memory: Cache or Broadcast
       - Custom control: Hash with manual management
    
    4. Performance Optimization:
       - Always broadcast small dimension tables
       - Cache frequently accessed data
       - Use appropriate partitioning strategy
       - Monitor memory usage
    
    5. Data Characteristics:
       - Static data: Broadcast or Cache
       - Dynamic data: Direct or Index
       - Skewed data: Hash partitioning
    """
    
    print(best_practices)

def advanced_lookup_scenarios():
    """
    Demonstrate advanced real-world lookup scenarios
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED LOOKUP SCENARIOS")
    print("="*80)
    
    transactions_df, customers_df, products_df = create_sample_data()
    
    # Scenario 1: Multi-level lookup (chained lookups)
    print("\n--- Scenario 1: Multi-Level Lookup ---")
    
    # Create order items data
    order_items_data = [
        (1, "TXN001", "P001", 2),
        (2, "TXN001", "P002", 1),
        (3, "TXN002", "P003", 3),
        (4, "TXN003", "P004", 5),
        (5, "TXN004", "P001", 1),
    ]
    
    order_items_schema = StructType([
        StructField("item_id", IntegerType()),
        StructField("transaction_id", StringType()),
        StructField("product_id", StringType()),
        StructField("quantity", IntegerType())
    ])
    
    order_items_df = spark.createDataFrame(order_items_data, order_items_schema)
    
    # Multi-level lookup: Orders -> Transactions -> Customers + Products
    enriched_orders = order_items_df \
        .join(broadcast(products_df), "product_id", "left") \
        .join(transactions_df, "transaction_id", "left") \
        .join(broadcast(customers_df), "customer_id", "left") \
        .select(
            "item_id",
            "transaction_id",
            "customer_name",
            "tier",
            "product_name",
            "category",
            "quantity",
            (col("quantity") * col("price")).alias("line_total")
        )
    
    print("Multi-Level Lookup Result:")
    enriched_orders.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Scenario 2: Conditional lookup (different lookup tables based on condition)
    print("\n--- Scenario 2: Conditional Lookup ---")
    
    # Create premium and standard pricing tables
    premium_pricing = spark.createDataFrame([
        ("P001", 0.9),  # 10% discount
        ("P002", 0.85),  # 15% discount
        ("P003", 0.95),
    ], ["product_id", "discount_factor"])
    
    standard_pricing = spark.createDataFrame([
        ("P001", 1.0),  # No discount
        ("P002", 1.0),
        ("P003", 1.0),
    ], ["product_id", "discount_factor"])
    
    # Apply conditional lookup based on customer tier
    conditional_result = enriched_orders \
        .join(
            when(col("tier") == "Platinum", broadcast(premium_pricing))
            .otherwise(broadcast(standard_pricing))
            .alias("pricing"),
            "product_id",
            "left"
        )
    
    # Note: Above won't work directly, here's the correct approach
    enriched_with_pricing = enriched_orders \
        .join(
            premium_pricing.withColumnRenamed("discount_factor", "premium_discount"),
            "product_id",
            "left"
        ) \
        .join(
            standard_pricing.withColumnRenamed("discount_factor", "standard_discount"),
            "product_id",
            "left"
        ) \
        .withColumn(
            "final_discount",
            when(col("tier") == "Platinum", col("premium_discount"))
            .otherwise(col("standard_discount"))
        ) \
        .withColumn(
            "discounted_total",
            col("line_total") * col("final_discount")
        ) \
        .select(
            "transaction_id",
            "customer_name",
            "tier",
            "product_name",
            "line_total",
            "final_discount",
            "discounted_total"
        )
    
    print("Conditional Lookup Result:")
    enriched_with_pricing.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Scenario 3: Fuzzy lookup (approximate matching)
    print("\n--- Scenario 3: Fuzzy Lookup (Soundex) ---")
    
    # Create customer data with potential typos
    customer_search = spark.createDataFrame([
        ("Jon Doe",),
        ("Jane Smyth",),
        ("Bob Jonson",),
    ], ["search_name"])
    
    # Use soundex for fuzzy matching
    customers_with_soundex = customers_df.withColumn(
        "name_soundex",
        soundex(col("customer_name"))
    )
    
    search_with_soundex = customer_search.withColumn(
        "search_soundex",
        soundex(col("search_name"))
    )
    
    fuzzy_matches = search_with_soundex.join(
        broadcast(customers_with_soundex),
        col("search_soundex") == col("name_soundex"),
        "left"
    ).select(
        "search_name",
        "customer_name",
        "customer_id",
        "tier"
    )
    
    print("Fuzzy Lookup Result:")
    fuzzy_matches.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Scenario 4: Temporal lookup (time-based lookup)
    print("\n--- Scenario 4: Temporal Lookup ---")
    
    # Create historical pricing data
    price_history = spark.createDataFrame([
        ("P001", "2024-01-01", "2024-01-15", 1000.00),
        ("P001", "2024-01-16", "2024-12-31", 1200.00),
        ("P002", "2024-01-01", "2024-01-20", 750.00),
        ("P002", "2024-01-21", "2024-12-31", 800.00),
    ], ["product_id", "valid_from", "valid_to", "price"])
    
    # Join with temporal condition
    temporal_lookup = order_items_df \
        .join(transactions_df, "transaction_id") \
        .join(
            price_history,
            (order_items_df.product_id == price_history.product_id) &
            (col("transaction_date") >= col("valid_from")) &
            (col("transaction_date
") <= col("valid_to")),
            "left"
        ) \
        .select(
            order_items_df.transaction_id,
            col("transaction_date"),
            order_items_df.product_id,
            "quantity",
            "valid_from",
            "valid_to",
            price_history.price,
            (col("quantity") * price_history.price).alias("total_amount")
        )
    
    print("Temporal Lookup Result:")
    temporal_lookup.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Scenario 5: Hierarchical lookup (parent-child relationships)
    print("\n--- Scenario 5: Hierarchical Lookup ---")
    
    # Create category hierarchy
    category_hierarchy = spark.createDataFrame([
        ("Electronics", "Technology", 1),
        ("Furniture", "Home & Living", 1),
        ("Technology", "All Products", 2),
        ("Home & Living", "All Products", 2),
    ], ["category", "parent_category", "level"])
    
    # Multi-level hierarchical lookup
    products_with_hierarchy = products_df \
        .join(
            category_hierarchy.alias("level1"),
            products_df.category == col("level1.category"),
            "left"
        ) \
        .join(
            category_hierarchy.alias("level2"),
            col("level1.parent_category") == col("level2.category"),
            "left"
        ) \
        .select(
            "product_id",
            "product_name",
            products_df.category.alias("category"),
            col("level1.parent_category").alias("parent_category"),
            col("level2.parent_category").alias("root_category")
        )
    
    print("Hierarchical Lookup Result:")
    products_with_hierarchy.show(truncate=False)

# PERFORMANCE MONITORING AND OPTIMIZATION

def performance_monitoring():
    """
    Demonstrate performance monitoring and optimization techniques
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PERFORMANCE MONITORING & OPTIMIZATION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create larger datasets for meaningful performance testing
    print("\n--- Creating Large Test Datasets ---")
    
    # Generate large transaction dataset
    large_transactions = spark.range(0, 100000).select(
        col("id").alias("transaction_id"),
        (col("id") % 1000).alias("customer_id"),
        (rand() * 10000).alias("amount"),
        date_add(lit("2024-01-01"), (col("id") % 365).cast("int")).alias("transaction_date")
    )
    
    # Generate customer lookup
    large_customers = spark.range(0, 1000).select(
        col("id").alias("customer_id"),
        concat(lit("Customer_"), col("id")).alias("customer_name"),
        when(col("id") % 4 == 0, "Platinum")
        .when(col("id") % 4 == 1, "Gold")
        .when(col("id") % 4 == 2, "Silver")
        .otherwise("Bronze").alias("tier")
    )
    
    print(f"Transactions: {large_transactions.count():,} records")
    print(f"Customers: {large_customers.count():,} records")
    
    # Test 1: Direct Join Performance
    print("\n--- Test 1: Direct Join ---")
    start_time = time.time()
    direct_result = large_transactions.join(large_customers, "customer_id")
    direct_count = direct_result.count()
    direct_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Time: {direct_time:.4f}s, Records: {direct_count:,}")
    
    # Test 2: Broadcast Join Performance
    print("\n--- Test 2: Broadcast Join ---")
    start_time = time.time()
    broadcast_result = large_transactions.join(broadcast(large_customers), "customer_id")
    broadcast_count = broadcast_result.count()
    broadcast_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Time: {broadcast_time:.4f}s, Records: {broadcast_count:,}")
    print(f"Speedup: {direct_time/broadcast_time:.2f}x")
    
    # Test 3: Cached Lookup Performance
    print("\n--- Test 3: Cached Lookup ---")
    large_customers.cache()
    large_customers.count()  # Force caching
    
    start_time = time.time()
    cached_result = large_transactions.join(large_customers, "customer_id")
    cached_count = cached_result.count()
    cached_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Time: {cached_time:.4f}s, Records: {cached_count:,}")
    
    # Second query on cached data
    start_time = time.time()
    cached_result2 = large_transactions.join(large_customers, "customer_id").filter(col("tier") == "Platinum")
    cached_count2 = cached_result2.count()
    cached_time2 = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Second query time: {cached_time2:.4f}s, Records: {cached_count2:,}")
    
    # Test 4: Partitioned Join Performance
    print("\n--- Test 4: Partitioned Join ---")
    partitioned_transactions = large_transactions.repartition(8, "customer_id")
    partitioned_customers = large_customers.repartition(8, "customer_id")
    
    start_time = time.time()
    partitioned_result = partitioned_transactions.join(partitioned_customers, "customer_id")
    partitioned_count = partitioned_result.count()
    partitioned_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Time: {partitioned_time:.4f}s, Records: {partitioned_count:,}")
    
    # Performance Summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PERFORMANCE SUMMARY")
    print("="*80)
    
    summary_df = spark.createDataFrame([
        ("Direct Join", direct_time, direct_count, 1.0),
        ("Broadcast Join", broadcast_time, broadcast_count, direct_time/broadcast_time),
        ("Cached Join", cached_time, cached_count, direct_time/cached_time),
        ("Partitioned Join", partitioned_time, partitioned_count, direct_time/partitioned_time),
    ], ["Method", "Time (s)", "Records", "Speedup"])
    
    summary_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Memory usage analysis
    print("\n--- Memory Usage Analysis ---")
    print(f"Cached customers memory: {large_customers.storageLevel}")
    
    # Cleanup
    large_customers.unpersist()

# ERROR HANDLING AND EDGE CASES
# ============================================================================
def error_handling_patterns():
    """
    Demonstrate error handling and edge cases in lookup patterns
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ERROR HANDLING & EDGE CASES")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create data with potential issues
    transactions_with_nulls = spark.createDataFrame([
        (1, "TXN001", 101, 1500.00),
        (2, "TXN002", None, 2500.00),  # Null customer_id
        (3, "TXN003", 999, 3500.00),   # Non-existent customer
        (4, "TXN004", 101, None),      # Null amount
    ], ["id", "transaction_id", "customer_id", "amount"])
    
    customers_df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (101, "John Doe", "Gold"),
        (102, "Jane Smith", "Silver"),
    ], ["customer_id", "customer_name", "tier"])
    
    # Edge Case 1: Handling null keys
    print("\n--- Edge Case 1: Null Keys ---")
    
    result_with_nulls = transactions_with_nulls.join(
        broadcast(customers_df),
        "customer_id",
        "left"
    ).withColumn(
        "customer_name",
        coalesce(col("customer_name"), lit("UNKNOWN"))
    ).withColumn(
        "tier",
        coalesce(col("tier"), lit("NONE"))
    )
    
    print("Handling Null Keys:")
    result_with_nulls.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 2: Duplicate keys in lookup table
    print("\n--- Edge Case 2: Duplicate Keys ---")
    
    customers_with_dupes = spark.createDataFrame([
        (101, "John Doe", "Gold"),
        (101, "John Doe Jr", "Platinum"),  # Duplicate
        (102, "Jane Smith", "Silver"),
    ], ["customer_id", "customer_name", "tier"])
    
    # Deduplicate before lookup
    deduped_customers = customers_with_dupes \
        .withColumn("row_num", row_number().over(
            Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy(desc("tier"))
        )) \
        .filter(col("row_num") == 1) \
        .drop("row_num")
    
    result_deduped = transactions_with_nulls.join(
        broadcast(deduped_customers),
        "customer_id",
        "left"
    )
    
    print("After Deduplication:")
    result_deduped.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 3: Empty lookup table
    print("\n--- Edge Case 3: Empty Lookup Table ---")
    
    empty_customers = customers_df.filter(col("customer_id") < 0)  # Empty result
    
    result_empty = transactions_with_nulls.join(
        broadcast(empty_customers),
        "customer_id",
        "left"
    ).withColumn(
        "lookup_status",
        when(col("customer_name").isNull(), "NOT_FOUND")
        .otherwise("FOUND")
    )
    
    print("Empty Lookup Table Result:")
    result_empty.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 4: Data type mismatches
    print("\n--- Edge Case 4: Data Type Mismatches ---")
    
    transactions_str_id = transactions_with_nulls.withColumn(
        "customer_id_str",
        col("customer_id").cast("string")
    )
    
    customers_int_id = customers_df  # Has integer customer_id
    
    # Safe join with type casting
    result_type_safe = transactions_str_id.join(
        broadcast(customers_int_id),
        transactions_str_id.customer_id_str == customers_int_id.customer_id.cast("string"),
        "left"
    ).select(
        transactions_str_id["*"],
        customers_int_id.customer_name,
        customers_int_id.tier
    )
    
    print("Type-Safe Join Result:")
    result_type_safe.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Edge Case 5: Very large lookup values
    print("\n--- Edge Case 5: Large Lookup Values ---")
    
    # Simulate large text fields
    customers_large = customers_df.withColumn(
        "large_field",
        concat(*[lit("X" * 100) for _ in range(10)])  # 1KB per record
    )
    
    # Use selective projection to minimize data transfer
    result_selective = transactions_with_nulls.join(
        broadcast(customers_large.select("customer_id", "customer_name", "tier")),
        "customer_id",
        "left"
    )
    
    print("Selective Projection Result:")
    result_selective.show(5, truncate=False)

def print_dataframe_info(df, name="DataFrame"):
    """
    Utility function to print DataFrame information
    """
    print(f"\n--- {name} Information ---")
    print(f"Schema:")
    df.printSchema()
    print(f"Count: {df.count()}")
    print(f"Partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    print(f"Sample Data:")
    df.show(5, truncate=False)


def optimize_lookup_table(df, key_column, broadcast_threshold_mb=10):
    """
    Utility function to automatically optimize lookup table
    
    Args:
        df: DataFrame to optimize
        key_column: Column to use as key
        broadcast_threshold_mb: Size threshold for broadcasting
    
    Returns:
        Optimized DataFrame
    """
    # Estimate size (rough approximation)
    sample_size = df.limit(100).count()
    if sample_size == 0:
        return df
    
    # Simple heuristic: if small, broadcast; otherwise partition
    if sample_size < 1000:  # Assuming small lookup
        print(f"Optimizing {key_column}: Using BROADCAST")
        return broadcast(df)
    else:
        print(f"Optimizing {key_column}: Using PARTITIONING")
        return df.repartition(8, key_column).cache()

def test_lookup_patterns():
    """
    Unit tests for lookup patterns
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("TESTING LOOKUP PATTERNS")
    print("="*80)
    
    transactions_df, customers_df, _ = create_sample_data()
    
    # Test 1: Verify join correctness
    print("\n--- Test 1: Join Correctness ---")
    
    direct_result = transactions_df.join(customers_df, "customer_id", "left")
    broadcast_result = transactions_df.join(broadcast(customers_df), "customer_id", "left")
    
    direct_count = direct_result.count()
    broadcast_count = broadcast_result.count()
    
    assert direct_count == broadcast_count, "Join counts don't match!"
    print(f"✓ Join counts match: {direct_count}")
    
    # Test 2: Verify data integrity
    print("\n--- Test 2: Data Integrity ---")
    
    # Check for null handling
    null_test = transactions_df.withColumn("customer_id", lit(None).cast("int"))
    null_result = null_test.join(customers_df, "customer_id", "left")
    null_count = null_result.filter(col("customer_name").isNull()).count()
    
    print(f"✓ Null handling verified: {null_count} null records")
    
    # Test 3: Verify broadcast behavior
    print("\n--- Test 3: Broadcast Verification ---")
    
    broadcast_df = broadcast(customers_df)
    result = transactions_df.join(broadcast_df, "customer_id")
    
    # Check execution plan for BroadcastHashJoin
    plan = result._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
    has_broadcast = "BroadcastHashJoin" in plan or "BroadcastExchange" in plan
    
    print(f"✓ Broadcast join detected: {has_broadcast}")
    
    # Test 4: Performance regression test
    print("\n--- Test 4: Performance Regression ---")
    
    import time
    
    # Baseline
    start = time.time()
    transactions_df.join(broadcast(customers_df), "customer_id").count()
    baseline_time = time.time() - start
    
    # Test
    start = time.time()
    transactions_df.join(broadcast(customers_df), "customer_id").count()
    test_time = time.time() - start
    
    regression_ratio = test_time / baseline_time
    print(f"✓ Performance ratio: {regression_ratio:.2f}x")
    
    if regression_ratio > 2.0:
        print("⚠ Warning: Performance regression detected!")
    
    # Test 5: Memory usage test
    print("\n--- Test 5: Memory Usage ---")
    
    customers_df.cache()
    customers_df.count()
    
    is_cached = customers_df.is_cached
    print(f"✓ Cache status: {is_cached}")
    
    customers_df.unpersist()
    
    print("\n✓ All tests passed!")
