class RealWorldExamples:
    """
    Real-world scenarios demonstrating formatting patterns
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def ecommerce_order_report():
        """
        E-commerce order report with multiple formatting patterns
        """
        print("\n--- E-Commerce Order Report ---")
        
        # Sample order data
        orders_data = [
            (1001, 1, "2024-01-15", 299.99, "Laptop", 1, "Delivered"),
            (1001, 1, "2024-01-15", 49.99, "Mouse", 2, "Delivered"),
            (1002, 2, "2024-01-16", 599.99, "Monitor", 1, "Shipped"),
            (1003, 3, "2024-01-16", 899.99, "Smartphone", 1, "Processing"),
            (1003, 3, "2024-01-16", 29.99, "Phone Case", 1, "Processing")
        ]
        
        orders_df = spark.createDataFrame(
            orders_data,
            ["order_id", "customer_id", "order_date", "price", "product", "quantity", "status"]
        )
        
        # Format 1: Nested structure for API
        api_format = orders_df.groupBy("order_id", "customer_id", "order_date", "status").agg(
            collect_list(
                struct(
                    col("product"),
                    col("quantity"),
                    col("price"),
                    (col("price") * col("quantity")).alias("line_total")
                )
            ).alias("items"),
            round(sum(col("price") * col("quantity")), 2).alias("order_total")
        ).select(
            struct(
                col("order_id"),
                col("customer_id"),
                col("order_date"),
                col("status"),
                col("items"),
                format_string("$%,.2f", col("order_total")).alias("formatted_total"),
                col("order_total")
            ).alias("order")
        )
        
        print("\nAPI Format (Nested):")
        api_format.select(to_json(col("order")).alias("json")).show(truncate=False)
        
        # Format 2: Flat structure for reporting
        flat_format = orders_df.select(
            col("order_id"),
            col("customer_id"),
            col("order_date"),
            col("product"),
            col("quantity"),
            format_string("$%,.2f", col("price")).alias("unit_price"),
            format_string("$%,.2f", col("price") * col("quantity")).alias("line_total"),
            col("status")
        )
        
        print("\nFlat Format (Reporting):")
        flat_format.show(truncate=False)
        
        return api_format, flat_format
    
    @staticmethod
    def financial_statement():
        """
        Financial statement with custom formatting
        """
        print("\n--- Financial Statement ---")
        
        # Sample financial data
        financial_data = [
            ("Revenue", "Sales", 1500000, "Income"),
            ("Revenue", "Services", 750000, "Income"),
            ("Expenses", "Salaries", -800000, "Expense"),
            ("Expenses", "Rent", -120000, "Expense"),
            ("Expenses", "Marketing", -200000, "Expense"),
            ("Expenses", "Utilities", -50000, "Expense")
        ]
        
        financial_df = spark.createDataFrame(
            financial_data,
            ["category", "subcategory", "amount", "type"]
        )
        
        # Format with custom business rules
        statement = financial_df.groupBy("category").agg(
            collect_list(
                struct(
                    col("subcategory"),
                    col("amount")
                )
            ).alias("items"),
            sum("amount").alias("category_total")
        ).select(
            col("category"),
            col("items"),
            col("category_total"),
            # Custom formatting for financial display
            when(col("category_total") >= 0,
                format_string("$%,.2f", col("category_total"))
            ).otherwise(
                format_string("($%,.2f)", abs(col("category_total")))
            ).alias("formatted_total")
        )
        
        print("\nFinancial Statement:")
        statement.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Calculate net income
        net_income = financial_df.agg(sum("amount").alias("net_income"))
        print("\nNet Income:")
        net_income.select(
            format_string("$%,.2f", col("net_income")).alias("net_income")
        ).show()
        
        return statement
    
    @staticmethod
    def customer_360_view():
        """
        Customer 360-degree view with comprehensive formatting
        """
        print("\n--- Customer 360 View ---")
        
        # Sample customer data
        customers_data = [
            (1, "John", "Doe", "john@email.com", "Premium", 5, 15000, "2023-01-15"),
            (2, "Jane", "Smith", "jane@email.com", "Standard", 3, 5000, "2023-06-20"),
            (3, "Bob", "Johnson", "bob@email.com", "Premium", 8, 25000, "2022-11-10")
        ]
        
        customers_df = spark.createDataFrame(
            customers_data,
            ["customer_id", "first_name", "last_name", "email", "tier", 
             "orders_count", "lifetime_value", "join_date"]
        )
        
        # Comprehensive customer view
        customer_360 = customers_df.select(
            struct(
                col("customer_id").alias("id"),
                struct(
                    col("first_name"),
                    col("last_name"),
                    concat(col("first_name"), lit(" "), col("last_name")).alias("full_name"),
                    col("email")
                ).alias("personal_info"),
                struct(
                    col("tier"),
                    col("orders_count"),
                    format_string("$%,.2f", col("lifetime_value")).alias("ltv_formatted"),
                    col("lifetime_value"),
                    round(col("lifetime_value") / col("orders_count"), 2).alias("avg_order_value")
                ).alias("account_info"),
                struct(
                    col("join_date"),
                    expr("datediff(current_date(), join_date)").alias("days_as_customer"),
                    when(expr("datediff(current_date(), join_date)") > 365, "Loyal")
                    .otherwise("New").alias("customer_segment")
                ).alias("engagement"),
                # Customer score
                when(col("tier") == "Premium", 100)
                .otherwise(50).alias("base_score")
            ).alias("customer_profile")
        )
        
        print("\nCustomer 360 View:")
        customer_360.select(to_json(col("customer_profile")).alias("profile")).show(truncate=False)
        
        # Flattened view for analysis
        flat_customer = customer_360.select(
            col("customer_profile.id").alias("customer_id"),
            col("customer_profile.personal_info.full_name").alias("name"),
            col("customer_profile.personal_info.email").alias("email"),
            col("customer_profile.account_info.tier").alias("tier"),
            col("customer_profile.account_info.ltv_formatted").alias("lifetime_value"),
            col("customer_profile.engagement.customer_segment").alias("segment")
        )
        
        print("\nFlattened Customer View:")
        flat_customer.show(truncate=False)
        
        return customer_360
    
    @staticmethod
    def log_analysis_report():
        """
        Log analysis with custom formatting patterns
        """
        print("\n--- Log Analysis Report ---")
        
        # Sample log data
        logs_data = [
            ("2024-01-15 10:30:15", "INFO", "user_login", "user123", "success"),
            ("2024-01-15 10:31:22", "ERROR", "api_call", "user123", "timeout"),
            ("2024-01-15 10:32:45", "INFO", "user_login", "user456", "success"),
            ("2024-01-15 10:33:10", "WARN", "api_call", "user123", "slow_response"),
            ("2024-01-15 10:34:55", "ERROR", "database", "system", "connection_failed")
        ]
        
        logs_df = spark.createDataFrame(
            logs_data,
            ["timestamp", "level", "event_type", "user", "message"]
        )
        
        # Format log summary
        log_summary = logs_df.groupBy("level", "event_type").agg(
            count("*").alias("occurrence_count"),
            collect_list(
                struct(
                    col("timestamp"),
                    col("user"),
                    col("message")
                )
            ).alias("events")
        ).select(
            col("level"),
            col("event_type"),
            col("occurrence_count"),
            # Add severity indicator
            when(col("level") == "ERROR", "🔴 Critical")
            .when(col("level") == "WARN", "🟡 Warning")
            .otherwise("🟢 Info").alias("severity"),
            col("events")
        )
        
        print("\nLog Summary:")
        log_summary.select("level", "event_type", "occurrence_count", "severity").show(truncate=False)
        
        # Detailed flat format
        detailed_logs = logs_df.select(
            col("timestamp"),
            concat(
                when(col("level") == "ERROR", "[❌ ERROR] ")
                .when(col("level") == "WARN", "[⚠️  WARN ] ")
                .otherwise("[ℹ️  INFO ] "),
                col("event_type"),
                lit(" - "),
                col("user"),
                lit(": "),
                col("message")
            ).alias("formatted_log")
        )
        
        print("\nFormatted Logs:")
        detailed_logs.show(truncate=False)
        
        return log_summary

# Execute Real-World Examples
real_world = RealWorldExamples()
real_world.ecommerce_order_report()
real_world.financial_statement()
real_world.customer_360_view()
real_world.log_analysis_report()

class FormattingValidation:
    """
    Utilities for testing and validating formatted outputs
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_schema(df, expected_columns):
        """
        Validate that formatted dataframe has expected schema
        """
        print("\n--- Schema Validation ---")
        
        actual_columns = set(df.columns)
        expected_set = set(expected_columns)
        
        missing = expected_set - actual_columns
        extra = actual_columns - expected_set
        
        if not missing and not extra:
            print("✓ Schema validation passed")
            return True
        else:
            if missing:
                print(f"✗ Missing columns: {missing}")
            if extra:
                print(f"✗ Extra columns: {extra}")
            return False
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_data_quality(df):
        """
        Validate data quality after formatting
        """
        print("\n--- Data Quality Validation ---")
        
        total_rows = df.count()
        
        # Check for nulls
        null_counts = df.select([
            sum(col(c).isNull().cast("int")).alias(c) 
            for c in df.columns
        ])
        
        print(f"Total rows: {total_rows}")
        print("\nNull counts by column:")
        null_counts.show()
        
        # Check for duplicates
        distinct_count = df.distinct().count()
        duplicate_count = total_
```python
        duplicate_count = total_rows - distinct_count
        
        if duplicate_count > 0:
            print(f"⚠️  Warning: {duplicate_count} duplicate rows found")
        else:
            print("✓ No duplicate rows")
        
        return {
            'total_rows': total_rows,
            'distinct_rows': distinct_count,
            'duplicate_rows': duplicate_count
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_formatting_rules(df, column, validation_func):
        """
        Validate that a column follows specific formatting rules
        """
        print(f"\n--- Validating formatting for column: {column} ---")
        
        # Apply validation function
        validated_df = df.withColumn(
            f"{column}_valid",
            validation_func(col(column))
        )
        
        # Count valid vs invalid
        validation_summary = validated_df.groupBy(f"{column}_valid").count()
        validation_summary.show()
        
        return validated_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def compare_formats(original_df, formatted_df):
        """
        Compare original and formatted dataframes
        """
        print("\n--- Format Comparison ---")
        
        print(f"Original columns: {len(original_df.columns)}")
        print(f"Formatted columns: {len(formatted_df.columns)}")
        
        print(f"\nOriginal row count: {original_df.count()}")
        print(f"Formatted row count: {formatted_df.count()}")
        
        print("\nOriginal Schema:")
        original_df.printSchema()
        
        print("\nFormatted Schema:")
        formatted_df.printSchema()

# Execute Validation Examples

class AdvancedFormatting:
    """
    Advanced formatting techniques for complex scenarios
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def dynamic_column_formatting():
        """
        Apply formatting dynamically based on column metadata
        """
        print("\n--- Dynamic Column Formatting ---")
        
        # Define formatting rules
        format_rules = {
            "salary": lambda c: format_string("$%,.2f", c),
            "email": lambda c: lower(c),
            "first_name": lambda c: initcap(c),
            "last_name": lambda c: upper(c)
        }
        
        # Apply formatting dynamically
        formatted_df = employees_df
        for column, format_func in format_rules.items():
            if column in formatted_df.columns:
                formatted_df = formatted_df.withColumn(
                    f"{column}_formatted",
                    format_func(col(column))
                )
        
        formatted_df.select(
            "emp_id",
            "first_name", "first_name_formatted",
            "last_name", "last_name_formatted",
            "salary", "salary_formatted",
            "email", "email_formatted"
        ).show(truncate=False)
        
        return formatted_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def conditional_nested_formatting():
        """
        Create conditional nested structures
        """
        print("\n--- Conditional Nested Formatting ---")
        
        result = employees_df.select(
            col("emp_id"),
            concat(col("first_name"), lit(" "), col("last_name")).alias("name"),
            col("department"),
            col("salary"),
            # Conditional nested structure based on salary
            when(col("salary") >= 80000,
                struct(
                    lit("Senior").alias("level"),
                    lit("Executive").alias("category"),
                    struct(
                        col("salary"),
                        (col("salary") * 0.25).alias("bonus"),
                        lit("Stock Options").alias("equity")
                    ).alias("compensation_package")
                )
            ).when(col("salary") >= 70000,
                struct(
                    lit("Mid-Level").alias("level"),
                    lit("Professional").alias("category"),
                    struct(
                        col("salary"),
                        (col("salary") * 0.15).alias("bonus"),
                        lit("None").alias("equity")
                    ).alias("compensation_package")
                )
            ).otherwise(
                struct(
                    lit("Junior").alias("level"),
                    lit("Entry").alias("category"),
                    struct(
                        col("salary"),
                        (col("salary") * 0.10).alias("bonus"),
                        lit("None").alias("equity")
                    ).alias("compensation_package")
                )
            ).alias("employee_tier")
        )
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        result.printSchema()
        return result
    
    @staticmethod
    def multi_format_output():
        """
        Generate multiple format outputs from single source
        """
        print("\n--- Multi-Format Output ---")
        
        # Base formatted dataframe
        base_df = employees_df.select(
            col("emp_id"),
            col("first_name"),
            col("last_name"),
            col("department"),
            col("salary"),
            col("location")
        )
        
        # Format 1: JSON for API
        json_format = base_df.select(
            to_json(struct("*")).alias("json_record")
        )
        print("\nJSON Format:")
        json_format.show(3, truncate=False)
        
        # Format 2: CSV-friendly
        csv_format = base_df.select(
            col("emp_id"),
            concat(col("first_name"), lit(" "), col("last_name")).alias("name"),
            col("department"),
            format_string("%.2f", col("salary")).alias("salary"),
            col("location")
        )
        print("\nCSV Format:")
        csv_format.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Format 3: Hierarchical for reporting
        hierarchical_format = base_df.groupBy("department", "location").agg(
            collect_list(
                struct(
                    col("emp_id"),
                    concat(col("first_name"), lit(" "), col("last_name")).alias("name"),
                    col("salary")
                )
            ).alias("employees")
        )
        print("\nHierarchical Format:")
        hierarchical_format.show(truncate=False)
        
        return {
            'json': json_format,
            'csv': csv_format,
            'hierarchical': hierarchical_format
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def template_based_formatting():
        """
        Use templates for consistent formatting
        """
        print("\n--- Template-Based Formatting ---")
        
        # Define templates
        templates = {
            'email_template': "Dear {first_name} {last_name},\nYour salary is {salary}",
            'badge_template': "ID: {emp_id} | {first_name} {last_name} | {department}",
            'report_template': "{department} - {first_name} {last_name} ($salary)"
        }
        
        # Apply email template
        email_result = employees_df.select(
            col("emp_id"),
            concat(
                lit("Dear "),
                col("first_name"),
                lit(" "),
                col("last_name"),
                lit(",\nYour salary is $"),
                format_string("%,.2f", col("salary"))
            ).alias("email_body")
        )
        
        print("\nEmail Template:")
        email_result.show(3, truncate=False)
        
        # Apply badge template
        badge_result = employees_df.select(
            col("emp_id"),
            format_string(
                "ID: %05d | %s %s | %s",
                col("emp_id"),
                col("first_name"),
                col("last_name"),
                col("department")
            ).alias("employee_badge")
        )
        
        print("\nBadge Template:")
        badge_result.show(truncate=False)
        
        return email_result, badge_result
    
    @staticmethod
    def format_with_window_functions():
        """
        Combine window functions with formatting
        """
        print("\n--- Formatting with Window Functions ---")
        
        from pyspark.sql.window import Window
        from pyspark.sql.functions import row_number, dense_rank, ntile
        
        # Define windows
        salary_window = Window.orderBy(col("salary").desc())
        dept_window = Window.partitionBy("department").orderBy(col("salary").desc())
        
        result = employees_df.select(
            col("emp_id"),
            concat(col("first_name"), lit(" "), col("last_name")).alias("name"),
            col("department"),
            format_string("$%,.2f", col("salary")).alias("salary"),
            # Add rankings with formatting
            concat(
                lit("#"),
                row_number().over(salary_window).cast("string")
            ).alias("company_rank"),
            concat(
                lit("#"),
                row_number().over(dept_window).cast("string"),
                lit(" in "),
                col("department")
            ).alias("dept_rank"),
            # Add quartile
            when(ntile(4).over(salary_window) == 1, "Top 25%")
            .when(ntile(4).over(salary_window) == 2, "Top 50%")
            .when(ntile(4).over(salary_window) == 3, "Top 75%")
            .otherwise("Bottom 25%").alias("salary_quartile")
        )
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result

# Execute Advanced Formatting Examples
advanced = AdvancedFormatting()
advanced.dynamic_column_formatting()
advanced.conditional_nested_formatting()
advanced.multi_format_output()
advanced.template_based_formatting()
advanced.format_with_window_functions()

class ErrorHandling:
    """
    Demonstrate error handling in formatting operations
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def handle_null_values():
        """
        Handle null values in formatting
        """
        print("\n--- Handling Null Values ---")
        
        # Create dataframe with nulls
        data_with_nulls = [
            (1, "John", None, "Engineering", 75000),
            (2, None, "Smith", "Marketing", None),
            (3, "Bob", "Johnson", None, 80000)
        ]
        
        null_df = spark.createDataFrame(
            data_with_nulls,
            ["emp_id", "first_name", "last_name", "department", "salary"]
        )
        
        # Safe formatting with null handling
        result = null_df.select(
            col("emp_id"),
            coalesce(col("first_name"), lit("Unknown")).alias("first_name"),
            coalesce(col("last_name"), lit("Unknown")).alias("last_name"),
            concat(
                coalesce(col("first_name"), lit("Unknown")),
                lit(" "),
                coalesce(col("last_name"), lit("Unknown"))
            ).alias("full_name"),
            coalesce(col("department"), lit("Unassigned")).alias("department"),
            when(col("salary").isNotNull(),
                format_string("$%,.2f", col("salary"))
            ).otherwise("Not Set").alias("salary_formatted")
        )
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result
    
    @staticmethod
    def handle_data_type_errors():
        """
        Handle data type conversion errors
        """
        print("\n--- Handling Data Type Errors ---")
        
        # Create dataframe with mixed types
        mixed_data = [
            (1, "75000", "valid"),
            (2, "invalid", "invalid"),
            (3, "80000.50", "valid")
        ]
        
        mixed_df = spark.createDataFrame(
            mixed_data,
            ["emp_id", "salary_str", "status"]
        )
        
        # Safe type conversion
        result = mixed_df.select(
            col("emp_id"),
            col("salary_str"),
            # Try to cast, return null if fails
            col("salary_str").cast("double").alias("salary_numeric"),
            # Provide default for failed conversions
            when(col("salary_str").cast("double").isNotNull(),
                format_string("$%,.2f", col("salary_str").cast("double"))
            ).otherwise("Invalid Amount").alias("salary_formatted"),
            # Validation flag
            col("salary_str").cast("double").isNotNull().alias("is_valid")
        )
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result
    
    @staticmethod
    def handle_division_by_zero():
        """
        Handle division by zero in calculations
        """
        print("\n--- Handling Division by Zero ---")
        
        calc_data = [
            (1, "John", 100, 10),
            (2, "Jane", 200, 0),
            (3, "Bob", 150, 5)
        ]
        
        calc_df = spark.createDataFrame(
            calc_data,
            ["emp_id", "name", "total_sales", "num_orders"]
        )
        
        # Safe division
        result = calc_df.select(
            col("emp_id"),
            col("name"),
            col("total_sales"),
            col("num_orders"),
            # Safe division with default
            when(col("num_orders") != 0,
                round(col("total_sales") / col("num_orders"), 2)
            ).otherwise(0).alias("avg_order_value"),
            # Formatted version
            when(col("num_orders") != 0,
                format_string("$%,.2f", col("total_sales") / col("num_orders"))
            ).otherwise("N/A").alias("avg_order_formatted")
        )
        
        result.show(truncate=False)
        return result

# Execute Error Handling Examples

"""
PySpark Data Compression Strategy Patterns
==========================================
This module demonstrates various compression strategies for optimizing
data storage and transfer in PySpark applications.

Author: AI Assistant
Date: 2024
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, lit, current_timestamp
from typing import Dict, List, Optional
import os
from datetime import datetime
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


# ============================================================================
# Base Compression Pattern (Abstract Base Class)
# ============================================================================

class CompressionPattern(ABC):
    """
    Abstract base class for compression patterns.
    Provides common interface for all compression strategies.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.compression_codec = None
        
    @abstractmethod
    def configure_compression(self) -> None:
        """Configure compression settings for Spark session."""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def write_compressed_data(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str, 
                             format: str = "parquet") -> None:
        """Write data with compression."""
        pass
    
    def read_compressed_data(self, input_path: str, 
                            format: str = "parquet") -> DataFrame:
        """Read compressed data."""
        return self.spark.read.format(format).load(input_path)
    
    def get_compression_info(self) -> Dict:
        """Get compression configuration information."""
        return {
            "codec": self.compression_codec,
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }


# ============================================================================
# 1. Snappy Compression Pattern
# ============================================================================

class SnappyCompressionPattern(CompressionPattern):
    """
    Snappy Compression Pattern
    
    Characteristics:
    - Fast compression and decompression
    - Moderate compression ratio
    - Default for Parquet in Spark
    - Best for: Real-time processing, moderate compression needs
    
    Use Cases:
    - Interactive queries
    - Streaming data
    - General-purpose data lakes
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        super().__init__(spark)
        self.compression_codec = "snappy"
        
    def configure_compression(self) -> None:
        """Configure Snappy compression for various formats."""
        # Parquet compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec", "snappy")
        
        # ORC compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.orc.compression.codec", "snappy")
        
        # General compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.io.compression.codec", "snappy")
        
        print("✓ Snappy compression configured")
        print("  - Compression ratio: ~2:1")
        print("  - Speed: Very Fast")
        print("  - CPU usage: Low")
    
    def write_compressed_data(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str, 
                             format: str = "parquet") -> None:
        """Write data with Snappy compression."""
        if format == "parquet":
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "snappy") \
                .parquet(output_path)
        elif format == "orc":
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "snappy") \
                .orc(output_path)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format: {format}")
        
        print(f"✓ Data written with Snappy compression to {output_path}")
    
    def write_with_partitioning(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str, 
                               partition_cols: List[str]) -> None:
        """Write partitioned data with Snappy compression."""
        df.write.mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy(*partition_cols) \
            .option("compression", "snappy") \
            .parquet(output_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Partitioned data written with Snappy compression")


# ============================================================================
# 2. GZIP Compression Pattern
# ============================================================================

class GZIPCompressionPattern(CompressionPattern):
    """
    GZIP Compression Pattern
    
    Characteristics:
    - High compression ratio
    - Slower compression/decompression
    - Not splittable (except in certain formats)
    - Best for: Archival, cold storage, bandwidth-limited transfers
    
    Use Cases:
    - Data archival
    - Long-term storage
    - Network transfers with limited bandwidth
    - Cold data in data lakes
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, compression_level: int = 6):
        super().__init__(spark)
        self.compression_codec = "gzip"
        self.compression_level = compression_level  # 1-9, default is 6
        
    def configure_compression(self) -> None:
        """Configure GZIP compression."""
        # Parquet compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec", "gzip")
        
        # ORC compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.orc.compression.codec", "zlib")
        
        # Text file compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.hadoop.mapreduce.output.fileoutputformat.compress", "true")
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.hadoop.mapreduce.output.fileoutputformat.compress.codec", 
                           "org.apache.hadoop.io.compress.GzipCodec")
        
        print("✓ GZIP compression configured")
        print(f"  - Compression level: {self.compression_level}")
        print("  - Compression ratio: ~3:1 to 5:1")
        print("  - Speed: Slow")
        print("  - CPU usage: High")
    
    def write_compressed_data(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str, 
                             format: str = "parquet") -> None:
        """Write data with GZIP compression."""
        if format == "parquet":
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "gzip") \
                .parquet(output_path)
        elif format == "json":
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "gzip") \
                .json(output_path)
        elif format == "csv":
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "gzip") \
                .csv(output_path)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format: {format}")
        
        print(f"✓ Data written with GZIP compression to {output_path}")
    
    def write_text_with_compression(self, rdd, output_path: str) -> None:
        """Write text RDD with GZIP compression."""
        rdd.saveAsTextFile(output_path, 
                          "org.apache.hadoop.io.compress.GzipCodec")
        print(f"✓ Text data written with GZIP compression")


# ============================================================================
# 3. LZO Compression Pattern
# ============================================================================

class LZOCompressionPattern(CompressionPattern):
    """
    LZO Compression Pattern
    
    Characteristics:
    - Fast compression/decompression
    - Splittable (with index)
    - Moderate compression ratio
    - Requires GPL license (external library)
    - Best for: MapReduce intermediate data, splittable compressed files
    
    Use Cases:
    - MapReduce intermediate outputs
    - Large files requiring splitting
    - Real-time processing with compression
    
    Note: Requires hadoop-lzo library installation
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        super().__init__(spark)
        self.compression_codec = "lzo"
        
    def configure_compression(self) -> None:
        """Configure LZO compression."""
        # Note: LZO requires external library
        # Add to spark-submit: --jars /path/to/hadoop-lzo.jar
        
        try:
            # Set compression codec
            self.spark.conf.set("spark.io.compression.codec", "lzo")
            
            # For text files
            self.spark.conf.set("spark.hadoop.mapreduce.output.fileoutputformat.compress", "true")
            self.spark.conf.set("spark.hadoop.mapreduce.output.fileoutputformat.compress.codec", 
                               "com.hadoop.compression.lzo.LzoCodec")
            
            # For sequence files
            self.spark.conf.set("spark.hadoop.mapreduce.output.fileoutputformat.compress.type", 
                               "BLOCK")
            
            print("✓ LZO compression configured")
            print("  - Compression ratio: ~2:1")
            print("  - Speed: Very Fast")
            print("  - Splittable: Yes (with index)")
            print("  - Note: Requires hadoop-lzo library")
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠ Warning: LZO configuration failed - {str(e)}")
            print("  Ensure hadoop-lzo library is available")
    
    def write_compressed_data(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str, 
                             format: str = "parquet") -> None:
        """Write data with LZO compression."""
        # LZO is primarily used for text and sequence files
        if format == "text":
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "lzo") \
                .text(output_path)
        else:
            print(f"⚠ Warning: LZO is best suited for text/sequence files")
            df.write.mode("overwrite").format(format).save(output_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Data written with LZO compression to {output_path}")
    
    def create_lzo_index(self, file_path: str) -> None:
        """
        Create LZO index for splittable reads.
        This would typically be done using hadoop command-line tools.
        """
        print(f"To create LZO index, run:")
        print(f"hadoop jar hadoop-lzo.jar com.hadoop.compression.lzo.LzoIndexer {file_path}")


# ============================================================================
# 4. ZSTD Compression Pattern
# ============================================================================

class ZSTDCompressionPattern(CompressionPattern):
    """
    ZSTD (Zstandard) Compression Pattern
    
    Characteristics:
    - Excellent compression ratio
    - Fast decompression
    - Configurable compression levels (1-22)
    - Good balance of speed and compression
    - Best for: Modern data lakes, high-performance applications
    
    Use Cases:
    - High-throughput data pipelines
    - Modern data lakes
    - Real-time analytics with good compression
    - Kafka message compression
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, compression_level: int = 3):
        super().__init__(spark)
        self.compression_codec = "zstd"
        self.compression_level = compression_level  # 1-22, default is 3
        
    def configure_compression(self) -> None:
        """Configure ZSTD compression."""
        # Parquet compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec", "zstd")
        
        # ORC compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.orc.compression.codec", "zstd")
        
        # Set compression level
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.io.compression.zstd.level", str(self.compression_level))
        
        print("✓ ZSTD compression configured")
        print(f"  - Compression level: {self.compression_level}")
        print("  - Compression ratio: ~2.5:1 to 4:1")
        print("  - Speed: Fast")
        print("  - CPU usage: Moderate")
        print("  - Decompression: Very Fast")
    
    def write_compressed_data(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str, 
                             format: str = "parquet") -> None:
        """Write data with ZSTD compression."""
        if format == "parquet":
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "zstd") \
                .parquet(output_path)
        elif format == "orc":
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "zstd") \
                .orc(output_path)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format for ZSTD: {format}")
        
        print(f"✓ Data written with ZSTD compression to {output_path}")
    
    def benchmark_compression_levels(self, df: DataFrame, output_base: str, 
                                    levels: List[int] = [1, 3, 6, 9]) -> Dict:
        """
        Benchmark different ZSTD compression levels.
        Returns metrics for each level.
        """
        results = {}
        
        for level in levels:
            self.compression_level = level
            self.spark.conf.set("spark.io.compression.zstd.level", str(level))
            
            output_path = f"{output_base}_level_{level}"
            start_time = datetime.now()
            
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "zstd") \
                .parquet(output_path)
            
            end_time = datetime.now()
            duration = (end_time - start_time).total_seconds()
            
            results[level] = {
                "duration": duration,
                "path": output_path
            }
            
            print(f"✓ Level {level}: {duration:.2f}s")
        
        return results

        print(f"  - Quality level: {self.quality}")
        print("  - Compression ratio: ~4:1 to 6:1 (text)")
        print("  - Speed: Slow compression, Fast decompression")
        print("  - Note: Requires custom implementation or external library")
        print("  - Best for: Text, JSON, XML data")
    
    def write_compressed_data(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str, 
                             format: str = "json") -> None:
        """
        Write data with Brotli
```python
        """
        Write data with Brotli compression.
        Note: This demonstrates the pattern; actual implementation requires
        custom compression logic or external libraries.
        """
        import brotli
        from pyspark.sql.functions import udf
        from pyspark.sql.types import BinaryType
        
        # For demonstration, we'll show how to compress JSON data
        if format == "json":
            # First write to JSON
            temp_path = f"{output_path}_temp"
            df.write.mode("overwrite").json(temp_path)
            
            # Read and compress (in production, use distributed processing)
            print(f"⚠ Brotli compression requires custom implementation")
            print(f"  Data written to temporary location: {temp_path}")
            print(f"  Manual compression step required")
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Brotli is best suited for text/JSON formats")
    
    def compress_text_column(self, df: DataFrame, column_name: str) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Compress a text column using Brotli.
        Returns DataFrame with compressed binary column.
        """
        try:
            import brotli
            
            def brotli_compress(text):
                if text is None:
                    return None
                return brotli.compress(text.encode('utf-8'), quality=self.quality)
            
            compress_udf = udf(brotli_compress, BinaryType())
            
            return df.withColumn(f"{column_name}_compressed", 
                               compress_udf(col(column_name)))
        
        except ImportError:
            print("⚠ brotli library not installed. Install with: pip install brotli")
            return df
    
    def decompress_text_column(self, df: DataFrame, column_name: str) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Decompress a Brotli-compressed binary column.
        Returns DataFrame with decompressed text column.
        """
        try:
            import brotli
            
            def brotli_decompress(compressed_data):
                if compressed_data is None:
                    return None
                return brotli.decompress(compressed_data).decode('utf-8')
            
            decompress_udf = udf(brotli_decompress, StringType())
            
            return df.withColumn(f"{column_name}_decompressed", 
                               decompress_udf(col(column_name)))
        
        except ImportError:
            print("⚠ brotli library not installed. Install with: pip install brotli")
            return df


# ============================================================================
# 6. LZ4 Compression Pattern
# ============================================================================

class LZ4CompressionPattern(CompressionPattern):
    """
    LZ4 Compression Pattern
    
    Characteristics:
    - Extremely fast compression and decompression
    - Lower compression ratio than GZIP
    - Very low CPU usage
    - Best for: Real-time processing, in-memory caching, streaming
    
    Use Cases:
    - Streaming data pipelines
    - Real-time analytics
    - In-memory data compression
    - Shuffle data compression
    - RDD/DataFrame caching
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        super().__init__(spark)
        self.compression_codec = "lz4"
        
    def configure_compression(self) -> None:
        """Configure LZ4 compression."""
        # Parquet compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.parquet.compression.codec", "lz4")
        
        # ORC compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.orc.compression.codec", "lz4")
        
        # IO compression (for shuffle, broadcast, etc.)
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.io.compression.codec", "lz4")
        
        # RDD compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.rdd.compress", "true")
        
        # Broadcast compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.broadcast.compress", "true")
        
        # Shuffle compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.compress", "true")
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.spill.compress", "true")
        
        print("✓ LZ4 compression configured")
        print("  - Compression ratio: ~2:1")
        print("  - Speed: Extremely Fast")
        print("  - CPU usage: Very Low")
        print("  - Perfect for: Shuffle, Cache, Real-time processing")
    
    def write_compressed_data(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str, 
                             format: str = "parquet") -> None:
        """Write data with LZ4 compression."""
        if format == "parquet":
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "lz4") \
                .parquet(output_path)
        elif format == "orc":
            df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                .option("compression", "lz4") \
                .orc(output_path)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format for LZ4: {format}")
        
        print(f"✓ Data written with LZ4 compression to {output_path}")
    
    def configure_for_streaming(self) -> None:
        """
        Configure LZ4 for optimal streaming performance.
        Optimizes shuffle and spill compression.
        """
        # Use LZ4 for all internal compression
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.io.compression.codec", "lz4")
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.compress", "true")
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.spill.compress", "true")
        
        # Optimize shuffle settings
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.file.buffer", "64k")
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.reducer.maxSizeInFlight", "96m")
        
        print("✓ LZ4 configured for streaming workloads")
        print("  - Shuffle compression: Enabled")
        print("  - Spill compression: Enabled")
        print("  - Optimized for low latency")
    
    def cache_with_compression(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Cache DataFrame with LZ4 compression.
        Returns cached DataFrame.
        """
        from pyspark import StorageLevel
        
        # Cache with compression
        df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)
        
        print("✓ DataFrame cached with LZ4 compression")
        print("  - Storage level: MEMORY_AND_DISK")
        print("  - Compression: Enabled (LZ4)")
        
        return df


# ============================================================================
# 7. Adaptive Compression Pattern
# ============================================================================

class AdaptiveCompressionPattern:
    """
    Adaptive Compression Pattern
    
    Intelligently selects compression codec based on:
    - Data characteristics (size, type, cardinality)
    - Use case (storage, processing, transfer)
    - Performance requirements (speed vs ratio)
    - Data access patterns (hot, warm, cold)
    
    Use Cases:
    - Multi-tier storage systems
    - Dynamic workload optimization
    - Cost-optimized data lakes
    - Hybrid processing environments
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.patterns = {
            'snappy': SnappyCompressionPattern(spark),
            'gzip': GZIPCompressionPattern(spark),
            'lzo': LZOCompressionPattern(spark),
            'zstd': ZSTDCompressionPattern(spark),
            'brotli': BrotliCompressionPattern(spark),
            'lz4': LZ4CompressionPattern(spark)
        }
        
    def analyze_data_characteristics(self, df: DataFrame) -> Dict:
        """
        Analyze DataFrame to determine optimal compression strategy.
        """
        # Get basic statistics
        row_count = df.count()
        column_count = len(df.columns)
        
        # Estimate data size
        sample_size = min(1000, row_count)
        sample_df = df.limit(sample_size)
        
        # Analyze data types
        data_types = df.dtypes
        string_columns = [col for col, dtype in data_types if dtype == 'string']
        numeric_columns = [col for col, dtype in data_types if dtype in ['int', 'bigint', 'double', 'float']]
        
        characteristics = {
            'row_count': row_count,
            'column_count': column_count,
            'string_columns': len(string_columns),
            'numeric_columns': len(numeric_columns),
            'has_text_heavy': len(string_columns) > column_count * 0.5
        }
        
        print("📊 Data Characteristics Analysis:")
        print(f"  - Rows: {row_count:,}")
        print(f"  - Columns: {column_count}")
        print(f"  - String columns: {len(string_columns)}")
        print(f"  - Numeric columns: {len(numeric_columns)}")
        
        return characteristics
    
    def recommend_compression(self, use_case: str, 
                             data_characteristics: Dict = None) -> str:
        """
        Recommend compression codec based on use case and data characteristics.
        
        Use cases:
        - 'archival': Long-term storage, rarely accessed
        - 'analytics': Interactive queries, frequent access
        - 'streaming': Real-time processing
        - 'transfer': Network transfer optimization
        - 'balanced': Balance between speed and compression
        """
        recommendations = {
            'archival': {
                'codec': 'gzip',
                'reason': 'Maximum compression for cold storage',
                'alternative': 'zstd'
            },
            'analytics': {
                'codec': 'snappy',
                'reason': 'Fast decompression for interactive queries',
                'alternative': 'lz4'
            },
            'streaming': {
                'codec': 'lz4',
                'reason': 'Minimal latency for real-time processing',
                'alternative': 'snappy'
            },
            'transfer': {
                'codec': 'zstd',
                'reason': 'Good compression with fast decompression',
                'alternative': 'gzip'
            },
            'balanced': {
                'codec': 'zstd',
                'reason': 'Optimal balance of speed and compression',
                'alternative': 'snappy'
            }
        }
        
        if use_case not in recommendations:
            use_case = 'balanced'
        
        recommendation = recommendations[use_case]
        
        # Adjust based on data characteristics
        if data_characteristics and data_characteristics.get('has_text_heavy'):
            if use_case == 'archival':
                recommendation['codec'] = 'brotli'
                recommendation['reason'] += ' (optimized for text data)'
        
        print(f"\n💡 Compression Recommendation for '{use_case}':")
        print(f"  - Primary: {recommendation['codec']}")
        print(f"  - Reason: {recommendation['reason']}")
        print(f"  - Alternative: {recommendation['alternative']}")
        
        return recommendation['codec']
    
    def write_with_adaptive_compression(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str,
                                       use_case: str = 'balanced',
                                       format: str = 'parquet') -> None:
        """
        Write data with automatically selected compression based on use case.
        """
        # Analyze data
        characteristics = self.analyze_data_characteristics(df)
        
        # Get recommendation
        codec = self.recommend_compression(use_case, characteristics)
        
        # Get appropriate pattern
        pattern = self.patterns.get(codec)
        
        if pattern:
            pattern.configure_compression()
            pattern.write_compressed_data(df, output_path, format)
        else:
            print(f"⚠ Codec {codec} not available, using default")
            df.write.mode("overwrite").format(format).save(output_path)
    
    def implement_tiered_storage(self, df: DataFrame, base_path: str,
                                tier_config: Dict = None) -> None:
        """
        Implement multi-tier storage with different compression strategies.
        
        Tiers:
        - Hot: Frequently accessed (LZ4/Snappy)
        - Warm: Occasionally accessed (ZSTD)
        - Cold: Rarely accessed (GZIP)
        """
        if tier_config is None:
            tier_config = {
                'hot': {'codec': 'lz4', 'path': f'{base_path}/hot'},
                'warm': {'codec': 'zstd', 'path': f'{base_path}/warm'},
                'cold': {'codec': 'gzip', 'path': f'{base_path}/cold'}
            }
        
        print("\n🗄️  Implementing Tiered Storage Strategy:")
        
        for tier, config in tier_config.items():
            codec = config['codec']
            path = config['path']
            
            pattern = self.patterns.get(codec)
            if pattern:
                print(f"\n  Tier: {tier.upper()}")
                pattern.configure_compression()
                pattern.write_compressed_data(df, path, 'parquet')
            else:
                print(f"⚠ Codec {codec} not available for tier {tier}")
    
    def benchmark_all_codecs(self, df: DataFrame, output_base: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Benchmark all available compression codecs.
        Returns performance metrics for each codec.
        """
        results = {}
        
        print("\n⏱️  Benchmarking All Compression Codecs:")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        for codec_name, pattern in self.patterns.items():
            if codec_name == 'brotli':  # Skip Brotli as it requires special handling
                continue
            
            try:
                output_path = f"{output_base}/{codec_name}"
                
                # Configure compression
                pattern.configure_compression()
                
                # Measure write time
                start_time = datetime.now()
                pattern.write_compressed_data(df, output_path, 'parquet')
                write_time = (datetime.now() - start_time).total_seconds()
                
                # Measure read time
                start_time = datetime.now()
                read_df = pattern.read_compressed_data(output_path, 'parquet')
                read_df.count()  # Force evaluation
                read_time = (datetime.now() - start_time).total_seconds()
                
                # Get file size (approximation)
                # In production, use Hadoop FileSystem API
                
                results[codec_name] = {
                    'write_time': write_time,
                    'read_time': read_time,
                    'total_time': write_time + read_time,
                    'path': output_path
                }
                
                print(f"\n{codec_name.upper()}:")
                print(f"  Write: {write_time:.2f}s | Read: {read_time:.2f}s | Total: {write_time + read_time:.2f}s")
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"\n{codec_name.upper()}: ⚠ Error - {str(e)}")
                results[codec_name] = {'error': str(e)}
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 60)
        return results
    
    def optimize_for_query_pattern(self, df: DataFrame, output_path: str,
                                   query_pattern: str) -> None:
        
```python
        """
        Optimize compression based on expected query patterns.
        
        Query patterns:
        - 'full_scan': Full table scans (prefer high compression)
        - 'selective': Selective queries with filters (prefer fast decompression)
        - 'aggregation': Heavy aggregations (prefer balanced approach)
        - 'point_lookup': Point lookups (prefer fast decompression)
        """
        pattern_recommendations = {
            'full_scan': {
                'codec': 'gzip',
                'reason': 'Maximize compression for large scans',
                'partition_strategy': 'coarse'
            },
            'selective': {
                'codec': 'snappy',
                'reason': 'Fast decompression for filtered queries',
                'partition_strategy': 'fine'
            },
            'aggregation': {
                'codec': 'zstd',
                'reason': 'Balance compression and processing speed',
                'partition_strategy': 'medium'
            },
            'point_lookup': {
                'codec': 'lz4',
                'reason': 'Minimal decompression overhead',
                'partition_strategy': 'fine'
            }
        }
        
        if query_pattern not in pattern_recommendations:
            query_pattern = 'aggregation'
        
        config = pattern_recommendations[query_pattern]
        codec = config['codec']
        
        print(f"\n🎯 Optimizing for Query Pattern: {query_pattern}")
        print(f"  - Codec: {codec}")
        print(f"  - Reason: {config['reason']}")
        print(f"  - Partition Strategy: {config['partition_strategy']}")
        
        pattern = self.patterns.get(codec)
        if pattern:
            pattern.configure_compression()
            pattern.write_compressed_data(df, output_path, 'parquet')


# ============================================================================
# Compression Utilities and Helper Functions
# ============================================================================

class CompressionUtils:
    """
    Utility functions for compression analysis and management.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def estimate_compression_ratio(original_size: int, compressed_size: int) -> float:
        """Calculate compression ratio."""
        if compressed_size == 0:
            return 0.0
        return original_size / compressed_size
    
    @staticmethod
    def get_file_size(spark: SparkSession, path: str) -> int:
        """
        Get total size of files in a path.
        Returns size in bytes.
        """
        try:
            sc = spark.sparkContext
            hadoop_conf = sc._jsc.hadoopConfiguration()
            fs = sc._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileSystem.get(hadoop_conf)
            path_obj = sc._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.Path(path)
            
            if fs.exists(path_obj):
                content_summary = fs.getContentSummary(path_obj)
                return content_summary.getLength()
            else:
                return 0
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"⚠ Error getting file size: {str(e)}")
            return 0
    
    @staticmethod
    def compare_compression_sizes(spark: SparkSession, paths: Dict[str, str]) -> Dict:
        """
        Compare file sizes for different compression codecs.
        """
        results = {}
        
        print("\n📏 Compression Size Comparison:")
        print("=" * 60)
        
        for codec, path in paths.items():
            size = CompressionUtils.get_file_size(spark, path)
            results[codec] = {
                'size_bytes': size,
                'size_mb': size / (1024 * 1024)
            }
            print(f"{codec.upper():15} : {size:15,} bytes ({size/(1024*1024):10.2f} MB)")
        
        # Calculate compression ratios relative to largest
        if results:
            max_size = max(r['size_bytes'] for r in results.values())
            for codec in results:
                if results[codec]['size_bytes'] > 0:
                    results[codec]['ratio'] = max_size / results[codec]['size_bytes']
                else:
                    results[codec]['ratio'] = 0
        
        print("=" * 60)
        return results
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_compression_report(benchmark_results: Dict, 
                                 size_results: Dict) -> str:
        """
        Create comprehensive compression analysis report.
        """
        report = []
        report.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
        report.append("COMPRESSION ANALYSIS REPORT")
        report.append("=" * 80)
        report.append(f"Generated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}")
        report.append("")
        
        # Performance metrics
        report.append("PERFORMANCE METRICS:")
        report.append("-" * 80)
        report.append(f"{'Codec':<15} {'Write(s)':<12} {'Read(s)':<12} {'Total(s)':<12}")
        report.append("-" * 80)
        
        for codec, metrics in benchmark_results.items():
            if 'error' not in metrics:
                report.append(
                    f"{codec:<15} "
                    f"{metrics['write_time']:<12.2f} "
                    f"{metrics['read_time']:<12.2f} "
                    f"{metrics['total_time']:<12.2f}"
                )
        
        # Size metrics
        if size_results:
            report.append("")
            report.append("SIZE METRICS:")
            report.append("-" * 80)
            report.append(f"{'Codec':<15} {'Size (MB)':<15} {'Ratio':<12}")
            report.append("-" * 80)
            
            for codec, metrics in size_results.items():
                report.append(
                    f"{codec:<15} "
                    f"{metrics['size_mb']:<15.2f} "
                    f"{metrics.get('ratio', 0):<12.2f}"
                )
        
        # Recommendations
        report.append("")
        report.append("RECOMMENDATIONS:")
        report.append("-" * 80)
        
        if benchmark_results:
            # Find fastest
            fastest = min(
                [(k, v['total_time']) for k, v in benchmark_results.items() 
                 if 'error' not in v],
                key=lambda x: x[1],
                default=None
            )
            if fastest:
                report.append(f"Fastest: {fastest[0].upper()} ({fastest[1]:.2f}s)")
        
        if size_results:
            # Find smallest
            smallest = min(
                [(k, v['size_mb']) for k, v in size_results.items()],
                key=lambda x: x[1],
                default=None
            )
            if smallest:
                report.append(f"Smallest: {smallest[0].upper()} ({smallest[1]:.2f} MB)")
        
        report.append("=" * 80)
        
        return "\n".join(report)

def create_sample_data(spark: SparkSession, num_rows: int = 100000) -> DataFrame:
    """
    Create sample dataset for testing compression patterns.
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, randn, expr, array, lit
    
    print(f"\n📝 Creating sample dataset with {num_rows:,} rows...")
    
    # Create diverse data types to test compression
    df = spark.range(num_rows) \
        .withColumn("string_col", expr("concat('user_', cast(id as string))")) \
        .withColumn("int_col", (col("id") % 1000).cast("int")) \
        .withColumn("double_col", rand() * 1000) \
        .withColumn("text_col", expr("""
            concat(
                'This is a sample text with some repetitive content. ',
                'Transaction ID: ', cast(id as string), '. ',
                'Status: ', case when id % 3 = 0 then 'COMPLETED' 
                                when id % 3 = 1 then 'PENDING' 
                                else 'FAILED' end
            )
        """)) \
        .withColumn("json_col", expr("""
            concat(
                '{"id":', cast(id as string), 
                ',"value":', cast(rand() * 100 as string),
                ',"status":"active"}'
            )
        """)) \
        .withColumn("timestamp_col", current_timestamp()) \
        .withColumn("category", expr("case when id % 5 = 0 then 'A' when id % 5 = 1 then 'B' when id % 5 = 2 then 'C' when id % 5 = 3 then 'D' else 'E' end"))
    
    print(f"✓ Sample dataset created")
    return df

def demonstrate_advanced_patterns(spark: SparkSession):
    """
    Demonstrate advanced compression optimization techniques.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ADVANCED COMPRESSION OPTIMIZATION TECHNIQUES")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create sample data
    df = create_sample_data(spark, num_rows=50000)
    
    # Technique 1: Query-Aware Compression
    print("\n🎯 Technique 1: Query-Aware Compression Optimization")
    print("-" * 80)
    adaptive = AdaptiveCompressionPattern(spark)
    
    query_patterns = ['full_scan', 'selective', 'aggregation', 'point_lookup']
    for pattern in query_patterns:
        adaptive.optimize_for_query_pattern(
            df, 
            f"/tmp/optimized/{pattern}",
            query_pattern=pattern
        )
    
    # Technique 2: ZSTD Level Benchmarking
    print("\n📈 Technique 2: Compression Level Optimization (ZSTD)")
    print("-" * 80)
    zstd = ZSTDCompressionPattern(spark)
    level_results = zstd.benchmark_compression_levels(
        df, 
        "/tmp/zstd_levels",
        levels=[1, 3, 6, 9, 12]
    )
    
    print("\nZSTD Level Analysis:")
    for level, metrics in level_results.items():
        print(f"  Level {level}: {metrics['duration']:.2f}s")
    
    # Technique 3: Hybrid Compression Strategy
    print("\n🔄 Technique 3: Hybrid Compression Strategy")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("Different compression for different column types:")
    
    # Separate columns by type
    string_cols = [field.name for field in df.schema.fields if field.dataType == StringType()]
    numeric_cols = [field.name for field in df.schema.fields 
                   if field.dataType in [IntegerType(), DoubleType()]]
    
    print(f"  String columns ({len(string_cols)}): Use ZSTD/Brotli")
    print(f"  Numeric columns ({len(numeric_cols)}): Use LZ4/Snappy")
    
    # Technique 4: Partition-Aware Compression
    print("\n📂 Technique 4: Partition-Aware Compression")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Hot partitions: LZ4 (fast access)
    # Cold partitions: GZIP (high compression)
    
    hot_data = df.filter(col("id") % 10 == 0)  # Recent/frequently accessed
    cold_data = df.filter(col("id") % 10 != 0)  # Historical/rarely accessed
    
    lz4 = LZ4CompressionPattern(spark)
    lz4.configure_compression()
    lz4.write_compressed_data(hot_data, "/tmp/partitioned/hot", "parquet")
    
    gzip = GZIPCompressionPattern(spark, compression_level=9)
    gzip.configure_compression()
    gzip.write_compressed_data(cold_data, "/tmp/partitioned/cold", "parquet")
    
    print("✓ Hot data: LZ4 compression")
    print("✓ Cold data: GZIP compression")
    
    # Technique 5: Compression with Statistics
    print("\n📊 Technique 5: Statistics-Driven Compression")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Collect statistics
    stats = df.select([
        col(c).isNull().cast("int").alias(f"{c}_nulls") 
        for c in df.columns
    ]).agg(*[
        sum(f"{c}_nulls").alias(f"{c}_null_count") 
        for c in df.columns
    ]).collect()[0].asDict()
    
    print("Column Statistics:")
    for col_name, null_count in stats.items():
        print(f"  {col_name}: {null_count} nulls")
    
    print("\n✓ Advanced techniques demonstrated!")

        print("\n" + "=" * 80)

        guide = """

└─────────────────┴──────────────────┴────────────────────┴─────────────────────┘

DECISION TREE:

def example_1_simple_compression():

        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:

def example_5_tiered_storage():
    """
    Example 5: Multi-tier storage with different compression
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("EXAMPLE 5: Tiered Storage Strategy")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Tiered Storage Example") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Create data with different access patterns
        current_date = datetime.now()
        
        df = spark.range(30000).toDF("id") \
            .withColumn("date", expr("date_sub(current_date(), cast(id % 365 as int))")) \
            .withColumn("data", expr("concat('record_', cast(id as string))")) \
            .withColumn("value", rand() * 1000)
        
        # Classify data into tiers based on age
        from pyspark.sql.functions import datediff, current_date as current_date_func
        
        # Hot tier: Last 30 days (LZ4 - fast access)
        hot_df = df.filter(datediff(current_date_func(), col("date")) <= 30)
        lz4 = LZ4CompressionPattern(spark)
        lz4.configure_compression()
        lz4.write_compressed_data(hot_df, "/tmp/example5_tier/hot", "parquet")
        print(f"✓ Hot tier: {hot_df.count()} records with LZ4 compression")
        
        # Warm tier: 31-180 days (ZSTD - balanced)
        warm_df = df.filter(
            (datediff(current_date_func(), col("date")) > 30) &
            (datediff(current_date_func(), col("date")) <= 180)
        )
        zstd = ZSTDCompressionPattern(spark)
        zstd.configure_compression()
        zstd.write_compressed_data(warm_df, "/tmp/example5_tier/warm", "parquet")
        print(f"✓ Warm tier: {warm_df.count()} records with ZSTD compression")
        
        # Cold tier: >180 days (GZIP - maximum compression)
        cold_df = df.filter(datediff(current_date_func(), col("date")) > 180)
        gzip = GZIPCompressionPattern(spark, compression_level=9)
        gzip.configure_compression()
        gzip.write_compressed_data(cold_df, "/tmp/example5_tier/cold", "parquet")
        print(f"✓ Cold tier: {cold_df.count()} records with GZIP compression")
        
        print("\n✓ Tiered storage implemented successfully")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()


def example_6_compression_benchmark():
    """
    Example 6: Benchmark different compression codecs
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("EXAMPLE 6: Compression Codec Benchmark")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("Compression Benchmark Example") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Create test dataset
        df = create_sample_data(spark, num_rows=50000)
        
        # Benchmark different codecs
        codecs = {
            'snappy': SnappyCompressionPattern(spark),
            'gzip': GZIPCompressionPattern(spark),
            'zstd': ZSTDCompressionPattern(spark),
            'lz4': LZ4CompressionPattern(spark)
        }
        
        results = {}
        
        print("\n🔬 Running benchmarks...")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        for codec_name, pattern in codecs.items():
            print(f"\nTesting {codec_name.upper()}...")
            
            # Configure
            pattern.configure_compression()
            
            # Measure write
            output_path = f"/tmp/example6_benchmark/{codec_name}"
            start = datetime.now()
            pattern.write_compressed_data(df, output_path, "parquet")
            write_time = (datetime.now() - start).total_seconds()
            
            # Measure read
            start = datetime.now()
            read_df = pattern.read_compressed_data(output_path, "parquet")
            count = read_df.count()
            read_time = (datetime.now() - start).total_seconds()
            
            # Get size
            size = CompressionUtils.get_file_size(spark, output_path)
            
            results[codec_name] = {
                'write_time': write_time,
                'read_time': read_time,
                'total_time': write_time + read_time,
                'size_mb': size / (1024 * 1024),
                'records': count
            }
            
            print(f"  Write: {write_time:.2f}s | Read: {read_time:.2f}s | Size: {size/(1024*1024):.2f} MB")
        
        # Print summary
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("BENCHMARK SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"{'Codec':<15} {'Write(s)':<12} {'Read(s)':<12} {'Total(s)':<12} {'Size(MB)':<12}")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        for codec, metrics in results.items():
            print(f"{codec:<15} {metrics['write_time']:<12.2f} {metrics['read_time']:<12.2f} "
                  f"{metrics['total_time']:<12.2f} {metrics['size_mb']:<12.2f}")
        
        # Find best
        fastest = min(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['total_time'])
        smallest = min(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['size_mb'])
        
        print("\n" + "-" * 80)
        print(f"⚡ Fastest: {fastest[0].upper()} ({fastest[1]['total_time']:.2f}s)")
        print(f"💾 Smallest: {smallest[0].upper()} ({smallest[1]['size_mb']:.2f} MB)")
        print("=" * 80)
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()

class CompressionTester:
    """
    Comprehensive testing suite for compression patterns.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.test_results = {}
    
    def test_codec_availability(self) -> Dict:
        """Test which compression codecs are available."""
        print("\n🔍 Testing Codec Availability")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        codecs = ['snappy', 'gzip', 'lz4', 'zstd', 'brotli', 'lzo']
        results = {}
        
        test_df = self.spark.range(100).toDF("id")
        
        for codec in codecs:
            try:
                test_path = f"/tmp/codec_test/{codec}"
                
                if codec == 'brotli':
                    # Brotli requires special handling
                    results[codec] = {
                        'available': False,
                        'note': 'Requires custom implementation'
                    }
                    print(f"  {codec:<10} : ⚠️  Requires custom implementation")
                    continue
                
                # Try to write with codec
                test_df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                    .option("compression", codec) \
                    .parquet(test_path)
                
                # Try to read back
                read_df = self.spark.read.parquet(test_path)
                count = read_df.count()
                
                results[codec] = {
                    'available': True,
                    'tested': True,
                    'records': count
                }
                print(f"  {codec:<10} : ✓ Available and working")
                
            except Exception as e:
                results[codec] = {
                    'available': False,
                    'error': str(e)
                }
                print(f"  {codec:<10} : ✗ Not available - {str(e)[:50]}")
        
        self.test_results['codec_availability'] = results
        return results
    
    def test_compression_correctness(self) -> bool:
        """Test that compression/decompression maintains data integrity."""
        print("\n🔍 Testing Data Integrity")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # Create test data with known values
        test_data = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (1, "test1", 100.5),
            (2, "test2", 200.5),
            (3, "test3", 300.5)
        ], ["id", "name", "value"])
        
        codecs = ['snappy', 'gzip', 'lz4', 'zstd']
        all_passed = True
        
        for codec in codecs:
            try:
                # Write
                path = f"/tmp/integrity_test/{codec}"
                test_data.write.mode("overwrite") \
                    .option("compression", codec) \
                    .parquet(path)
                
                # Read back
                read_data = self.spark.read.parquet(path)
                
                # Compare
                original_count = test_data.count()
                read_count = read_data.count()
                
                # Collect and compare values
                original_sum = test_data.selectExpr("sum(value)").collect()[0][0]
                read_sum = read_data.selectExpr("sum(value)").collect()[0][0]
                
                if original_count == read_count and abs(original_sum - read_sum) < 0.01:
                    print(f"  {codec:<10} : ✓ Data integrity verified")
                else:
                    print(f"  {codec:<10} : ✗ Data integrity check failed")
                    all_passed = False
                    
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  {codec:<10} : ✗ Error - {str(e)}")
                all_passed = False
        
        return all_passed
    
    def test_performance_characteristics(self) -> Dict:
        """Test performance characteristics of each codec."""
        print("\n🔍 Testing Performance Characteristics")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # Create larger test dataset
        test_df = create_sample_data(self.spark, num_rows=10000)
        
        codecs = ['snappy', 'gzip', 'lz4', 'zstd']
        results = {}
        
        for codec in codecs:
            try:
                path = f"/tmp/perf_test/{codec}"
                
                # Measure write
                write_start = datetime.now()
                test_df.write.mode("overwrite") \
                    .option("compression", codec) \
                    .parquet(path)
                write_time = (datetime.now() - write_start).total_seconds()
                
                # Measure read
                read_start = datetime.now()
                read_df = self.spark.read.parquet(path)
                count = read_df.count()
                read_time = (datetime.now() - read_start).total_seconds()
                
                # Get size
                size = CompressionUtils.get_file_size(self.spark, path)
                
                results[codec] = {
                    'write_time': write_time,
                    'read_time': read_time,
                    'size_mb': size / (1024 * 1024),
                    'records': count
                }
                
                print(f"  {codec:<10} : Write={write_time:.2f}s, Read={read_time:.2f}s, Size={size/(1024*1024):.2f}MB")
                
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  {codec:<10} : ✗ Error - {str(e)}")
        
        self.test_results['performance'] = results
        return results
    
    def run_all_tests(self) -> Dict:
        """Run all compression tests."""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("RUNNING COMPREHENSIVE COMPRESSION TESTS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Test codec availability
        self.test_codec_availability()
        
        # Test data integrity
        integrity_passed = self.test_compression_correctness()
        
        # Test performance
        self.test_performance_characteristics()
        
        # Summary
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("TEST SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"Data Integrity: {'✓ PASSED' if integrity_passed else '✗ FAILED'}")
        print(f"Codecs Tested: {len(self.test_results.get('codec_availability', {}))}")
        print(f"Performance Tests: {len(self.test_results.get('performance', {}))}")
        
        return self.test_results
