# ============================================================================
# 6. MEMORY SPILL STRATEGY PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class SpillStrategy(Enum):
    """Enumeration of spill strategies."""
    MEMORY_ONLY = "MEMORY_ONLY"  # Never spill to disk
    AGGRESSIVE_SPILL = "AGGRESSIVE_SPILL"  # Spill early to avoid OOM
    BALANCED_SPILL = "BALANCED_SPILL"  # Balance memory and disk usage
    DISK_OPTIMIZED = "DISK_OPTIMIZED"  # Optimize for disk I/O


class MemorySpillStrategyPattern:
    """
    Implements memory spill strategies for handling data that doesn't fit in memory.
    
    When execution memory is exhausted during operations like sorts or aggregations,
    this pattern controls how data is spilled to disk.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, 
                 spill_strategy: str = "BALANCED_SPILL",
                 spill_threshold: float = 0.8,
                 compression_codec: str = "lz4"):
        """
        Initialize Memory Spill Manager.
        
        Args:
            spill_strategy: Strategy for spilling data to disk
            spill_threshold: Memory threshold before spilling (0.0-1.0)
            compression_codec: Codec for compressing spilled data (lz4, snappy, etc.)
        """
        self.spill_strategy = spill_strategy
        self.spill_threshold = spill_threshold
        self.compression_codec = compression_codec
        self.spill_metrics = {
            "total_spills": 0,
            "total_spilled_bytes": 0,
            "spill_operations": []
        }
        
    def configure_spark(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Configure Spark for memory spill management.
        """
        # Basic spill configuration
        spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.spill.compress", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.compress", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.io.compression.codec", self.compression_codec)
        
        # Strategy-specific configuration
        if self.spill_strategy == "MEMORY_ONLY":
            # Maximize memory usage, minimize spilling
            spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.spill", "false")
            spark.conf.set("spark.memory.fraction", "0.8")
            
        elif self.spill_strategy == "AGGRESSIVE_SPILL":
            # Spill early to avoid OOM
            spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.spill", "true")
            spark.conf.set("spark.memory.fraction", "0.4")
            spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.memoryFraction", "0.3")
            
        elif self.spill_strategy == "BALANCED_SPILL":
            # Balance memory and disk usage
            spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.spill", "true")
            spark.conf.set("spark.memory.fraction", "0.6")
            spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.memoryFraction", "0.5")
            
        elif self.spill_strategy == "DISK_OPTIMIZED":
            # Optimize for disk I/O performance
            spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.spill", "true")
            spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.file.buffer", "128k")
            spark.conf.set("spark.reducer.maxSizeInFlight", "96m")
            spark.conf.set("spark.shuffle.io.maxRetries", "5")
        
        # Configure spill directory
        spark.conf.set("spark.local.dir", "/tmp/spark-spill")
        
        logger.info(f"Memory Spill Strategy Pattern configured:")
        logger.info(f"  - Spill Strategy: {self.spill_strategy}")
        logger.info(f"  - Spill Threshold: {self.spill_threshold}")
        logger.info(f"  - Compression Codec: {self.compression_codec}")
    
    def simulate_sort_with_spill(self, spark: SparkSession, num_records: int = 10000000):
        """
        Simulate a large sort operation that may require spilling.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
            num_records: Number of records to sort
        """
        logger.info(f"\n=== Simulating Sort Operation ({num_records} records) ===")
        
        # Create large dataset for sorting
        df = spark.range(0, num_records).select(
            col("id"),
            (rand() * 1000000).cast("int").alias("sort_key"),
            (rand() * 100).cast("int").alias("value"),
            concat(lit("Data_"), col("id")).alias("text_data")
        )
        
        logger.info("Starting sort operation...")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Perform sort that may trigger spilling
        sorted_df = df.orderBy("sort_key", "value")
        
        # Trigger execution
        result_count = sorted_df.count()
        
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        logger.info(f"Sort operation completed:")
        logger.info(f"  - Records sorted: {result_count}")
        logger.info(f"  - Execution time: {execution_time:.2f}s")
        logger.info(f"  - Strategy: {self.spill_strategy}")
        
        # Record spill metrics
        self.record_spill_operation("sort", num_records, execution_time)
        
        return sorted_df
    
    def simulate_aggregation_with_spill(self, spark: SparkSession, num_records: int = 10000000):
        """
        Simulate a large aggregation that may require spilling.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
            num_records: Number of records to aggregate
        """
        logger.info(f"\n=== Simulating Aggregation Operation ({num_records} records) ===")
        
        # Create large dataset for aggregation
        df = spark.range(0, num_records).select(
            (col("id") % 100000).alias("group_key"),
            (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value1"),
            (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value2"),
            (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value3")
        )
        
        logger.info("Starting aggregation operation...")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Perform aggregation that may trigger spilling
        agg_df = df.groupBy("group_key").agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            sum("value1").alias("sum_value1"),
            avg("value1").alias("avg_value1"),
            sum("value2").alias("sum_value2"),
            avg("value2").alias("avg_value2"),
            sum("value3").alias("sum_value3"),
            avg("value3").alias("avg_value3")
        )
        
        # Trigger execution
        result_count = agg_df.count()
        
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        logger.info(f"Aggregation operation completed:")
        logger.info(f"  - Groups aggregated: {result_count}")
        logger.info(f"  - Execution time: {execution_time:.2f}s")
        logger.info(f"  - Strategy: {self.spill_strategy}")
        
        # Record spill metrics
        self.record_spill_operation("aggregation", num_records, execution_time)
        
        return agg_df
    
    def simulate_join_with_spill(self, spark: SparkSession, num_records: int = 5000000):
        """
        Simulate a large join operation that may require spilling.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
            num_records: Number of records per DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"\n=== Simulating Join Operation ({num_records} records per side) ===")
        
        # Create large datasets for join
        df1 = spark.range(0, num_records).select(
            col("id").alias("key"),
            (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value1"),
            concat(lit("Left_"), col("id")).alias("data1")
        )
        
        df2 = spark.range(0, num_records).select(
            col("id").alias("key"),
            (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value2"),
            concat(lit("Right_"), col("id")).alias("data2")
        )
        
        logger.info("Starting join operation...")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Perform join that may trigger spilling
        joined_df = df1.join(df2, on="key", how="inner")
        
        # Trigger execution
        result_count = joined_df.count()
        
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        logger.info(f"Join operation completed:")
        logger.info(f"  - Records joined: {result_count}")
        logger.info(f"  - Execution time: {execution_time:.2f}s")
        logger.info(f"  - Strategy: {self.spill_strategy}")
        
        # Record spill metrics
        self.record_spill_operation("join", num_records * 2, execution_time)
        
        return joined_df
    
    def record_spill_operation(self, operation_type: str, records: int, execution_time: float):
        """
        Record metrics for a spill operation.
        
        Args:
            operation_type: Type of operation (sort, aggregation, join)
            records: Number of records processed
            execution_time: Time taken for the operation
        """
        self.spill_metrics["total_spills"] += 1
        
        spill_info = {
            "operation": operation_type,
            "records": records,
            "execution_time": execution_time,
            "strategy": self.spill_strategy,
            "timestamp": time.time()
        }
        
        self.spill_metrics["spill_operations"].append(spill_info)
    
    def get_spill_statistics(self) -> Dict:
        """
        Get statistics about spill operations.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing spill statistics
        """
        if not self.spill_metrics["spill_operations"]:
            return {
                "total_operations": 0,
                "average_execution_time": 0,
                "operations": []
            }
        
        total_time = sum(op["execution_time"] for op in self.spill_metrics["spill_operations"])
        avg_time = total_time / len(self.spill_metrics["spill_operations"])
        
        return {
            "total_operations": self.spill_metrics["total_spills"],
            "average_execution_time": avg_time,
            "total_execution_time": total_time,
            "strategy": self.spill_strategy,
            "operations": self.spill_metrics["spill_operations"]
        }
    
    def compare_spill_strategies(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Compare different spill strategies by running the same workload.
        """
        logger.info("\n=== Comparing Spill Strategies ===")
        
        strategies = ["MEMORY_ONLY", "AGGRESSIVE_SPILL", "BALANCED_SPILL", "DISK_OPTIMIZED"]
        results = {}
        
        for strategy in strategies:
            logger.info(f"\n--- Testing {strategy} ---")
            
            # Reconfigure with new strategy
            self.spill_strategy = strategy
            self.configure_spark(spark)
            
            # Run test workload
            try:
                start_time = time.time()
                self.simulate_sort_with_spill(spark, num_records=1000000)
                total_time = time.time() - start_time
                
                results[strategy] = {
                    "success": True,
                    "execution_time": total_time
                }
                
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Strategy {strategy} failed: {str(e)}")
                results[strategy] = {
                    "success": False,
                    "error": str(e)
                }
        
        # Display comparison
        logger.info("\n=== Strategy Comparison Results ===")
        for strategy, result in results.items():
            if result["success"]:
                logger.info(f"{strategy}: {result['execution_time']:.2f}s")
            else:
                logger.info(f"{strategy}: FAILED - {result.get('error', 'Unknown error')}")
        
        return results
    
    def demonstrate_memory_spill(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Demonstrate memory spill pattern with various operations.
        """
        self.configure_spark(spark)
        
        logger.info("=== Memory Spill Strategy Pattern Demo ===")
        
        # Demonstrate different operations that may trigger spilling
        self.simulate_sort_with_spill(spark, num_records=2000000)
        self.simulate_aggregation_with_spill(spark, num_records=2000000)
        self.simulate_join_with_spill(spark, num_records=1000000)
        
        # Display spill statistics
        logger.info("\n=== Spill Statistics ===")
        stats = self.get_spill_statistics()
        logger.info(f"Total operations: {stats['total_operations']}")
        logger.info(f"Average execution time: {stats['average_execution_time']:.2f}s")
        logger.info(f"Total execution time: {stats['total_execution_time']:.2f}s")
        
        logger.info("\nOperation details:")
        for op in stats['operations']:
            logger.info(f"  - {op['operation']}: {op['records']} records, "
                       f"{op['execution_time']:.2f}s")

       - Adaptive query execution for dynamic optimization
       - Configurable shuffle partitions and memory fractions
    
    3. STORAGE MEMORY PATTERN
       - Manages cached/persisted RDDs and DataFrames
       - Multiple storage levels (MEMORY_ONLY, MEMORY_AND_DISK, etc.)
       - Compression support for efficient storage
    
    4. MEMORY BORROWING PATTERN
       - Allows execution and storage to borrow from each other
       - Dynamic memory allocation based on workload
       - Improves overall memory utilization
    
    5. MEMORY EVICTION PATTERN
       - Implements LRU, LFU, and FIFO eviction strategies
       - Priority-based eviction for important datasets
       - Automatic eviction when storage memory is full
    
    6. MEMORY SPILL STRATEGY PATTERN
       - Handles data that doesn't fit in memory
       - Multiple strategies: MEMORY_ONLY, AGGRESSIVE_SPILL, BALANCED_SPILL
       - Compressed spilling to disk for better performance
    
    BEST PRACTICES:
    ---------------
    - Use unified memory manager for flexible memory allocation
    - Configure execution memory based on workload characteristics
    - Choose appropriate storage levels for cached data
    - Enable memory borrowing for dynamic workloads
    - Implement eviction strategies for memory-constrained environments
    - Configure spill strategies to prevent OOM errors
    - Monitor memory usage and adjust configurations accordingly
    - Use compression for both storage and spilling
    - Consider off-heap memory for large-scale applications
    - Profile your applications to identify memory bottlenecks
    """
    
    print(summary)
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("Demonstration Complete!")
    print("=" * 80)

def create_memory_optimized_spark_session(
    app_name: str,
    executor_memory: str = "4g",
    driver_memory: str = "2g",
    memory_fraction: float = 0.6,
    storage_fraction: float = 0.5,
    enable_adaptive: bool = True
) -> SparkSession:
    """
    Create a SparkSession with optimized memory configuration.
    
    Args:
        app_name: Name of the application
        executor_memory: Memory per executor
        driver_memory: Memory for driver
        memory_fraction: Fraction of heap for execution and storage
        storage_fraction: Fraction of unified memory for storage
        enable_adaptive: Enable adaptive query execution
        
    Returns:
        Configured SparkSession
    """
    builder = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName(app_name) \
        .config("spark.executor.memory", executor_memory) \
        .config("spark.driver.memory", driver_memory) \
        .config("spark.memory.fraction", str(memory_fraction)) \
        .config("spark.memory.storageFraction", str(storage_fraction)) \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", str(enable_adaptive).lower()) \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true") \
        .config("spark.shuffle.spill.compress", "true") \
        .config("spark.io.compression.codec", "lz4") \
        .config("spark.rdd.compress", "true")
    
    return builder.getOrCreate()


def monitor_memory_usage(spark: SparkSession) -> Dict:
    """
    Monitor current memory usage of the Spark application.
    
    Args:
        spark: Active SparkSession
        
    Returns:
        Dictionary containing memory usage information
    """
    sc = spark.sparkContext
    
    # Get configuration
    executor_memory = sc._conf.get("spark.executor.memory", "1g")
    driver_memory = sc._conf.get("spark.driver.memory", "1g")
    memory_fraction = float(sc._conf.get("spark.memory.fraction", "0.6"))
    storage_fraction = float(sc._conf.get("spark.memory.storageFraction", "0.5"))
    
    # Calculate memory allocations
    memory_info = {
        "executor_memory": executor_memory,
        "driver_memory": driver_memory,
        "memory_fraction": memory_fraction,
        "storage_fraction": storage_fraction,
        "execution_fraction": 1 - storage_fraction,
        "configurations": {
            "adaptive_enabled": sc._conf.get("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "false"),
            "shuffle_compress": sc._conf.get("spark.shuffle.spill.compress", "false"),
            "compression_codec": sc._conf.get("spark.io.compression.codec", "lz4"),
            "off_heap_enabled": sc._conf.get("spark.memory.offHeap.enabled", "false")
        }
    }
    
    return memory_info


def print_memory_configuration(spark: SparkSession):
    """
    Print detailed memory configuration of the Spark session.
    
    Args:
        spark: Active SparkSession
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SPARK MEMORY CONFIGURATION")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    memory_info = monitor_memory_usage(spark)
    
    print(f"\nMemory Allocation:")
    print(f"  Executor Memory: {memory_info['executor_memory']}")
    print(f"  Driver Memory: {memory_info['driver_memory']}")
    print(f"  Memory Fraction: {memory_info['memory_fraction']}")
    print(f"  Storage Fraction: {memory_info['storage_fraction']}")
    print(f"  Execution Fraction: {memory_info['execution_fraction']}")
    
    print(f"\nConfigurations:")
    for key, value in memory_info['configurations'].items():
        print(f"  {key}: {value}")
    
    print("=" * 80)

class MemoryPerformanceTester:
    """
    Utility class for testing memory performance with different configurations.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.test_results = []
    
    def run_performance_test(self, 
                            spark: SparkSession,
                            test_name: str,
                            test_function,
                            *args, **kwargs):
        """
        Run a performance test and record results.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
            test_name: Name of the test
            test_function: Function to test
            *args, **kwargs: Arguments for test function
        """
        logger.info(f"\nRunning performance test: {test_name}")
        
        start_time = time.time()
        
        try:
            result = test_function(spark, *args, **kwargs)
            execution_time = time.time() - start_time
            
            test_result = {
                "test_name": test_name,
                "success": True,
                "execution_time": execution_time,
                "timestamp": time.time()
            }
            
            logger.info(f"Test '{test_name}' completed in {execution_time:.2f}s")
            
        except Exception as e:
            execution_time = time.time() - start_time
            
            test_result = {
                "test_name": test_name,
                "success": False,
                "execution_time": execution_time,
                "error": str(e),
                "timestamp": time.time()
            }
            
            logger.error(f"Test '{test_name}' failed: {str(e)}")
        
        self.test_results.append(test_result)
        return test_result
    
    def get_test_summary(self) -> Dict:
        """
        Get summary of all performance tests.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing test summary
        """
        successful_tests = [t for t in self.test_results if t["success"]]
        failed_tests = [t for t in self.test_results if not t["success"]]
        
        summary = {
            "total_tests": len(self.test_results),
            "successful_tests": len(successful_tests),
            "failed_tests": len(failed_tests),
            "average_execution_time": sum(t["execution_time"] for t in successful_tests) / len(successful_tests) if successful_tests else 0,
            "total_execution_time": sum(t["execution_time"] for t in self.test_results),
            "results": self.test_results
        }
        
        return summary
    
    def print_test_summary(self):
        """Print formatted test summary."""
        summary = self.get_test_summary()
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("PERFORMANCE TEST SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"Total Tests: {summary['total_tests']}")
        print(f"Successful: {summary['successful_tests']}")
        print(f"Failed: {summary['failed_tests']}")
        print(f"Average Execution Time: {summary['average_execution_time']:.2f}s")
        print(f"Total Execution
```python
 Time: {summary['total_execution_time']:.2f}s")
        
        print("\nDetailed Results:")
        for result in summary['results']:
            status = "✓ SUCCESS" if result['success'] else "✗ FAILED"
            print(f"  {status} - {result['test_name']}: {result['execution_time']:.2f}s")
            if not result['success']:
                print(f"    Error: {result.get('error', 'Unknown error')}")
        
        print("=" * 80)

def example_unified_memory_usage():
    """
    Example of using Unified Memory Manager Pattern in a real scenario.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("EXAMPLE: Unified Memory Manager Pattern")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create unified memory manager
    manager = UnifiedMemoryManagerPattern(
        total_memory_fraction=0.7,  # 70% of heap for execution + storage
        storage_fraction=0.4,        # 40% of unified memory for storage
        enable_off_heap=True         # Enable off-heap memory
    )
    
    spark = manager.create_spark_session("RealWorldExample")
    
    try:
        # Simulate a real-world ETL pipeline
        print("\nSimulating ETL Pipeline...")
        
        # 1. Read large dataset
        raw_data = spark.range(0, 5000000).select(
            col("id").alias("customer_id"),
            (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("purchase_amount"),
            (rand() * 10).cast("int").alias("product_category"),
            date_sub(current_date(), (rand() * 365).cast("int")).alias("purchase_date")
        )
        
        # 2. Cache frequently accessed data (uses storage memory)
        print("Caching reference data...")
        reference_data = spark.range(0, 10).select(
            col("id").alias("product_category"),
            concat(lit("Category_"), col("id")).alias("category_name")
        )
        reference_data.cache()
        reference_data.count()
        
        # 3. Perform complex aggregation (uses execution memory)
        print("Performing aggregation...")
        daily_sales = raw_data.groupBy("purchase_date", "product_category").agg(
            count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
            sum("purchase_amount").alias("total_sales"),
            avg("purchase_amount").alias("avg_transaction")
        )
        
        # 4. Join with reference data
        print("Joining with reference data...")
        enriched_sales = daily_sales.join(
            reference_data,
            on="product_category",
            how="left"
        )
        
        # 5. Final aggregation
        print("Computing final metrics...")
        final_metrics = enriched_sales.groupBy("category_name").agg(
            sum("total_sales").alias("category_total_sales"),
            avg("avg_transaction").alias("category_avg_transaction"),
            count("*").alias("days_with_sales")
        )
        
        # Show results
        print("\nFinal Metrics:")
        final_metrics.show(10)
        
        # Display memory stats
        print("\nMemory Statistics:")
        stats = manager.get_memory_stats(spark)
        for key, value in stats.items():
            print(f"  {key}: {value}")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()


def example_memory_spill_scenario():
    """
    Example of handling memory spill in a large-scale join operation.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("EXAMPLE: Memory Spill Strategy Pattern")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create spill manager with balanced strategy
    spill_manager = MemorySpillStrategyPattern(
        spill_strategy="BALANCED_SPILL",
        spill_threshold=0.8,
        compression_codec="lz4"
    )
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("LargeScaleJoinExample") \
        .config("spark.executor.memory", "2g") \
        .config("spark.driver.memory", "2g") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        spill_manager.configure_spark(spark)
        
        print("\nSimulating large-scale data join...")
        
        # Create large fact table (sales transactions)
        fact_table = spark.range(0, 10000000).select(
            col("id").alias("transaction_id"),
            (col("id") % 1000000).alias("customer_id"),
            (col("id") % 10000).alias("product_id"),
            (rand() * 1000).cast("decimal(10,2)").alias("amount"),
            date_sub(current_date(), (rand() * 365).cast("int")).alias("transaction_date")
        )
        
        # Create dimension table (customer info)
        dimension_table = spark.range(0, 1000000).select(
            col("id").alias("customer_id"),
            concat(lit("Customer_"), col("id")).alias("customer_name"),
            (rand() * 5).cast("int").alias("customer_segment")
        )
        
        print("Performing join operation (may trigger spilling)...")
        
        # Perform join that will likely trigger spilling
        joined_data = fact_table.join(
            dimension_table,
            on="customer_id",
            how="inner"
        )
        
        # Aggregate results
        segment_analysis = joined_data.groupBy("customer_segment").agg(
            count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_revenue"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_transaction"),
            countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers")
        )
        
        print("\nSegment Analysis Results:")
        segment_analysis.show()
        
        # Display spill statistics
        print("\nSpill Statistics:")
        stats = spill_manager.get_spill_statistics()
        print(f"  Total Operations: {stats['total_operations']}")
        print(f"  Average Execution Time: {stats.get('average_execution_time', 0):.2f}s")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()


def example_memory_eviction_scenario():
    """
    Example of memory eviction in a caching-heavy workload.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("EXAMPLE: Memory Eviction Pattern")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create eviction manager with LRU strategy
    eviction_manager = MemoryEvictionPattern(
        eviction_strategy="LRU",
        max_storage_memory_mb=512  # Limited memory to trigger eviction
    )
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("CacheHeavyWorkload") \
        .config("spark.executor.memory", "2g") \
        .config("spark.driver.memory", "2g") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        eviction_manager.configure_spark(spark)
        
        print("\nSimulating cache-heavy analytics workload...")
        
        # Scenario: Multiple analytical datasets that need caching
        datasets = {}
        
        # Dataset 1: Customer analytics (high priority, frequently accessed)
        print("\n1. Caching customer analytics data...")
        customer_data = spark.range(0, 500000).select(
            col("id").alias("customer_id"),
            (rand() * 100).cast("int").alias("lifetime_value"),
            (rand() * 5).cast("int").alias("segment")
        )
        datasets['customer_analytics'] = customer_data
        eviction_manager.add_cached_block(
            "customer_analytics", 
            customer_data, 
            size_mb=200, 
            priority=10  # High priority
        )
        
        # Dataset 2: Product catalog (medium priority)
        print("\n2. Caching product catalog...")
        product_data = spark.range(0, 100000).select(
            col("id").alias("product_id"),
            concat(lit("Product_"), col("id")).alias("product_name"),
            (rand() * 1000).cast("decimal(10,2)").alias("price")
        )
        datasets['product_catalog'] = product_data
        eviction_manager.add_cached_block(
            "product_catalog", 
            product_data, 
            size_mb=150, 
            priority=5
        )
        
        # Dataset 3: Historical transactions (low priority)
        print("\n3. Caching historical transactions...")
        transaction_data = spark.range(0, 300000).select(
            col("id").alias("transaction_id"),
            (col("id") % 500000).alias("customer_id"),
            (rand() * 500).cast("decimal(10,2)").alias("amount")
        )
        datasets['historical_transactions'] = transaction_data
        eviction_manager.add_cached_block(
            "historical_transactions", 
            transaction_data, 
            size_mb=180, 
            priority=1  # Low priority
        )
        
        # Access customer analytics multiple times (increase LRU score)
        print("\n4. Accessing customer analytics data...")
        for i in range(3):
            eviction_manager.access_cached_block("customer_analytics")
            customer_data.filter(col("segment") == i).count()
        
        # Access product catalog once
        eviction_manager.access_cached_block("product_catalog")
        product_data.filter(col("price") > 100).count()
        
        # Try to add new dataset that requires eviction
        print("\n5. Adding new dataset (triggers eviction)...")
        new_data = spark.range(0, 400000).select(
            col("id"),
            (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value")
        )
        datasets['new_dataset'] = new_data
        eviction_manager.add_cached_block(
            "new_dataset", 
            new_data, 
            size_mb=250, 
            priority=5
        )
        
        # Display final statistics
        print("\n6. Final Eviction Statistics:")
        stats = eviction_manager.get_eviction_stats()
        print(f"  Total Blocks: {stats['total_blocks']}")
        print(f"  Memory Usage: {stats['memory_usage_mb']:.2f} MB / {stats['memory_limit_mb']} MB")
        print(f"  Memory Utilization: {stats['memory_utilization']:.2%}")
        
        print("\n  Remaining Cached Blocks:")
        for block in stats['blocks']:
            print(f"    - {block['name']}: {block['size_mb']} MB, "
                  f"accessed {block['access_count']} times")
        
    finally:
        # Cleanup
        for df in datasets.values():
            df.unpersist()
        spark.stop()

class MemoryOptimizationAdvisor:
    """
    Provides recommendations for memory optimization based on workload analysis.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.recommendations = []
    
    def analyze_workload(self, 
                        workload_type: str,
                        data_size_gb: float,
                        executor_count: int,
                        current_memory_gb: float) -> Dict:
        """
        Analyze workload and provide memory optimization recommendations.
        
        Args:
            workload_type: Type of workload (etl, analytics, ml, streaming)
            data_size_gb: Size of data in GB
            executor_count: Number of executors
            current_memory_gb: Current memory per executor in GB
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing recommendations
        """
        recommendations = {
            "workload_type": workload_type,
            "current_config": {
                "data_size_gb": data_size_gb,
                "executor_count": executor_count,
                "memory_per_executor_gb": current_memory_gb,
                "total_memory_gb": executor_count * current_memory_gb
            },
            "recommendations": []
        }
        
        # Calculate recommended memory
        data_per_executor = data_size_gb / executor_count
        
        if workload_type.lower() == "etl":
            # ETL workloads: moderate caching, heavy shuffles
            recommended_memory = max(data_per_executor * 1.5, 4.0)
            recommendations["recommendations"].extend([
                f"Recommended memory per executor: {recommended_memory:.1f}GB",
                "Use BALANCED_SPILL strategy for shuffles",
                "Set spark.memory.fraction to 0.6",
                "Set spark.memory.storageFraction to 0.4",
                "Enable adaptive query execution"
            ])
            
        elif workload_type.lower() == "analytics":
            # Analytics: heavy caching, moderate shuffles
            recommended_memory = max(data_per_executor * 2.0, 4.0)
            recommendations["recommendations"].extend([
                f"Recommended memory per executor: {recommended_memory:.1f}GB",
                "Use MEMORY_AND_DISK storage level for caching",
                "Set spark.memory.fraction to 0.7",
                "Set spark.memory.storageFraction to 0.6",
                "Implement LRU eviction strategy",
                "Enable compression for cached data"
            ])
            
        elif workload_type.lower() == "ml":
            # ML workloads: very heavy caching, iterative computations
            recommended_memory = max(data_per_executor * 3.0, 8.0)
            recommendations["recommendations"].extend([
                f"Recommended memory per executor: {recommended_memory:.1f}GB",
                "Use MEMORY_ONLY storage level when possible",
                "Set spark.memory.fraction to 0.8",
                "Set spark.memory.storageFraction to 0.7",
                "Enable off-heap memory for additional capacity",
                "Consider increasing executor count for better parallelism"
            ])
            
        elif workload_type.lower() == "streaming":
            # Streaming: moderate memory, focus on throughput
            recommended_memory = max(data_per_executor * 1.2, 2.0)
            recommendations["recommendations"].extend([
                f"Recommended memory per executor: {recommended_memory:.1f}GB",
                "Use MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER for checkpointing",
                "Set spark.memory.fraction to 0.5",
                "Enable AGGRESSIVE_SPILL to prevent OOM",
                "Configure appropriate batch intervals",
                "Monitor backpressure and adjust accordingly"
            ])
        
        # Add general recommendations
        if current_memory_gb < recommended_memory * 0.7:
            recommendations["recommendations"].append(
                f"⚠️  WARNING: Current memory ({current_memory_gb}GB) is significantly "
                f"lower than recommended ({recommended_memory:.1f}GB)"
            )
        
        if data_per_executor > current_memory_gb * 2:
            recommendations["recommendations"].append(
                "⚠️  WARNING: Data per executor exceeds 2x memory. "
                "Consider increasing executor count or memory."
            )
        
        return recommendations
    
    def print_recommendations(self, recommendations: Dict):
        """Print formatted recommendations."""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("MEMORY OPTIMIZATION RECOMMENDATIONS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        print(f"\nWorkload Type: {recommendations['workload_type'].upper()}")
        
        print("\nCurrent Configuration:")
        config = recommendations['current_config']
        print(f"  Data Size: {config['data_size_gb']:.2f} GB")
        print(f"  Executor Count: {config['executor_count']}")
        print(f"  Memory per Executor: {config['memory_per_executor_gb']:.2f} GB")
        print(f"  Total Memory: {config['total_memory_gb']:.2f} GB")
        
        print("\nRecommendations:")
        for i, rec in enumerate(recommendations['recommendations'], 1):
            print(f"  {i}. {rec}")
        
        print("=" * 80)


class MemoryLeakDetector:
    """
    Detects potential memory leaks in Spark applications.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.memory_snapshots = []
        self.cached_rdds = {}
    
    def take_snapshot(self, spark: SparkSession, label: str):
        """
        Take a memory snapshot at a specific point.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
            label: Label for this snapshot
        """
        snapshot = {
            "label": label,
            "timestamp": time.time(),
            "cached_rdds_count": len(self.cached_rdds),
            "memory_info": monitor_memory_usage(spark)
        }
        
        self.memory_snapshots.append(snapshot)
        logger.info(f"Memory snapshot taken: {label}")
    
    def register_cached_rdd(self, name: str, df):
        """
        Register a cached RDD/DataFrame for tracking.
        
        Args:
            name: Name of the cached dataset
            df: DataFrame or RDD
        """
        self.cached_rdds[name] = {
            "dataframe": df,
            "cached_at": time.time()
        }
    
    def unregister_cached_rdd(self, name: str):
        """
        Unregister a cached RDD/DataFrame.
        
        Args:
            name: Name of the cached dataset
        """
        if name in self.cached_rdds:
            del self.cached_rdds[name]
    
    def detect_leaks(self) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Detect potential memory leaks based on snapshots.
        
        Returns:
            List of potential memory leak warnings
        """
        warnings = []
        
        # Check for uncleaned cached RDDs
        current_time = time.time()
        for name, info in self.cached_rdds.items():
            age = current_time - info["cached_at"]
            if age > 3600:  # Cached for more than 1 hour
                warnings.append({
                    "type": "stale_cache",
                    "message": f"RDD '{name}' has been cached for {age/3600:.1f} hours",
                    "recommendation": f"Consider unpersisting '{name}' if no longer needed"
                })
        
        # Check for memory growth trend
        if len(self.memory_snapshots) >= 3:
            # Simple trend detection
            recent_snapshots = self.memory_snapshots[-3:]
            cached_counts = [s["cached_rdds_count"] for s in recent_snapshots]
            
            if all(cached_counts[i] < cached_counts[i+1] for i in range(len(cached_counts)-1)):
                warnings.append({
                    "type": "cache_growth",
                    "message": "Continuous growth in cached RDDs detected",
                    "recommendation": "Review caching strategy and implement eviction policy"
                })
        
        return warnings
    
    def print_leak_report(self):
        """Print memory leak detection report."""
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("MEMORY LEAK DETECTION REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        warnings = self.detect_leaks()
        
        if not warnings:
            print("\n✓ No memory leaks detected")
        else:
            print(f"\n⚠️  {len(warnings)} potential issue(s) detected:")
            for i, warning in enumerate(warnings, 1):
                print(f"\n{i}. {warning['type'].upper()}")
                print(f"   Message: {warning['message']}")
                print(f"   Recommendation: {warning['recommendation']}")
        
        print("\nMemory Snapshots:")
        for snapshot in self.memory_snapshots:
            print(f"  - {snapshot['label']}: {snapshot['cached_rdds_count']} cached RDDs")
        
        print("\nCurrently Cached RDDs:")
        if not self.cached_rdds:
            print("  (none)")
        else:
            for name, info in self.cached_rdds.items():
                age = time.time() - info["cached_at"]
                print(f"  - {name}: cached for {age:.1f}s")
        
        print("=" * 80)

def example_memory_leak_detection():
    """
    Example of using the Memory Leak Detector.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("EXAMPLE: Memory Leak Detection")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    detector = MemoryLeakDetector()
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("MemoryLeakDetection") \
        .config("spark.executor.memory", "2g") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    try:
        # Take initial snapshot
        detector.take_snapshot(spark, "Initial State")
        
        # Cache some datasets
        print("\nCaching datasets...")
        df1 = spark.range(0, 100000).select(col("id"), (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value"))
        df1.cache()
        df1.count()
        detector.register_cached_rdd("dataset_1", df1)
        detector.take_snapshot(spark, "After caching dataset_1")
        
        time.sleep(1)
        
        df2 = spark.range(0, 100000).select(col("id"), (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value"))
        df2.cache()
        df2.count()
        detector.register_cached_rdd("dataset_2", df2)
        detector.take_snapshot(spark, "After caching dataset_2")
        
        time.sleep(1)
        
        df3 = spark.range(0, 100000).select(col("id"), (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value"))
        df3.cache()
        df3.count()
        detector.register_cached_rdd("dataset_3", df3)
        detector.take_snapshot(spark, "After caching dataset_3")
        
        # Simulate forgetting to unpersist
        print("\nSimulating memory leak (not unpersisting cached data)...")
        
        # Print leak detection report
        detector.print_leak_report()
        
        # Cleanup properly
        print("\nCleaning up...")
        df1.unpersist()
        detector.unregister_cached_rdd("dataset_1")
        df2.unpersist()
        detector.unregister_cached_rdd("dataset_2")
        df3.unpersist()
        detector.unregister_cached_rdd("dataset_3")
        
        detector.take_snapshot(spark, "After cleanup")
        detector.print_leak_report()
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()

class MemoryStrategyBenchmark:
    """
    Benchmark different memory strategies to find optimal configuration.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.benchmark_results = []
    
    def benchmark_storage_levels(self, 
                                 spark: SparkSession,
                                 data_size: int = 1000000) -> Dict:
        """
        Benchmark different storage levels for caching.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
            data_size: Number of records to test with
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing benchmark results
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("BENCHMARKING STORAGE LEVELS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        storage_levels = [
            ("MEMORY_ONLY", pyspark.StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY),
            ("MEMORY_ONLY_SER", pyspark.StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY_SER),
            ("MEMORY_AND_DISK", pyspark.StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK),
            ("MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER", pyspark.StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER)
        ]
        
        results = {}
        
        # Create test dataset
        base_df = spark.range(0, data_size).select(
            col("id"),
            (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value"),
            concat(lit("Data_"), col("id")).alias("text")
        )
        
        for level_name, level in storage_levels:
            print(f"\nTesting {level_name}...")
            
            # Cache with specific storage level
            df = base_df.persist(level)
            
            # Measure cache time
            cache_start = time.time()
            count = df.count()
            cache_time = time.time() - cache_start
            
            # Measure read time (from cache)
            read_start = time.time()
            for _ in range(3):
                df.filter(col("value") > 500).count()
            avg_read_time = (time.time() - read_start) / 3
            
            # Unpersist
            df.unpersist()
            
            results[level_name] = {
                "cache_time": cache_time,
                "avg_read_time": avg_read_time,
                "total_time": cache_time + avg_read_time,
                "records": count
            }
            
            print(f"  Cache time: {cache_time:.3f}s")
            print(f"  Avg read time: {avg_read_time:.3f}s")
        
        # Find best performer
        best_level = min(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['total_time'])
        
        print(f"\n✓ Best performing storage level: {best_level[0]}")
        print(f"  Total time: {best_level[1]['total_time']:.3f}s")
        
        return results
    
    def benchmark_spill_strategies(self, 
                                   spark: SparkSession,
                                   data_size: int = 5000000) -> Dict:
        """
        Benchmark different spill strategies.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
            data_size: Number of records to test with
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing benchmark results
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("BENCHMARKING SPILL STRATEGIES")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        strategies = ["AGGRESSIVE_SPILL", "BALANCED_SPILL", "DISK_OPTIMIZED"]
        results = {}
        
        for strategy in strategies:
            print(f"\nTesting {strategy}...")
            
            # Configure strategy
            spill_manager = MemorySpillStrategyPattern(
                spill_strategy=strategy,
                compression_codec="lz4"
            )
            spill_manager.configure_spark(spark)
            
            # Run test workload
            start_time = time.time()
            
            df = spark.range(0, data_size).select(
                (col("id") % 10000).alias("key"),
                (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value")
            )
            
            # Perform operation that may trigger spilling
            result = df.groupBy("key").agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                sum("value").alias("sum"),
                avg("value").alias("avg")
            )
            
            result_count = result.count()
            execution_time = time.time() - start_time
            
            results[strategy] = {
                "execution_time": execution_time,
                "result_count": result_count
            }
            
            print(f"  Execution time: {execution_time:.3f}s")
            print(f"  Result count: {result_count}")
        
        # Find best performer
        best_strategy = min(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['execution_time'])
        
        print(f"\n✓ Best performing spill strategy: {best_strategy[0]}")
        print(f"  Execution time: {best_strategy[1]['execution_time']:.3f}s")
        
        return results
    
    def benchmark_memory_fractions(self, 
                                   spark: SparkSession,
                                   data_size: int = 2000000) -> Dict:
        """
        Benchmark different memory fraction configurations.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
            data_size: Number of records to test with
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing benchmark results
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("BENCHMARKING MEMORY FRACTIONS")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Test different memory.fraction and storageFraction combinations
        configs = [
            (0.5, 0.3),  # Conservative
            (0.6, 0.5),  # Balanced (default)
            (0.7, 0.6),  # Storage-heavy
            (0.8, 0.4),  # Execution-heavy
        ]
        
        results = {}
        
        for memory_frac, storage_frac in configs:
            config_name = f"M{int(memory_frac*100)}_S{int(storage_frac*100)}"
            print(f"\nTesting {config_name} (memory={memory_frac}, storage={storage_frac})...")
            
            # Reconfigure Spark
            spark.conf.set("spark.memory.fraction", str(memory_frac))
            spark.conf.set("spark.memory.storageFraction", str(storage_frac))
            
            # Run mixed workload (caching + aggregation)
            start_time = time.time()
            
            # Create and cache dataset
            df = spark.range(0, data_size).select(
                col("id"),
                (rand() * 1000).cast("int").alias("value"),
                (col("id") % 100).alias("group")
            )
            df.cache()
            df.count()
            
            # Perform aggregation
            result = df.groupBy("group").agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                sum("value").alias("sum"),
                avg("value").alias("avg")
            )
            result.count()
            
            execution_time = time.time() - start_time
            
            # Cleanup
            df.unpersist()
            
            results[config_name] = {
                "memory_fraction": memory_frac,
                "storage_fraction": storage_frac,
                "execution_time": execution_time
            }
            
            print(f"  Execution time: {execution_time:.3f}s")
        
        # Find best performer
        best_config = min(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['execution_time'])
        
        print(f"\n✓ Best performing configuration: {best_config[0]}")
        print(f"  Execution time: {best_config[1]['execution_time']:.3f}s")
        
        return results
    
    def run_full_benchmark(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Run complete benchmark suite.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("RUNNING FULL BENCHMARK SUITE")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Benchmark 1: Storage Levels
        storage_results = self.benchmark_storage_levels(spark)
        
        # Benchmark 2: Spill Strategies
        spill_results = self.benchmark_spill_strategies(spark)
        
        # Benchmark 3: Memory Fractions
        fraction_results = self.benchmark_memory_fractions(spark)
        
        # Compile summary
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("BENCHMARK SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        print("\n1. Storage Levels:")
        for level, metrics in storage_results.items():
            print(f"   {level}: {metrics['total_time']:.3f}s total")
        
        print("\n2. Spill Strategies:")
        for strategy, metrics in spill_results.items():
            print(f"   {strategy}: {metrics['execution_time']:.3f}s")
        
        print("\n3. Memory Fractions:")
        for config, metrics in fraction_results.items():
            print(f"   {config}: {metrics['execution_time']:.3f}s")
        
        return {
            "storage_levels": storage_results,
            "spill_strategies": spill_results,
            "memory_fractions": fraction_results
        }

def use_case_large_scale_etl():
    """
    Real-world use case: Large-scale ETL pipeline with memory optimization.
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("USE CASE: Large-Scale ETL Pipeline")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create optimized Spark session for ETL
    spark = create_memory_optimized_spark_session(
        app_name="LargeScaleETL",
        executor_memory="8g",
        driver_memory="4g",
        memory_fraction=0.6,
        storage_fraction=0.4,
        enable_adaptive=True
    )
    
    try:
        print("\nScenario: Processing 10M customer transactions")
        print("Goal: Extract, transform, and aggregate data efficiently")
        
        # Initialize memory managers
        spill_manager = MemorySpillStrategyPattern(
            spill_strategy="BALANCED_SPILL",
            compression_codec="lz4"
        )
        spill_manager.configure_spark(spark)
        
        storage_manager = StorageMemoryPattern(
            default_storage_level="MEMORY_AND_DISK",
            enable_compression=True
        )
        storage_manager.configure_spark(spark)
        
        # Step 1: Read raw data
        print("\n1. Reading raw transaction data...")
        raw_transactions = spark.range(0, 10000000).select(
            col("id").alias("transaction_id"),
            (col("id") % 1000000).alias("customer_id"),
            (col("id") % 10000).alias("product_id"),
            (rand() * 1000).cast("decimal(10,2)").alias("amount"),
            date_sub(current_date(), (rand() * 365).cast("int")).alias("transaction_date"),
            (rand() * 5).cast("int").alias("store_id")
        )
        
        # Step 2: Cache reference data
        print("\n2. Loading and caching reference data...")
        customers = spark.range(0, 1000000).select(
            col("id").alias("customer_id"),
            concat(lit("Customer_"), col("id")).alias("customer_name"),
            (rand() * 5).cast("int").alias("segment")
        )
        storage_manager.cache_dataset(customers, "customers", "MEMORY_AND_DISK")
        
        products = spark.range(0, 10000).select(
            col("id").alias("product_id"),
            concat(lit("Product_"), col("id")).alias("product_name"),
            (rand() * 10).cast("int").alias("category")
        )
        storage_manager.cache_dataset(products, "products", "MEMORY_ONLY")
        
        # Step 3: Join and enrich
        print("\n3. Enriching transaction data...")
        enriched = raw_transactions \
            .join(customers, on="customer_id", how="left") \
            .join(products, on="product_id", how="left")
        
        # Step 4: Aggregate
        print("\n4. Computing aggregations...")
        daily_summary = enriched.groupBy("transaction_date", "segment", "category").agg(
            count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_revenue"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_transaction"),
            countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers")
        )
        
        # Step 5: Materialize results
        print("\n5. Materializing results...")
        result_count = daily_summary.count()
        
        print(f"\nETL Pipeline completed successfully!")
        print(f"  Processed: 10,000,000 transactions")
        print(f"  Generated: {result_count} summary records")
        
        # Show sample results
        print("\nSample Results:")
        daily_summary.orderBy(col("total_revenue").desc()).show(10)
        
        # Display memory stats
        print("\nMemory Statistics:")
        for dataset_info in storage_manager.list_cached_datasets():
            print(f"  - {dataset_info}")
        
        # Cleanup
        storage_manager.unpersist_dataset("customers")
        storage_manager.unpersist_dataset("products")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()


def use_case_iterative_ml_training():
    """

    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("USE CASE: Iterative ML Model Training")

    )
    
    try:
        print("\nScenario: Training model with iterative algorithm")
        print("Goal: Efficiently cache training data and manage iterations")
        
        # Initialize storage manager
        storage_manager = StorageMemoryPattern(
            default_storage_level="MEMORY_ONLY",
            enable_compression=True
        )
        storage_manager.configure_spark(spark)
        
        # Step 1: Prepare training data
        print("\n1. Preparing training data
```python
...")
        training_data = spark.range(0, 1000000).select(
            col("id"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("feature1"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("feature2"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("feature3"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("feature4"),
            (rand() * 100).alias("feature5"),
            (rand() * 2).cast("int").alias("label")
        )
        
        # Step 2: Cache training data (critical for iterative algorithms)
        print("\n2. Caching training data for iterative processing...")
        storage_manager.cache_dataset(
            training_data, 
            "training_data", 
            "MEMORY_ONLY"  # Keep in memory for fast iterations
        )
        
        # Step 3: Simulate iterative training
        print("\n3. Running iterative training (10 iterations)...")
        num_iterations = 10
        iteration_times = []
        
        for iteration in range(num_iterations):
            iter_start = time.time()
            
            # Simulate model training step
            # In real ML, this would be gradient computation, weight updates, etc.
            result = training_data.groupBy("label").agg(
                count("*").alias("count"),
                avg("feature1").alias("avg_f1"),
                avg("feature2").alias("avg_f2"),
                avg("feature3").alias("avg_f3"),
                avg("feature4").alias("avg_f4"),
                avg("feature5").alias("avg_f5")
            )
            
            # Force computation
            result.count()
            
            iter_time = time.time() - iter_start
            iteration_times.append(iter_time)
            
            print(f"  Iteration {iteration + 1}: {iter_time:.3f}s")
        
        # Display training statistics
        avg_iter_time = sum(iteration_times) / len(iteration_times)
        total_time = sum(iteration_times)
        
        print(f"\nTraining completed!")
        print(f"  Total iterations: {num_iterations}")
        print(f"  Average iteration time: {avg_iter_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"  Total training time: {total_time:.3f}s")
        print(f"  Speedup from caching: ~{iteration_times[0]/avg_iter_time:.2f}x")
        
        # Cleanup
        storage_manager.unpersist_dataset("training_data")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()


def use_case_real_time_analytics():

    spark = create_memory_optimized_spark_session(

        executor_memory="4g",

        enable_adaptive=True
    )
    
    try:
        print("\nScenario: Real-time analytics with rotating cached datasets")
        print("Goal: Maintain recent data in cache with automatic eviction")
        
        # Initialize eviction manager
        eviction_manager = MemoryEvictionPattern(
            eviction_strategy="LRU",
            max_storage_memory_mb=1024
        )
        eviction_manager.configure_spark(spark)
        
        # Simulate processing multiple time windows
        print("\n1. Processing time-windowed data...")
        
        num_windows = 5
        window_size = 500000
        
        for window_id in range(num_windows):
            print(f"\nProcessing window {window_id + 1}...")
            
            # Generate data for this time window
            window_data = spark.range(0, window_size).select(
                col("id"),
                lit(window_id).alias("window_id"),
                (rand() * 100).cast("int").alias("metric1"),
                (rand() * 100).cast("int").alias("metric2"),
                current_timestamp().alias("timestamp")
            )
            
            # Cache this window's data
            eviction_manager.add_cached_block(
                f"window_{window_id}",
                window_data,
                size_mb=250,
                priority=num_windows - window_id  # More recent = higher priority
            )
            
            # Compute analytics for this window
            analytics = window_data.groupBy("window_id").agg(
                count("*").alias("record_count"),
                avg("metric1").alias("avg_metric1"),
                avg("metric2").alias("avg_metric2")
            )
            
            print(f"  Window {window_id + 1} analytics:")
            analytics.show()
            
            # Access recent windows (simulating dashboard queries)
            if window_id > 0:
                eviction_manager.access_cached_block(f"window_{window_id - 1}")
        
        # Display final eviction statistics
        print("\n2. Final cache statistics:")
        stats = eviction_manager.get_eviction_stats()
        print(f"  Total blocks in cache: {stats['total_blocks']}")
        print(f"  Memory usage: {stats['memory_usage_mb']:.2f} MB / {stats['memory_limit_mb']} MB")
        print(f"  Memory utilization: {stats['memory_utilization']:.2%}")
        
        print("\n  Cached windows:")
        for block in stats['blocks']:
            print(f"    - {block['name']}: accessed {block['access_count']} times")
        
    finally:
        spark.stop()

class InteractiveMemoryConfigurator:
    """
    Interactive tool to help configure memory settings based on requirements.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.config = {}
    
    def gather_requirements(self):
        """
        Gather requirements interactively (simulated for script).
        In a real interactive scenario, this would use input().
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("INTERACTIVE MEMORY CONFIGURATION TOOL")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        # Simulated inputs (in real use, these would be user inputs)
        requirements = {
            "workload_type": "analytics",  # etl, analytics, ml, streaming
            "data_size_gb": 100,
            "executor_count": 10,
            "executor_cores": 4,
            "cluster_memory_gb": 80,
            "caching_needed": True,
            "shuffle_heavy": True,
            "iterative": False
        }
        
        self.config = requirements
        return requirements
    
    def calculate_configuration(self, requirements: Dict) -> Dict:
        """
        Calculate optimal configuration based on requirements.
        
        Args:
            requirements: Dictionary of requirements
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary of recommended configuration
        """
        data_size = requirements["data_size_gb"]
        executor_count = requirements["executor_count"]
        cluster_memory = requirements["cluster_memory_gb"]
        
        # Calculate memory per executor
        memory_per_executor = cluster_memory / executor_count
        
        # Adjust memory fraction based on workload
        if requirements["workload_type"] == "ml":
            memory_fraction = 0.8
            storage_fraction = 0.7
        elif requirements["workload_type"] == "analytics":
            memory_fraction = 0.7
            storage_fraction = 0.6
        elif requirements["workload_type"] == "streaming":
            memory_fraction = 0.5
            storage_fraction = 0.3
        else:  # ETL
            memory_fraction = 0.6
            storage_fraction = 0.4
        
        # Adjust for caching needs
        if requirements["caching_needed"]:
            storage_fraction = min(storage_fraction + 0.1, 0.8)
        
        # Calculate shuffle partitions
        if requirements["shuffle_heavy"]:
            shuffle_partitions = executor_count * requirements["executor_cores"] * 4
        else:
            shuffle_partitions = executor_count * requirements["executor_cores"] * 2
        
        # Determine spill strategy
        if data_size / executor_count > memory_per_executor * 2:
            spill_strategy = "AGGRESSIVE_SPILL"
        else:
            spill_strategy = "BALANCED_SPILL"
        
        # Determine storage level
        if requirements["iterative"] and requirements["caching_needed"]:
            default_storage_level = "MEMORY_ONLY"
        elif requirements["caching_needed"]:
            default_storage_level = "MEMORY_AND_DISK"
        else:
            default_storage_level = "MEMORY_AND_DISK_SER"
        
        config = {
            "executor_memory": f"{int(memory_per_executor)}g",
            "executor_cores": requirements["executor_cores"],
            "executor_instances": executor_count,
            "driver_memory": f"{int(memory_per_executor * 0.5)}g",
            "memory_fraction": memory_fraction,
            "storage_fraction": storage_fraction,
            "shuffle_partitions": shuffle_partitions,
            "spill_strategy": spill_strategy,
            "default_storage_level": default_storage_level,
            "enable_adaptive": True,
            "compression_codec": "lz4",
            "off_heap_enabled": data_size > 500
        }
        
        return config
    
    def generate_spark_config(self, config: Dict) -> str:
        """
        Generate Spark configuration code.
        
        Args:
            config: Configuration dictionary
            
        Returns:
            String containing Spark configuration code
        """
        spark_config = f"""
# Generated Spark Configuration
# =============================

spark = SparkSession.builder \\
    .appName("OptimizedSparkApp") \\
    .config("spark.executor.memory", "{config['executor_memory']}") \\
    .config("spark.executor.cores", "{config['executor_cores']}") \\
    .config("spark.executor.instances", "{config['executor_instances']}") \\
    .config("spark.driver.memory", "{config['driver_memory']}") \\
    .config("spark.memory.fraction", "{config['memory_fraction']}") \\
    .config("spark.memory.storageFraction", "{config['storage_fraction']}") \\
    .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "{config['shuffle_partitions']}") \\
    .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "{str(config['enable_adaptive']).lower()}") \\
    .config("spark.shuffle.compress", "true") \\
    .config("spark.io.compression.codec", "{config['compression_codec']}") \\
    .config("spark.rdd.compress", "true") \\
    .config("spark.memory.offHeap.enabled", "{str(config['off_heap_enabled']).lower()}")

if {config['off_heap_enabled']}:
    spark = spark.config("spark.memory.offHeap.size", "2g")

spark = spark.getOrCreate()

# Recommended Settings:
# - Spill Strategy: {config['spill_strategy']}
# - Default Storage Level: {config['default_storage_level']}
# - Enable compression for cached data
# - Monitor memory usage via Spark UI
"""
        return spark_config
    
    def run(self):
        """Run the interactive configurator."""
        # Gather requirements
        requirements = self.gather_requirements()
        
        print("\nYour Requirements:")
        for key, value in requirements.items():
            print(f"  {key}: {value}")
        
        # Calculate configuration
        config = self.calculate_configuration(requirements)
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("RECOMMENDED CONFIGURATION")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        print("\nMemory Settings:")
        print(f"  Executor Memory: {config['executor_memory']}")
        print(f"  Driver Memory: {config['driver_memory']}")
        print(f"  Memory Fraction: {config['memory_fraction']}")
        print(f"  Storage Fraction: {config['storage_fraction']}")
        
        print("\nExecution Settings:")
        print(f"  Shuffle Partitions: {config['shuffle_partitions']}")
        print(f"  Spill Strategy: {config['spill_strategy']}")
        print(f"  Adaptive Execution: {config['enable_adaptive']}")
        
        print("\nStorage Settings:")
        print(f"  Default Storage Level: {config['default_storage_level']}")
        print(f"  Compression Codec: {config['compression_codec']}")
        print(f"  Off-Heap Enabled: {config['off_heap_enabled']}")
        
        # Generate code
        spark_code = self.generate_spark_config(config)
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("GENERATED SPARK CONFIGURATION CODE")
        print("=" * 80)
        print(spark_code)
        
        return config

    - OutOfMemoryError: Increase executor memory or enable spilling
    - Slow performance: Check for excessive spilling or GC
    - Cache eviction: Increase storage memory fraction
    - Shuffle errors: Increase shuffle memory or partitions

class ThresholdRulePattern:
    """
    Validates that numeric values meet threshold criteria.
    Use cases: Transaction amounts, inventory levels, performance metrics
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def apply_threshold_rules(df, column: str, min_threshold: float = None, 
                             max_threshold: float = None, rule_name: str = "threshold_check"):
        """
        Apply threshold validation rules to a numeric column.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column name to validate
            min_threshold: Minimum acceptable value
            max_threshold: Maximum acceptable value
            rule_name: Name for the rule
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with quality flags and metrics
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying threshold rule on column: {column}")
        
        # Create validation conditions
        conditions = []
        
        if min_threshold is not None:
            conditions.append(col(column) >= min_threshold)
        
        if max_threshold is not None:
            conditions.append(col(column) <= max_threshold)
        
        # Combine conditions
        if conditions:
            validation_expr = conditions[0]
            for condition in conditions[1:]:
                validation_expr = validation_expr & condition
        else:
            validation_expr = lit(True)
        
        # Add quality flag column
        result_df = df.withColumn(
            f"{rule_name}_flag",
            when(col(column).isNull(), lit("NULL"))
            .when(validation_expr, lit("PASS"))
            .otherwise(lit("FAIL"))
        )
        
        # Calculate metrics
        metrics = result_df.agg(
            count("*").alias("total_records"),
            _sum(when(col(f"{rule_name}_flag") == "PASS", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("passed"),
            _sum(when(col(f"{rule_name}_flag") == "FAIL", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("failed"),
            _sum(when(col(f"{rule_name}_flag") == "NULL", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("null_values")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        pass_rate = (metrics['passed'] / metrics['total_records'] * 100) if metrics['total_records'] > 0 else 0
        
        logger.info(f"Threshold Rule Results - Pass Rate: {pass_rate:.2f}%")
        
        return result_df, {
            "rule_name": rule_name,
            "rule_type": "THRESHOLD",
            "column": column,
            "min_threshold": min_threshold,
            "max_threshold": max_threshold,
            "total_records": metrics['total_records'],
            "passed": metrics['passed'],
            "failed": metrics['failed'],
            "null_values": metrics['null_values'],
            "pass_rate": pass_rate
        }


# ============================================================================
# 2. RANGE RULE PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class RangeRulePattern:
    """
    Validates that values fall within acceptable ranges (inclusive/exclusive).
    Use cases: Age ranges, date ranges, score ranges
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def apply_range_rules(df, column: str, lower_bound: float, upper_bound: float,
                         inclusive: bool = True, rule_name: str = "range_check"):
        """
        Apply range validation rules to a column.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column name to validate
            lower_bound: Lower bound of the range
            upper_bound: Upper bound of the range
            inclusive: Whether bounds are inclusive (True) or exclusive (False)
            rule_name: Name for the rule
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with quality flags and metrics
        """
        logger.info(f"Applying range rule on column: {column}, range: [{lower_bound}, {upper_bound}]")
        
        # Create range condition based on inclusive/exclusive
        if inclusive:
            range_condition = (col(column) >= lower_bound) & (col(column) <= upper_bound)
        else:
            range_condition = (col(column) > lower_bound) & (col(column) < upper_bound)
        
        # Add quality flag column
        result_df = df.withColumn(
            f"{rule_name}_flag",
            when(col(column).isNull(), lit("NULL"))
            .when(range_condition, lit("PASS"))
            .otherwise(lit("FAIL"))
        )
        
        # Add violation details
        result_df = result_df.withColumn(
            f"{rule_name}_violation_type",
            when(col(f"{rule_name}_flag") == "FAIL",
                 when(col(column) < lower_bound, lit("BELOW_RANGE"))
                 .when(col(column) > upper_bound, lit("ABOVE_RANGE"))
                 .otherwise(lit("UNKNOWN")))
            .otherwise(lit(None))
        )
        
        # Calculate metrics
        metrics = result_df.agg(
            count("*").alias("total_records"),
            _sum(when(col(f"{rule_name}_flag") == "PASS", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("passed"),
            _sum(when(col(f"{rule_name}_flag") == "FAIL", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("failed"),
            _sum(when(col(f"{rule_name}_violation_type") == "BELOW_RANGE", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("below_range"),
            _sum(when(col(f"{rule_name}_violation_type") == "ABOVE_RANGE", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("above_range"),
            _min(column).alias("min_value"),
            _max(column).alias("max_value")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        pass_rate = (metrics['passed'] / metrics['total_records'] * 100) if metrics['total_records'] > 0 else 0
        
        logger.info(f"Range Rule Results - Pass Rate: {pass_rate:.2f}%")
        
        return result_df, {
            "rule_name": rule_name,
            "rule_type": "RANGE",
            "column": column,
            "lower_bound": lower_bound,
            "upper_bound": upper_bound,
            "inclusive": inclusive,
            "total_records": metrics['total_records'],
            "passed": metrics['passed'],
            "failed": metrics['failed'],
            "below_range": metrics['below_range'],
            "above_range": metrics['above_range'],
            "min_value": metrics['min_value'],
            "max_value": metrics['max_value'],
            "pass_rate": pass_rate
        }
