print("=" * 80)
print("""
Purpose: Compare complete snapshots of data at different points in time
Use Case: Data quality monitoring, reconciliation, drift detection
Key Features:
- Captures periodic snapshots
- Performs deep comparison between snapshots
- Identifies schema changes
- Detects data drift and anomalies
- Generates detailed comparison reports
""")

class SnapshotComparisonPattern:
    """
    Implements Snapshot Comparison Pattern for temporal data analysis
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
        self.snapshot_path = f"{base_path}/snapshots"
        self.comparison_path = f"{base_path}/comparisons"
        
    def initialize_snapshot_tables(self):
        """Initialize snapshot and comparison tables"""
        # Snapshot metadata schema
        snapshot_meta_schema = StructType([
            StructField("snapshot_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("snapshot_timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("table_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("snapshot_type", StringType(), False),  # FULL, INCREMENTAL
            StructField("record_count", LongType(), False),
            StructField("snapshot_hash", StringType(), False),
            StructField("schema_hash", StringType(), False),
            StructField("data_path", StringType(), False),
            StructField("created_by", StringType(), True),
            StructField("tags", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
        ])
        
        # Comparison results schema
        comparison_schema = StructType([
            StructField("comparison_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("comparison_timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            StructField("snapshot_id_1", StringType(), False),
            StructField("snapshot_id_2", StringType(), False),
            StructField("comparison_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("records_added", LongType(), True),
            StructField("records_removed", LongType(), True),
            StructField("records_modified", LongType(), True),
            StructField("records_unchanged", LongType(), True),
            StructField("schema_changes", ArrayType(StringType()), True),
            StructField("statistical_differences", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True),
            StructField("drift_score", StringType(), True),
            StructField("comparison_details_path", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        # Create tables
        empty_snapshot_df = self.spark.createDataFrame([], snapshot_meta_schema)
        empty_snapshot_df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite") \
            .save(f"{self.snapshot_path}/metadata")
        
        empty_comparison_df = self.spark.createDataFrame([], comparison_schema)
        empty_comparison_df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite") \
            .save(self.comparison_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Snapshot tables initialized at: {self.snapshot_path}")
        print(f"✓ Comparison table initialized at: {self.comparison_path}")
    
    def create_snapshot(self, data_df, table_name, snapshot_type="FULL", 
                       created_by="system", tags=None):
        """Create a snapshot of the current data"""
        snapshot_id = f"SNAP-{table_name}-{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}"
        snapshot_timestamp = datetime.now()
        
        # Calculate snapshot hash
        record_count = data_df.count()
        
        # Calculate schema hash
        schema_str = str(data_df.schema)
        schema_hash = hashlib.sha256(schema_str.encode()).hexdigest()
        
        # Calculate data hash (sample-based for large datasets)
        sample_data = data_df.limit(1000).toPandas().to_json()
        snapshot_hash = hashlib.sha256(sample_data.encode()).hexdigest()
        
        # Save snapshot data
        data_path = f"{self.snapshot_path}/data/{snapshot_id}"
        data_df.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite").save(data_path)
        
        # Save snapshot metadata
        metadata = [(
            snapshot_id,
            snapshot_timestamp,
            table_name,
            snapshot_type,
            record_count,
            snapshot_hash,
            schema_hash,
            data_path,
            created_by,
            tags or {}
        )]
        
        metadata_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            metadata,
            self.spark.read.format("delta").load(f"{self.snapshot_path}/metadata").schema
        )
        
        metadata_df.write.format("delta").mode("append") \
            .save(f"{self.snapshot_path}/metadata")
        
        print(f"✓ Created snapshot: {snapshot_id}")
        print(f"  - Records: {record_count}")
        print(f"  - Schema Hash: {schema_hash[:16]}...")
        print(f"  - Data Hash: {snapshot_hash[:16]}...")
        
        return snapshot_id
    
    def compare_snapshots(self, snapshot_id_1, snapshot_id_2, key_columns,
                         comparison_type="FULL"):
        """
        Compare two snapshots and generate detailed comparison report
        
        Args:
            snapshot_id_1: First snapshot ID (older)
            snapshot_id_2: Second snapshot ID (newer)
            key_columns: List of columns that uniquely identify records
            comparison_type: Type of comparison (FULL, SCHEMA_ONLY, DATA_ONLY)
        """
        comparison_id = f"COMP-{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S%f')}"
        
        # Load snapshot metadata
        metadata_df = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(f"{self.snapshot_path}/metadata")
        
        snap1_meta = metadata_df.filter(col("snapshot_id") == snapshot_id_1).first()
        snap2_meta = metadata_df.filter(col("snapshot_id") == snapshot_id_2).first()
        
        if not snap1_meta or not snap2_meta:
            print("✗ One or both snapshots not found")
            return None
        
        # Load snapshot data
        snap1_data = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(snap1_meta["data_path"])
        snap2_data = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(snap2_meta["data_path"])
        
        print(f"\n✓ Comparing snapshots:")
        print(f"  Snapshot 1: {snapshot_id_1} ({snap1_meta['record_count']} records)")
        print(f"  Snapshot 2: {snapshot_id_2} ({snap2_meta['record_count']} records)")
        
        # Schema comparison
        schema_changes = self._compare_schemas(snap1_data.schema, snap2_data.schema)
        
        if comparison_type == "SCHEMA_ONLY":
            return self._save_comparison_results(
                comparison_id, snapshot_id_1, snapshot_id_2, comparison_type,
                0, 0, 0, 0, schema_changes, {}, "N/A", None
            )
        
        # Data comparison
        key_expr = concat_ws("||", *[col(c) for c in key_columns])
        
        # Add keys to both datasets
        snap1_keyed = snap1_data.withColumn("_key", key_expr)
        snap2_keyed = snap2_data.withColumn("_key", key_expr)
        
        # Find added records (in snap2 but not in snap1)
        added = snap2_keyed.join(snap1_keyed, "_key", "left_anti")
        records_added = added.count()
        
        # Find removed records (in snap1 but not in snap2)
        removed = snap1_keyed.join(snap2_keyed, "_key", "left_anti")
        records_removed = removed.count()
        
        # Find common records
        common = snap1_keyed.alias("s1").join(
            snap2_keyed.alias("s2"),
            col("s1._key") == col("s2._key"),
            "inner"
        )
        
        # Compare common records for modifications
        compare_columns = [c for c in snap1_data.columns if c in snap2_data.columns 
                          and c not in key_columns]
        
        # Create hash for comparison
        snap1_hash = common.withColumn(
            "_hash1",
            md5(concat_ws("||", *[coalesce(col(f"s1.{c}").cast("string"), lit("NULL")) 
                                 for c in compare_columns]))
        )
        
        snap2_hash = snap1_hash.withColumn(
            "_hash2",
            md5(concat_ws("||", *[coalesce(col(f"s2.{c}").cast("string"), lit("NULL")) 
                                 for c in compare_columns]))
        )
        
        modified = snap2_hash.filter(col("_hash1") != col("_hash2"))
        records_modified = modified.count()
        
        unchanged = snap2_hash.filter(col("_hash1") == col("_hash2"))
        records_unchanged = unchanged.count()
        
        # Calculate statistical differences
        stats_diff = self._calculate_statistical_differences(
            snap1_data, snap2_data, compare_columns
        )
        
        # Calculate drift score
        total_records = max(snap1_meta["record_count"], snap2_meta["record_count"])
        drift_score = ((records_added + records_removed + records_modified) / total_records * 100) \
                     if total_records > 0 else 0
        
        # Save detailed comparison data
        details_path = f"{self.comparison_path}/details/{comparison_id}"
        
        # Save added, removed, and modified records
        if records_added > 0:
            added.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite") \
                .save(f"{details_path}/added")
        
        if records_removed > 0:
            removed.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite") \
                .save(f"{details_path}/removed")
        
        if records_modified > 0:
            # Save detailed field-level differences
            field_diffs = self._calculate_field_differences(
                modified, compare_columns, key_columns
            )
            field_diffs.write.format("delta").mode("overwrite") \
                .save(f"{details_path}/modified")
        
        # Save comparison results
        self._save_comparison_results(
            comparison_id, snapshot_id_1, snapshot_id_2, comparison_type,
            records_added, records_removed, records_modified, records_unchanged,
            schema_changes, stats_diff, f"{drift_score:.2f}%", details_path
        )
        
        # Print summary
        print(f"\n✓ Comparison Summary:")
        print(f"  - Records Added: {records_added}")
        print(f"  - Records Removed: {records_removed}")
        print(f"  - Records Modified: {records_modified}")
        print(f"  - Records Unchanged: {records_unchanged}")
        print(f"  - Drift Score: {drift_score:.2f}%")
        print(f"  - Schema Changes: {len(schema_changes)}")
        
        return comparison_id
    
    def _compare_schemas(self, schema1, schema2):
        """Compare two schemas and identify differences"""
        changes = []
        
        fields1 = {f.name: f for f in schema1.fields}
        fields2 = {f.name: f for f in schema2.fields}
        
        # Find added fields
        for name in fields2:
            if name not in fields1:
                changes.append(f"ADDED: {name} ({fields2[name].dataType})")
        
        # Find removed fields
        for name in fields1:
            if name not in fields2:
                changes.append(f"REMOVED: {name} ({fields1[name].dataType})")
        
        # Find modified fields
        for name in fields1:
            if name in fields2:
                if str(fields1[name].dataType) != str(fields2[name].dataType):
                    changes.append(
                        f"MODIFIED: {name} ({fields1[name].dataType} -> {fields2[name].dataType})"
                    )
                if fields1[name].nullable != fields2[name].nullable:
                    changes.append(
                        f"NULLABILITY: {name} ({fields1[name].nullable} -> {fields2[name].nullable})"
                    )
        
        return changes
    
    def _calculate_statistical_differences(self, df1, df2, columns):
        """Calculate statistical differences between two datasets"""
        stats_diff = {}
        
        for col_name in columns:
            try:
                # Check if column is numeric
                if str(df1.schema[col_name].dataType) in ['IntegerType', 'LongType', 
                                                           'FloatType', 'DoubleType']:
                    # Calculate basic statistics
                    stats1 = df1.select(col_name).summary("mean", "stddev", "min", "max")
                    stats2 = df2.select(col_name).summary("mean", "stddev", "min", "max")
                    
                    stats1_dict = {row['summary']: row[col_name] 
                                  for row in stats1.collect()}
                    stats2_dict = {row['summary']: row[col_name] 
                                  for row in stats2.collect()}
                    
                    # Calculate differences
                    if stats1_dict.get('mean') and stats2_dict.get('mean'):
                        mean_diff = float(stats2_dict['mean']) - float(stats1_dict['mean'])
                        stats_diff[f"{col_name}_mean_diff"] = f"{mean_diff:.2f}"
            except:
                pass  # Skip columns that can't be compared statistically
        
        return stats_diff
    
    def _calculate_field_differences(self, modified_df, compare_columns, key_columns):
        """Calculate field-level differences for modified records"""
        key_expr = concat_ws("||", *[col(f"s1.{c}") for c in key_columns])
        
        # Create array of field differences
        field_diff_exprs = []
        for c in compare_columns:
            fiel
```python
d_diff_exprs.append(
                when(
                    col(f"s1.{c}") != col(f"s2.{c}"),
                    struct(
                        lit(c).alias("field_name"),
                        col(f"s1.{c}").cast("string").alias("old_value"),
                        col(f"s2.{c}").cast("string").alias("new_value")
                    )
                )
            )
        
        field_diffs = modified_df.withColumn("record_key", key_expr) \
            .withColumn("differences", 
                       array(*field_diff_exprs)) \
            .withColumn("differences", 
                       expr("filter(differences, x -> x is not null)")) \
            .select("record_key", "differences", 
                   *[col(f"s2.{c}").alias(c) for c in key_columns])
        
        return field_diffs
    
    def _save_comparison_results(self, comparison_id, snapshot_id_1, snapshot_id_2,
                                comparison_type, records_added, records_removed,
                                records_modified, records_unchanged, schema_changes,
                                stats_diff, drift_score, details_path):
        """Save comparison results to the comparison table"""
        comparison_record = [(
            comparison_id,
            datetime.now(),
            snapshot_id_1,
            snapshot_id_2,
            comparison_type,
            records_added,
            records_removed,
            records_modified,
            records_unchanged,
            schema_changes,
            stats_diff,
            drift_score,
            details_path
        )]
        
        comparison_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            comparison_record,
            self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.comparison_path).schema
        )
        
        comparison_df.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(self.comparison_path)
        
        print(f"✓ Comparison results saved: {comparison_id}")
        
        return comparison_id
    
    def get_snapshot_history(self, table_name):
        """Get snapshot history for a table"""
        metadata_df = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(f"{self.snapshot_path}/metadata")
        return metadata_df.filter(col("table_name") == table_name) \
                         .orderBy(col("snapshot_timestamp").desc())
    
    def get_comparison_results(self, comparison_id):
        """Retrieve comparison results"""
        comparison_df = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.comparison_path)
        return comparison_df.filter(col("comparison_id") == comparison_id)
    
    def get_comparison_details(self, comparison_id, detail_type="modified"):
        """
        Get detailed comparison data
        
        Args:
            comparison_id: Comparison ID
            detail_type: Type of detail (added, removed, modified)
        """
        comparison_results = self.get_comparison_results(comparison_id).first()
        
        if not comparison_results:
            print(f"✗ Comparison {comparison_id} not found")
            return None
        
        details_path = comparison_results["comparison_details_path"]
        
        if not details_path:
            print("✗ No detailed comparison data available")
            return None
        
        try:
            detail_df = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(f"{details_path}/{detail_type}")
            return detail_df
        except:
            print(f"✗ No {detail_type} records found")
            return None
    
    def generate_drift_report(self, table_name, time_window_days=30):
        """Generate drift report for a table over time"""
        cutoff_date = datetime.now() - timedelta(days=time_window_days)
        
        # Get all comparisons for the table
        metadata_df = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(f"{self.snapshot_path}/metadata")
        snapshots = metadata_df.filter(
            (col("table_name") == table_name) &
            (col("snapshot_timestamp") >= cutoff_date)
        ).select("snapshot_id", "snapshot_timestamp", "record_count")
        
        comparison_df = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.comparison_path)
        
        # Join with snapshot metadata
        drift_report = comparison_df.alias("comp").join(
            snapshots.alias("s1"),
            col("comp.snapshot_id_1") == col("s1.snapshot_id"),
            "inner"
        ).join(
            snapshots.alias("s2"),
            col("comp.snapshot_id_2") == col("s2.snapshot_id"),
            "inner"
        ).select(
            col("comp.comparison_id"),
            col("comp.comparison_timestamp"),
            col("s1.snapshot_timestamp").alias("snapshot1_time"),
            col("s2.snapshot_timestamp").alias("snapshot2_time"),
            col("comp.drift_score"),
            col("comp.records_added"),
            col("comp.records_removed"),
            col("comp.records_modified"),
            col("s1.record_count").alias("snapshot1_count"),
            col("s2.record_count").alias("snapshot2_count")
        ).orderBy(col("comp.comparison_timestamp").desc())
        
        return drift_report
    
    def detect_anomalies(self, table_name, threshold_percent=10.0):
        """
        Detect anomalies in data changes
        
        Args:
            table_name: Table name to analyze
            threshold_percent: Threshold for anomaly detection (drift percentage)
        """
        drift_report = self.generate_drift_report(table_name)
        
        # Parse drift score and filter anomalies
        anomalies = drift_report.withColumn(
            "drift_numeric",
            expr("cast(regexp_replace(drift_score, '%', '') as double)")
        ).filter(col("drift_numeric") > threshold_percent)
        
        return anomalies

class IntegratedMutationTracking:
    """
    Integrated mutation tracking using all five patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark, base_path):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
        
        # Initialize all patterns
        self.changelog = ChangeLogPattern(spark, f"{base_path}/integrated/changelog")
        self.audit = AuditTrailPattern(spark, f"{base_path}/integrated/audit")
        self.version = VersionHistoryPattern(spark, f"{base_path}/integrated/version")
        self.delta = DeltaTrackingPattern(spark, f"{base_path}/integrated/delta")
        self.snapshot = SnapshotComparisonPattern(spark, f"{base_path}/integrated/snapshot")
        
    def initialize_all(self):
        """Initialize all tracking patterns"""
        print("Initializing integrated mutation tracking system...")
        self.changelog.initialize_changelog_table()
        self.audit.initialize_audit_trail()
        self.version.initialize_version_table()
        self.delta.initialize_delta_tracking()
        self.snapshot.initialize_snapshot_tables()
        print("✓ All tracking patterns initialized")
    
    def track_insert(self, table_name, data_df, user_id, record_id_col="id"):
        """Track INSERT operation across all patterns"""
        print(f"\n--- Tracking INSERT operation for {table_name} ---")
        
        # 1. Change Log
        self.changelog.log_insert(table_name, data_df, user=user_id)
        print("✓ Logged to Change Log")
        
        # 2. Audit Trail
        for row in data_df.collect():
            self.audit.log_event(
                event_type="WRITE",
                table_name=table_name,
                user_id=user_id,
                record_id=str(row[record_id_col]),
                action_description=f"Inserted new record",
                data_classification="INTERNAL",
                success=True
            )
        print("✓ Logged to Audit Trail")
        
        # 3. Version History
        for row in data_df.collect():
            data_dict = row.asDict()
            record_id = str(data_dict[record_id_col])
            self.version.insert_version(record_id, data_dict, created_by=user_id)
        print("✓ Created Version History")
        
        # 4. Delta Tracking
        batch_id = f"INSERT-{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}"
        self.delta.detect_deltas(data_df, key_columns=[record_id_col], batch_id=batch_id)
        print("✓ Tracked Deltas")
        
        # 5. Snapshot
        snapshot_id = self.snapshot.create_snapshot(
            data_df,
            table_name=table_name,
            created_by=user_id,
            tags={"operation": "INSERT", "user": user_id}
        )
        print(f"✓ Created Snapshot: {snapshot_id}")
        
        return {
            "operation": "INSERT",
            "table": table_name,
            "records": data_df.count(),
            "snapshot_id": snapshot_id
        }
    
    def track_update(self, table_name, old_data_df, new_data_df, user_id, 
                    record_id_col="id"):
        """Track UPDATE operation across all patterns"""
        print(f"\n--- Tracking UPDATE operation for {table_name} ---")
        
        # 1. Change Log
        self.changelog.log_update(table_name, old_data_df, new_data_df, 
                                 key_col=record_id_col, user=user_id)
        print("✓ Logged to Change Log")
        
        # 2. Audit Trail
        joined = old_data_df.alias("old").join(
            new_data_df.alias("
```python
new"),
            col(f"old.{record_id_col}") == col(f"new.{record_id_col}")
        )
        
        for row in joined.collect():
            self.audit.log_event(
                event_type="WRITE",
                table_name=table_name,
                user_id=user_id,
                record_id=str(row[f"old.{record_id_col}"]),
                action_description=f"Updated record",
                data_classification="INTERNAL",
                success=True
            )
        print("✓ Logged to Audit Trail")
        
        # 3. Version History
        for row in new_data_df.collect():
            data_dict = row.asDict()
            record_id = str(data_dict[record_id_col])
            self.version.update_version(record_id, data_dict, created_by=user_id,
                                       comment="Record updated")
        print("✓ Updated Version History")
        
        # 4. Delta Tracking
        batch_id = f"UPDATE-{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}"
        self.delta.detect_deltas(new_data_df, key_columns=[record_id_col], 
                                batch_id=batch_id)
        print("✓ Tracked Deltas")
        
        # 5. Snapshot
        snapshot_id = self.snapshot.create_snapshot(
            new_data_df,
            table_name=table_name,
            created_by=user_id,
            tags={"operation": "UPDATE", "user": user_id}
        )
        print(f"✓ Created Snapshot: {snapshot_id}")
        
        return {
            "operation": "UPDATE",
            "table": table_name,
            "records": new_data_df.count(),
            "snapshot_id": snapshot_id
        }
    
    def track_delete(self, table_name, deleted_data_df, user_id, record_id_col="id"):
        """Track DELETE operation across all patterns"""
        print(f"\n--- Tracking DELETE operation for {table_name} ---")
        
        # 1. Change Log
        self.changelog.log_delete(table_name, deleted_data_df, user=user_id)
        print("✓ Logged to Change Log")
        
        # 2. Audit Trail
        for row in deleted_data_df.collect():
            self.audit.log_event(
                event_type="DELETE",
                table_name=table_name,
                user_id=user_id,
                record_id=str(row[record_id_col]),
                action_description=f"Deleted record",
                data_classification="INTERNAL",
                success=True
            )
        print("✓ Logged to Audit Trail")
        
        # 3. Version History - Mark as deleted in comments
        for row in deleted_data_df.collect():
            data_dict = row.asDict()
            record_id = str(data_dict[record_id_col])
            data_dict["_deleted"] = True
            self.version.update_version(record_id, data_dict, created_by=user_id,
                                       comment="Record deleted",
                                       tags={"deleted": "true"})
        print("✓ Updated Version History (marked as deleted)")
        
        print(f"✓ Tracked DELETE operation")
        
        return {
            "operation": "DELETE",
            "table": table_name,
            "records": deleted_data_df.count()
        }
    
    def generate_comprehensive_report(self, table_name, start_date=None, end_date=None):
        """Generate comprehensive mutation report across all patterns"""
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print(f"COMPREHENSIVE MUTATION REPORT: {table_name}")
        print(f"{'='*80}")
        
        # 1. Change Log Summary
        print("\n1. CHANGE LOG SUMMARY:")
        changelog_data = self.changelog.get_changelog(table_name, start_date, end_date)
        changelog_summary = changelog_data.groupBy("operation_type").count()
        changelog_summary.show()
        
        # 2. Audit Trail Summary
        print("\n2. AUDIT TRAIL SUMMARY:")
        audit_data = self.audit.get_table_access_log(table_name)
        if start_date:
            audit_data = audit_data.filter(col("event_timestamp") >= start_date)
        if end_date:
            audit_data = audit_data.filter(col("event_timestamp") <= end_date)
        
        audit_summary = audit_data.groupBy("event_type", "user_id").count()
        audit_summary.show()
        
        # 3. Version History Summary
        print("\n3. VERSION HISTORY SUMMARY:")
        version_data = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.version.version_path)
        version_summary = version_data.groupBy("version_type").count()
        version_summary.show()
        
        # 4. Delta Tracking Summary
        print("\n4. DELTA TRACKING SUMMARY:")
        delta_data = self.spark.read.format("delta").load(self.delta.delta_path)
        delta_summary = delta_data.groupBy("delta_type", "processing_status").count()
        delta_summary.show()
        
        # 5. Snapshot Drift Analysis
        print("\n5. SNAPSHOT DRIFT ANALYSIS:")
        drift_report = self.snapshot.generate_drift_report(table_name, time_window_days=365)
        if drift_report.count() > 0:
            drift_report.show(truncate=False)
        else:
            print("No drift data available")
        
        return {
            "changelog_summary": changelog_summary,
            "audit_summary": audit_summary,
            "version_summary": version_summary,
            "delta_summary": delta_summary,
            "drift_report": drift_report
        }

INTEGRATION STRATEGIES:

def inner_join_elimination_example():
    """
    Demonstrates scenarios where inner joins can be eliminated or optimized
    """
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 1A: Join with columns from only one table (INEFFICIENT) ---")
    # INEFFICIENT: Joining but only using columns from orders
    inefficient_query = orders_df.join(
        customers_df,
        orders_df.customer_id == customers_df.customer_id,
        "inner"
    ).select(
        orders_df.order_id,
        orders_df.order_date,
        orders_df.amount
    )
    
    print("Query Plan (Before Optimization):")
    inefficient_query.explain(True)
    inefficient_query.show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 1B: Optimized - Direct selection (EFFICIENT) ---")
    # EFFICIENT: Since we only need orders data and customer_id is not null,
    # we can eliminate the join
    efficient_query = orders_df.select(
        col("order_id"),
        col("order_date"),
        col("amount")
    )
    
    print("Query Plan (After Optimization):")
    efficient_query.explain(True)
    efficient_query.show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 1C: Join for filtering only (can use semi-join) ---")
    # When join is only used for filtering, use semi-join instead
    customers_with_orders = customers_df.join(
        orders_df,
        customers_df.customer_id == orders_df.customer_id,
        "left_semi"  # More efficient than inner join when only filtering
    )
    
    print("Customers with orders (using semi-join):")
    customers_with_orders.show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 1D: Aggregation without join columns ---")
    # INEFFICIENT
    inefficient_agg = orders_df.join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    ).groupBy(orders_df.order_date).agg(
        _sum("amount").alias("total_amount")
    )
    
    # EFFICIENT - Join eliminated
    efficient_agg = orders_df.groupBy("order_date").agg(
        _sum("amount").alias("total_amount")
    )
    
    print("Efficient aggregation without unnecessary join:")
    efficient_agg.show()

def left_join_elimination_example():
    """
    Demonstrates scenarios where left joins can be eliminated
    """
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 2A: Left join with no right-side columns (INEFFICIENT) ---")
    # INEFFICIENT: Left join but not using any columns from customers

        "customer_id",
        "left"
    ).select(

    )
    
    print("Query Plan (After Optimization):")
    efficient_left.explain(True)
    efficient_left.show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 2C: Left join for null checking (can be optimized) ---")
    # INEFFICIENT: Using left join to find orders without matching customers
    inefficient_null_check = orders_df.join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "left"
    ).filter(customers_df.customer_id.isNull())
    
    # EFFICIENT: Use anti-join instead
    efficient_null_check = orders_df.join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "left_anti"
    )
    
    print("Orders without matching customers (using anti-join):")

    # When aggregating only left table columns, join can be eliminated

    ).groupBy(orders_df.customer_id).agg(

    )
    
    print("Aggregation on left table only (optimized):")
    efficient_agg_left.show()

def semi_join_elimination_example():
    """
    Demonstrates semi join optimization patterns
    """
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 3A: Basic Semi Join ---")
    # Find customers who have placed orders
    customers_with_orders = customers_df.join(
        orders_df,
        "customer_id",
        "left_semi"
    )
    
    print("Customers with orders (semi-join):")
    customers_with_orders.show()
    customers_with_orders.explain(True)
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 3B: Semi Join vs IN clause ---")
    # Using IN clause (converted to semi-join internally)
    customer_ids_with_orders = orders_df.select("customer_id").distinct()
    customers_using_in = customers_df.filter(
        col("customer_id").isin([row.customer_id for row in customer_ids_with_orders.collect()])
    )
    
    print("Customers with orders (using IN):")
    customers_using_in.show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 3C: Semi Join with additional filters ---")
    # Semi join with filter pushdown
    high_value_orders = orders_df.filter(col("amount") > 200)
    customers_with_high_value = customers_df.join(
        high_value_orders,
        "customer_id",
        "left_semi"
    )
    
    print("Customers with high-value orders:")
    customers_with_high_value.show()
    customers_with_high_value.explain(True)
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 3D: Optimized Semi Join using broadcast ---")
    # When right table is small, broadcast can eliminate shuffle
    from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
    
    # Create a small filtered dataset
    active_customers = customers_df.filter(col("customer_id") <= 3)
    
    # Orders from active customers using broadcast semi-join
    orders_from_active = orders_df.join(
        broadcast(active_customers),
        "customer_id",
        "left_semi"
    )
    
    print("Orders from active customers (broadcast semi-join):")
    orders_from_active.show()
    orders_from_active.explain(True)

def self_join_elimination_example():
    """
    Demonstrates self join optimization patterns
    """
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 5A: Self Join for comparison (INEFFICIENT) ---")
    # INEFFICIENT: Self join to find customers in the same city
    customers_alias1 = customers_df.alias("c1")
    customers_alias2 = customers_df.alias("c2")
    
    inefficient_self_join = customers_alias1.join(
        customers_alias2,
        (col("c1.city") == col("c2.city")) & (col("c1.customer_id") < col("c2.customer_id")),
        "inner"
    ).select(
        col("c1.name").alias("customer1"),
        col("c2.name").alias("customer2"),
        col("c1.city")
    )
    
    print("Self join to find customers in same city:")
    inefficient_self_join.show()
    inefficient_self_join.explain(True)
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 5B: Using Window Functions instead (EFFICIENT) ---")
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    from pyspark.sql.functions import row_number, lag, lead, collect_list
    
    # EFFICIENT: Using window function to collect customers by city
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("city").orderBy("customer_id")
    
    customers_with_row = customers_df.withColumn(
        "row_num",
        row_number().over(window_spec)
    )
    
    print("Customers numbered within city (using window function):")
    customers_with_row.show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 5C: Self Join for finding previous/next records (INEFFICIENT) ---")
    # INEFFICIENT: Self join to find previous order
    orders_alias1 = orders_df.alias("o1")
    orders_alias2 = orders_df.alias("o2")
    
    inefficient_prev_order = orders_alias1.join(
        orders_alias2,
        (col("o1.customer_id") == col("o2.customer_id")) & 
        (col("o1.order_date") > col("o2.order_date")),
        "left"
    ).select(
        col("o1.order_id"),
        col("o1.order_date"),
        col("o1.amount"),
        col("o2.order_id").alias("prev_order_id"),
        col("o2.amount").alias("prev_amount")
    )
    
    print("Self join to find previous order (inefficient):")
    inefficient_prev_order.show(5)
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 5D: Using LAG/LEAD instead (EFFICIENT) ---")
    # EFFICIENT: Using window functions LAG/LEAD
    window_by_customer = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy("order_date")
    
    efficient_prev_order = orders_df.withColumn(
        "prev_order_id",
        lag("order_id", 1).over(window_by_customer)
    ).withColumn(
        "prev_amount",
        lag("amount", 1).over(window_by_customer)
    ).withColumn(
        "next_order_id",
        lead("order_id", 1).over(window_by_customer)
    )
    
    print("Using LAG/LEAD for previous/next order (efficient):")
    efficient_prev_order.show()
    efficient_prev_order.explain(True)
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 5E: Self Join for ranking (INEFFICIENT) ---")
    # INEFFICIENT: Self join to rank orders by amount
    inefficient_ranking = orders_alias1.join(
        orders_alias2,
        col("o1.amount") <= col("o2.amount"),
        "left"
    ).groupBy(
        col("o1.order_id"),
        col("o1.amount")
    ).agg(
        count("*").alias("rank")
    ).orderBy("rank")
    
    print("Self join for ranking (inefficient):")
    inefficient_ranking.show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 5F: Using RANK/DENSE_RANK instead (EFFICIENT) ---")
    from pyspark.sql.functions import rank, dense_rank, percent_rank
    
    # EFFICIENT: Using window ranking functions
    window_for_ranking = Window.orderBy(col("amount").desc())
    
    efficient_ranking = orders_df.withColumn(
        "rank",
        rank().over(window_for_ranking)
    ).withColumn(
        "dense_rank",
        dense_rank().over(window_for_ranking)
    ).withColumn(
        "percent_rank",
        percent_rank().over(window_for_ranking)
    )
    
    print("Using RANK/DENSE_RANK (efficient):")
    efficient_ranking.show()
    efficient_ranking.explain(True)
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 5G: Self Join for running totals (INEFFICIENT) ---")
    # INEFFICIENT: Self join for cumulative sum
    inefficient_running_total = orders_alias1.join(
        orders_alias2,
        (col("o1.customer_id") == col("o2.customer_id")) & 
        (col("o1.order_date") >= col("o2.order_date")),
        "left"
    ).groupBy(
        col("o1.order_id"),
        col("o1.customer_id"),
        col("o1.order_date"),
        col("o1.amount")
    ).agg(
        _sum(col("o2.amount")).alias("running_total")
    ).orderBy("customer_id", "order_date")
    
    print("Self join for running total (inefficient):")
    inefficient_running_total.show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 5H: Using Window SUM instead (EFFICIENT) ---")
    # EFFICIENT: Using window function for running total
    from pyspark.sql.functions import sum as spark_sum
    
    window_running = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy("order_date") \
        .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
    
    efficient_running_total = orders_df.withColumn(
        "running_total",
        spark_sum("amount").over(window_running)
    ).withColumn(
        "running_count",
        count("*").over(window_running)
    ).withColumn(
        "running_avg",
        avg("amount").over(window_running)
    )
    
    print("Using window function for running total (efficient):")
    efficient_running_total.orderBy("customer_id", "order_date").show()
    efficient_running_total.explain(True)
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 5I: Self Join for duplicate detection (ALTERNATIVE) ---")
    # Finding potential duplicates using self join
    
    # Add some duplicate-like data for demonstration
    extended_orders = orders_df.union(
        spark.createDataFrame([
            (108, 1, "2024-01-15", 250.50)  # Potential duplicate
        ], orders_df.schema)
    )
    
    # INEFFICIENT: Self join approach
    duplicates_self_join = extended_orders.alias("o1").join(
        extended_orders.alias("o2"),
        (col("o1.customer_id") == col("o2.customer_id")) &
        (col("o1.order_date") == col("o2.order_date")) &
        (col("o1.amount") == col("o2.amount")) &
        (col("o1.order_id") < col("o2.order_id")),
        "inner"
    ).select(
        col("o1.order_id").alias("order_id_1"),
        col("o2.order_id").alias("order_id_2"),
        col("o1.customer_id"),
        col("o1.amount")
    )
    
    print("Duplicate detection using self join:")
    duplicates_self_join.show()
    
    # EFFICIENT: Using window function
    from pyspark.sql.functions import count as spark_count
    
    window_duplicates = Window.partitionBy("customer_id", "order_date", "amount")
    
    duplicates_window = extended_orders.withColumn(
        "duplicate_count",
        spark_count("*").over(window_duplicates)
    ).withColumn(
        "row_num",
        row_number().over(window_duplicates)
    ).filter(col("duplicate_count") > 1)
    
    print("Duplicate detection using window function (efficient):")
    duplicates_window.show()

self_join_elimination_example()

def advanced_optimization_techniques():
    """
    Demonstrates advanced techniques for join elimination and optimization
    """
    
    print("\n--- Technique 1: Predicate Pushdown ---")
    # Pushing filters before joins reduces data shuffle
    
    # INEFFICIENT: Filter after join
    inefficient_filter = orders_df.join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    ).filter(col("amount") > 200)
    
    # EFFICIENT: Filter before join
    efficient_filter = orders_df.filter(col("amount") > 200).join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    )
    
    print("Filter pushdown optimization:")
    efficient_filter.show()
    efficient_filter.explain(True)
    
    print("\n--- Technique 2: Broadcast Join for Small Tables ---")
    from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
    
    # When one table is small, broadcast it to avoid shuffle
    broadcast_join = orders_df.join(
        broadcast(customers_df),
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    )
    
    print("Broadcast join for small table:")
    broadcast_join.show(5)
    broadcast_join.explain(True)
    
    print("\n--- Technique 3: Join Reordering ---")
    # Join smaller results first
    
    # Filter both tables first
    high_value_orders = orders_df.filter(col("amount") > 300)
    active_customers = customers_df.filter(col("customer_id") <= 3)
    
    # Join the filtered (smaller) datasets
    optimized_join = high_value_orders.join(
        active_customers,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    )
    
    print("Join reordering with filters:")
    optimized_join.show()
    
    print("\n--- Technique 4: Avoiding Cartesian Products ---")
    # Always include join conditions to avoid cartesian products
    
    # BAD: This creates a cartesian product
    # cartesian = customers_df.crossJoin(orders_df)  # Avoid this!
    
    # GOOD: Proper join condition
    proper_join = customers_df.join(
        orders_df,
        customers_df.customer_id == orders_df.customer_id,
        "inner"
    )
    
    print("Proper join with condition (avoiding cartesian):")
    print(f"Customers count: {customers_df.count()}")
    print(f"Orders count: {orders_df.count()}")
    print(f"Joined count: {proper_join.count()}")
    
    print("\n--- Technique 5: Using Bucketing and Partitioning ---")
    # Write data with bucketing for optimized joins
    
    # Example: Save orders bucketed by customer_id
    output_path = "/tmp/bucketed_orders"
    
    # Note: This is an example - adjust path for your environment
    try:
        orders_df.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .bucketBy(4, "customer_id") \
            .sortBy("order_date") \
            .saveAsTable("bucketed_orders", path=output_path)
        
        print("Data bucketed by customer_id for optimized joins")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Bucketing example (would optimize joins): {e}")
    
    print("\n--- Technique 6: Caching Intermediate Results ---")
    # Cache frequently used join results
    
    frequent_join = orders_df.join(customers_df, "customer_id", "inner")
    frequent_join.cache()
    
    # Now use it multiple times
    result1 = frequent_join.filter(col("amount") > 200).count()
    result2 = frequent_join.groupBy("city").agg(_sum("amount")).count()
    
    print(f"Cached join used multiple times efficiently")
    print(f"High value orders: {result1}")
    print(f"Cities with orders: {result2}")
    
    # Don't forget to unpersist when done
    frequent_join.unpersist()

advanced_optimization_techniques()

    ).groupBy(orders_df.customer_id).agg(

    )

    )
    
    print("Final result with customer details:")

    print("\n--- Use Case 2: Product Performance Report ---")

    from pyspark.sql.functions import concat_ws
    
    # First aggregate at order_items level
    product_stats = order_items_df.groupBy("product_id").agg(
        count("*").alias("times_ordered"),
        _sum("quantity").alias("total_quantity")
    )
    
    # Then join with product details for enrichment
    product_report = product_stats.join(
        products_df,
        "product_id",
        "inner"
    ).select(
        "product_id",
        "product_name",
        "category",
        "price",
        "times_ordered",
        "total_quantity",
        (col("total_quantity") * col("price")).alias("total_revenue")
    ).orderBy(col("total_revenue").desc())
    
    print("Product performance report:")
    product_report.show()
    
    print("\n--- Use Case 3: Customer Segmentation ---")

    from pyspark.sql.functions import when
    
    # Calculate customer segments
    customer_segments = orders_df.groupBy("customer_id").agg(
        count("*").alias("order_count"),
        _sum("amount").alias("total_spent"),
        avg("amount").alias("avg_spent")
    ).withColumn(
        "segment",
        when(col("total_spent") > 500, "Premium")
        .when(col("total_spent") > 200, "Regular")
        .otherwise("Basic")
    ).withColumn(
        "frequency",
        when(col("order_count") >= 3, "High")
        .when(col("order_count") >= 2, "Medium")
        .otherwise("Low")
    )
    
    # Join with customer info only for final display
    segmented_customers = customer_segments.join(
        customers_df.select("customer_id", "name", "email"),

        "inner"
    ).select(

        "email",
        "segment",
        "frequency",
        "order_count",
        "total_spent",
        "avg_spent"
    )
    
    print("Customer segmentation:")
    segmented_customers.show()
    
    print("\n--- Use Case 4: Time-Series Analysis ---")
    # Analyze trends without redundant joins
    
    from pyspark.sql.functions import to_date, date_format, month, year
    
    # Daily order trends
    daily_trends = orders_df.groupBy("order_date").agg(
        count("*").alias("order_count"),
        _sum("amount").alias("daily_revenue"),
        avg("amount").alias("avg_order_value")
    ).orderBy("order_date")
    
    print("Daily order trends:")
    daily_trends.show()
    
    # Add window functions for moving averages without self-joins
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    
    window_7day = Window.orderBy("order_date") \
        .rowsBetween(-6, Window.currentRow)
    
    trends_with_ma = daily_trends.withColumn(
        "moving_avg_7day",

    ).withColumn(
        "cumulative_revenue",

            Window.orderBy("order_date")
            .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
        )
    )
    
    print("Trends with moving averages:")
    trends_with_ma.show()
    
    print("\n--- Use Case 5: Inventory and Order Analysis ---")
    # Complex analysis with optimized join strategy
    
    # Step 1: Aggregate order items
    order_summary = order_items_df.groupBy("order_id").agg(

    # Step 2: Join with orders
    order_details = order_summary.join(
        orders_df,

        "inner"
    )
    
    # Step 3: Aggregate by customer
    customer_order_summary = order_details.groupBy("customer_id").agg(

    ).orderBy(col("total_spent").desc())
    
    print("Comprehensive customer order summary:")

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("BEST PRACTICES SUMMARY")

def print_best_practices():
    """
    Print comprehensive best practices for join elimination
    """
    
    best_practices = """
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║           JOIN ELIMINATION BEST PRACTICES                              ║
    ╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
    ║                                                                        ║
    ║ 1. INNER JOIN ELIMINATION                                             ║
    ║    • Avoid joins when selecting only from one table                   ║
    ║    • Use semi-joins for existence checks                              ║
    ║    • Push down filters before joining                                 ║
    ║                                                                        ║
    ║ 2. LEFT JOIN ELIMINATION                                              ║
    ║    • Remove left joins when right-side columns aren't used            ║
    ║    • Convert to anti-joins for NULL checks                            ║
    ║    • Eliminate when aggregating only left-side columns                ║
    ║                                                                        ║
    ║ 3. SEMI JOIN OPTIMIZATION                                             ║
    ║    • Use for filtering operations                                     ║
    ║    • Apply broadcast for small lookup tables                          ║
    ║    • Prefer over IN clauses for large datasets                        ║
    ║                                                                        ║
    ║ 4. OUTER JOIN ELIMINATION                                             ║
    ║    • Convert to inner joins when filtering NULLs                      ║
    ║    • Consider UNION instead of FULL OUTER when appropriate            ║
    ║    • Avoid when only one side's columns are needed                    ║
    ║                                                                        ║
    ║ 5. SELF JOIN ELIMINATION                                              ║
    ║    • Replace with window functions (LAG, LEAD, RANK)                  ║
    ║    • Use for running totals, rankings, comparisons                    ║
    ║    • Significantly reduces shuffle operations                         ║
    ║                                                                        ║
    ║ 6. GENERAL OPTIMIZATION STRATEGIES                                    ║
    ║    • Filter early, join late                                          ║
    ║    • Broadcast small tables (<10MB)                                   ║
    ║    • Use bucketing for repeated joins on same keys                    ║
    ║    • Cache intermediate results when reused                           ║
    ║    • Avoid cartesian products (always use join conditions)            ║
    ║    • Monitor query plans with explain()                               ║
    ║    • Use appropriate join types (inner, left, semi, anti)             ║
    ║    • Partition data strategically                                     ║
    ║                                                                        ║
    ║ 7. PERFORMANCE MONITORING                                             ║
    ║    • Use .explain(True) to analyze physical plans                     ║
    ║    • Check for shuffle operations in query plans                      ║
    ║    • Monitor Spark UI for stage execution times                       ║
    ║    • Profile with different data sizes                                ║
    ║                                                                        ║
    ║ 8. WHEN TO USE EACH JOIN TYPE                                         ║
    ║    • INNER: Both sides must match                                     ║
    ║    • LEFT: Keep all left records, match right                         ║
    ║    • LEFT_SEMI: Filter left by right existence                        ║
    ║    • LEFT_ANTI: Filter left by right non-existence                    ║
    ║    • FULL_OUTER: Keep all records from both sides                     ║
    ║    • CROSS: Cartesian product (use sparingly!)                        ║
    ║                                                                        ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    
    KEY TAKEAWAYS:
    
    ✓ Always question if a join is necessary
    ✓ Window functions often replace self-joins
    ✓ Filter before joining to reduce data size
    ✓ Use appropriate join types for the use case
    ✓ Monitor and optimize based on query plans
    ✓ Broadcast small dimension tables
    ✓ Cache frequently accessed joined datasets
    ✓ Partition and bucket for repeated join patterns
    
    COMMON ANTI-PATTERNS TO AVOID:
    
    ✗ Joining tables just to filter them out
    ✗ Using FULL OUTER when INNER or LEFT would work
    ✗ Self-joins for sequential operations
    ✗ Multiple joins when aggregation can be done first
    
```python
    ✗ Cartesian products without proper join conditions
    ✗ Not broadcasting small lookup tables
    ✗ Filtering after expensive joins instead of before
    ✗ Using joins when window functions are more appropriate
    """
    
    print(best_practices)

print_best_practices()

def query_plan_analysis():
    """

    """
    
    print("\n--- Analyzing Different Join Strategies ---")
    
    # Example 1: Inefficient query
    print("\n1. INEFFICIENT QUERY PLAN:")
    print("-" * 40)
    inefficient = orders_df.join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    ).join(
        order_items_df,
        "order_id",
        "inner"
    ).select("order_id", "amount")
    
    print("Query: Multiple joins but selecting only from orders table")
    inefficient.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    # Example 2: Optimized query
    print("\n2. OPTIMIZED QUERY PLAN:")
    print("-" * 40)
    optimized = orders_df.select("order_id", "amount")
    
    print("Query: Direct selection without unnecessary joins")
    optimized.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    # Example 3: Window function vs self-join
    print("\n3. WINDOW FUNCTION PLAN:")
    print("-" * 40)
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    from pyspark.sql.functions import row_number
    
    window_query = orders_df.withColumn(
        "rank",
        row_number().over(Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy(col("amount").desc()))
    ).filter(col("rank") == 1)
    
    print("Query: Top order per customer using window function")

    # Example 4: Broadcast join

    from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
    
    broadcast_query = orders_df.join(
        broadcast(customers_df),
        "customer_id",

    )
    
    print("Query: Broadcast join for small table")

def advanced_scenarios():
    """
    Demonstrates advanced scenarios and edge cases
    """
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 1: Multiple Join Conditions ---")
    # Joining on multiple columns
    
    # Create extended order data with additional join key
    extended_orders = orders_df.withColumn("order_year", lit("2024"))
    extended_customers = customers_df.withColumn("active_year", lit("2024"))
    
    multi_condition_join = extended_orders.join(
        extended_customers,
        (extended_orders.customer_id == extended_customers.customer_id) &
        (extended_orders.order_year == extended_customers.active_year),
        "inner"
    )
    
    print("Join with multiple conditions:")
    multi_condition_join.select(
        "order_id", 
        "name", 
        "amount", 
        "order_year"
    ).show(5)
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 2: Null-Safe Join ---")
    # Handling nulls in join conditions
    
    from pyspark.sql.functions import when, isnull
    
    # Add some null customer_ids for demonstration
    orders_with_nulls = orders_df.union(
        spark.createDataFrame([
            (108, None, "2024-01-22", 150.00)
        ], orders_df.schema)
    )
    
    # Regular join (nulls won't match)
    regular_null_join = orders_with_nulls.join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "left"
    )
    
    print("Left join with nulls:")
    regular_null_join.select("order_id", "customer_id", "name", "amount").show()
    
    # Null-safe join using eqNullSafe
    null_safe_join = orders_with_nulls.join(
        customers_df,
        orders_with_nulls.customer_id.eqNullSafe(customers_df.customer_id),
        "left"
    )
    
    print("Null-safe join:")
    null_safe_join.select(
        orders_with_nulls.order_id,
        orders_with_nulls.customer_id,
        customers_df.name,
        orders_with_nulls.amount
    ).show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 3: Join with Aggregation Pushdown ---")
    # Aggregate before joining for better performance
    
    # INEFFICIENT: Join then aggregate
    inefficient_agg = orders_df.join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    ).groupBy("city").agg(
        _sum("amount").alias("total_revenue"),
        count("order_id").alias("order_count")
    )
    
    print("Join then aggregate (less efficient):")
    inefficient_agg.show()
    
    # EFFICIENT: Aggregate then join
    order_agg = orders_df.groupBy("customer_id").agg(
        _sum("amount").alias("customer_total"),
        count("*").alias("customer_orders")
    )
    
    efficient_agg = order_agg.join(
        customers_df.select("customer_id", "city"),
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    ).groupBy("city").agg(
        _sum("customer_total").alias("total_revenue"),
        _sum("customer_orders").alias("order_count")
    )
    
    print("Aggregate then join (more efficient):")
    efficient_agg.show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 4: Skewed Join Optimization ---")
    # Handling data skew in joins
    
    from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, floor
    
    # Simulate skewed data (most orders from customer 1)
    skewed_orders = orders_df.union(
        spark.createDataFrame([
            (109, 1, "2024-01-23", 100.00),
            (110, 1, "2024-01-24", 150.00),
            (111, 1, "2024-01-25", 200.00),
        ], orders_df.schema)
    )
    
    # Technique: Salt the skewed key
    salted_orders = skewed_orders.withColumn(
        "salt",
        floor(rand() * 3).cast("int")
    ).withColumn(
        "salted_key",
        concat_ws("_", col("customer_id"), col("salt"))
    )
    
    salted_customers = customers_df.withColumn(
        "salt",
        floor(rand() * 3).cast("int")
    ).withColumn(
        "salted_key",
        concat_ws("_", col("customer_id"), col("salt"))
    )
    
    # Join on salted key
    skew_optimized_join = salted_orders.join(
        salted_customers,
        "salted_key",
        "inner"
    ).select(
        salted_orders.order_id,
        salted_orders.customer_id,
        salted_customers.name,
        salted_orders.amount
    )
    
    print("Skew-optimized join using salting:")
    skew_optimized_join.show(5)
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 5: Conditional Join Logic ---")
    # Different join strategies based on conditions
    
    from pyspark.sql.functions import coalesce
    
    # Left join with default values for unmatched records
    conditional_join = orders_df.join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "left"
    ).select(
        col("order_id"),
        col("customer_id"),
        coalesce(col("name"), lit("Unknown Customer")).alias("customer_name"),
        coalesce(col("city"), lit("Unknown City")).alias("customer_city"),
        col("amount")
    )
    
    print("Join with default values for unmatched records:")
    conditional_join.show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 6: Range Join Optimization ---")
    # Joining on range conditions
    
    # Create price ranges
    price_ranges = spark.createDataFrame([
        ("Budget", 0.0, 100.0),
        ("Standard", 100.01, 300.0),
        ("Premium", 300.01, 1000.0),
        ("Luxury", 1000.01, 10000.0)
    ], ["tier", "min_price", "max_price"])
    
    # Range join
    range_join = orders_df.join(
        price_ranges,
        (col("amount") >= col("min_price")) & (col("amount") <= col("max_price")),
        "inner"
    ).select(
        "order_id",
        "amount",
        "tier"
    )
    
    print("Range join for price tiers:")
    range_join.show()
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 7: Deduplication Before Join ---")
    # Remove duplicates before joining
    
    # Simulate duplicates
    orders_with_dupes = orders_df.union(
        orders_df.filter(col("order_id") == 101)
    )
    
    print(f"Orders with duplicates count: {orders_with_dupes.count()}")
    
    # INEFFICIENT: Join with duplicates
    join_with_dupes = orders_with_dupes.join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    )
    
    print(f"Join result with duplicates: {join_with_dupes.count()}")
    
    # EFFICIENT: Deduplicate first
    deduped_orders = orders_with_dupes.dropDuplicates(["order_id"])
    join_deduped = deduped_orders.join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    )
    
    print(f"Join result after deduplication: {join_deduped.count()}")
    
    print("\n--- Scenario 8: Complex Multi-Way Join Optimization ---")
    # Optimize multiple joins by ordering them correctly
    
    # Get counts to determine join order
    print(f"Customers: {customers_df.count()} rows")
    print(f"Orders: {orders_df.count()} rows")
    print(f"Order Items: {order_items_df.count()} rows")
    print(f"Products: {products_df.count()} rows")
    
    # OPTIMIZED: Join in order of increasing cardinality
    # and broadcast small tables
    multi_way_optimized = order_items_df \
        .join(broadcast(products_df), "product_id", "inner") \
        .join(orders_df, "order_id", "inner") \
        .join(broadcast(customers_df), "customer_id", "inner") \
        .select(
            "order_id",
            "customer_id",
            "name",
            "product_name",
            "quantity",
            "price",
            (col("quantity") * col("price")).alias("line_total")
        )
    
    print("Optimized multi-way join:")
    multi_way_optimized.show()
    multi_way_optimized.explain(mode="simple")

def test_join_elimination():
    """
    Validate that join elimination produces correct results
    """
    
    print("\n--- Test 1: Verify Inner Join Elimination ---")
    
    # Original query with join
    with_join = orders_df.join(
        customers_df,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    ).select("order_id", "amount").orderBy("order_id")
    
    # Optimized query without join
    without_join = orders_df.select("order_id", "amount").orderBy("order_id")
    
    # Compare results
    join_result = with_join.collect()
    optimized_result = without_join.collect()
    
    assert join_result == optimized_result, "Results don't match!"
    print("✓ Inner join elimination validated - results match")
    
    print("\n--- Test 2: Verify Semi Join vs Inner Join ---")
    
    # Semi join
    semi_result = customers_df.join(
        orders_df,
        "customer_id",
        "left_semi"
    ).select("customer_id").orderBy("customer_id").collect()
    
    # Inner join with distinct
    inner_distinct = customers_df.join(
        orders_df,
        "customer_id",
        "inner"
    ).select(customers_df.customer_id).distinct().orderBy("customer_id").collect()
    
    assert semi_result == inner_distinct, "Semi join results don't match!"
    print("✓ Semi join validated - results match inner join with distinct")
    
    print("\n--- Test 3: Verify Window Function vs Self Join ---")
    
    # Self join for running total
    orders_alias1 = orders_df.alias("o1")
    orders_alias2 = orders_df.alias("o2")
    
    self_join_result = orders_alias1.join(
        orders_alias2,
        (col("o1.customer_id") == col("o2.customer_id")) & 
        (col("o1.order_date") >= col("o2.order_date")),
        "left"
    ).groupBy(
        col("o1.order_id"),
        col("o1.customer_id"),
        col("o1.order_date"),
        col("o1.amount")
    ).agg(
        _sum(col("o2.amount")).alias("running_total")
    ).orderBy("customer_id", "order_date")
    
    # Window function
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy("order_date") \
        .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
    
    window_result = orders_df.withColumn(
        "running_total",
        spark_sum("amount").over(window_spec)
    ).select("order_id", "customer_id", "order_date", "amount", "running_total") \
     .orderBy("customer_id", "order_date")
    
    # Compare counts and sample data
    sj_count = self_join_result.count()
    w_count = window_result.count()
    
    assert sj_count == w_count, f"Row counts don't match: {sj_count} vs {w_count}"
    print("✓ Window function validated - produces same row count as self join")
    
    print("\n--- Test 4: Verify Anti Join vs Left Join with NULL filter ---")
    
    # Anti join
    anti_result = orders_df.join(
        customers_df.filter(col("customer_id")
```python
 > 100),  # Filter to create some non-matches
        "customer_id",
        "left_anti"
    ).select("order_id").orderBy("order_id").collect()
    
    # Left join with NULL filter
    left_null_result = orders_df.join(
        customers_df.filter(col("customer_id") > 100),
        "customer_id",
        "left"
    ).filter(customers_df.customer_id.isNull()) \

    assert anti_result == left_null_result, "Anti join results don't match!"

def analyze_join_performance(df, description="Query"):
    """
    Utility function to analyze join performance
    
    Args:
        df: DataFrame to analyze
        description: Description of the query
    """
    print(f"\n--- Analyzing: {description} ---")
    print(f"Row count: {df.count()}")
    print(f"Partition count: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Show execution plan
    print("\nExecution Plan:")
    df.explain(mode="simple")
    
    return df

def compare_queries(query1, query2, name1="Query 1", name2="Query 2"):
    """
    Compare two queries for performance and correctness
    
    Args:
        query1: First DataFrame query
        query2: Second DataFrame query
        name1: Name of first query
        name2: Name of second query
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print(f"COMPARING: {name1} vs {name2}")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    
    # Timing
    import time
    
    start = time.time()
    count1 = query1.count()
    time1 = time.time() - start
    
    start = time.time()
    count2 = query2.count()
    time2 = time.time() - start
    
    print(f"\n{name1}:")
    print(f"  Rows: {count1}")
    print(f"  Time: {time1:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Partitions: {query1.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    print(f"\n{name2}:")
    print(f"  Rows: {count2}")
    print(f"  Time: {time2:.4f}s")
    print(f"  Partitions: {query2.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    if time1 > 0:
        speedup = time1 / time2
        print(f"\nSpeedup: {speedup:.2f}x")
        if speedup > 1:
            print(f"✓ {name2} is faster")
        else:
            print(f"✓ {name1} is faster")
    
    # Verify results match
    if count1 == count2:
        print("✓ Row counts match")
    else:
        print(f"✗ Row counts differ: {count1} vs {count2}")

def get_join_statistics(df):
    """
    Get statistics about joins in a DataFrame
    
    Args:
        df: DataFrame to analyze
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary with join statistics
    """
    plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
    
    stats = {
        "has_broadcast_join": "BroadcastHashJoin" in plan,
        "has_sort_merge_join": "SortMergeJoin" in plan,
        "has_shuffle_hash_join": "ShuffledHashJoin" in plan,
        "has_cartesian": "CartesianProduct" in plan,
        "has_broadcast_nested_loop": "BroadcastNestedLoopJoin" in plan
    }
    
    print("\nJoin Statistics:")
    for key, value in stats.items():
        symbol = "✓" if value else "✗"
        print(f"  {symbol} {key.replace('_', ' ').title()}: {value}")
    
    return stats

def generate_optimized_join_code(join_type, left_table, right_table, join_key):
    """
    Generate optimized join code based on join type
    
    Args:
        join_type: Type of join (inner, left, semi, anti, etc.)
        left_table: Name of left table
        right_table: Name of right table
        join_key: Join key column
    
    Returns:
        String containing optimized PySpark code
    """
    
    code_templates = {
        "inner_unnecessary": f"""
# BEFORE (Inefficient):
result = {left_table}_df.join(
    {right_table}_df,
    "{join_key}",
    "inner"
).select({left_table}_df.columns)

# AFTER (Optimized):
result = {left_table}_df.select("*")
""",
        
        "left_to_semi": f"""
# BEFORE (Inefficient):
result = {left_table}_df.join(
    {right_table}_df,
    "{join_key}",
    "inner"
).select({left_table}_df.columns).distinct()

# AFTER (Optimized):
result = {left_table}_df.join(
    {right_table}_df,
    "{join_key}",
    "left_semi"
)
""",
        
        "self_to_window": f"""
# BEFORE (Inefficient - Self Join):
{left_table}_alias1 = {left_table}_df.alias("t1")
{left_table}_alias2 = {left_table}_df.alias("t2")

result = {left_table}_alias1.join(
    {left_table}_alias2,
    (col("t1.{join_key}") == col("t2.{join_key}")) & 
    (col("t1.value") >= col("t2.value")),
    "left"
).groupBy("t1.id").agg(sum("t2.value").alias("running_total"))

# AFTER (Optimized - Window Function):
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.functions import sum

window_spec = Window.partitionBy("{join_key}").orderBy("value") \\
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)

result = {left_table}_df.withColumn(
    "running_total",
    sum("value").over(window_spec)
)
""",
        
        "broadcast": f"""
# BEFORE (Regular Join):
result = {left_table}_df.join(
    {right_table}_df,
    "{join_key}",
    "inner"
)

# AFTER (Broadcast Join - when {right_table} is small):
from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast

result = {left_table}_df.join(
    broadcast({right_table}_df),
    "{join_key}",
    "inner"
)
"""
    }
    
    return code_templates

# Generate examples
print("\n--- Generated Optimization Code Examples ---")

╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗

╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

1. INNER JOIN ELIMINATION PATTERN
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
   
   When to Apply:
   • Selecting columns from only one side of the join
   • Join is used only for filtering (use semi-join instead)
   • Aggregating without using joined table columns
   
   Performance Impact: 
   • Eliminates shuffle operations
   • Reduces memory usage
   • Speeds up query execution by 2-10x
   
   Example Use Cases:
   • Getting order details when customer data isn't needed
   • Filtering records based on existence in another table
   • Simple aggregations on single table

2. LEFT JOIN ELIMINATION PATTERN
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
   
   When to Apply:
   • No columns from right table are used in output
   • Filtering out NULL values from right side (convert to inner)
   • Checking for non-existence (use anti-join instead)
   
   Performance Impact:
   • Reduces data processed
   • Eliminates unnecessary outer join overhead
   • Improves query speed by 1.5-5x
   
   Example Use Cases:
   • Finding records without matches (anti-join)
   • Aggregating left table only
   • Existence checks

3. SEMI JOIN ELIMINATION PATTERN
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
   
   When to Apply:
   • Filtering left table based on right table existence
   • Alternative to IN or EXISTS clauses
   • When right table columns are not needed
   
   Performance Impact:
   • More efficient than inner join + distinct
   • Reduces data shuffle
   • Speeds up filtering by 2-5x
   
   Example Use Cases:
   • Finding customers who placed orders
   • Filtering products that were sold
   • Existence-based filtering

4. OUTER JOIN ELIMINATION PATTERN
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
   
   When to Apply:
   • Filtering NULLs converts to inner join
   • Only one side's columns are needed
   • UNION can replace FULL OUTER in some cases
   
   Performance Impact:
   • Converts expensive outer join to inner join
   • Reduces memory for NULL handling
   • Improves performance by 2-8x
   
   Example Use Cases:
   • Full outer with NULL filters
   • Combining datasets with UNION instead
   • Simplifying join logic

5. SELF JOIN ELIMINATION PATTERN
   ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
   
   When to Apply:
   • Ranking, running totals, or sequential operations
   • Comparing current row with previous/next
   • Finding duplicates or patterns
   
   Performance Impact:
   • Eliminates expensive self-join shuffle
   • Uses window functions (single pass)
   • Speeds up queries by 5-20x
   
   Example Use Cases:
   • Running totals and moving averages
   • Ranking and percentile calculations
   • LAG/LEAD operations
   • Row numbering
