def optimization_techniques(df):
    """
    Advanced optimization techniques for scanning patterns
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("OPTIMIZATION TECHNIQUES")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    print("\n[Optimization 1] Predicate Pushdown")
    
    # Write data in Parquet format
    pushdown_path = "/tmp/predicate_pushdown"
    df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(pushdown_path)
    
    # Query with predicates (pushed down to storage layer)
    start_time = time.time()
    optimized = spark.read.parquet(pushdown_path) \
        .filter(col('amount') > 500) \
        .select('transaction_id', 'amount', 'category')
    
    result_count = optimized.count()
    print(f"\nPredicate pushdown result: {result_count:,} records")
    print(f"Execution time: {time.time() - start_time:.3f} seconds")
    print("\n--- Notice predicate pushdown in plan ---")
    optimized.explain(extended=False)
    
    
    print("\n[Optimization 2] Column Pruning")
    start_time = time.time()
    
    # Select only needed columns (reduces I/O)
    column_pruned = spark.read.parquet(pushdown_path) \
        .select('category', 'amount') \
        .groupBy('category') \
        .agg(sum('amount').alias('total'))
    
    column_pruned.show()
    print(f"Execution time: {time.time() - start_time:.3f} seconds")
    
    
    print("\n[Optimization 3] Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)")
    
    # Enable AQE
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true")
    
    start_time = time.time()
    
    aqe_query = df.groupBy('region', 'category') \
        .agg(sum('amount').alias('revenue')) \
        .orderBy(desc('revenue'))
    
    aqe_query.show(10)
    print(f"Execution time with AQE: {time.time() - start_time:.3f} seconds")
    
    
    print("\n[Optimization 4] Dynamic Partition Pruning")
    
    # Create dimension table
    high_value_categories = df.groupBy('category') \
        .agg(sum('amount').alias('total_revenue')) \
        .filter(col('total_revenue') > 100000) \
        .select('category')
    
    # Partition main table
    dpp_path = "/tmp/dynamic_partition_pruning"
    df.write.mode("overwrite").partitionBy("category").parquet(dpp_path)
    fact_table = spark.read.parquet(dpp_path)
    
    start_time = time.time()
    
    # Join will trigger dynamic partition pruning
    result = fact_table.join(
        high_value_categories,
        on='category',
        how='inner'
    ).groupBy('category') \
     .agg(count('*').alias('transaction_count'))
    
    result.show()
    print(f"Execution time with DPP: {time.time() - start_time:.3f} seconds")
    
    
    print("\n[Optimization 5] Broadcast Join Optimization")
    start_time = time.time()
    
    # Small lookup table
    category_lookup = spark.createDataFrame([
        {'category': 'Electronics', 'tax_rate': 0.08},
        {'category': 'Clothing', 'tax_rate': 0.06},
        {'category': 'Food', 'tax_rate': 0.02},
        {'category': 'Books', 'tax_rate': 0.0},

    ])

        broadcast(category_lookup),
        on='category',
        how='inner'
    ).withColumn('tax_amount', col('amount') * col('tax_rate')) \

     )

        .parquet(zorder_path)
    
    zorder_df = spark.read.parquet(zorder_path)
    
    start_time = time.time()
    
    # Multi-dimensional query benefits from Z-ordering

        (col('category') == 'Electronics') &
        (col('region') == 'North') &
        (col('transaction_date') >= '2023-06-01')
    ).count()
    
    print(f"Z-ordered scan result: {result:,} records")

def compare_scan_strategies(df, query_predicate, strategies):
    """
    Utility function to compare multiple scanning strategies
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        query_predicate: Filter condition to apply
        strategies: Dict of strategy names and DataFrame configurations
    
    Returns:
        Performance comparison results
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SCANNING STRATEGY COMPARISON")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    results = {}
    
    for strategy_name, strategy_df in strategies.items():
        print(f"\nTesting: {strategy_name}")
        start_time = time.time()
        
        result = strategy_df.filter(query_predicate).count()
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        results[strategy_name] = {
            'time': execution_time,
            'count': result
        }
        
        print(f"  Time: {execution_time:.3f}s, Count: {result:,}")
    
    # Find best strategy
    best_strategy = min(results.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['time'])
    print(f"\n🏆 Best Strategy: {best_strategy[0]} ({best_strategy[1]['time']:.3f}s)")
    
    return results


def generate_scan_report(df, output_path="/tmp/scan_report.txt"):
    """
    Generate a comprehensive scanning performance report
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        output_path: Path to save the report
    """
    print(f"\n📝 Generating scan performance report...")
    
    report_lines = []
    report_lines.append("=" * 80)
    report_lines.append("DATA SCANNING PERFORMANCE REPORT")
    report_lines.append("=" * 80)
    report_lines.append(f"\nGenerated at: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}")
    
    # Dataset statistics
    report_lines.append("\n\nDATASET STATISTICS")
    report_lines.append("-" * 80)
    report_lines.append(f"Total records: {df.count():,}")
    report_lines.append(f"Total partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Schema info
    report_lines.append(f"\nSchema:")
    for field in df.schema.fields:
        report_lines.append(f"  - {field.name}: {field.dataType}")
    
    # Column statistics
    report_lines.append("\n\nCOLUMN STATISTICS")
    report_lines.append("-" * 80)
    
    numeric_cols = [f.name for f in df.schema.fields 
                   if str(f.dataType) in ['IntegerType', 'LongType', 'DoubleType', 'FloatType']]
    
    if numeric_cols:
        stats = df.select(numeric_cols).summary()
        report_lines.append(stats.toPandas().to_string())
    
    # Partition distribution
    report_lines.append("\n\nPARTITION DISTRIBUTION")
    report_lines.append("-" * 80)
    
    partition_counts = df.rdd.mapPartitions(lambda x: [sum(1 for _ in x)]).collect()
    for i, count in enumerate(partition_counts):
        report_lines.append(f"Partition {i}: {count:,} records")
    
    # Write report
    report_content = "\n".join(report_lines)
    
    # In a real environment, write to file
    # with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
    #     f.write(report_content)
    
    print(report_content)
    print(f"\n✓ Report generated successfully")
    
    return report_content


def create_optimal_scan_strategy(df, query_patterns):
    """
    Automatically determine optimal scanning strategy based on query patterns
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        query_patterns: List of common query patterns
    
    Returns:
        Recommended scanning strategy
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("AUTOMATIC SCAN STRATEGY OPTIMIZATION")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    recommendations = []
    
    # Analyze query patterns
    for i, pattern in enumerate(query_patterns):
        print(f"\n[Pattern {i+1}] Analyzing: {pattern['description']}")
        
        # Check selectivity
        sample = df.sample(withReplacement=False, fraction=0.01)
        sample_result = sample.filter(pattern['predicate']).count()
        sample_total = sample.count()
        
        selectivity = (sample_result / sample_total * 100) if sample_total > 0 else 0
        
        print(f"  Estimated selectivity: {selectivity:.2f}%")
        
        # Recommend strategy based on selectivity and pattern
        if selectivity < 1:
            strategy = "Index Scan (Bucketing) or Partition Scan"
            reason = "Very high selectivity - index/partition will be most efficient"
        elif selectivity < 10:
            strategy = "Partition Scan or Range Scan"
            reason = "High selectivity - partition pruning recommended"
        elif selectivity < 50:
            strategy = "Range Scan with Parallel Processing"
            reason = "Moderate selectivity - range scan with parallelism"
        else:
            strategy = "Full Table Scan with Parallel Processing"
            reason = "Low selectivity - full scan is acceptable"
        
        recommendations.append({
            'pattern': pattern['description'],
            'selectivity': selectivity,
            'strategy': strategy,
            'reason': reason
        })
        
        print(f"  ✓ Recommended: {strategy}")
        print(f"  Reason: {reason}")
    
    # Summary
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("STRATEGY RECOMMENDATIONS SUMMARY")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    for rec in recommendations:
        print(f"\n{rec['pattern']}")
        print(f"  Selectivity: {rec['selectivity']:.2f}%")
        print(f"  Strategy: {rec['strategy']}")
        print(f"  Reason: {rec['reason']}")
    
    return recommendations

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
import struct
import base64

# Initialize Spark Session
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("Column Encoding Patterns") \
    .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
    .getOrCreate()

# ============================================================================
# 1. DICTIONARY ENCODING PATTERN (Refined)
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Replace repeated values with integer codes to save space
# Use Case: Columns with low cardinality (categories, statuses, etc.)

class DictionaryEncoder:
    """
    Dictionary encoding for categorical columns with efficient lookup.
    Stores unique values once and references them by integer codes.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def encode(df: DataFrame, column: str) -> Tuple[DataFrame, Dict]:
        """
        Encode a column using dictionary encoding.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column name to encode
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (encoded DataFrame, dictionary mapping)
        """
        # Create dictionary of unique values
        unique_values = df.select(column).distinct().rdd.flatMap(lambda x: x).collect()
        
        # Create bidirectional mapping
        value_to_code = {value: idx for idx, value in enumerate(unique_values)}
        code_to_value = {idx: value for value, idx in value_to_code.items()}
        
        # Broadcast dictionary for efficient lookup
        broadcast_dict = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(value_to_code)
        
        # Create UDF for encoding
        @F.udf(IntegerType())
        def encode_udf(value):
            return broadcast_dict.value.get(value, -1)
        
        # Apply encoding
        encoded_df = df.withColumn(
            f"{column}_encoded",
            encode_udf(F.col(column))
        )
        
        return encoded_df, code_to_value
    
    @staticmethod
    def decode(df: DataFrame, column: str, dictionary: Dict) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Decode a dictionary-encoded column.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame with encoded column
            column: Encoded column name
            dictionary: Code to value mapping
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with decoded column
        """
        broadcast_dict = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(dictionary)
        
        @F.udf(StringType())
        def decode_udf(code):
            return broadcast_dict.value.get(code, "UNKNOWN")
        
        decoded_df = df.withColumn(
            f"{column}_decoded",
            decode_udf(F.col(column))
        )
        
        return decoded_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def get_compression_stats(df: DataFrame, original_col: str, encoded_col: str) -> Dict:
        """Calculate compression statistics."""
        original_size = df.select(F.length(original_col).alias("len")).agg(
            F.sum("len").alias("total")
        ).collect()[0]["total"]
        
        # Assuming 4 bytes per integer
        encoded_size = df.count() * 4
        
        return {
            "original_size_bytes": original_size,
            "encoded_size_bytes": encoded_size,
            "compression_ratio": original_size / encoded_size if encoded_size > 0 else 0
        }


# ============================================================================
# 2. RUN-LENGTH ENCODING PATTERN (Refined)
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Compress sequences of repeated values
# Use Case: Columns with long runs of identical values (flags, statuses over time)

class RunLengthEncoder:
    """
    Run-Length Encoding for sequences with repeated values.
    Stores value and count of consecutive occurrences.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def encode(df: DataFrame, column: str, partition_cols: List[str] = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Encode column using run-length encoding.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column to encode
            partition_cols: Columns to partition by (optional)
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with RLE encoding (value, run_length, run_id)
        """
        # Create row number for change detection
        if partition_cols:
            window_spec = Window.partitionBy(partition_cols).orderBy(F.monotonically_increasing_id())
        else:
            window_spec = Window.orderBy(F.monotonically_increasing_id())
        
        # Add row number
        df_with_row = df.withColumn("row_num", F.row_number().over(window_spec))
        
        # Detect value changes
        df_with_change = df_with_row.withColumn(
            "value_changed",
            F.when(
                F.col(column) != F.lag(column, 1).over(window_spec),
                1
            ).otherwise(0)
        )
        
        # Create run IDs
        df_with_runs = df_with_change.withColumn(
            "run_id",
            F.sum("value_changed").over(
                window_spec.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
            )
        )
        
        # Group by run and calculate run length
        partition_cols_list = partition_cols if partition_cols else []
        rle_df = df_with_runs.groupBy(partition_cols_list + ["run_id", column]).agg(
            F.count("*").alias("run_length"),
            F.min("row_num").alias("start_position")
        ).orderBy(partition_cols_list + ["start_position"])
        
        return rle_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def decode(rle_df: DataFrame, value_col: str, length_col: str = "run_length") -> DataFrame:
        """
        Decode RLE encoded data back to original format.
        
        Args:
            rle_df: RLE encoded DataFrame
            value_col: Column containing values
            length_col: Column containing run lengths
            
        Returns:
            Decoded DataFrame
        """
        # Explode runs back to individual rows
        decoded_df = rle_df.withColumn(
            "repeat_array",
            F.array_repeat(F.col(value_col), F.col(length_col))
        ).withColumn(
            value_col,
            F.explode("repeat_array")
        ).drop("repeat_array", length_col)
        
        return decoded_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def calculate_compression_ratio(original_df: DataFrame, rle_df: DataFrame) -> float:
        """Calculate compression ratio achieved by RLE."""
        original_count = original_df.count()
        compressed_count = rle_df.count()
        
        return original_count / compressed_count if compressed_count > 0 else 0


# ============================================================================
# 3. BIT-PACKING ENCODING PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Pack multiple small integers into fewer bytes
# Use Case: Columns with small integer ranges (0-255, flags, small IDs)

class BitPackingEncoder:
    """
    Bit-packing encoding for efficient storage of small integers.
    Packs multiple values into single bytes.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def encode_boolean_flags(df: DataFrame, flag_columns: List[str]) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Pack multiple boolean columns into a single integer.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            flag_columns: List of boolean column names
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with packed flags column
        """
        if len(flag_columns) > 64:
            raise ValueError("Maximum 64 boolean flags supported")
        
        # Create bit-packing expression
        packed_expr = F.lit(0)
        for idx, col_name in enumerate(flag_columns):
            # Shift and OR each boolean flag
            packed_expr = packed_expr | (
                F.when(F.col(col_name), F.lit(1)).otherwise(F.lit(0)) << idx
            )
        
        result_df = df.withColumn("packed_flags", packed_expr)
        
        return result_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def decode_boolean_flags(df: DataFrame, packed_col: str, 
                            flag_names: List[str]) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Unpack boolean flags from packed integer.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame with packed column
            packed_col: Name of packed column
            flag_names: Names for unpacked flags
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with unpacked boolean columns
        """
        result_df = df
        
        for idx, flag_name in enumerate(flag_names):
            # Extract bit at position idx
            result_df = result_df.withColumn(
                flag_name,
                ((F.col(packed_col) >> idx) & 1) == 1
            )
        
        return result_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def pack_small_integers(df: DataFrame, columns: List[str], 
                           bits_per_value: int = 8) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Pack multiple small integers into binary representation.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            columns: Columns to pack (must fit in bits_per_value)
            bits_per_value: Bits allocated per value
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with packed binary column
        """
        max_value = (1 << bits_per_value) - 1
        
        @F.udf(StringType())
        def pack_udf(*values):
            # Pack values into bytes
            packed_bytes = bytearray()
            for value in values:
                if value is None:
                    value = 0
                if value > max_value:
                    value = max_value
                packed_bytes.append(int(value))
            
            # Return base64 encoded string
            return base64.b64encode(packed_bytes).decode('utf-8')
        
        result_df = df.withColumn(
            "packed_integers",
            pack_udf(*[F.col(c) for c in columns])
        )
        
        return result_df


# ============================================================================
# 4. DELTA ENCODING PATTERN (Refined)
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Store differences between consecutive values instead of absolute values
# Use Case: Monotonically increasing sequences (timestamps, IDs, counters)

class DeltaEncoder:
    """
    Delta encoding for sequences with small differences.
    Stores first value and deltas, reducing storage for incremental data.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def encode(df: DataFrame, column: str, partition_cols: List[str] = None,
               order_cols: List[str] = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Encode column using delta encoding.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column to encode
            partition_cols: Partition columns
            order_cols: Ordering columns
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with delta-encoded values
        """
        # Define window specification
        if partition_cols:
            window_spec = Window.partitionBy(partition_cols)
        else:
            window_spec = Window.partitionBy()
        
        if order_cols:
            for order_col in order_cols:
                window_spec = window_spec.orderBy(order_col)
        else:
            window_spec = window_spec.orderBy(F.monotonically_increasing_id())
        
        # Calculate delta (current - previous)
        delta_df = df.withColumn(
            f"{column}_delta",
            F.col(column) - F.coalesce(
                F.lag(column, 1).over(window_spec),
                F.lit(0)
            )
        ).withColumn(
            f"{column}_is_base",
            F.when(F.lag(column, 1).over(window_spec).isNull(), True).otherwise(False)
        )
        
        return delta_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def encode_with_base(df: DataFrame, column: str, 
                        partition_cols: List[str] = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Delta encoding with explicit base values per partition.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column to encode
            partition_cols: Partition columns
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with base values and deltas
        """
        if partition_cols:
            window_spec = Window.partitionBy(partition_cols).orderBy(F.monotonically_increasing_id())
        else:
            window_spec = Window.orderBy(F.monotonically_increasing_id())
        
        # Get base value (first in partition)
        base_window = Window.partitionBy(partition_cols) if partition_cols else Window.partitionBy()
        
        result_df = df.withColumn(
            f"{column}_base",
            F.first(column).over(base_window)
        ).withColumn(
            f"{column}_delta",
            F.col(column) - F.col(f"{column}_base")
        )
        
        return result_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def decode(df: DataFrame, delta_col: str, base_col: str = None,
               partition_cols: List[str] = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Decode delta-encoded values.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame with delta-encoded values
            delta_col: Delta column name
            base_col: Base value column (if using base encoding)
            partition_cols: Partition columns
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with reconstructed original values
        """
        if base_col:
            # Simple reconstruction: base + delta
            decoded_df = df.withColumn(
                f"{delta_col}_decoded",
                F.col(base_col) + F.col(delta_col)
            )
        else:
            # Cumulative sum of deltas
            if partition_cols:
                window_spec = Window.partitionBy(partition_cols).orderBy(F.monotonically_increasing_id())
            else:
                window_spec = Window.orderBy(F.monotonically_increasing_id())
            
            decoded_df = df.withColumn(
                f"{delta_col}_decoded",
                F.sum(delta_col).over(
                    window_spec.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
                )
            )
        
        return decoded_df


# ============================================================================
# 5. PREFIX ENCODING PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Store common prefixes once and reference them
# Use Case: Strings with common prefixes (URLs, file paths, hierarchical codes)

class PrefixEncoder:
    """
    Prefix encoding for strings with common prefixes.
    Extracts and stores common prefixes separately.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def encode_with_common_prefix(df: DataFrame, column: str, 
                                  min_prefix_length: int = 3) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Encode strings by extracting common prefixes.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: String column to encode
            min_prefix_length: Minimum prefix length to extract
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with prefix and suffix columns
        """
        @F.udf(StructType([
            StructField("prefix", StringType(), True),
            StructField("suffix", StringType(), True),
            StructField("prefix_length", IntegerType(), True)
        ]))
        def extract_prefix(value):
            if not value or len(value) < min_prefix_length:
                return ("", value, 0)
            
            # Find common prefix (simplified - in production, use trie or prefix tree)
            prefix_len = min_prefix_
```python
            prefix_len = min_prefix_length
            prefix = value[:prefix_len]
            suffix = value[prefix_len:]
            
            return (prefix, suffix, prefix_len)
        
        result_df = df.withColumn(
            "prefix_data",
            extract_prefix(F.col(column))
        ).select(
            "*",
            F.col("prefix_data.prefix").alias(f"{column}_prefix"),
            F.col("prefix_data.suffix").alias(f"{column}_suffix"),
            F.col("prefix_data.prefix_length").alias(f"{column}_prefix_len")
        ).drop("prefix_data")
        
        return result_df
    
    @staticmethod
    def encode_with_dictionary_prefix(df: DataFrame, column: str,
                                     max_prefixes: int = 1000) -> Tuple[DataFrame, Dict]:
        """
        Encode using a dictionary of common prefixes.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column to encode
            max_prefixes: Maximum number of unique prefixes to store
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (encoded DataFrame, prefix dictionary)
        """
        # Find most common prefixes
        prefix_df = df.withColumn(
            "temp_prefix",
            F.substring(F.col(column), 1, 10)  # Extract first 10 chars
        ).groupBy("temp_prefix").agg(
            F.count("*").alias("frequency")
        ).orderBy(F.desc("frequency")).limit(max_prefixes)
        
        # Create prefix dictionary
        prefixes = prefix_df.collect()
        prefix_dict = {row["temp_prefix"]: idx for idx, row in enumerate(prefixes)}
        
        broadcast_prefixes = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(prefix_dict)
        
        @F.udf(StructType([
            StructField("prefix_id", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("suffix", StringType(), True)
        ]))
        def encode_with_dict(value):
            if not value:
                return (-1, value)
            
            # Find matching prefix
            for prefix, prefix_id in broadcast_prefixes.value.items():
                if value.startswith(prefix):
                    return (prefix_id, value[len(prefix):])
            
            return (-1, value)
        
        encoded_df = df.withColumn(
            "encoded_data",
            encode_with_dict(F.col(column))
        ).select(
            "*",
            F.col("encoded_data.prefix_id").alias(f"{column}_prefix_id"),
            F.col("encoded_data.suffix").alias(f"{column}_suffix")
        ).drop("encoded_data")
        
        # Invert dictionary for decoding
        decode_dict = {v: k for k, v in prefix_dict.items()}
        
        return encoded_df, decode_dict
    
    @staticmethod
    def decode(df: DataFrame, prefix_col: str, suffix_col: str,
              prefix_dict: Dict = None) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Decode prefix-encoded strings.
        
        Args:
            df: Encoded DataFrame
            prefix_col: Prefix column name
            suffix_col: Suffix column name
            prefix_dict: Dictionary mapping prefix IDs to prefixes
            
        Returns:
            Decoded DataFrame
        """
        if prefix_dict:
            broadcast_dict = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(prefix_dict)
            
            @F.udf(StringType())
            def decode_udf(prefix_id, suffix):
                if prefix_id == -1:
                    return suffix
                prefix = broadcast_dict.value.get(prefix_id, "")
                return prefix + (suffix or "")
            
            decoded_df = df.withColumn(
                "decoded_value",
                decode_udf(F.col(prefix_col), F.col(suffix_col))
            )
        else:
            # Simple concatenation
            decoded_df = df.withColumn(
                "decoded_value",
                F.concat(F.col(prefix_col), F.col(suffix_col))
            )
        
        return decoded_df


# ============================================================================
# 6. ADAPTIVE ENCODING PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Automatically select best encoding based on data characteristics
# Use Case: Mixed data types, varying cardinality, dynamic workloads

class AdaptiveEncoder:
    """
    Adaptive encoding that selects the best encoding strategy based on data analysis.
    Analyzes column characteristics and applies optimal encoding.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def analyze_column(df: DataFrame, column: str) -> Dict:
        """
        Analyze column characteristics to determine best encoding.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column to analyze
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with analysis results
        """
        stats = df.select(column).summary("count", "min", "max").collect()
        
        # Get basic statistics
        total_count = int(stats[0][column])
        distinct_count = df.select(column).distinct().count()
        null_count = df.filter(F.col(column).isNull()).count()
        
        # Calculate cardinality ratio
        cardinality_ratio = distinct_count / total_count if total_count > 0 else 0
        
        # Analyze data type
        col_type = df.schema[column].dataType
        
        # Check for sequential pattern (for numeric columns)
        is_sequential = False
        avg_delta = None
        
        if isinstance(col_type, (IntegerType, LongType, DoubleType, FloatType)):
            window_spec = Window.orderBy(F.monotonically_increasing_id())
            delta_df = df.withColumn(
                "delta",
                F.col(column) - F.lag(column, 1).over(window_spec)
            ).filter(F.col("delta").isNotNull())
            
            if delta_df.count() > 0:
                delta_stats = delta_df.agg(
                    F.avg("delta").alias("avg_delta"),
                    F.stddev("delta").alias("stddev_delta")
                ).collect()[0]
                
                avg_delta = delta_stats["avg_delta"]
                stddev_delta = delta_stats["stddev_delta"]
                
                # Sequential if standard deviation is low
                if stddev_delta is not None and avg_delta is not None:
                    is_sequential = stddev_delta < abs(avg_delta) * 0.1
        
        # Check for run-length encoding potential
        window_spec = Window.orderBy(F.monotonically_increasing_id())
        runs_df = df.withColumn(
            "value_changed",
            F.when(F.col(column) != F.lag(column, 1).over(window_spec), 1).otherwise(0)
        )
        run_count = runs_df.filter(F.col("value_changed") == 1).count()
        run_ratio = run_count / total_count if total_count > 0 else 1
        
        return {
            "total_count": total_count,
            "distinct_count": distinct_count,
            "null_count": null_count,
            "cardinality_ratio": cardinality_ratio,
            "data_type": str(col_type),
            "is_sequential": is_sequential,
            "avg_delta": avg_delta,
            "run_count": run_count,
            "run_ratio": run_ratio
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def select_encoding(analysis: Dict) -> str:
        """
        Select best encoding strategy based on analysis.
        
        Args:
            analysis: Column analysis results
            
        Returns:
            Recommended encoding strategy
        """
        cardinality_ratio = analysis["cardinality_ratio"]
        run_ratio = analysis["run_ratio"]
        is_sequential = analysis["is_sequential"]
        
        # Decision tree for encoding selection
        if cardinality_ratio < 0.01:
            # Very low cardinality - use dictionary encoding
            return "dictionary"
        elif run_ratio < 0.3:
            # Many consecutive duplicates - use run-length encoding
            return "run_length"
        elif is_sequential and analysis["avg_delta"] is not None:
            # Sequential numeric data - use delta encoding
            return "delta"
        elif cardinality_ratio < 0.1:
            # Low to medium cardinality - use dictionary encoding
            return "dictionary"
        elif "String" in analysis["data_type"]:
            # String data - try prefix encoding
            return "prefix"
        else:
            # Default - no encoding or bit-packing for small integers
            if "Integer" in analysis["data_type"] or "Boolean" in analysis["data_type"]:
                return "bit_packing"
            return "none"
    
    @staticmethod
    def encode(df: DataFrame, column: str, 
               encoding_strategy: str = None) -> Tuple[DataFrame, Dict]:
        """
        Apply adaptive encoding to a column.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            column: Column to encode
            encoding_strategy: Force specific strategy (optional)
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (encoded DataFrame, encoding metadata)
        """
        # Analyze column if strategy not specified
        if encoding_strategy is None:
            analysis = AdaptiveEncoder.analyze_column(df, column)
            encoding_strategy = AdaptiveEncoder.select_encoding(analysis)
        else:
            analysis = {}
        
        metadata = {
            "column": column,
            "strategy": encoding_strategy,
            "analysis": analysis
        }
        
        # Apply selected encoding
        if encoding_strategy == "dictionary":
            encoded_df, dictionary = DictionaryEncoder.encode(df, column)
            metadata["dictionary"] = dictionary
            
        elif encoding_strategy == "run_length":
            encoded_df = RunLengthEncoder.encode(df, column)
            
        elif encoding_strategy == "delta":
            encoded_df = DeltaEncoder.encode(df, column)
            
        elif encoding_strategy == "prefix":
            encoded_df, prefix_dict = PrefixEncoder.encode_with_dictionary_prefix(df, column)
            metadata["prefix_dictionary"] = prefix_dict
            
        elif encoding_strategy == "bit_packing":
            # For single column, just mark for bit-packing
            encoded_df = df.withColumn(f"{column}_bitpack_ready", F.col(column))
            
        else:
            # No encoding
            encoded_df = df
            metadata["strategy"] = "none"
        
        return encoded_df, metadata
    
    @staticmethod
    def encode_dataframe(df: DataFrame, columns: List[str] = None) -> Tuple[DataFrame, Dict]:
        """
        Apply adaptive encoding to multiple columns in a DataFrame.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            columns: Columns to encode (None = all columns)
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (encoded DataFrame, encoding metadata for all columns)
        """
        if columns is None:
            columns = df.columns
        
        result_df = df
        all_metadata = {}
        
        for column in columns:
            print(f"Analyzing and encoding column: {column}")
            result_df, metadata = AdaptiveEncoder.encode(result_df, column)
            all_metadata[column] = metadata
            print(f"  Selected strategy: {metadata['strategy']}")
        
        return result_df, all_metadata

    print(f"  Compression Ratio: {rle_ratio:.2f}x")
    
    # Delta encoding on counter
    delta_encoded = DeltaEncoder.encode(large_df, "counter", order_cols=["id"])
    print(f"\nDelta Encoding (counter column):")
    print(f"  Average delta: {delta_encoded.select(F.avg('counter_delta')).collect()[0][0]:.2f}")
    
    # Adaptive encoding
    adaptive_encoded, adaptive_meta = AdaptiveEncoder.encode_dataframe(
        large_df,
        columns=["status", "counter", "url"]
    )
    print(f"\nAdaptive Encoding Results:")
    for col, meta in adaptive_meta.items():
        print(f"  {col}: {meta['strategy']}")


# ============================================================================
# UTILITY FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

def create_encoding_report(df: DataFrame, columns: List[str] = None) -> DataFrame:
    """
    Generate a comprehensive encoding recommendation report.
    
    Args:
        df: Input DataFrame
        columns: Columns to analyze (None = all columns)
        
    Returns:
        DataFrame with encoding recommendations
    """
    if columns is None:
        columns = df.columns
    
    report_data = []
    
    for col in columns:
        analysis = AdaptiveEncoder.analyze_column(df, col)
        recommended = AdaptiveEncoder.select_encoding(analysis)
        
        report_data.append((
            col,
            analysis['data_type'],
            analysis['total_count'],
            analysis['distinct_count'],
            analysis['cardinality_ratio'],
            analysis['run_ratio'],
            analysis['is_sequential'],
            recommended
        ))
    
    report_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        report_data,
        ["column_name", "data_type", "total_count", "distinct_count",
         "cardinality_ratio", "run_ratio", "is_sequential", "recommended_encoding"]
    )
    
    return report_df


def estimate_storage_savings(df: DataFrame, encoding_metadata: Dict) -> Dict:
    """
    Estimate storage savings from encoding.
    
    Args:
        df: Original DataFrame
        encoding_metadata: Metadata from encoding operations
        
    Returns:
        Dictionary with storage estimates
    """
    total_rows = df.count()
    savings_estimate = {}
    
    for col, meta in encoding_metadata.items():
        strategy = meta['strategy']
        
        if strategy == "dictionary":
            # Estimate: 4 bytes per integer vs average string length
            dict_size = len(meta.get('dictionary', {}))
            encoded_size = total_rows * 4 + dict_size * 50  # Rough estimate
            original_size = total_rows * 20  # Assume avg 20 bytes per string
            savings = (original_size - encoded_size) / original_size * 100
            
        elif strategy == "run_length":
            # Based on run ratio
            run_ratio = meta['analysis'].get('run_ratio', 1.0)
            savings = (1 - run_ratio) * 100
            
        elif strategy == "delta":
            # Delta encoding typically saves 50-70% for sequential data
            savings = 60 if meta['analysis'].get('is_sequential') else 30
            
        elif strategy == "prefix":
            # Estimate based on prefix dictionary size
            savings = 40  # Rough estimate
            
        elif strategy == "bit_packing":
            # Boolean: 1 bit vs 1 byte
            savings = 87.5  # (8-1)/8 * 100
            
        else:
            savings = 0
        
        savings_estimate[col] = {
            'strategy': strategy,
            'estimated_savings_percent': round(savings, 2)
        }
    
    return savings_estimate


# ============================================================================
# MAIN EXECUTION
# ============================================================================

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Run demonstrations
    demonstrate_encoding_patterns()
    
    # Additional examples
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)

         ["Active", "Inactive", "Pending"][i % 3],
         100 + i * 5,

         i % 2 == 0,
         i % 3 == 0)
        for i in range(100)
    ]
    
    sample_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        sample_data,
        ["id", "status", "counter", "url", "is_active", "is_premium"]
    )

    report.show(truncate=False)

        sample_df,
        columns=["status", "counter", "url"]
    )

    print("\nEstimated Storage Savings:")
    for col, info in savings.items():
        print(f"{col}: {info['estimated_savings_percent']}% ({info['strategy']})")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ENCODING PATTERNS DEMONSTRATION COMPLETE")
    print("=" * 80)

```

## Summary and Best Practices

This comprehensive implementation provides six column encoding patterns for PySpark:

### 1. **Dictionary Encoding Pattern**
- **Best for**: Low cardinality columns (statuses, categories, countries)
- **Compression**: 5-10x for typical categorical data
- **Overhead**: Dictionary storage and lookup

### 2
### 2. **Run-Length Encoding Pattern**
- **Best for**: Columns with consecutive repeated values
- **Compression**: 2-100x depending on run lengths
- **Overhead**: Additional columns for run_id and run_length

### 3. **Bit-Packing Encoding Pattern**
- **Best for**: Boolean flags and small integers (0-255)
- **Compression**: 8x for booleans, 2-4x for small integers
- **Overhead**: Packing/unpacking computation

### 4. **Delta Encoding Pattern**
- **Best for**: Sequential/monotonic numeric data (timestamps, counters, IDs)
- **Compression**: 2-4x for typical sequential data
- **Overhead**: Cumulative sum for decoding

### 5. **Prefix Encoding Pattern**
- **Best for**: Strings with common prefixes (URLs, file paths, hierarchical codes)
- **Compression**: 2-5x depending on prefix commonality
- **Overhead**: Prefix dictionary and string operations

### 6. **Adaptive Encoding Pattern**
- **Best for**: Mixed workloads, unknown data characteristics
- **Compression**: Automatically selects optimal strategy
- **Overhead**: Initial analysis phase

def advanced_example_2_incremental_encoding():
    """Advanced: Incremental encoding for streaming data"""
    print("\nAdvanced Example 2: Incremental Encoding for Streaming")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Simulate initial batch
    initial_data = [(i, f"status_{i % 3}", 100 + i) for i in range(100)]
    initial_df = spark.createDataFrame(initial_data, ["id", "status", "value"])
    
    print("Initial batch:")
    initial_df.show(5)
    
    # Create initial encodings
    print("\nCreating initial encodings...")
    status_encoded, status_dict = DictionaryEncoder.encode(initial_df, "status")
    print(f"Initial dictionary: {status_dict}")
    
    # Simulate new batch with new values
    new_data = [(i, f"status_{i % 5}", 200 + i) for i in range(100, 120)]
    new_df = spark.createDataFrame(new_data, ["id", "status", "value"])
    
    print("\nNew batch:")
    new_df.show(5)
    
    # Handle new values in incremental encoding
    print("\nHandling new values...")
    new_statuses = new_df.select("status").distinct().rdd.flatMap(lambda x: x).collect()
    
    # Update dictionary with new values
    next_id = max(status_dict.values()) + 1
    updated_dict = status_dict.copy()
    
    for status in new_statuses:
        if status not in updated_dict:
            updated_dict[status] = next_id
            next_id += 1
            print(f"Added new value to dictionary: {status} -> {updated_dict[status]}")
    
    print(f"\nUpdated dictionary: {updated_dict}")
    
    # Encode new batch with updated dictionary
    broadcast_dict = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(updated_dict)
    
    @F.udf(IntegerType())
    def encode_incremental(value):
        return broadcast_dict.value.get(value, -1)
    
    new_encoded = new_df.withColumn(
        "status_encoded",
        encode_incremental(F.col("status"))
    )
    
    print("\nNew batch encoded:")
    new_encoded.show(5)


def advanced_example_3_partitioned_encoding():
    """Advanced: Partition-aware encoding"""
    print("\nAdvanced Example 3: Partition-Aware Encoding")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Create partitioned data
    partitioned_data = []
    import random
    
    for region in ["US", "EU", "APAC"]:
        for i in range(100):
            partitioned_data.append((
                region,
                i,
                random.choice(["active", "inactive"]),
                1000 + i * 10
            ))
    
    partitioned_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        partitioned_data,
        ["region", "seq", "status", "counter"]
    )
    
    print("Partitioned data sample:")
    partitioned_df.show(10)
    
    # Apply partition-aware delta encoding
    print("\nApplying partition-aware delta encoding...")
    partitioned_delta = DeltaEncoder.encode(
        partitioned_df,
        "counter",
        partition_cols=["region"],
        order_cols=["seq"]
    )
    
    print("Delta encoding per partition:")
    partitioned_delta.groupBy("region").agg(
        F.avg("counter_delta").alias("avg_delta"),
        F.min("counter_delta").alias("min_delta"),
        F.max("counter_delta").alias("max_delta")
    ).show()
    
    # Apply partition-aware RLE
    print("\nApplying partition-aware RLE...")
    partitioned_rle = RunLengthEncoder.encode(
        partitioned_df,
        "status",
        partition_cols=["region"]
    )
    
    print("RLE compression per partition:")
    partitioned_rle.groupBy("region").agg(
        F.sum("run_length").alias("total_rows"),
        F.count("*").alias("num_runs")
    ).withColumn(
        "compression_ratio",
        F.col("total_rows") / F.col("num_runs")
    ).show()


def advanced_example_4_custom_encoding():
    """Advanced: Custom encoding pattern"""
    print("\nAdvanced Example 4: Custom Encoding Pattern")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Example: Frequency-based encoding (Huffman-like)
    custom_data = [(i, random.choice(["A"]*50 + ["B"]*30 + ["C"]*15 + ["D"]*5)) 
                   for i in range(1000)]
    custom_df = spark.createDataFrame(custom_data, ["id", "value"])
    
    print("Original data distribution:")
    custom_df.groupBy("value").count().orderBy(F.desc("count")).show()
    
    # Create frequency-based encoding (assign shorter codes to frequent values)
    freq_dist = custom_df.groupBy("value").count().orderBy(F.desc("count")).collect()
    
    # Assign codes based on frequency (most frequent = smallest code)
    freq_encoding = {row["value"]: idx for idx, row in enumerate(freq_dist)}
    
    print(f"\nFrequency-based encoding: {freq_encoding}")
    print("(Lower codes = higher frequency = better compression)")
    
    broadcast_encoding = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(freq_encoding)
    
    @F.udf(IntegerType())
    def freq_encode(value):
        return broadcast_encoding.value.get(value, -1)
    
    freq_encoded = custom_df.withColumn(
        "value_encoded",
        freq_encode(F.col("value"))
    )
    
    print("\nEncoded data sample:")
    freq_encoded.show(10)
    
    print("\nEncoding distribution:")
    freq_encoded.groupBy("value_encoded").count().orderBy("value_encoded").show()

"""
COLUMN ENCODING PATTERNS - COMPREHENSIVE GUIDE
==============================================

WHEN TO USE EACH PATTERN:

1. Dictionary Encoding
   ✓ Categorical columns with < 10% unique values
   ✓ Status codes, country codes, product categories
   ✓ Repeated string values
   ✗ High cardinality columns
   ✗ Unique identifiers

2. Run-Length Encoding
   ✓ Sorted or time-series data with duplicates
   ✓ Status flags over time
   ✓ Sensor readings with stable values
   ✗ Random/unsorted data
   ✗ High variance columns

3. Bit-Packing
   ✓ Boolean flags (multiple per row)
   ✓ Small integer ranges (0-255)
   ✓ Enum values with few options
   ✗ Large integer ranges
   ✗ Floating point numbers

4. Delta Encoding
   ✓ Sequential IDs or counters
   ✓ Timestamps
   ✓ Monotonically increasing values
   ✗ Random numbers
   ✗ Non-sequential data

5. Prefix Encoding
   ✓ URLs with common domains
   ✓ File paths with shared directories
   ✓ Hierarchical identifiers
   ✗ Random strings
   ✗ Short strings

6. Adaptive Encoding
   ✓ Unknown data characteristics
   ✓ Mixed workloads
   ✓ Evolving data patterns
   ✓ Production environments

COMPRESSION RATIOS (Typical):
- Dictionary: 5-10x for low cardinality
- Run-Length: 2-100x depending on runs
- Bit-Packing: 8x for booleans
- Delta: 2-4x for sequential data
- Prefix: 2-5x for common prefixes
- Adaptive: Varies based on selection

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- All encodings are reversible (lossless)
- Consider query patterns when choosing encoding
- Combine multiple strategies for optimal results
- Monitor performance in production
- Re-evaluate as data patterns change
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from datetime import datetime
from typing import List, Optional
import logging

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class DataMergePatterns:
    """
    A comprehensive class implementing various data merge strategy patterns in PySpark.
    Useful for CDC (Change Data Capture) and data lake operations.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Initialize the DataMergePatterns class.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
        """
        self.spark = spark
        logger.info("DataMergePatterns initialized")
    
    # ==================== PATTERN 1: INSERT-ONLY MERGE PATTERN ====================
    def insert_only_merge(
        self,
        target_df: DataFrame,
        source_df: DataFrame,
        key_columns: List[str],
        target_path: str
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Insert-Only Merge Pattern: Only insert new records that don't exist in target.
        Use Case: Append-only logs, event streams, immutable data
        
        Args:
            target_df: Existing target DataFrame
            source_df: New source DataFrame with records to insert
            key_columns: List of columns to identify unique records
            target_path: Path to save the merged data
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with merged results
        """
        logger.info("Starting Insert-Only Merge Pattern")
        
        # Add metadata columns
        source_with_metadata = source_df.withColumn(
            "inserted_at", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "merge_type", lit("INSERT")
        )
        
        # Perform left anti join to get only new records
        # Records in source that are NOT in target
        new_records = source_with_metadata.join(
            target_df,
            on=key_columns,
            how="left_anti"
        )
        
        # Union with existing target data
        merged_df = target_df.unionByName(new_records, allowMissingColumns=True)
        
        # Write merged data
        merged_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(target_path)
        
        logger.info(f"Insert-Only Merge completed. New records: {new_records.count()}")
        return merged_df
    
    
    # ==================== PATTERN 2: UPDATE-ONLY MERGE PATTERN ====================
    def update_only_merge(
        self,
        target_df: DataFrame,
        source_df: DataFrame,
        key_columns: List[str],
        update_columns: List[str],
        target_path: str
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Update-Only Merge Pattern: Only update existing records, don't insert new ones.
        Use Case: Dimension updates, profile corrections, status changes
        
        Args:
            target_df: Existing target DataFrame
            source_df: Source DataFrame with updates
            key_columns: Columns to match records
            update_columns: Columns to update
            target_path: Path to save the merged data
            
        Returns:
            Updated DataFrame
        """
        logger.info("Starting Update-Only Merge Pattern")
        
        # Add update metadata
        source_with_metadata = source_df.withColumn(
            "updated_at", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "merge_type", lit("UPDATE")
        )
        
        # Find matching records (inner join)
        matching_keys = target_df.select(key_columns).join(
            source_with_metadata.select(key_columns),
            on=key_columns,
            how="inner"
        )
        
        # Get records to update from target
        records_to_update = target_df.join(
            matching_keys,
            on=key_columns,
            how="inner"
        )
        
        # Get records to keep unchanged
        records_to_keep = target_df.join(
            matching_keys,
            on=key_columns,
            how="left_anti"
        )
        
        # Get updated values from source
        updated_records = source_with_metadata.join(
            matching_keys,
            on=key_columns,
            how="inner"
        )
        
        # Combine: unchanged records + updated records
        merged_df = records_to_keep.unionByName(
            updated_records, 
            allowMissingColumns=True
        )
        
        # Write merged data
        merged_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(target_path)
        
        logger.info(f"Update-Only Merge completed. Updated records: {updated_records.count()}")
        return merged_df
    
    
    # ==================== PATTERN 3: DELETE-ONLY MERGE PATTERN ====================
    def delete_only_merge(
        self,
        target_df: DataFrame,
        delete_keys_df: DataFrame,
        key_columns: List[str],
        target_path: str,
        soft_delete: bool = True
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Delete-Only Merge Pattern: Remove or mark records as deleted.
        Use Case: GDPR compliance, data cleanup, soft deletes
        
        Args:
            target_df: Existing target DataFrame
            delete_keys_df: DataFrame containing keys of records to delete
            key_columns: Columns to identify records to delete
            target_path: Path to save the merged data
            soft_delete: If True, mark as deleted; if False, physically remove
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame after deletions
        """
        logger.info(f"Starting Delete-Only Merge Pattern (soft_delete={soft_delete})")
        
        if soft_delete:
            # Soft delete: Mark records as deleted
            # Add deleted flag to target if not exists
            if "is_deleted" not in target_df.columns:
                target_df = target_df.withColumn("is_deleted", lit(False))
            
            # Mark matching records as deleted
            merged_df = target_df.join(
                delete_keys_df.select(key_columns).withColumn("_to_delete", lit(True)),
                on=key_columns,
                how="left"
            ).withColumn(
                "is_deleted",
                when(col("_to_delete") == True, lit(True)).otherwise(col("is_deleted"))
            ).withColumn(
                "deleted_at",
                when(col("_to_delete") == True, current_timestamp()).otherwise(col("deleted_at"))
            ).drop("_to_delete")
            
        else:
            # Hard delete: Physically remove records
            merged_df = target_df.join(
                delete_keys_df.select(key_columns),
                on=key_columns,
                how="left_anti"
            )
        
        # Write merged data
        merged_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(target_path)
        
        delete_count = target_df.count() - merged_df.filter(
            col("is_deleted") == False if soft_delete else lit(True)
        ).count()
        
        logger.info(f"Delete-Only Merge completed. Deleted records: {delete_count}")
        return merged_df
    
    
    # ==================== PATTERN 4: FULL MERGE PATTERN ====================
    def full_merge_pattern(
        self,
        target_df: DataFrame,
        source_df: DataFrame,
        key_columns: List[str],
        target_path: str,
        scd_type: int = 1
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Full Merge Pattern: Handle INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations.
        Use Case: Complete CDC implementation, full data synchronization
        
        Args:
            target_df: Existing target DataFrame
            source_df: Source DataFrame with all changes
            key_columns: Columns to identify unique records
            target_path: Path to save the merged data
            scd_type: Slowly Changing Dimension type (1 or 2)
            
        Returns:
            Fully merged DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Starting Full Merge Pattern (SCD Type {scd_type})")
        
        # Add operation type if not present in source
        if "operation" not in source_df.columns:
            source_df = source_df.withColumn("operation", lit("UPSERT"))
        
        # Add metadata
        source_with_metadata = source_df.withColumn(
            "merge_timestamp", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "record_version", lit(1)
        )
        
        if scd_type == 1:
            # SCD Type 1: Overwrite existing records
            merged_df = self._full_merge_scd1(
                target_df, source_with_metadata, key_columns
            )
        else:
            # SCD Type 2: Keep history
            merged_df = self._full_merge_scd2(
                target_df, source_with_metadata, key_columns
            )
        
        # Write merged data
        merged_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(target_path)
        
        logger.info("Full Merge Pattern completed")
        return merged_df
    
    
    def _full_merge_scd1(
        self,
        target_df: DataFrame,
        source_df: DataFrame,
        key_columns: List[str]
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """SCD Type 1 implementation for full merge"""
        
        # Separate operations
        inserts = source_df.filter(col("operation") == "INSERT")
        updates = source_df.filter(col("operation").isin(["UPDATE", "UPSERT"]))
        deletes = source_df.filter(col("operation") == "DELETE")
        
        # Process deletes (soft delete)
        if "is_deleted" not in target_df.columns:
            target_df = target_df.withColumn("is_deleted", lit(False))
        
        target_after_delete = target_df.join(
            deletes.select(key_columns).withColumn("_delete_flag", lit(True)),
            on=key_columns,
            how="left"
        ).withColumn(
            "is_deleted",
            when(col("_delete_flag") == True, lit(True)).otherwise(col("is_deleted"))
        ).drop("_delete_flag")
        
        # Process updates
        target_after_update = target_after_delete.join(
            updates.select("*"),
            on=key_columns,
            how="left"
        )
        
        # Coalesce to get updated values
        for column in updates.columns:
            if column not in key_columns and column in target_after_delete.columns:
                target_after_update = target_after_update.withColumn(
                    column,
                    coalesce(updates[column], target_after_delete[column])
                )
        
        # Process inserts
        new_records = inserts.join(
            target_after_update.select(key_columns),
            on=key_columns,
            how="left_anti"
        )
        
        # Union all
        merged_df = target_after_update.unionByName(
            new_records,
            allowMissingColumns=True
        )
        
        return merged_df
    
    
    def _full_merge_scd2(
        self,
        target_df: DataFrame,
        source_df: DataFrame,
        key_columns: List[str]
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """SCD Type 2 implementation for full merge"""
        
        # Add SCD Type 2 columns if not present
        if "effective_start_date" not in target_df.columns:
            target_df = target_df.withColumn(
                "effective_start_date", current_timestamp()
            ).withColumn(
                "effective_end_date", lit(None).cast(TimestampType())
            ).withColumn(
                "is_current", lit(True)
            )
        
        # Close existing records that are being updated
        updated_keys = source_df.filter(
            col("operation").isin(["UPDATE", "UPSERT"])
        ).select(key_columns)
        
        target_closed = target_df.join(
            updated_keys.withColumn("_update_flag", lit(True)),
            on=key_columns,
            how="left"
        ).withColumn(
            "effective_end_date",
            when(col("_update_flag") == True, current_timestamp())
            .otherwise(col("effective_end_date"))
        ).withColumn(
            "is_current",
            when(col("_update_flag") == True, lit(False))
            .otherwise(col("is_current"))
        ).drop("_update_flag")
        
        # Add new versions
        new_versions = source_df.filter(
            col("operation").isin(["INSERT", "UPDATE", "UPSERT"])
        ).withColumn(
            "effective_start_date", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "effective_end_date", lit(None).cast(TimestampType())
        ).withColumn(
            "is_current", lit(True)
        )
        
        # Union all
        merged_df = target_closed.unionByName(
            new_versions,
            allowMissingColumns=True
        )
        
        return merged_df
    
    
    # ==================== PATTERN 5: CONDITIONAL MERGE PATTERN ====================
    def conditional_merge_pattern(
        self,
        target_df: DataFrame,
        source_df: DataFrame,
        key_columns: List[str],
        condition_column: str,
        condition_logic: str,
        target_path: str
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Conditional Merge Pattern: Apply merge based on business rules/conditions.
        Use Case: Quality gates, approval workflows, conditional updates
        
        Args:
            target_df: Existing target DataFrame
            source_df: Source DataFrame
            key_columns: Columns to identify records
            condition_column: Column to evaluate condition
            condition_logic: SQL-like condition (e.g., "status = 'APPROVED'")
            target_path: Path to save the merged data
            
        Returns:
            Conditionally merged DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Starting Conditional Merge Pattern with condition: {condition_logic}")
        
        # Filter source data based on condition
        qualified_source = source_df.filter(expr(condition_logic)).withColumn(
            "merge_timestamp", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "merge_condition", lit(condition_logic)
        )
        
        # Records that don't meet condition go to quarantine
        quarantine_records = source_df.filter(~expr(condition_logic)).withColumn(
            "quarantine_reason", lit(f"Failed condition: {condition_logic}")
        ).withColumn(
            "quarantine_timestamp", current_timestamp()
        )
        
        # Perform merge only with qualified records
        # Get records to update
        target_to_update = target_df.join(
            qualified_source.select(key_columns),
            on=key_columns,
            how="inner"
        )
        
        # Get records to keep unchanged
        target_to_keep = target_df.join(
            qualified_source.select(key_columns),
            on=key_columns,
            how="left_anti"
        )
        
        # Get new records from qualified source
        new_records = qualified_source.join(
            target_df.select(key_columns),
            on=key_columns,
            how="left_anti"
        )
        
        # Merge: keep unchanged + qualified source
        merged_df = target_to_keep.unionByName(
            qualified_source,
            allowMissingColumns=True
        ).unionByName(
            new_records,
            allowMissingColumns=True
        )
        
```python
        # Write merged data
        merged_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(target_path)
        
        # Write quarantine records to separate location
        if quarantine_records.count() > 0:
            quarantine_path = target_path.replace("/merged/", "/quarantine/")
            quarantine_records.write.mode("append").parquet(quarantine_path)
            logger.warning(f"Quarantined {quarantine_records.count()} records")
        
        logger.info(f"Conditional Merge completed. Merged: {qualified_source.count()}")
        return merged_df
    
    
    # ==================== PATTERN 6: PARTITION-LEVEL MERGE PATTERN ====================
    def partition_level_merge_pattern(
        self,
        target_path: str,
        source_df: DataFrame,
        key_columns: List[str],
        partition_columns: List[str],
        merge_mode: str = "overwrite"
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Partition-Level Merge Pattern: Merge data at partition level for efficiency.
        Use Case: Large datasets, time-series data, incremental loads
        
        Args:
            target_path: Path to partitioned target data
            source_df: Source DataFrame with new/updated data
            key_columns: Columns to identify unique records
            partition_columns: Columns used for partitioning
            merge_mode: 'overwrite' or 'merge' at partition level
            
        Returns:
            Merged DataFrame
        """
        logger.info(f"Starting Partition-Level Merge Pattern (mode={merge_mode})")
        
        # Add merge metadata
        source_with_metadata = source_df.withColumn(
            "merge_timestamp", current_timestamp()
        ).withColumn(
            "partition_merge_mode", lit(merge_mode)
        )
        
        # Get distinct partitions from source
        source_partitions = source_with_metadata.select(
            partition_columns
        ).distinct().collect()
        
        logger.info(f"Processing {len(source_partitions)} partitions")
        
        if merge_mode == "overwrite":
            # Overwrite mode: Replace entire partitions
            result_df = self._partition_overwrite_merge(
                target_path,
                source_with_metadata,
                partition_columns
            )
        else:
            # Merge mode: Merge within partitions
            result_df = self._partition_merge_within(
                target_path,
                source_with_metadata,
                key_columns,
                partition_columns
            )
        
        logger.info("Partition-Level Merge completed")
        return result_df
    
    
    def _partition_overwrite_merge(
        self,
        target_path: str,
        source_df: DataFrame,
        partition_columns: List[str]
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """Overwrite specific partitions with source data"""
        
        # Enable dynamic partition overwrite
        self.spark.conf.set(
            "spark.sql.sources.partitionOverwriteMode", "dynamic"
        )
        
        # Write source data - will overwrite only affected partitions
        source_df.write.mode("overwrite").partitionBy(
            *partition_columns
        ).parquet(target_path)
        
        # Read back the complete dataset
        merged_df = self.spark.read.parquet(target_path)
        
        return merged_df
    
    
    def _partition_merge_within(
        self,
        target_path: str,
        source_df: DataFrame,
        key_columns: List[str],
        partition_columns: List[str]
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """Merge records within each partition"""
        
        # Read existing target data
        try:
            target_df = self.spark.read.parquet(target_path)
        except:
            # If target doesn't exist, just write source
            source_df.write.mode("overwrite").partitionBy(
                *partition_columns
            ).parquet(target_path)
            return source_df
        
        # Get partitions that need merging
        source_partitions = source_df.select(partition_columns).distinct()
        
        # Get target data for affected partitions
        target_affected = target_df.join(
            source_partitions,
            on=partition_columns,
            how="inner"
        )
        
        # Get target data for unaffected partitions
        target_unaffected = target_df.join(
            source_partitions,
            on=partition_columns,
            how="left_anti"
        )
        
        # Merge within affected partitions
        # Remove old versions of records being updated
        target_to_keep = target_affected.join(
            source_df.select(key_columns + partition_columns),
            on=key_columns + partition_columns,
            how="left_anti"
        )
        
        # Combine: unaffected partitions + kept records + new/updated records
        merged_df = target_unaffected.unionByName(
            target_to_keep,
            allowMissingColumns=True
        ).unionByName(
            source_df,
            allowMissingColumns=True
        )
        
        # Write merged data
        merged_df.write.mode("overwrite").partitionBy(
            *partition_columns
        ).parquet(target_path)
        
        return merged_df

        (2, "Jane Smith Updated", "jane.new@email.com", "Active", "2024-01-01", "UPDATE"),
        (6, "David Lee", "david@email.com", "Active", "2024-01-03", "INSERT"),
        (7, "Emma Davis", "emma@email.com", "Pending", "2024-01-03", "INSERT"),
        (3, "Bob Johnson", "bob@email.com", "Active", "2024-01-01", "UPDATE"),
    ]
    
    source_schema = StructType([
        StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("email", StringType(), True),
        StructField("status", StringType(), True),
        StructField("partition_date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("operation", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    source_df = spark.createDataFrame(source_data, source_schema)
    
    # Delete keys
    delete_data = [(5,)]
    delete_schema = StructType([
        StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), False)
    ])
    delete_df = spark.createDataFrame(delete_data, delete_schema)
    
    return target_df, source_df, delete_df
